Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi

The Abhidhamma Mātikā

Ekaṃ [M 0.0001][V 0.0001] samayaṃ bhagavā devesu viharati tāvatiṃsabhavane pāricchattakamūle paṇḍukambalasilāyaṃ. Tatra kho bhagavā devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ abhidhammakathaṃ kathesi.

At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the devas in the Tāvatiṃsa heaven, at the foot of the Pāricchattaka tree, on the Paṇḍukambala stone. There the Blessed One expounded the Abhidhamma to the Tāvatiṃsa devas.

1. Dhammasaṅgaṇīmātikā

1. The Dhammasaṅgaṇī Mātikā

Tikamātikā

The Matrix of Triads

Kusalā dhammā (dha. sa. tikamātikā 1-22), akusalā dhammā, abyākatā dhammā. Sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā dhammā, dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā dhammā, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā dhammā. Vipākā dhammā, vipākadhammadhammā, nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Upādiṇṇupādāniyā [V 0.0002] dhammā, anupādiṇṇupādāniyā dhammā, anupādiṇṇaanupādāniyā dhammā. Saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā dhammā, asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā dhammā, asaṃkiliṭṭhaasaṃkilesikā dhammā. Savitakkasavicārā dhammā, avitakkavicāramattā dhammā, avitakkaavicārā dhammā. Pītisahagatā dhammā, sukhasahagatā dhammā, upekkhāsahagatā dhammā. Dassanena pahātabbā dhammā, bhāvanāya pahātabbā dhammā, neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā dhammā. Dassanena pahātabbahetukā dhammā, bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā dhammā, neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā dhammā[M 0.0002]. Ācayagāmino dhammā, apacayagāmino dhammā, nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino dhammā. Sekkhā dhammā, asekkhā dhammā, nevasekkhanāsekkhā dhammā. Parittā dhammā, mahaggatā dhammā, appamāṇā dhammā. Parittārammaṇā dhammā, mahaggatārammaṇā dhammā, appamāṇārammaṇā dhammā. Hīnā dhammā, majjhimā dhammā, paṇītā dhammā. Micchattaniyatā dhammā, sammattaniyatā dhammā, aniyatā dhammā. Maggārammaṇā dhammā, maggahetukā dhammā, maggādhipatino dhammā. Uppannā dhammā, anuppannā dhammā, uppādino dhammā. Atītā dhammā, anāgatā dhammā, paccuppannā dhammā. Atītārammaṇā dhammā, anāgatārammaṇā dhammā, paccuppannārammaṇā dhammā. Ajjhattā dhammā, bahiddhā dhammā, ajjhattabahiddhā dhammā. Ajjhattārammaṇā dhammā, bahiddhārammaṇā dhammā, ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā dhammā. Sanidassanasappaṭighā dhammā, anidassanasappaṭighā dhammā, anidassanaappaṭighā dhammā (dha. sa. tikamātikā 1-22).

Wholesome states, unwholesome states, indeterminate states. States associated with pleasant feeling, states associated with painful feeling, states associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. Resultant states, states that are result-producing, states that are neither resultant nor result-producing. States that are clung to and objects of clinging, states that are not clung to but are objects of clinging, states that are neither clung to nor objects of clinging. Defiled and defiling states, undefiled but defiling states, undefiled and non-defiling states. States with applied and sustained thought, states with sustained thought but without applied thought, states without applied and sustained thought. States accompanied by joy, states accompanied by happiness, states accompanied by equanimity. States to be abandoned by seeing, states to be abandoned by cultivation, states to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation. States with roots that are to be abandoned by seeing, states with roots that are to be abandoned by cultivation, states with roots that are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation. States leading to accumulation, states leading to decline, states leading neither to accumulation nor to decline. States of a trainee, states of one beyond training, states that are neither of a trainee nor of one beyond training. Limited states, exalted states, immeasurable states. States with limited objects, states with exalted objects, states with immeasurable objects. Inferior states, middling states, sublime states. States fixed in wrongness, states fixed in rightness, indeterminate states. States with the path as object, states with the path as cause, states with the path as dominant condition. Arisen states, unarisen states, states that are to arise. Past states, future states, present states. States with past objects, states with future objects, states with present objects. Internal states, external states, internal and external states. States with internal objects, states with external objects, states with internal and external objects. States that are visible and resistant, states that are invisible but resistant, states that are invisible and non-resistant.

Dvāvīsatitikaṃ.

The Twenty-Two Triads.

Dukamātikā

The Matrix of Dyads

Hetugocchakaṃ

The Root Cluster

Hetū dhammā, na hetū dhammā. Sahetukā dhammā, ahetukā dhammā. Hetusampayuttā dhammā, hetuvippayuttā dhammā. Hetū ceva dhammā sahetukā ca, sahetukā ceva dhammā na ca hetū. Hetū ceva [V 0.0003] dhammā hetusampayuttā ca, hetusampayuttā ceva dhammā na ca hetū. Na hetū kho pana dhammā sahetukāpi, ahetukāpi. Hetugocchakaṃ.

States that are roots, states that are not roots. States with roots, states without roots. States associated with roots, states dissociated from roots. States that are roots and are with roots; and states that are with roots but are not roots. States that are roots and are associated with roots; and states that are associated with roots but are not roots. But states that are not roots are either with roots or without roots. The Root Cluster.

Cūḷantaradukaṃ

The Lesser Intermediate Dyad

Sappaccayā dhammā, appaccayā dhammā. Saṅkhatā dhammā, asaṅkhatā dhammā. Sanidassanā dhammā, anidassanā dhammā. Sappaṭighā dhammā, appaṭighā [M 0.0003] dhammā. Rūpino dhammā, arūpino dhammā. Lokiyā dhammā, lokuttarā dhammā. Kenaci viññeyyā dhammā, kenaci na viññeyyā dhammā. Cūḷantaradukaṃ.

States that are causally related, states that are not causally related. Conditioned states, unconditioned states. Visible states, invisible states. Impingent states, non-impingent states. Material states, immaterial states. Mundane states, supramundane states. States cognizable in some way, states not cognizable in any way. The Lesser Intermediate Dyad.

Āsavagocchakaṃ

The Taint Cluster

Āsavā dhammā, no āsavā dhammā. Sāsavā dhammā, anāsavā dhammā. Āsavasampayuttā dhammā, āsavavippayuttā dhammā. Āsavā ceva dhammā sāsavā ca, sāsavā ceva dhammā no ca āsavā. Āsavā ceva dhammā āsavasampayuttā ca, āsavasampayuttā ceva dhammā no ca āsavā. Āsavavippayuttā kho pana dhammā sāsavāpi, anāsavāpi. Āsavagocchakaṃ.

States that are taints, states that are not taints. States with taints, states without taints. States associated with taints, states dissociated from taints. States that are taints and are with taints; and states that are with taints but are not taints. States that are taints and are associated with taints; and states that are associated with taints but are not taints. But states dissociated from taints are either with taints or without taints. The Taint Cluster.

Saññojanagocchakaṃ

The Fetter Cluster

Saññojanā dhammā, no saññojanā dhammā. Saññojaniyā dhammā, asaññojaniyā dhammā. Saññojanasampayuttā dhammā, saññojanavippayuttā dhammā. Saññojanā ceva dhammā saññojaniyā ca, saññojaniyā ceva dhammā no ca saññojanā. Saññojanā ceva dhammā saññojanasampayuttā ca, saññojanasampayuttā ceva dhammā no ca saññojanā. Saññojanavippayuttā kho pana dhammā saññojaniyāpi, asaññojaniyāpi. Saññojanagocchakaṃ.

States that are fetters, states that are not fetters. States liable to fetters, states not liable to fetters. States associated with fetters, states dissociated from fetters. States that are fetters and are liable to fetters; and states that are liable to fetters but are not fetters. States that are fetters and are associated with fetters; and states that are associated with fetters but are not fetters. But states dissociated from fetters are either liable to fetters or not liable to fetters. The Fetter Cluster.

Ganthagocchakaṃ

The Grouping on Ties

Ganthā dhammā, no ganthā dhammā. Ganthaniyā dhammā, aganthaniyā dhammā. Ganthasampayuttā dhammā, ganthavippayuttā dhammā. Ganthā ceva dhammā ganthaniyā ca, ganthaniyā ceva dhammā no ca ganthā[V 0.0004]. Ganthā ceva dhammā ganthasampayuttā ca, ganthasampayuttā ceva dhammā no ca ganthā. Ganthavippayuttā kho pana dhammā ganthaniyāpi, aganthaniyāpi. Ganthagocchakaṃ.

States that are ties, states that are not ties. States liable to ties, states not liable to ties. States associated with ties, states dissociated from ties. States that are ties and are liable to ties; and states that are liable to ties but are not ties. States that are ties and are associated with ties; and states that are associated with ties but are not ties. But states dissociated from ties are either liable to ties or not liable to ties. The Grouping on Ties.

Oghagocchakaṃ

The Grouping on Floods

Oghā [M 0.0004] dhammā, no oghā dhammā. Oghaniyā dhammā, anoghaniyā dhammā. Oghasampayuttā dhammā, oghavippayuttā dhammā. Oghā ceva dhammā oghaniyā ca, oghaniyā ceva dhammā no ca oghā. Oghā ceva dhammā oghasampayuttā ca, oghasampayuttā ceva dhammā no ca oghā. Oghavippayuttā kho pana dhammā oghaniyāpi, anoghaniyāpi. Oghagocchakaṃ.

States that are floods, states that are not floods. States liable to floods, states not liable to floods. States associated with floods, states dissociated from floods. States that are floods and are liable to floods; and states that are liable to floods but are not floods. States that are floods and are associated with floods; and states that are associated with floods but are not floods. But states dissociated from floods are either liable to floods or not liable to floods. The Grouping on Floods.

Yogagocchakaṃ

The Grouping on Yokes

Yogā dhammā, no yogā dhammā. Yoganiyā dhammā, ayoganiyā dhammā. Yogasampayuttā dhammā, yogavippayuttā dhammā. Yogā ceva dhammā yoganiyā ca, yoganiyā ceva dhammā no ca yogā. Yogā ceva dhammā yogasampayuttā ca, yogasampayuttā ceva dhammā no ca yogā. Yogavippayuttā kho pana dhammā yoganiyāpi, ayoganiyāpi. Yogagocchakaṃ.

States that are yokes, states that are not yokes. States liable to yokes, states not liable to yokes. States associated with yokes, states dissociated from yokes. States that are yokes and are liable to yokes; and states that are liable to yokes but are not yokes. States that are yokes and are associated with yokes; and states that are associated with yokes but are not yokes. But states dissociated from yokes are either liable to yokes or not liable to yokes. The Grouping on Yokes.

Nīvaraṇagocchakaṃ

The Grouping on Hindrances

Nīvaraṇā dhammā, no nīvaraṇā dhammā. Nīvaraṇiyā dhammā, anīvaraṇiyā dhammā. Nīvaraṇasampayuttā dhammā, nīvaraṇavippayuttā dhammā. Nīvaraṇā ceva dhammā nīvaraṇiyā ca, nīvaraṇiyā ceva dhammā no ca nīvaraṇā. Nīvaraṇā ceva dhammā nīvaraṇasampayuttā ca, nīvaraṇasampayuttā ceva dhammā no ca nīvaraṇā. Nīvaraṇavippayuttā kho pana dhammā nīvaraṇiyāpi, anīvaraṇiyāpi. Nīvaraṇagocchakaṃ.

States that are hindrances, states that are not hindrances. States liable to hindrances, states not liable to hindrances. States associated with hindrances, states dissociated from hindrances. States that are hindrances and are liable to hindrances; and states that are liable to hindrances but are not hindrances. States that are hindrances and are associated with hindrances; and states that are associated with hindrances but are not hindrances. But states dissociated from hindrances are either liable to hindrances or not liable to hindrances. The Grouping on Hindrances.

Parāmāsagocchakaṃ

The Grouping on Grasping

Parāmāsā dhammā, no parāmāsā dhammā. Parāmaṭṭhā dhammā, aparāmaṭṭhā dhammā. Parāmāsasampayuttā dhammā, parāmāsavippayuttā dhammā. Parāmāsā ceva dhammā [M 0.0005] parāmaṭṭhā ca, parāmaṭṭhāceva [V 0.0005] dhammā no ca parāmāsā. Parāmāsavippayuttā kho pana dhammā parāmaṭṭhāpi, aparāmaṭṭhāpi. Parāmāsagocchakaṃ.

Phenomena that are graspings, phenomena that are not graspings. Phenomena that are grasped, phenomena that are not grasped. Phenomena associated with grasping, phenomena dissociated from grasping. Phenomena that are graspings and are grasped; phenomena that are grasped but are not graspings. But phenomena dissociated from grasping are grasped as well as not grasped. The Grouping on Grasping.

Mahantaradukaṃ

The Great Intermediate Dyad

Sārammaṇā dhammā, anārammaṇā dhammā. Cittā dhammā, no cittā dhammā. Cetasikā dhammā, acetasikā dhammā. Cittasampayuttā dhammā, cittavippayuttā dhammā. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhā dhammā, cittavisaṃsaṭṭhā dhammā. Cittasamuṭṭhānā dhammā, no cittasamuṭṭhānā dhammā. Cittasahabhuno dhammā, no cittasahabhuno dhammā. Cittānuparivattino dhammā, no cittānuparivattino dhammā. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā dhammā, no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānā dhammā. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno dhammā, no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuno dhammā. Cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino dhammā, no cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattino dhammā. Ajjhattikā dhammā, bāhirā dhammā. Upādā dhammā, no upādā dhammā. Upādiṇṇā dhammā, anupādiṇṇā dhammā. Mahantaradukaṃ.

Phenomena with an object, phenomena without an object. Phenomena that are consciousness, phenomena that are not consciousness. Phenomena that are mental factors, phenomena that are not mental factors. Phenomena associated with consciousness, phenomena dissociated from consciousness. Phenomena conjoined with consciousness, phenomena disjoined from consciousness. Phenomena originating from consciousness, phenomena not originating from consciousness. Phenomena coexistent with consciousness, phenomena not coexistent with consciousness. Phenomena consequential to consciousness, phenomena not consequential to consciousness. Phenomena conjoined with and originating from consciousness, phenomena not conjoined with and originating from consciousness. Phenomena conjoined with, originating from, and coexistent with consciousness; phenomena not conjoined with, originating from, and coexistent with consciousness. Phenomena conjoined with, originating from, and consequential to consciousness; phenomena not conjoined with, originating from, and consequential to consciousness. Internal phenomena, external phenomena. Phenomena that are clingings, phenomena that are not clingings. Phenomena affected by clinging, phenomena unaffected by clinging. The Great Intermediate Dyad.

Upādānagocchakaṃ

The Grouping on Clinging

Upādānā dhammā, no upādānā dhammā. Upādāniyā dhammā, anupādāniyā dhammā. Upādānasampayuttā dhammā, upādānavippayuttā dhammā. Upādānā ceva dhammā upādāniyā ca, upādāniyā ceva dhammā no ca upādānā. Upādānā ceva dhammā upādānasampayuttā ca, upādānasampayuttā ceva dhammā no ca upādānā. Upādānavippayuttā kho pana dhammā upādāniyāpi, anupādāniyāpi. Upādānagocchakaṃ.

Phenomena that are clingings, phenomena that are not clingings. Phenomena liable to clinging, phenomena not liable to clinging. Phenomena associated with clinging, phenomena dissociated from clinging. Phenomena that are clingings and liable to clinging; phenomena that are liable to clinging but are not clingings. Phenomena that are clingings and associated with clinging; phenomena that are associated with clinging but are not clingings. But phenomena dissociated from clinging are liable to clinging as well as not liable to clinging. The Grouping on Clinging.

Kilesagocchakaṃ

The Grouping on Defilements

Kilesā dhammā, no kilesā dhammā. Saṃkilesikā dhammā, asaṃkilesikā dhammā. Saṃkiliṭṭhā dhammā, asaṃkiliṭṭhā dhammā. Kilesasampayuttā dhammā, kilesavippayuttā dhammā. Kilesā [M 0.0006] ceva dhammā saṃkilesikā ca, saṃkilesikā ceva dhammā no ca kilesā. Kilesā ceva dhammā saṃkiliṭṭhā ca, saṃkiliṭṭhā ceva dhammā no ca kilesā. Kilesā ceva dhammā kilesasampayuttā [V 0.0006] ca, kilesasampayuttā ceva dhammā no ca kilesā. Kilesavippayuttā kho pana dhammā saṃkilesikāpi, asaṃkilesikāpi. Kilesagocchakaṃ.

Phenomena that are defilements, phenomena that are not defilements. Phenomena that are defiling, phenomena that are not defiling. Phenomena that are defiled, phenomena that are undefiled. Phenomena associated with defilements, phenomena dissociated from defilements. Phenomena that are defilements and are defiling; phenomena that are defiling but are not defilements. Phenomena that are defilements and are defiled; phenomena that are defiled but are not defilements. Phenomena that are defilements and associated with defilements; phenomena that are associated with defilements but are not defilements. But phenomena dissociated from defilements are defiling as well as not defiling. The Grouping on Defilements.

Piṭṭhidukaṃ

The Back Dyads

Dassanena pahātabbā dhammā, na dassanena pahātabbā dhammā. Bhāvanāya pahātabbā dhammā, na bhāvanāya pahātabbā dhammā. Dassanena pahātabbahetukā dhammā, na dassanena pahātabbahetukā dhammā. Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā dhammā, na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā dhammā. Savitakkā dhammā, avitakkā dhammā. Savicārā dhammā, avicārā dhammā. Sappītikā dhammā, appītikā dhammā. Pītisahagatā dhammā, na pītisahagatā dhammā. Sukhasahagatā dhammā, na sukhasahagatā dhammā. Upekkhāsahagatā dhammā, na upekkhāsahagatā dhammā. Kāmāvacarā dhammā, na kāmāvacarā dhammā. Rūpāvacarā dhammā, na rūpāvacarā dhammā. Arūpāvacarā dhammā, na arūpāvacarā dhammā. Pariyāpannā dhammā, apariyāpannā dhammā. Niyyānikā dhammā, aniyyānikā dhammā. Niyatā dhammā, aniyatā dhammā. Sauttarā dhammā, anuttarā dhammā. Saraṇā dhammā, araṇā dhammā. Piṭṭhidukaṃ.

Phenomena to be abandoned by vision, phenomena not to be abandoned by vision. Phenomena to be abandoned by development, phenomena not to be abandoned by development. Phenomena having roots to be abandoned by vision, phenomena not having roots to be abandoned by vision. Phenomena having roots to be abandoned by development, phenomena not having roots to be abandoned by development. Phenomena with applied thought, phenomena without applied thought. Phenomena with sustained thought, phenomena without sustained thought. Phenomena with joy, phenomena without joy. Phenomena accompanied by joy, phenomena not accompanied by joy. Phenomena accompanied by pleasure, phenomena not accompanied by pleasure. Phenomena accompanied by equanimity, phenomena not accompanied by equanimity. Phenomena of the sensuous sphere, phenomena not of the sensuous sphere. Phenomena of the fine-material sphere, phenomena not of the fine-material sphere. Phenomena of the immaterial sphere, phenomena not of the immaterial sphere. Included phenomena, unincluded phenomena. Phenomena that lead out, phenomena that do not lead out. Determinate phenomena, indeterminate phenomena. Surpassable phenomena, unsurpassable phenomena. Phenomena with defilements, phenomena without defilements. The Back Dyads.

Abhidhammadukamātikā.

The Matrix of the Abhidhamma Dyads.

Suttantikadukamātikā

The Suttanta Matrix of Dyads

Vijjābhāgino dhammā, avijjābhāgino dhammā. Vijjūpamā dhammā, vajirūpamā dhammā. Bālā dhammā, paṇḍitā dhammā. Kaṇhā dhammā[M 0.0007], sukkā dhammā. Tapanīyā dhammā, atapanīyā dhammā. Adhivacanā dhammā, adhivacanapathā dhammā. Nirutti dhammā, niruttipathā dhammā. Paññatti dhammā, paññattipathā dhammā. Nāmañca, rūpañca. Avijjā ca, bhavataṇhā ca. Bhavadiṭṭhi ca, vibhavadiṭṭhi ca. Sassatadiṭṭhi ca, ucchedadiṭṭhi ca. Antavā diṭṭhi ca, anantavā diṭṭhi ca. Pubbantānudiṭṭhi ca, aparantānudiṭṭhi ca. Ahirikañca, anottappañca. Hirī ca, ottappañca. Dovacassatā ca, pāpamittatā ca. Sovacassatā ca, kalyāṇamittatā ca. Āpattikusalatā ca, āpattivuṭṭhānakusalatā ca. Samāpattikusalatā ca, samāpattivuṭṭhānakusalatā ca. Dhātukusalatā ca, manasikārakusalatā [V 0.0007] ca. Āyatanakusalatā ca, paṭiccasamuppādakusalatā ca. Ṭhānakusalatā ca, aṭṭhānakusalatā ca. Ajjavo ca, maddavo ca. Khanti ca, soraccañca. Sākhalyañca, paṭisanthāro ca. Indriyesu aguttadvāratā ca, bhojane amattaññutā ca. Indriyesu guttadvāratā ca, bhojane mattaññutā ca. Muṭṭhassaccañca, asampajaññañca. Sati ca, sampajaññañca. Paṭisaṅkhānabalañca, bhāvanābalañca. Samatho ca, vipassanā ca. Samathanimittañca, paggāhanimittañca. Paggāho ca, avikkhepo ca. Sīlavipatti ca, diṭṭhivipatti ca. Sīlasampadā ca, diṭṭhisampadā ca. Sīlavisuddhi ca, diṭṭhivisuddhi ca. Diṭṭhivisuddhi kho pana, yathādiṭṭhissa ca padhānaṃ. Saṃvego ca saṃvejaniyesu ṭhānesu, saṃviggassa ca yoniso padhānaṃ. Asantuṭṭhitā ca kusalesu dhammesu, appaṭivānitā ca padhānasmiṃ. Vijjā ca, vimutti ca. Khaye ñāṇaṃ, anuppāde ñāṇanti.

Phenomena partaking of true knowledge, phenomena partaking of ignorance. Phenomena like lightning, phenomena like a thunderbolt. Foolish phenomena, wise phenomena. Dark phenomena, bright phenomena. Phenomena that cause remorse, phenomena that do not cause remorse. Designations, paths of designation. Expressions, paths of expression. Concepts, paths of concepts. Name-and-form. Ignorance and craving for being. View of being and view of non-being. Eternalist view and annihilationist view. View of finitude and view of infinitude. Views concerning the past and views concerning the future. Shamelessness and lack of moral dread. Moral shame and moral dread. Intractability and bad friendship. Tractability and good friendship. Skill in offenses and skill in rehabilitation from them. Skill in attainments and skill in emerging from them. Skill in the elements and skill in attention. Skill in the bases and skill in dependent origination. Skill in what is possible and skill in what is impossible. Honesty and gentleness. Patience and meekness. Friendliness and hospitality. Unguardedness of the sense faculties and immoderation in eating. Guardedness of the sense faculties and moderation in eating. Unmindfulness and lack of clear comprehension. Mindfulness and clear comprehension. The power of reflection and the power of development. Serenity and insight. The sign of serenity and the sign of exertion. Exertion and non-distraction. Failure in virtue and failure in view. Accomplishment in virtue and accomplishment in view. Purification of virtue and purification of view. And purification of view, on the other hand, and the striving of one who has seen things as they are. A sense of urgency in regard to things that should arouse it, and the wise striving of one who is stirred. Non-contentment with wholesome states and indefatigability in striving. True knowledge and liberation. Knowledge of destruction, knowledge of non-arising.

Suttantikadukamātikā.

The Suttanta Matrix of Dyads.

Dhammasaṅgaṇīmātikā niṭṭhitā.

The Matrix of the Dhammasaṅgaṇī is finished.

2. Vibhaṅgamātikā

2. The Vibhaṅga Matrix

Khandhavibhaṅgo

Analysis of the Aggregates

Pañcakkhandhā [M 0.0008] – (vibha. 1) rūpakkhandho vedanākkhandho saññākkhandho saṅkhārakkhandho viññāṇakkhandhoti. Khandhavibhaṅgaṃ.

The five aggregates: the aggregate of form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of volitional formations, the aggregate of consciousness. The Analysis of the Aggregates.

Āyatanavibhaṅgo

Analysis of the Bases

Dvādasāyatanāni (vibha. 154) – cakkhāyatanaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ sotāyatanaṃ saddāyatanaṃ ghānāyatanaṃ gandhāyatanaṃ jivhāyatanaṃ rasāyatanaṃ kāyāyatanaṃ phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ manāyatanaṃ dhammāyatananti. Āyatanavibhaṅgaṃ.

The twelve bases: the eye base, the form base, the ear base, the sound base, the nose base, the odor base, the tongue base, the taste base, the body base, the tangible base, the mind base, the mental-object base. The Analysis of the Bases.

Dhātuvibhaṅgo

Analysis of the Elements

Aṭṭhārasa [V 0.0008] dhātuyo (vibha. 183) – cakkhudhātu rūpadhātu cakkhuviññāṇadhātu, sotadhātu saddadhātu sotaviññāṇadhātu, ghānadhātu gandhadhātu ghānaviññāṇadhātu, jivhādhātu rasadhātu jivhāviññāṇadhātu, kāyadhātu phoṭṭhabbadhātu kāyaviññāṇadhātu, manodhātu dhammadhātu manoviññāṇadhātūti. Dhātuvibhaṅgaṃ.

The eighteen elements (Vibh. 183): the eye element, the form element, the eye-consciousness element; the ear element, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element; the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element; the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element; the body element, the tangible element, the body-consciousness element; the mind element, the mental-object element, the mind-consciousness element. The Analysis of the Elements.

Saccavibhaṅgo

The Analysis of the Truths

Cattāri ariyasaccāni (vibha. 189) – dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccanti. Saccavibhaṅgaṃ.

The Four Noble Truths (Vibh. 189): the noble truth of suffering, the noble truth of the origin of suffering, the noble truth of the cessation of suffering, and the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering. The Analysis of the Truths.

Indriyavibhaṅgo

The Analysis of the Faculties

Bāvīsatindriyāni (vibha. 219) – cakkhundriyaṃ sotindriyaṃ ghānindriyaṃ jivhindriyaṃ kāyindriyaṃ manindriyaṃ itthindriyaṃ purisindriyaṃ jīvitindriyaṃ sukhindriyaṃ [M 0.0009] dukkhindriyaṃ somanassindriyaṃ domanassindriyaṃ upekkhindriyaṃ saddhindriyaṃ vīriyindriyaṃ satindriyaṃ samādhindriyaṃ paññindriyaṃ anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ aññindriyaṃ aññātāvindriyanti. Indriyavibhaṅgaṃ.

The twenty-two faculties (Vibh. 219): the eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, the body faculty, the mind faculty, the female faculty, the male faculty, the life faculty, the faculty of pleasure, the faculty of pain, the faculty of joy, the faculty of displeasure, the faculty of equanimity, the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom, the faculty of 'I shall come to know the unknown,' the faculty of final knowledge, and the faculty of one who has final knowledge. The Analysis of the Faculties.

Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅgo

The Analysis of Dependent Origination

Avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā (vibha. 225), saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ, nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatanaṃ, saḷāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā, taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ, upādānapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā sambhavanti, evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti. Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅgaṃ.

With ignorance as condition, volitional formations arise (Vibh. 225); with volitional formations as condition, consciousness arises; with consciousness as condition, name-and-form arises; with name-and-form as condition, the six sense bases arise; with the six sense bases as condition, contact arises; with contact as condition, feeling arises; with feeling as condition, craving arises; with craving as condition, clinging arises; with clinging as condition, becoming arises; with becoming as condition, birth arises; with birth as condition, aging and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair arise. Thus is the origin of this whole mass of suffering. The Analysis of Dependent Origination.

Satipaṭṭhānavibhaṅgo

The Analysis of the Foundations of Mindfulness

Cattāro [V 0.0009] satipaṭṭhānā (vibha. 355) – idha bhikkhu ajjhattaṃ kāye kāyānupassī viharati, bahiddhā kāye kāyānupassī viharati, ajjhattabahiddhā kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

The Four Foundations of Mindfulness (Vibh. 355): Here, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body internally; he dwells contemplating the body in the body externally; he dwells contemplating the body in the body both internally and externally, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.

Ajjhattaṃ vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati, bahiddhā vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati, ajjhattabahiddhā vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings internally; he dwells contemplating feelings in feelings externally; he dwells contemplating feelings in feelings both internally and externally, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.

Ajjhattaṃ citte cittānupassī viharati, bahiddhā citte cittānupassī viharati, ajjhattabahiddhā citte cittānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

He dwells contemplating mind in mind internally; he dwells contemplating mind in mind externally; he dwells contemplating mind in mind both internally and externally, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.

Ajjhattaṃ [M 0.0010] dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati, bahiddhā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati, ajjhattabahiddhā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Satipaṭṭhānavibhaṅgaṃ.

He dwells contemplating dhammas in dhammas internally; he dwells contemplating dhammas in dhammas externally; he dwells contemplating dhammas in dhammas both internally and externally, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. The Analysis of the Foundations of Mindfulness.

Sammappadhānavibhaṅgo

The Analysis of the Right Exertions

Cattāro sammappadhānā (vibha. 390) – idha bhikkhu anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati.

The Four Right Exertions (Vibh. 390): Here, a bhikkhu generates desire, makes an effort, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome states.

Uppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati.

He generates desire, makes an effort, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives for the abandoning of arisen evil, unwholesome states.

Anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati.

He generates desire, makes an effort, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives for the arising of unarisen wholesome states.

Uppannānaṃ [V 0.0010] kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati. Sammappadhānavibhaṅgaṃ.

He generates desire, makes an effort, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives for the maintenance of arisen wholesome states, for their non-disappearance, growth, increase, development, and culmination. The Analysis of the Right Exertions.

Iddhipādavibhaṅgo

The Analysis of the Bases of Spiritual Power

Cattāro iddhipādā (vibha. 430) – idha bhikkhu chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīriyasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, cittasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīmaṃsāsamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti. Iddhipādavibhaṅgaṃ.

The Four Bases of Spiritual Power (Vibh. 430): Here, a bhikkhu develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration due to desire and formations of striving; he develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration due to energy and formations of striving; he develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration due to mind and formations of striving; he develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration due to investigation and formations of striving. The Analysis of the Bases of Spiritual Power.

Bojjhaṅgavibhaṅgo

The Analysis of the Enlightenment Factors

Satta [M 0.0011] bojjhaṅgā (vibha. 466) – satisambojjhaṅgo dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo pītisambojjhaṅgo passaddhisambojjhaṅgo samādhisambojjhaṅgo upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo. Bojjhaṅgavibhaṅgaṃ.

The Seven Enlightenment Factors (Vibh. 466): the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of investigation of dhammas, the enlightenment factor of energy, the enlightenment factor of rapture, the enlightenment factor of tranquility, the enlightenment factor of concentration, and the enlightenment factor of equanimity. The Analysis of the Enlightenment Factors.

Maggaṅgavibhaṅgo

The Analysis of the Path Factors

Ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo (vibha. 486). Seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo sammāsati sammāsamādhi. Maggaṅgavibhaṅgaṃ.

The Noble Eightfold Path (Vibh. 486), that is: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration. The Analysis of the Path Factors.

Jhānavibhaṅgo

The Analysis of Jhāna

Idha bhikkhu pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharati (vibha. 508) ācāragocarasampanno aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu indriyesu guttadvāro bhojane mattaññū pubbarattāpararattaṃ jāgariyānuyogamanuyutto sātaccaṃ nepakkaṃ bodhipakkhikānaṃ dhammānaṃ bhāvanānuyogamanuyutto.

Here, a bhikkhu dwells restrained by the Pātimokkha restraint (Vibh. 508), accomplished in conduct and resort, seeing danger in the slightest faults. Having undertaken the training rules, he trains in them. He guards the doors of his sense faculties, is moderate in eating, and is devoted to wakefulness in the early and late watches of the night. He is persistent and prudent, devoted to the development of the qualities that pertain to enlightenment.

So [V 0.0011] abhikkante paṭikkante sampajānakārī hoti, ālokite vilokite sampajānakārī hoti, samiñjite pasārite sampajānakārī hoti, saṅghāṭipattacīvaradhāraṇe sampajānakārī hoti, asite pīte khāyite sāyite sampajānakārī hoti, uccārapassāvakamme sampajānakārī hoti, gate ṭhite nisinne sutte jāgarite bhāsite tuṇhībhāve sampajānakārī hoti.

He is one who acts with clear comprehension when going forward and returning; when looking ahead and looking around; when bending and stretching his limbs; when carrying his outer robe, bowl, and robes; when eating, drinking, consuming food, and tasting; when defecating and urinating; and when walking, standing, sitting, falling asleep, waking up, speaking, and keeping silent.

So [M 0.0012] vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajati araññaṃ rukkhamūlaṃ pabbataṃ kandaraṃ giriguhaṃ susānaṃ vanapatthaṃ abbhokāsaṃ palālapuñjaṃ appasaddaṃ appanigghosaṃ vijanavātaṃ manussarāhasseyyakaṃ paṭisallānasāruppaṃ.

He resorts to a secluded dwelling—a forest, the root of a tree, a mountain, a ravine, a mountain cave, a charnel ground, a forest thicket, an open space, or a heap of straw—which is quiet, with little noise, secluded from people, private, and suitable for seclusion.

So araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā nisīdati pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā, so abhijjhaṃ loke pahāya vigatābhijjhena cetasā viharati, abhijjhāya cittaṃ parisodheti, byāpādapadosaṃ pahāya abyāpannacitto viharati sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī, byāpādapadosā cittaṃ parisodheti, thinamiddhaṃ pahāya vigatathinamiddho viharati ālokasaññī sato sampajāno, thinamiddhā cittaṃ parisodheti, uddhaccakukkuccaṃ pahāya anuddhato viharati ajjhattaṃ vūpasantacitto, uddhaccakukkuccā cittaṃ parisodheti, vicikicchaṃ pahāya tiṇṇavicikiccho viharati akathaṃkathī kusalesu dhammesu, vicikicchāya cittaṃ parisodheti.

Having gone to the forest, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut, he sits down, folding his legs crosswise, setting his body erect, and establishing mindfulness before him. Abandoning covetousness for the world, he dwells with a mind free from covetousness; he purifies his mind of covetousness. Abandoning ill will and hatred, he dwells with a mind free from ill will, compassionate for the welfare of all living beings; he purifies his mind of ill will and hatred. Abandoning sloth and torpor, he dwells free from sloth and torpor, perceiving light, mindful and clearly comprehending; he purifies his mind of sloth and torpor. Abandoning restlessness and remorse, he dwells unagitated, with a mind inwardly stilled; he purifies his mind of restlessness and remorse. Abandoning doubt, he dwells having overcome doubt, free from perplexity about wholesome states; he purifies his mind of doubt.

So ime pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeti, yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti “upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī”ti, tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati.

Having abandoned these five hindrances—defilements of the mind that weaken wisdom—quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, he enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, with rapture and happiness born of seclusion. With the stilling of applied and sustained thought, he enters and dwells in the second jhāna, which has internal confidence and unification of mind, is without applied and sustained thought, and has rapture and happiness born of concentration. With the fading away of rapture, he dwells equanimously, mindful, and clearly comprehending, and experiences happiness with the body; he enters and dwells in the third jhāna, of which the noble ones declare: ‘Equanimous and mindful, one dwells happily.’ With the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and grief, he enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna, which is neither-painful-nor-pleasant and includes the purification of mindfulness by equanimity.

Sabbaso [M 0.0013][V 0.0012] rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā “ananto ākāso”ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati, sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma “anantaṃ viññāṇa”nti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati, sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma “natthi kiñcī”ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati, sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Jhānavibhaṅgaṃ.

By completely transcending perceptions of form, with the passing away of perceptions of sensory impact, and by not attending to perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite,’ one enters and dwells in the base of infinite space. By completely transcending the base of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite,’ one enters and dwells in the base of infinite consciousness. By completely transcending the base of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing,’ one enters and dwells in the base of nothingness. By completely transcending the base of nothingness, one enters and dwells in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. The Analysis of Jhāna.

Appamaññāvibhaṅgo

The Analysis of the Immeasurables

Catasso appamaññāyo (vibha. 642) – idha bhikkhu mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.

There are four immeasurables (Vibh. 642). Here, a bhikkhu dwells pervading one direction with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, identifying with all, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility and without ill will.

Karuṇāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhisabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ karuṇāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.

He dwells pervading one direction with a mind imbued with compassion, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, identifying with all, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind imbued with compassion, abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility and without ill will.

Muditāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ muditāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.

He dwells pervading one direction with a mind imbued with altruistic joy, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, identifying with all, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind imbued with altruistic joy, abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility and without ill will.

Upekkhāsahagatena [M 0.0014] cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati. Appamaññāvibhaṅgaṃ.

He dwells pervading one direction with a mind imbued with equanimity, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, identifying with all, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind imbued with equanimity, abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility and without ill will. The Analysis of the Immeasurables.

Sikkhāpadavibhaṅgo

The Analysis of the Training Rules

Pañca [V 0.0013] sikkhāpadāni (vibha. 703) – pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, adinnādānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, musāvādā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ. Sikkhāpadavibhaṅgaṃ.

There are five training rules (Vibh. 703): the training rule of abstaining from the destruction of life, the training rule of abstaining from taking what is not given, the training rule of abstaining from sexual misconduct, the training rule of abstaining from false speech, the training rule of abstaining from distilled and fermented intoxicants which are the basis for heedlessness. The Analysis of the Training Rules.

Paṭisambhidāvibhaṅgo

The Analysis of the Analytical Knowledges

Catasso paṭisambhidā (vibha. 718) – atthapaṭisambhidā dhammapaṭisambhidā niruttipaṭisambhidā paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā. Paṭisambhidāvibhaṅgaṃ.

There are four analytical knowledges (Vibh. 718): analytical knowledge of meaning, analytical knowledge of the Dhamma, analytical knowledge of language, and analytical knowledge of perspicuity. The Analysis of the Analytical Knowledges.

Ñāṇavibhaṅgo

The Analysis of Knowledge

Ekavidhena ñāṇavatthu (vibha. 751) – pañca viññāṇā na hetū, ahetukā, hetuvippayuttā, sappaccayā, saṅkhatā, arūpā, lokiyā, sāsavā, saṃyojaniyā, ganthaniyā, oghaniyā, yoganiyā, nīvaraṇiyā, parāmaṭṭhā, upādāniyā, saṃkilesikā, abyākatā, sārammaṇā, acetasikā, vipākā, upādiṇṇupādāniyā, asaṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikā, na savitakkasavicārā, na avitakkavicāramattā, avitakkaavicārā, na pītisahagatā, neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbā, neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā, nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino, nevasekkhanāsekkhā, parittā, kāmāvacarā, na [M 0.0015] rūpāvacarā, na arūpāvacarā, pariyāpannā, no apariyāpannā, aniyatā, aniyyānikā.

The singlefold basis of knowledge (Vibh. 751): The five consciousnesses are not roots, are rootless, dissociated from roots, conditioned, constructed, immaterial, worldly, tainted, connected with fetters, connected with ties, connected with floods, connected with yokes, connected with hindrances, grasped, subject to clinging, subject to defilement, indeterminate, with an object, not mental factors, resultant, clung to and subject to clinging, undefiled but subject to defilement, not with applied and sustained thought, not without applied thought but with only sustained thought, without applied and sustained thought, not accompanied by rapture, to be abandoned neither by vision nor by development, with roots to be abandoned neither by vision nor by development, neither leading to accumulation nor to diminution, neither of a trainee nor of one beyond training, limited, of the sense sphere, not of the form sphere, not of the formless sphere, included, not unincluded, unfixed, not leading to release.

Uppannavatthukā, uppannārammaṇā, purejātavatthukā, purejātārammaṇā, ajjhattikavatthukā, bāhirārammaṇā, asambhinnavatthukā, asambhinnārammaṇā, nānāvatthukā, nānārammaṇā, na aññamaññassa gocaravisayaṃ paccanubhonti, na asamannāhārā uppajjanti, na amanasikārā uppajjanti, na abbokiṇṇā uppajjanti, na apubbaṃ acarimaṃ uppajjanti, na aññamaññassa samanantarā uppajjanti.

They have an arisen basis, an arisen object, a prenascent basis, a prenascent object, an internal basis, an external object, an unmixed basis, an unmixed object, diverse bases, and diverse objects. They do not experience one another's field and range; they do not arise without the convergence of conditions; they do not arise without attention; they do not arise intermingled; they do not arise without a preceding and a succeeding; they do not arise immediately after one another.

Pañca viññāṇā anābhogā, pañcahi viññāṇehi na kañci dhammaṃ paṭivijānāti, aññatra [V 0.0014] abhinipātamattā, pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ samanantarāpi na kañci dhammaṃ paṭivijānāti, pañcahi viññāṇehi na kañci iriyāpathaṃ kappeti, pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ samanantarāpi na kañci iriyāpathaṃ kappeti, pañcahi viññāṇehi na kāyakammaṃ na vacīkammaṃ paṭṭhapeti, pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ samanantarāpi na kāyakammaṃ na vacīkammaṃ paṭṭhapeti, pañcahi viññāṇehi na kusalākusalaṃ dhammaṃ samādiyati, pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ samanantarāpi na kusalākusalaṃ dhammaṃ samādiyati, pañcahi viññāṇehi na samāpajjati na vuṭṭhāti, pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ samanantarāpi na samāpajjati na vuṭṭhāti, pañcahi viññāṇehi na cavati na uppajjati, pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ samanantarāpi na cavati na uppajjati, pañcahi viññāṇehi na supati na paṭibujjhati na supinaṃ passati, pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ samanantarāpi na supati na paṭibujjhati na supinaṃ passati, yāthāvakavatthuvibhāvanā paññā. Evaṃ ekavidhena ñāṇavatthu.

The five consciousnesses are unreflective. By the five consciousnesses one does not discern any phenomenon apart from a mere impact. Even immediately after the five consciousnesses one does not discern any phenomenon. By the five consciousnesses one does not adopt any posture. Even immediately after the five consciousnesses one does not adopt any posture. By the five consciousnesses one does not initiate bodily or verbal action. Even immediately after the five consciousnesses one does not initiate bodily or verbal action. By the five consciousnesses one does not undertake wholesome or unwholesome states. Even immediately after the five consciousnesses one does not undertake wholesome or unwholesome states. By the five consciousnesses one does not attain or emerge from meditative absorption. Even immediately after the five consciousnesses one does not attain or emerge from meditative absorption. By the five consciousnesses one does not pass away or take rebirth. Even immediately after the five consciousnesses one does not pass away or take rebirth. By the five consciousnesses one does not sleep, awaken, or see a dream. Even immediately after the five consciousnesses one does not sleep, awaken, or see a dream. Wisdom is the clear understanding of the object as it really is. Thus is the singlefold basis of knowledge.

Duvidhena [M 0.0016] ñāṇavatthu – lokiyā paññā, lokuttarā paññā. Kenaci viññeyyā paññā, kenaci na viññeyyā paññā. Sāsavā paññā, anāsavā paññā. Āsavavippayuttā sāsavā paññā, āsavavippayuttā anāsavā paññā. Saṃyojaniyā paññā, asaṃyojaniyā paññā. Saṃyojanavippayuttā saṃyojaniyā paññā, saṃyojanavippayuttā asaṃyojaniyā paññā. Ganthaniyā paññā, aganthaniyā paññā. Ganthavippayuttā ganthaniyā paññā, ganthavippayuttā aganthaniyā paññā.

The basis of knowledge is twofold: mundane wisdom and supramundane wisdom. Wisdom cognizable by some, wisdom not cognizable by some. Wisdom with taints, wisdom without taints. Wisdom with taints, dissociated from taints; wisdom without taints, dissociated from taints. Wisdom connected with fetters, wisdom not connected with fetters. Wisdom connected with fetters, dissociated from fetters; wisdom not connected with fetters, dissociated from fetters. Wisdom connected with ties, wisdom not connected with ties. Wisdom connected with ties, dissociated from ties; wisdom not connected with ties, dissociated from ties.

Oghaniyā paññā, anoghaniyā paññā. Oghavippayuttā oghaniyā paññā, oghavippayuttā anoghaniyā paññā. Yoganiyā paññā, ayoganiyā paññā. Yogavippayuttā yoganiyā paññā, yogavippayuttā ayoganiyā paññā. Nīvaraṇiyā paññā, anīvaraṇiyā paññā. Nīvaraṇavippayuttā nīvaraṇiyā paññā, nīvaraṇavippayuttā anīvaraṇiyā paññā. Parāmaṭṭhā paññā, aparāmaṭṭhā paññā. Parāmāsavippayuttā parāmaṭṭhā paññā, parāmāsavippayuttā aparāmaṭṭhā paññā. Upādiṇṇā paññā, anupādiṇṇā paññā. Upādāniyā paññā, anupādāniyā paññā. Upādānavippayuttā upādāniyā paññā, upādānavippayuttā anupādāniyā paññā.

Wisdom connected with the floods, wisdom not connected with the floods. Wisdom connected with the floods, dissociated from the floods; wisdom not connected with the floods, dissociated from the floods. Wisdom connected with the yokes, wisdom not connected with the yokes. Wisdom connected with the yokes, dissociated from the yokes; wisdom not connected with the yokes, dissociated from the yokes. Wisdom connected with the hindrances, wisdom not connected with the hindrances. Wisdom connected with the hindrances, dissociated from the hindrances; wisdom not connected with the hindrances, dissociated from the hindrances. Wisdom that is grasped, wisdom that is not grasped. Grasped wisdom, dissociated from grasping; ungrasped wisdom, dissociated from grasping. Wisdom that is clung to, wisdom that is not clung to. Wisdom subject to clinging, wisdom not subject to clinging. Wisdom subject to clinging, dissociated from clinging; wisdom not subject to clinging, dissociated from clinging.

Saṃkilesikā paññā, asaṃkilesikā paññā. Kilesavippayuttā saṃkilesikā paññā, kilesavippayuttā [V 0.0015] asaṃkilesikā paññā. Savitakkā paññā, avitakkā paññā. Savicārā paññā, avicārā paññā. Sappītikā paññā, appītikā paññā. Pītisahagatā paññā, na pītisahagatā paññā. Sukhasahagatā paññā, na sukhasahagatā paññā. Upekkhāsahagatā paññā, na upekkhāsahagatā paññā[M 0.0017]. Kāmāvacarā paññā, na kāmāvacarā paññā. Rūpāvacarā paññā, na rūpāvacarā paññā. Arūpāvacarā paññā, na arūpāvacarā paññā. Pariyāpannā paññā, apariyāpannā paññā. Niyyānikā paññā, aniyyānikā paññā. Niyatā paññā, aniyatā paññā. Sauttarā paññā, anuttarā paññā. Atthajāpikā paññā, jāpitatthā paññā. Evaṃ duvidhena ñāṇavatthu.

Wisdom subject to defilement, wisdom not subject to defilement. Wisdom subject to defilement, dissociated from defilements; wisdom not subject to defilement, dissociated from defilements. Wisdom with initial thought, wisdom without initial thought. Wisdom with sustained thought, wisdom without sustained thought. Wisdom with zest, wisdom without zest. Wisdom accompanied by zest, wisdom not accompanied by zest. Wisdom accompanied by happiness, wisdom not accompanied by happiness. Wisdom accompanied by equanimity, wisdom not accompanied by equanimity. Wisdom of the sense-sphere, wisdom not of the sense-sphere. Wisdom of the form-sphere, wisdom not of the form-sphere. Wisdom of the formless-sphere, wisdom not of the formless-sphere. Included wisdom, unincluded wisdom. Wisdom that leads to release, wisdom that does not lead to release. Fixed wisdom, unfixed wisdom. Surpassable wisdom, unsurpassable wisdom. Wisdom that illuminates the meaning, wisdom whose meaning is illuminated. Thus the basis of knowledge is twofold.

Tividhena ñāṇavatthu – cintāmayā paññā, sutamayā paññā, bhāvanāmayā paññā. Dānamayā paññā, sīlamayā paññā, bhāvanāmayā paññā. Adhisīle paññā, adhicitte paññā, adhipaññāya paññā. Āyakosallaṃ, apāyakosallaṃ, upāyakosallaṃ.

The basis of knowledge is threefold: wisdom consisting of reflection, wisdom consisting of learning, and wisdom consisting of mental development. Wisdom consisting of giving, wisdom consisting of virtue, and wisdom consisting of mental development. Wisdom in higher virtue, wisdom in the higher mind, and wisdom in higher wisdom. Skill in progress, skill in decline, and skill in the means.

Vipākā paññā, vipākadhammadhammā paññā, nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā paññā. Upādiṇṇupādāniyā paññā, anupādiṇṇupādāniyā paññā, anupādiṇṇaanupādāniyā paññā. Savitakkasavicārā paññā, avitakkavicāramattā paññā, avitakkaavicārā paññā. Pītisahagatā paññā, sukhasahagatā paññā, upekkhāsahagatā paññā. Ācayagāminī paññā, apacayagāminī paññā, nevācayagāmināpacayagāminī paññā. Sekkhā paññā, asekkhā paññā, nevasekkhanāsekkhā paññā. Parittā paññā, mahaggatā paññā, appamāṇā paññā. Parittārammaṇā paññā, mahaggatārammaṇā paññā, appamāṇārammaṇā paññā. Maggārammaṇā paññā, maggahetukā paññā, maggādhipatinī paññā. Uppannā paññā, anuppannā paññā, uppādinī paññā. Atītā paññā, anāgatā paññā, paccuppannā paññā. Atītārammaṇā paññā, anāgatārammaṇā paññā, paccuppannārammaṇā paññā. Ajjhattā paññā, bahiddhā paññā, ajjhattabahiddhā paññā. Ajjhattārammaṇā paññā, bahiddhārammaṇā paññā, ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā paññā.

Resultant wisdom, wisdom productive of result, wisdom that is neither resultant nor productive of result. Wisdom that is clung to and subject to clinging, wisdom that is not clung to but is subject to clinging, wisdom that is neither clung to nor subject to clinging. Wisdom with initial and sustained thought, wisdom with only sustained thought, wisdom without initial and sustained thought. Wisdom accompanied by zest, wisdom accompanied by happiness, wisdom accompanied by equanimity. Wisdom leading to accumulation, wisdom leading to diminution, wisdom leading neither to accumulation nor to diminution. Wisdom of a trainee, wisdom of an adept, wisdom of one who is neither a trainee nor an adept. Limited wisdom, exalted wisdom, immeasurable wisdom. Wisdom with a limited object, wisdom with an exalted object, wisdom with an immeasurable object. Wisdom with the path as object, wisdom with the path as cause, wisdom with the path as dominant principle. Arisen wisdom, unarisen wisdom, wisdom that produces. Past wisdom, future wisdom, present wisdom. Wisdom with a past object, wisdom with a future object, wisdom with a present object. Internal wisdom, external wisdom, internal and external wisdom. Wisdom with an internal object, wisdom with an external object, wisdom with an internal and external object.

Savitakkasavicārā [M 0.0018] paññā atthi vipākā, atthi vipākadhammadhammā, atthi nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Atthi upādiṇṇupādāniyā, atthi anupādiṇṇupādāniyā, atthi anupādiṇṇaanupādāniyā[V 0.0016]. Atthi pītisahagatā, atthi sukhasahagatā, atthi upekkhāsahagatā. Atthi ācayagāminī, atthi apacayagāminī, atthi nevācayagāmināpacayagāminī. Atthi sekkhā, atthi asekkhā, atthi nevasekkhanāsekkhā. Atthi parittā, atthi mahaggatā, atthi appamāṇā. Atthi parittārammaṇā, atthi mahaggatārammaṇā, atthi appamāṇārammaṇā. Atthi maggārammaṇā, atthi maggahetukā, atthi maggādhipatinī. Atthi uppannā, atthi anuppannā, atthi uppādinī. Atthi atītā, atthi anāgatā, atthi paccuppannā. Atthi atītārammaṇā, atthi anāgatārammaṇā, atthi paccuppannārammaṇā. Atthi ajjhattā, atthi bahiddhā, atthi ajjhattabahiddhā. Atthi ajjhattārammaṇā, atthi bahiddhārammaṇā, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā.

There is wisdom with initial and sustained thought; it is resultant, it is productive of result, and it is neither resultant nor productive of result. It is clung to and subject to clinging, it is not clung to but is subject to clinging, and it is neither clung to nor subject to clinging. It is accompanied by zest, it is accompanied by happiness, and it is accompanied by equanimity. It leads to accumulation, it leads to diminution, and it leads neither to accumulation nor to diminution. It is of a trainee, it is of an adept, and it is of one who is neither a trainee nor an adept. It is limited, it is exalted, and it is immeasurable. It has a limited object, it has an exalted object, and it has an immeasurable object. It has the path as object, it has the path as cause, and it has the path as dominant principle. It has arisen, it has not arisen, and it is one that produces. It is past, it is future, and it is present. It has a past object, it has a future object, and it has a present object. It is internal, it is external, and it is internal and external. It has an internal object, it has an external object, and it has an internal and external object.

Avitakkavicāramattā paññā atthi vipākā, atthi vipākadhammadhammā, atthi nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Atthi upādiṇṇupādāniyā, atthi anupādiṇṇupādāniyā, atthi anupādiṇṇaanupādāniyā. Atthi ācayagāminī, atthi apacayagāminī, atthi nevācayagāmināpacayagāminī. Atthi sekkhā, atthi asekkhā, atthi nevasekkhanāsekkhā. Atthi uppannā, atthi anuppannā, atthi uppādinī. Atthi atītā, atthi anāgatā, atthi paccuppannā. Atthi ajjhattā, atthi bahiddhā, atthi ajjhattabahiddhā.

Wisdom with only sustained thought: there is that which is resultant, that which is productive of result, and that which is neither resultant nor productive of result. There is that which is clung to and subject to clinging, that which is not clung to but is subject to clinging, and that which is neither clung to nor subject to clinging. There is that which leads to accumulation, that which leads to diminution, and that which leads neither to accumulation nor to diminution. There is that of a trainee, that of an adept, and that of one who is neither a trainee nor an adept. There is that which has arisen, that which has not arisen, and that which produces. There is that which is past, that which is future, and that which is present. There is that which is internal, that which is external, and that which is internal and external.

Avitakkaavicārā paññā atthi vipākā, atthi vipākadhammadhammā, atthi nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Atthi upādiṇṇupādāniyā, atthi anupādiṇṇupādāniyā, atthi anupādiṇṇaanupādāniyā. Atthi pītisahagatā, atthi sukhasahagatā, atthi [M 0.0019] upekkhāsahagatā. Atthi ācayagāminī, atthi apacayagāminī, atthi nevācayagāmināpacayagāminī. Atthi sekkhā, atthi asekkhā, atthi nevasekkhanāsekkhā. Atthi parittārammaṇā, atthi mahaggatārammaṇā, atthi appamāṇārammaṇā. Atthi maggārammaṇā, atthi maggahetukā, atthi maggādhipatinī. Atthi uppannā, atthi anuppannā, atthi uppādinī. Atthi atītā, atthi anāgatā, atthi paccuppannā. Atthi atītārammaṇā, atthi anāgatārammaṇā, atthi paccuppannārammaṇā. Atthi ajjhattā, atthi bahiddhā, atthi ajjhattabahiddhā. Atthi ajjhattārammaṇā, atthi bahiddhārammaṇā, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā.

Wisdom without initial and sustained thought: there is that which is resultant, that which is productive of result, and that which is neither resultant nor productive of result. There is that which is clung to and subject to clinging, that which is not clung to but is subject to clinging, and that which is neither clung to nor subject to clinging. There is that which is accompanied by zest, that which is accompanied by happiness, and that which is accompanied by equanimity. There is that which leads to accumulation, that which leads to diminution, and that which leads neither to accumulation nor to diminution. There is that of a trainee, that of an adept, and that of one who is neither a trainee nor an adept. There is that with a limited object, that with an exalted object, and that with an immeasurable object. There is that with the path as object, that with the path as cause, and that with the path as dominant principle. There is that which has arisen, that which has not arisen, and that which produces. There is that which is past, that which is future, and that which is present. There is that with a past object, that with a future object, and that with a present object. There is that which is internal, that which is external, and that which is internal and external. There is that with an internal object, that with an external object, and that with an internal and external object.

Pītisahagatā paññā, sukhasahagatā paññā atthi vipākā, atthi vipākadhammadhammā, atthi nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā[V 0.0017]. Atthi upādiṇṇupādāniyā, atthi anupādiṇṇupādāniyā, atthi anupādiṇṇaanupādāniyā. Atthi savitakkasavicārā, atthi avitakkavicāramattā, atthi avitakkaavicārā. Atthi ācayagāminī, atthi apacayagāminī, atthi nevācayagāmināpacayagāminī. Atthi sekkhā, atthi asekkhā, atthi nevasekkhanāsekkhā. Atthi parittā, atthi mahaggatā, atthi appamāṇā. Atthi parittārammaṇā, atthi mahaggatārammaṇā, atthi appamāṇārammaṇā. Atthi maggārammaṇā, atthi maggahetukā, atthi maggādhipatinī. Atthi uppannā, atthi anuppannā, atthi uppādinī. Atthi atītā, atthi anāgatā, atthi paccuppannā. Atthi atītārammaṇā, atthi anāgatārammaṇā, atthi paccuppannārammaṇā. Atthi ajjhattā, atthi bahiddhā, atthi ajjhattabahiddhā. Atthi ajjhattārammaṇā, atthi bahiddhārammaṇā, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā.

Wisdom accompanied by rapture and wisdom accompanied by happiness: there is resultant, there is productive of result, there is neither resultant nor productive of result. There is grasped and fuel for clinging, there is ungrasped but fuel for clinging, there is ungrasped and not fuel for clinging. There is with applied and sustained thought, there is with only sustained thought, there is without applied and sustained thought. There is that which leads to accumulation, that which leads to decline, and that which leads neither to accumulation nor to decline. There is of a trainee, there is of an adept, and there is of neither a trainee nor an adept. There is limited, there is exalted, there is immeasurable. There is with a limited object, there is with an exalted object, there is with an immeasurable object. There is with the path as object, there is with the path as cause, there is with the path as predominance. There is arisen, there is unarisen, and there is productive. There is past, there is future, and there is present. There is with a past object, there is with a future object, there is with a present object. There is internal, there is external, and there is both internal and external. There is with an internal object, there is with an external object, and there is with both an internal and external object.

Upekkhāsahagatā paññā atthi vipākā, atthi vipākadhammadhammā, atthi nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammā. Atthi upādiṇṇupādāniyā[M 0.0020], atthi anupādiṇṇupādāniyā, atthi anupādiṇṇaanupādāniyā. Atthi ācayagāminī, atthi apacayagāminī, atthi nevācayagāmināpacayagāminī. Atthi sekkhā, atthi asekkhā, atthi nevasekkhanāsekkhā. Atthi parittā, atthi mahaggatā, atthi appamāṇā. Atthi parittārammaṇā, atthi mahaggatārammaṇā, atthi appamāṇārammaṇā. Atthi maggārammaṇā, atthi maggahetukā, atthi maggādhipatinī. Atthi uppannā, atthi anuppannā, atthi uppādinī. Atthi atītā, atthi anāgatā, atthi paccuppannā. Atthi atītārammaṇā, atthi anāgatārammaṇā, atthi paccuppannārammaṇā. Atthi ajjhattā, atthi bahiddhā, atthi ajjhattabahiddhā. Atthi ajjhattārammaṇā, atthi bahiddhārammaṇā, atthi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇā. Evaṃ tividhena ñāṇavatthu.

Wisdom accompanied by equanimity: there is resultant, there is productive of result, there is neither resultant nor productive of result. There is grasped and fuel for clinging, there is ungrasped but fuel for clinging, there is ungrasped and not fuel for clinging. There is that which leads to accumulation, that which leads to decline, and that which leads neither to accumulation nor to decline. There is of a trainee, there is of an adept, and there is of neither a trainee nor an adept. There is limited, there is exalted, there is immeasurable. There is with a limited object, there is with an exalted object, there is with an immeasurable object. There is with the path as object, there is with the path as cause, there is with the path as predominance. There is arisen, there is unarisen, and there is productive. There is past, there is future, and there is present. There is with a past object, there is with a future object, there is with a present object. There is internal, there is external, and there is both internal and external. There is with an internal object, there is with an external object, and there is with both an internal and external object. Thus the basis of knowledge is threefold.

Catubbidhena ñāṇavatthu – kammassakatañāṇaṃ, saccānulomikaṃ ñāṇaṃ, maggasamaṅgissa ñāṇaṃ, phalasamaṅgissa ñāṇaṃ. Dukkhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ. Kāmāvacarā paññā, rūpāvacarā paññā, arūpāvacarā paññā, apariyāpannā paññā. Dhamme ñāṇaṃ, anvaye ñāṇaṃ, paricce ñāṇaṃ, sammuti ñāṇaṃ. Atthi paññā ācayāya, no apacayāya, atthi paññā apacayāya, no ācayāya, atthi paññā ācayāya ceva, apacayāya ca, atthi paññā nevācayāya, no apacayāya. Atthi paññā nibbidāya, no paṭivedhāya, atthi paññā paṭivedhāya, no nibbidāya[V 0.0018], atthi paññā nibbidāya ceva, paṭivedhāya ca, atthi paññā neva nibbidāya, no paṭivedhāya. Hānabhāginī paññā, ṭhitibhāginī paññā, visesabhāginī paññā, nibbedhabhāginī paññā.

The fourfold basis of knowledge: knowledge of kamma as one's own property, knowledge in conformity with the truths, knowledge of one possessing the path, knowledge of one possessing the fruition. Knowledge of suffering, knowledge of the origin of suffering, knowledge of the cessation of suffering, knowledge of the path leading to the cessation of suffering. Sense-sphere wisdom, form-sphere wisdom, formless-sphere wisdom, supramundane wisdom. Knowledge of phenomena, inferential knowledge, knowledge of the minds of others, conventional knowledge. There is wisdom for accumulation, not for decline; there is wisdom for decline, not for accumulation; there is wisdom for both accumulation and decline; there is wisdom for neither accumulation nor decline. There is wisdom for revulsion, not for penetration; there is wisdom for penetration, not for revulsion; there is wisdom for both revulsion and penetration; there is wisdom for neither revulsion nor penetration. Wisdom partaking of decline, wisdom partaking of stability, wisdom partaking of distinction, wisdom partaking of penetration.

Catasso [M 0.0021] paṭisambhidā. Catasso paṭipadā. Cattāri ārammaṇāni. Jarāmaraṇe ñāṇaṃ, jarāmaraṇasamudaye ñāṇaṃ, jarāmaraṇanirodhe ñāṇaṃ, jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ. Jātiyā ñāṇaṃ…pe… bhave ñāṇaṃ…pe… upādāne ñāṇaṃ…pe… taṇhāya ñāṇaṃ…pe… vedanāya ñāṇaṃ…pe… phasse ñāṇaṃ…pe… saḷāyatane ñāṇaṃ…pe… nāmarūpe ñāṇaṃ…pe… viññāṇe ñāṇaṃ…pe… saṅkhāresu ñāṇaṃ, saṅkhārasamudaye ñāṇaṃ, saṅkhāranirodhe ñāṇaṃ, saṅkhāranirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ. Evaṃ catubbidhena ñāṇavatthu.

The four analytical knowledges. The four practices. The four objects. Knowledge of aging and death, knowledge of the origin of aging and death, knowledge of the cessation of aging and death, knowledge of the practice leading to the cessation of aging and death. Knowledge of birth… and so on… knowledge of existence… knowledge of clinging… knowledge of craving… knowledge of feeling… knowledge of contact… knowledge of the six sense bases… knowledge of name-and-form… knowledge of consciousness… knowledge of volitional formations, knowledge of the origin of volitional formations, knowledge of the cessation of volitional formations, knowledge of the practice leading to the cessation of volitional formations. Thus the basis of knowledge is fourfold.

Pañcavidhena ñāṇavatthu – pañcaṅgiko sammāsamādhi, pañcañāṇiko sammāsamādhi. Evaṃ pañcavidhena ñāṇavatthu.

The fivefold basis of knowledge: right concentration with five factors, right concentration with five knowledges. Thus the basis of knowledge is fivefold.

Chabbidhena ñāṇavatthu – chasu abhiññāsu paññā. Evaṃ chabbidhena ñāṇavatthu.

The sixfold basis of knowledge: wisdom in the six direct knowledges. Thus the basis of knowledge is sixfold.

Sattavidhena ñāṇavatthu – sattasattati ñāṇavatthūni. Evaṃ sattavidhena ñāṇavatthu.

The sevenfold basis of knowledge: the seventy-seven bases of knowledge. Thus the basis of knowledge is sevenfold.

Aṭṭhavidhena ñāṇavatthu – catūsu maggesu, catūsu phalesu paññā. Evaṃ aṭṭhavidhena ñāṇavatthu.

The eightfold basis of knowledge: wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits. Thus the basis of knowledge is eightfold.

Navavidhena ñāṇavatthu – navasu anupubbavihārasamāpattīsu paññā. Evaṃ navavidhena ñāṇavatthu.

The ninefold basis of knowledge: wisdom in the nine successive attainments. Thus the basis of knowledge is ninefold.

Dasavidhena ñāṇavatthu – dasa tathāgatassa tathāgatabalāni, yehi balehi samannāgato tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti. Katamāni dasa? Idha tathāgato ṭhānañca ṭhānato aṭṭhānañca aṭṭhānato yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, yampi tathāgato ṭhānañca ṭhānato aṭṭhānañca aṭṭhānato yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ [V 0.0019] hoti. Yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ [M 0.0022] ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

The tenfold basis of knowledge: the ten powers of a Tathāgata, endowed with which the Tathāgata claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets in motion the divine wheel. What are the ten? Here, the Tathāgata understands as it actually is the possible as possible and the impossible as impossible. That the Tathāgata understands as it actually is the possible as possible and the impossible as impossible, this is a power of the Tathāgata. Relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets in motion the divine wheel.

Puna caparaṃ tathāgato atītānāgatapaccuppannānaṃ kammasamādānānaṃ ṭhānaso hetuso vipākaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi tathāgato atītānāgatapaccuppannānaṃ kammasamādānānaṃ ṭhānaso hetuso vipākaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti. Yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

Furthermore, the Tathāgata understands as it actually is the results of past, future, and present kamma undertakings in terms of their conditions and causes. That the Tathāgata understands as it actually is the results of past, future, and present kamma undertakings in terms of their conditions and causes, this is a power of the Tathāgata. Relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets in motion the divine wheel.

Puna caparaṃ tathāgato sabbatthagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, yampi tathāgato sabbatthagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti. Yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

Furthermore, the Tathāgata understands as it actually is the path that leads to all destinations. That the Tathāgata understands as it actually is the path that leads to all destinations, this is a power of the Tathāgata. Relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets in motion the divine wheel.

Puna caparaṃ tathāgato anekadhātunānādhātulokaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, yampi tathāgato anekadhātunānādhātulokaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti. Yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

Furthermore, the Tathāgata understands as it actually is the world with its many and various elements. That the Tathāgata understands as it actually is the world with its many and various elements, this is a power of the Tathāgata. Relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets in motion the divine wheel.

Puna caparaṃ tathāgato sattānaṃ nānādhimuttikataṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, yampi tathāgato sattānaṃ nānādhimuttikataṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti. Yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

Furthermore, the Tathāgata understands as they really are the diverse inclinations of beings. And because the Tathāgata understands as they really are the diverse inclinations of beings, this too is a power of the Tathāgata. Relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the herd-leader’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the supreme Wheel of Brahma.

Puna caparaṃ tathāgato parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ indriyaparopariyattaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, yampi tathāgato parasattānaṃ [M 0.0023] parapuggalānaṃ indriyaparopariyattaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti. Yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

Furthermore, the Tathāgata understands as it really is the superiority and inferiority of the faculties of other beings, other persons. And because the Tathāgata understands as it really is the superiority and inferiority of the faculties of other beings, other persons, this too is a power of the Tathāgata. Relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the herd-leader’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the supreme Wheel of Brahma.

Puna caparaṃ tathāgato jhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattīnaṃ saṃkilesaṃ vodānaṃ vuṭṭhānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, yampi tathāgato jhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattīnaṃ saṃkilesaṃ vodānaṃ vuṭṭhānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti[V 0.0020], idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti. Yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

Furthermore, the Tathāgata understands as they really are the defilement, the cleansing, and the emergence in regard to the jhānas, liberations, concentrations, and attainments. And because the Tathāgata understands as they really are the defilement, the cleansing, and the emergence in regard to the jhānas, liberations, concentrations, and attainments, this too is a power of the Tathāgata. Relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the herd-leader’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the supreme Wheel of Brahma.

Puna caparaṃ tathāgato pubbenivāsānussatiṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, yampi tathāgato pubbenivāsānussatiṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti. Yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

Furthermore, the Tathāgata understands as it really is the recollection of past lives. And because the Tathāgata understands as it really is the recollection of past lives, this too is a power of the Tathāgata. Relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the herd-leader’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the supreme Wheel of Brahma.

Puna caparaṃ tathāgato sattānaṃ cutūpapātaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, yampi tathāgato sattānaṃ cutūpapātaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti. Yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

Furthermore, the Tathāgata understands as it really is the passing away and reappearance of beings. And because the Tathāgata understands as it really is the passing away and reappearance of beings, this too is a power of the Tathāgata. Relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the herd-leader’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the supreme Wheel of Brahma.

Puna caparaṃ tathāgato āsavānaṃ khayaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, yampi tathāgato āsavānaṃ khayaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti. Yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

Furthermore, the Tathāgata understands as it really is the destruction of the taints. And because the Tathāgata understands as it really is the destruction of the taints, this too is a power of the Tathāgata. Relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the herd-leader’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the supreme Wheel of Brahma.

Imāni [M 0.0024] dasa tathāgatassa tathāgatabalāni. Yehi balehi samannāgato tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti. Evaṃ dasavidhena ñāṇavatthu.

These are the ten powers of the Tathāgata. Endowed with these powers, the Tathāgata claims the herd-leader’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the supreme Wheel of Brahma. Thus the tenfold basis of knowledge.

Ñāṇavibhaṅgaṃ.

The Analysis of Knowledge.

Khuddakavatthuvibhaṅgo

Analysis of the Minor Items

Ekakaṃ

The Ones

Jātimado (vibha. 832), gottamado, ārogyamado, yobbanamado, jīvitamado, lābhamado, sakkāramado, garukāramado, purekkhāramado, parivāramado, bhogamado, vaṇṇamado, sutamado[V 0.0021], paṭibhānamado, rattaññumado, piṇḍapātikamado, anavaññātamado, iriyāpathamado, iddhimado, yasamado, sīlamado, jhānamado, sippamado, ārohamado, pariṇāhamado, saṇṭhānamado, pāripūrimado, mado, pamādo, thambho, sārambho, atricchatā, mahicchatā, pāpicchatā, siṅgaṃ, tintiṇaṃ, cāpalyaṃ, asabhāgavutti, arati, tandī, vijambhitā, bhattasammado, cetaso ca līnattaṃ, kuhanā, lapanā, nemittikatā, nippesikatā, lābhena lābhaṃ nijigīsanatā, “seyyohamasmī”ti māno, “sadisohamasmī”ti māno, “hīnohamasmī”ti māno. Seyyassa “seyyohamasmī”ti māno, seyyassa “sadisohamasmī”ti māno, seyyassa “hīnohamasmī”ti māno, sadisassa “seyyohamasmī”ti māno, sadisassa “sadisohamasmī”ti māno, sadisassa “hīnohamasmī”ti māno, hīnassa “seyyohamasmī”ti māno, hīnassa [M 0.0025] “sadisohamasmī”ti māno, hīnassa “hīnohamasmī”ti māno, māno, atimāno, mānātimāno, omāno, adhimāno, asmimāno, micchāmāno, ñātivitakko, janapadavitakko, amaravitakko, parānuddayatāpaṭisaṃyutto vitakko, lābhasakkārasilokapaṭisaṃyutto vitakko, anavaññattipaṭisaṃyutto vitakko (vibha. 832). Ekakaṃ.

Intoxication with birth (Vibh. 832), intoxication with clan, intoxication with health, intoxication with youth, intoxication with life, intoxication with gain, intoxication with honour, intoxication with respect, intoxication with precedence, intoxication with retinue, intoxication with wealth, intoxication with beauty, intoxication with learning, intoxication with wit, intoxication with seniority, intoxication with the ascetic practice of eating only almsfood, intoxication with not being despised, intoxication with deportment, intoxication with psychic power, intoxication with fame, intoxication with virtue, intoxication with the jhānas, intoxication with skill, intoxication with height, intoxication with girth, intoxication with form, intoxication with physical perfection, intoxication, negligence, obstinacy, contentiousness, excessive desire, great desire, evil desire, horn-like arrogance, chattering, fickleness, unseemly conduct, discontent, sloth, yawning, drowsiness from food, and mental sluggishness, scheming, garrulity, hinting, belittling, desiring to obtain gain with gain, the conceit ‘I am superior,’ the conceit ‘I am equal,’ the conceit ‘I am inferior.’ In regard to a superior: the conceit ‘I am superior,’ the conceit ‘I am equal,’ the conceit ‘I am inferior.’ In regard to an equal: the conceit ‘I am superior,’ the conceit ‘I am equal,’ the conceit ‘I am inferior.’ In regard to an inferior: the conceit ‘I am superior,’ the conceit ‘I am equal,’ the conceit ‘I am inferior.’ Conceit, excessive conceit, conceit beyond conceit, disparaging conceit, over-conceit, the conceit ‘I am,’ wrong conceit, thought about relatives, thought about the country, thought about immortality, thought connected with worldly concern for others, thought connected with gain, honour, and renown, thought connected with not being despised (Vibh. 832). The Ones.

Dukaṃ

The Dyad
