Kodho ca upanāho ca, makkho ca paḷāso ca, issā ca macchariyañca, māyā ca sāṭheyyañca, avijjā ca bhavataṇhā ca, bhavadiṭṭhi ca vibhavadiṭṭhi ca, sassatadiṭṭhi ca ucchedadiṭṭhi ca, antavādiṭṭhi ca anantavādiṭṭhi ca, pubbantānudiṭṭhi ca aparantānudiṭṭhi ca, ahirikañca anottappañca, dovacassatā ca pāpamittatā ca, anajjavo ca amaddavo ca, akkhanti ca asoraccañca, asākhalyañca appaṭisanthāro ca, indriyesu aguttadvāratā ca bhojane amattaññutā ca, muṭṭhassaccañca asampajaññañca, sīlavipatti ca diṭṭhivipatti ca, ajjhattasaṃyojanañca bahiddhāsaṃyojanañca. Dukaṃ.

Anger and hostility, contempt and spite, envy and stinginess, deceit and craftiness, ignorance and craving for existence, the view of existence and the view of non-existence, the eternalist view and the annihilationist view, the view that the world is finite and the view that it is infinite, views concerning the past and views concerning the future, shamelessness and lack of moral dread, difficulty of admonition and bad friendship, crookedness and harshness, impatience and lack of gentleness, unfriendliness and lack of courtesy, unguardedness in the sense faculties and lack of moderation in eating, unmindfulness and lack of clear comprehension, corruption of virtue and corruption of view, internal fetters and external fetters. The Dyad.

Tikaṃ

The Triad

Tīṇi akusalamūlāni, tayo akusalavitakkā, tisso akusalasaññā, tisso akusaladhātuyo, tīṇi duccaritāni, tayo āsavā, tīṇi saṃyojanāni, tisso taṇhā, aparāpi tisso taṇhā, aparāpi tisso taṇhā, tisso esanā, tisso vidhā, tīṇi bhayāni[V 0.0022], tīṇi tamāni, tīṇi titthāyatanāni, tayo kiñcanā, tīṇi aṅgaṇāni, tīṇi malāni, tīṇi visamāni, aparānipi tīṇi visamāni, tayo aggī, tayo kasāvā, aparepi tayo kasāvā.

Three unwholesome roots, three unwholesome thoughts, three unwholesome perceptions, three unwholesome elements, three kinds of misconduct, three taints, three fetters, three cravings, another three cravings, yet another three cravings, three searches, three conceits, three fears, three darknesses, three sectarian tenets, three impediments, three stains, three impurities, three kinds of wrongness, another three kinds of wrongness, three fires, three blemishes, another three blemishes.

Assādadiṭṭhi [M 0.0026] attānudiṭṭhi micchādiṭṭhi, arati vihesā adhammacariyā, dovacassatā pāpamittatā nānattasaññā, uddhaccaṃ kosajjaṃ pamādo, asantuṭṭhitā asampajaññatā mahicchatā, ahirikaṃ anottappaṃ pamādo, anādariyaṃ dovacassatā pāpamittatā, assaddhiyaṃ avadaññutā kosajjaṃ, uddhaccaṃ asaṃvaro dussīlyaṃ, ariyānaṃ adassanakamyatā saddhammaṃ asotukamyatā upārambhacittatā, muṭṭhassaccaṃ asampajaññaṃ cetaso vikkhepo, ayoniso manasikāro kummaggasevanā cetaso ca līnattaṃ. Tikaṃ.

The view of gratification, the view of self, and wrong view; discontent, vexation, and unrighteous conduct; difficulty of admonition, bad friendship, and perception of diversity; restlessness, laziness, and negligence; discontent, lack of clear comprehension, and great ambition; shamelessness, lack of moral dread, and negligence; disrespect, difficulty of admonition, and bad friendship; lack of faith, ungenerosity, and laziness; restlessness, lack of restraint, and immorality; unwillingness to see the noble ones, unwillingness to hear the good Dhamma, and a fault-finding mind; unmindfulness, lack of clear comprehension, and mental distraction; unwise attention, following a wrong path, and mental sluggishness. The Triad.

Catukkaṃ

The Tetrad

Cattāro āsavā, cattāro ganthā, cattāro oghā, cattāro yogā, cattāri upādānāni, cattāro taṇhuppādā, cattāri agatigamanāni, cattāro vipariyāsā, cattāro anariyavohārā, aparepi cattāro anariyavohārā, cattāri duccaritāni, aparāpi cattāri duccaritāni, cattāri bhayāni, (aparānipi cattāri bhayāni,) catasso diṭṭhiyo. Catukkaṃ.

Four taints, four bodily ties, four floods, four yokes, four kinds of clinging, four origins of craving, four wrong courses, four perversions, four ignoble expressions, another four ignoble expressions, four kinds of misconduct, another four kinds of misconduct, four fears, (another four fears,) four views. The Tetrad.

Pañcakaṃ

The Pentad

Pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni, pañcuddhambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni, pañca macchariyāni, pañca saṅgā, pañca sallā, pañca cetokhilā, pañca cetasovinibandhā, pañca nīvaraṇāni, pañca kammāni ānantarikāni, pañca diṭṭhiyo, pañca verā, pañca byasanā, pañca akkhantiyā ādīnavā, pañca bhayāni, pañca diṭṭhadhammanibbānavādā. Pañcakaṃ.

Five lower fetters, five higher fetters, five kinds of stinginess, five ties, five darts, five mental barrennesses, five mental bondages, five hindrances, five deeds with immediate result, five views, five enmities, five calamities, five dangers in impatience, five fears, five doctrines of Nibbāna in this very life. The Pentad.

Chakkaṃ

The Hexad.

Cha vivādamūlāni, cha chandarāgā dhammā, cha virodhavatthūni, cha taṇhākāyā, cha agāravā, cha parihāniyā dhammā, aparepi [M 0.0027] cha parihāniyā dhammā, cha somanassupavicārā, cha [V 0.0023] domanassupavicārā, cha upekkhupavicārā, cha gehasitāni somanassāni, cha gehasitāni domanassāni, cha gehasitā upekkhā, cha diṭṭhiyo. Chakkaṃ.

Six roots of dispute, six things based on sensual desire, six grounds for conflict, six classes of craving, six kinds of irreverence, six things that lead to decline, another six things that lead to decline, six explorations of joy, six explorations of sorrow, six explorations of equanimity, six kinds of joy based on the household life, six kinds of sorrow based on the household life, six kinds of equanimity based on the household life, six views. The Hexad.

Sattakaṃ

The Heptad.

Satta anusayā, satta saṃyojanāni, satta pariyuṭṭhānāni, satta asaddhammā, satta duccaritāni, satta mānā, satta diṭṭhiyo. Sattakaṃ.

Seven underlying tendencies, seven fetters, seven obsessions, seven bad qualities, seven kinds of misconduct, seven conceits, seven views. The Heptad.

Aṭṭhakaṃ

The Octad.

Aṭṭha kilesavatthūni, aṭṭha kusītavatthūni, aṭṭhasu lokadhammesu cittassa paṭighāto, aṭṭha anariyavohārā, aṭṭha micchattā, aṭṭha purisadosā, aṭṭha asaññivādā, aṭṭha nevasaññināsaññivādā. Aṭṭhakaṃ.

Eight grounds for the defilements, eight grounds for laziness, mental aversion towards the eight worldly conditions, eight ignoble expressions, eight wrong states, eight personal faults, eight theses about non-perception, eight theses about neither-perception-nor-non-perception. The Octad.

Navakaṃ

The Ennead.

Nava āghātavatthūni, nava purisamalāni, navavidhā mānā, nava taṇhāmūlakā dhammā, nava iñjitāni, nava maññitāni, nava phanditāni, nava papañcitāni, nava saṅkhatāni. Navakaṃ.

Nine grounds for resentment, nine personal stains, nine kinds of conceit, nine things rooted in craving, nine agitations, nine conceivings, nine tremblings, nine proliferations, nine conditioned things. The Ennead.

Dasakaṃ

The Decad.

Dasa kilesavatthūni, dasa āghātavatthūni, dasa akusalakammapathā, dasa saṃyojanāni, dasa micchattā, dasavatthukā micchādiṭṭhi, dasavatthukā antaggāhikā diṭṭhi. Dasakaṃ.

Ten grounds for the defilements, ten grounds for resentment, ten unwholesome courses of action, ten fetters, ten wrong states, wrong view with its ten bases, the view that holds to extremes with its ten bases. The Decad.

Aṭṭhārasa taṇhāvicaritāni ajjhattikassa upādāya, aṭṭhārasa taṇhāvicaritāni bāhirassa upādāya, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññuhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā chattiṃsa taṇhāvicaritāni honti[M 0.0028], iti atītāni chattiṃsa taṇhāvicaritāni, anāgatāni chattiṃsa taṇhāvicaritāni, paccuppannāni chattiṃsa taṇhāvicaritāni, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññuhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā aṭṭha taṇhāvicaritasataṃ hoti, yāni ca dvāsaṭṭhi diṭṭhigatāni brahmajāle veyyākaraṇe vuttāni bhagavatā.

Eighteen courses of craving in regard to the internal, eighteen courses of craving in regard to the external. Having been brought together and summarized, they become thirty-six courses of craving. Thus, there are thirty-six courses of craving in the past, thirty-six courses of craving in the future, and thirty-six courses of craving in the present. Having been brought together and summarized, they become one hundred and eight courses of craving. And the sixty-two speculative views spoken of by the Blessed One in the exposition of the Brahmajāla.

Khuddakavatthuvibhaṅgaṃ.

The Analysis of Minor Items.

Dhammahadayavibhaṅgo

The Analysis of the Heart of the Dhamma.

Kati [V 0.0024] khandhā, kati āyatanāni, kati dhātuyo, kati saccāni, kati indriyāni, kati hetū, kati āhārā, kati phassā, kati vedanā, kati saññā, kati cetanā, kati cittāni (vibha. 978)?

How many aggregates? How many sense-bases? How many elements? How many truths? How many faculties? How many causes? How many nutriments? How many contacts? How many feelings? How many perceptions? How many volitions? How many consciousnesses? (Vibhaṅga 978).

Pañcakkhandhā, dvādasāyatanāni, aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo, cattāri saccāni, bāvīsatindriyāni, nava hetū, cattāro āhārā, satta phassā, satta vedanā, satta saññā, satta cetanā, satta cittāni (vibha. 978).

Five aggregates, twelve sense-bases, eighteen elements, four truths, twenty-two faculties, nine causes, four nutriments, seven contacts, seven feelings, seven perceptions, seven volitions, seven consciousnesses (Vibhaṅga 978).

Dhammahadayavibhaṅgaṃ.

The Analysis of the Heart of the Dhamma.

Vibhaṅgamātikā niṭṭhitā.

The Matrix of the Analysis is concluded.

3. Dhātukathāmātikā

3. The Matrix of the Discourse on Elements.

Nayamātikā

The Matrix of Methods.

Saṅgaho asaṅgaho (dhātu. 1). Saṅgahitena asaṅgahitaṃ. Asaṅgahitena saṅgahitaṃ. Saṅgahitena saṅgahitaṃ. Asaṅgahitena asaṅgahitaṃ. Sampayogo vippayogo. Sampayuttena vippayuttaṃ. Vippayuttena sampayuttaṃ. Sampayuttena sampayuttaṃ. Vippayuttena [M 0.0029] vippayuttaṃ. Saṅgahitena sampayuttaṃ vippayuttaṃ. Sampayuttena saṅgahitaṃ asaṅgahitaṃ. Asaṅgahitena sampayuttaṃ vippayuttaṃ. Vippayuttena saṅgahitaṃ asaṅgahitaṃ.

Inclusion and non-inclusion (Dhātukathā 1). Unincluded by what is included. Included by what is unincluded. Included by what is included. Unincluded by what is unincluded. Association and dissociation. Dissociated by what is associated. Associated by what is dissociated. Associated by what is associated. Dissociated by what is dissociated. Associated and dissociated by what is included. Included and unincluded by what is associated. Associated and dissociated by what is unincluded. Included and unincluded by what is dissociated.

Abbhantaramātikā

The Interior Matrix.

Pañcakkhandhā. Dvādasāyatanāni. Aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo. Cattāri saccāni. Bāvīsatindriyāni. Paṭiccasamuppādo. Cattāro satipaṭṭhānā. Cattāro sammappadhānā. Cattāro iddhipādā[V 0.0025]. Cattāri jhānāni. Catasso appamaññāyo. Pañcindriyāni. Pañca balāni. Satta bojjhaṅgā. Ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo. Phasso vedanā saññā cetanā cittaṃ adhimokkho manasikāro.

The five aggregates. The twelve sense-bases. The eighteen elements. The four truths. The twenty-two faculties. Dependent origination. The four foundations of mindfulness. The four right exertions. The four bases for spiritual power. The four jhānas. The four immeasurables. The five faculties. The five powers. The seven factors of enlightenment. The noble eightfold path. Contact, feeling, perception, volition, consciousness, decision, attention.

Nayamukhamātikā

The Matrix of the Gateway to Methods.

Tīhi saṅgaho. Tīhi asaṅgaho. Catūhi sampayogo. Catūhi vippayogo.

Inclusion by three. Non-inclusion by three. Association by four. Dissociation by four.

Lakkhaṇamātikā

The Matrix of Characteristics.

Sabhāgo. Visabhāgo.

Homogeneous. Heterogeneous.

Bāhiramātikā

The External Matrix.

Sabbāpi dhammasaṅgaṇī dhātukathāya mātikāti.

The entire Dhammasaṅgaṇī is the matrix for the Dhātukathā.

Dhātukathāmātikā niṭṭhitā.

The Matrix of the Discourse on Elements is concluded.

4. Puggalapaññattimātikā

4. The Matrix of the Designations of Persons.

Cha paññattiyo (pu. pa. mātikā 1) – khandhapaññatti āyatanapaññatti dhātupaññatti saccapaññatti indriyapaññatti puggalapaññattīti.

Six designations (Puggalapaññatti Mātikā 1): the designation of aggregates, the designation of sense-bases, the designation of elements, the designation of truths, the designation of faculties, and the designation of persons.

Puggalapaññattimātikā niṭṭhitā.

The Matrix of the Designations of Persons is concluded.

5. Kathāvatthumātikā

5. The Matrix of the Points of Controversy.

Puggalakathā

The Discussion on the Person.

Suddhasaccikaṭṭhaanulomapaccanīkaṃ

The Forward and Reverse Methods on the Pure and Real Meaning.

Puggalo [M 0.0030][V 0.0026] upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti (kathā. 1), āmantā. Yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Is a person to be found in the real and ultimate sense? (Kathāvatthu 1). Yes. Is that person to be found in the real and ultimate sense from that which is the real and ultimate sense? That should not be said.

Ājānāhi niggahaṃ – hañci puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, tena vata re vattabbe “yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi “vattabbe kho ‘puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena’, no ca vattabbe ‘yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti, micchā.

Acknowledge the refutation! If a person is to be found in the real and ultimate sense, then it should be said: ‘From that which is the real and ultimate sense, that person is to be found in the real and ultimate sense.’ That you say, ‘It should be said, “a person is to be found in the real and ultimate sense,” but it should not be said, “from that which is the real and ultimate sense, that person is to be found in the real and ultimate sense,”’ is wrong.

No ce pana vattabbe “yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti, no ca vata re vattabbe “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi “vattabbe kho ‘puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena’, no ca vattabbe ‘yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti, micchā.

But if it should not be said, ‘From that which is the real and ultimate sense, that person is to be found in the real and ultimate sense,’ then it should not be said, ‘A person is to be found in the real and ultimate sense.’ That you say, ‘It should be said, “a person is to be found in the real and ultimate sense,” but it should not be said, “from that which is the real and ultimate sense, that person is to be found in the real and ultimate sense,”’ is wrong.

Anulomapañcakaṃ.

The Forward Pentad.

Puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Is a person not to be found in the real and ultimate sense? Yes. Is that person not to be found in the real and ultimate sense from that which is the real and ultimate sense? That should not be said.

Ājānāhi [M 0.0031] paṭikammaṃ – hañci puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, tena vata re vattabbe “yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Acknowledge the rejoinder! If a person is not to be found in the real and ultimate sense, then it should be said: ‘From that which is the real and ultimate sense, that person is not to be found in the real and ultimate sense.’ That you say, ‘It should be said, “a person is not to be found in the real and ultimate sense,” but it should not be said, “from that which is the real and ultimate sense, that person is not to be found in the real and ultimate sense,”’ is wrong.

No ce pana vattabbe “yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti, no ca vata re vattabbe “puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi “vattabbe kho ‘puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena’, no ca vattabbe ‘yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti, micchā.

But if it should not be said, ‘From that which is the real and ultimate sense, that person is not to be found in the real and ultimate sense,’ then it should not be said, ‘A person is not to be found in the real and ultimate sense.’ That you say, ‘It should be said, “a person is not to be found in the real and ultimate sense,” but it should not be said, “from that which is the real and ultimate sense, that person is not to be found in the real and ultimate sense,”’ is wrong.

Paṭikammacatukkaṃ.

The Rejoinder Tetrad.

Tvaṃ ce pana maññasi “vattabbe kho ‘puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena’, no ca vattabbe ‘yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti. Tena tava tattha hetāya paṭiññāya hevaṃ paṭijānantaṃ hevaṃ niggahetabbe, atha taṃ niggaṇhāma, suniggahito ca hosi –

But if you think, ‘It should be said, “a person is not to be found in the real and ultimate sense,” but it should not be said, “from that which is the real and ultimate sense, that person is not to be found in the real and ultimate sense,”’ then, on the basis of that reason and proposition of yours, one who makes such a claim should be refuted thus. Now we refute you, and you are well refuted:

Hañci puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, tena vata re vattabbe “yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. If a person is not to be found in the real and ultimate sense, then it should be said: ‘From that which is the real and ultimate sense, that person is not to be found in the real and ultimate sense.’ That you say, ‘It should be said, “a person is not to be found in the real and ultimate sense,” but it should not be said, “from that which is the real and ultimate sense, that person is not to be found in the real and ultimate sense,”’ is wrong.

No [M 0.0032] ce pana vattabbe “yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti, no ca vata re vattabbe “puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. But if it should not be said, ‘From that which is the real and ultimate sense, that person is not to be found in the real and ultimate sense,’ then it should not be said, ‘A person is not to be found in the real and ultimate sense.’ That you say, ‘It should be said, “a person is not to be found in the real and ultimate sense,” but it should not be said, “from that which is the real and ultimate sense, that person is not to be found in the real and ultimate sense,”’—this of yours is wrong.

Niggahacatukkaṃ.

The Refutation Tetrad.

Ese [V 0.0028] ce dunniggahite hevamevaṃ tattha dakkha, “vattabbe kho ‘puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena’, no ca vattabbe ‘yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti, no ca mayaṃ tayā tattha hetāya paṭiññāya hevaṃ paṭijānantā hevaṃ niggahetabbā, atha maṃ niggaṇhāsi, dunniggahitā ca homa –

If this is a poor refutation, you are clever in this matter, saying: ‘It should be said, “a person is to be found in the real and ultimate sense,” but it should not be said, “from that which is the real and ultimate sense, that person is to be found in the real and ultimate sense.”’ But we, who make such a claim, should not be refuted by you on the basis of that reason and proposition. If you refute me, we would be poorly refuted:

Hañci puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, tena vata re vattabbe “yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi “vattabbe kho ‘puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena’, no ca vattabbe ‘yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti, micchā.

But if it should not be said, ‘From that which is the real and ultimate sense, that person is to be found in the real and ultimate sense,’ then it should not be said, ‘A person is to be found in the real and ultimate sense.’ That you say, ‘It should be said, “a person is to be found in the real and ultimate sense,” but it should not be said, “from that which is the real and ultimate sense, that person is to be found in the real and ultimate sense,”’—this of yours is wrong.

Upanayanacatukkaṃ.

The Application Tetrad.

Na [M 0.0033] hevaṃ niggahetabbe, tena hi yaṃ niggaṇhāsi – hañci puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, tena vata re vattabbe “yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi “vattabbe kho ‘puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena’, no ca vattabbe ‘yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti, micchā.

One should not be refuted thus. Therefore, as to your refutation—‘If a person is to be found in the real and ultimate sense, then it should be said: “From that which is the real and ultimate sense, that person is to be found in the real and ultimate sense.” But that you say, “It should be said, ‘a person is to be found in the real and ultimate sense,’ but it should not be said, ‘from that which is the real and ultimate sense, that person is to be found in the real and ultimate sense,’” is wrong.’

No ce pana vattabbe “yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti, no ca vata re vattabbe “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi “vattabbe kho ‘puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena’, no ca vattabbe ‘yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti[V 0.0029], idaṃ te micchā. Tena hi ye kate niggahe, se niggahe dukkaṭe. Sukate paṭikamme. Sukatā paṭipādanāti.

But if it should not be said, ‘Is the person found in a real and ultimate sense in the same way as that which is a real and ultimate matter?’ then indeed it should not be said, ‘The person is found in a real and ultimate sense.’ What you say there—‘It should be said, “The person is found in a real and ultimate sense,” but it should not be said, “Is the person found in a real and ultimate sense in the same way as that which is a real and ultimate matter?”’—is wrong for you. Therefore, the refutation you made is a faulty refutation. The counter-argument was well-made. The demonstration was well-made.

Niggamanacatukkaṃ.

The Concluding Tetrad.

Paṭhamo niggaho.

The First Refutation.

The Tetrad on the Counter-argument.

Now we refute you, and you are well refuted:

Hañci puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, tena vata re vattabbe “yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi “vattabbe kho ‘puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena’, no ca vattabbe ‘yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti, micchā.

If the person is found in a real and ultimate sense, then indeed it should be said, ‘Is the person found in a real and ultimate sense in the same way as that which is a real and ultimate matter?’ What you say there—‘It should be said, “The person is found in a real and ultimate sense,” but it should not be said, “Is the person found in a real and ultimate sense in the same way as that which is a real and ultimate matter?”’—is wrong.

No ce pana vattabbe “yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti, no ca vata re vattabbe “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti, yaṃ tattha vadesi “vattabbe kho ‘puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena’, no ca vattabbe ‘yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti, idaṃ te micchā.

But if it should not be said, ‘Is the person found in a real and ultimate sense in the same way as that which is a real and ultimate matter?’ then indeed it should not be said, ‘The person is found in a real and ultimate sense.’ What you say there—‘It should be said, “The person is found in a real and ultimate sense,” but it should not be said, “Is the person found in a real and ultimate sense in the same way as that which is a real and ultimate matter?”’—is wrong for you.

Niggahacatukkaṃ.

The Tetrad of Refutation.

Ese [V 0.0031] ce dunniggahite hevamevaṃ tattha dakkha, “vattabbe kho ‘puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena’, no ca vattabbe ‘yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti, no ca mayaṃ tayā tattha hetāya paṭiññāya hevaṃ paṭijānantā hevaṃ niggahetabbā, atha maṃ niggaṇhāsi, dunniggahitā ca homa –

If, when you are thus being badly refuted, you are still clever enough to say, ‘It should be said, “The person is not found in a real and ultimate sense,” but it should not be said, “Is the person not found in a real and ultimate sense in the same way as that which is a real and ultimate matter?”’ then we, who do not hold to that reason and that thesis of yours, should not be refuted by you thus. Yet you refute me, and we are badly refuted:

Hañci [M 0.0036] puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, tena vata re vattabbe “yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi “vattabbe kho ‘puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena’, no ca vattabbe ‘yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti, micchā.

If the person is not found in a real and ultimate sense, then indeed it should be said, ‘The person is not found in a real and ultimate sense in the same way as that which is a real and ultimate matter.’ What you say there—‘It should be said, “The person is not found in a real and ultimate sense,” but it should not be said, “Is the person not found in a real and ultimate sense in the same way as that which is a real and ultimate matter?”’—is wrong.

No ce pana vattabbe “yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti, no ca vata re vattabbe “puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi “vattabbe kho ‘puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena’, no ca vattabbe ‘yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti, idaṃ te micchā.

But if it should not be said, ‘Is the person not found in a real and ultimate sense in the same way as that which is a real and ultimate matter?’ then indeed it should not be said, ‘The person is not found in a real and ultimate sense.’ What you say there—‘It should be said, “The person is not found in a real and ultimate sense,” but it should not be said, “Is the person not found in a real and ultimate sense in the same way as that which is a real and ultimate matter?”’—is wrong for you.

Upanayanacatukkaṃ.

The Tetrad of Application.

Na hevaṃ niggahetabbe, tena hi yaṃ niggaṇhāsi – hañci puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, tena vata re vattabbe “yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi “vattabbe kho ‘puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena’, no ca vattabbe ‘yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti, micchā.

One should not be refuted thus. Therefore, as to what you refute—‘If the person is not found in a real and ultimate sense, then indeed it should be said, “The person is not found in a real and ultimate sense in the same way as that which is a real and ultimate matter.” What you say there—“It should be said, ‘The person is not found in a real and ultimate sense,’ but it should not be said, ‘Is the person not found in a real and ultimate sense in the same way as that which is a real and ultimate matter?’”’—is wrong.

No ce pana vattabbe “yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti, no ca vata re vattabbe “puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi “vattabbe kho ‘puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena’, no ca vattabbe ‘yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti[V 0.0032], idaṃ te micchā, tena hi ye kate niggahe[M 0.0037], se niggahe dukkaṭe. Sukate paṭikamme, sukatā paṭipādanāti.

But if it should not be said, ‘Is the person not found in a real and ultimate sense in the same way as that which is a real and ultimate matter?’, then indeed it should not be said, ‘The person is not found in a real and ultimate sense.’ What you say there—‘It should be said, “The person is not found in a real and ultimate sense,” but it should not be said, “Is the person not found in a real and ultimate sense in the same way as that which is a real and ultimate matter?”’—is wrong. Therefore, the refutation you have made is a faulty refutation. The counter-argument is well-made; the demonstration is well-made.

Niggamanacatukkaṃ.

The Concluding Tetrad.

Dutiyo niggaho.

The Second Refutation.

Okāsasaccikaṭṭhaanulomapaccanīkaṃ

Location and Ultimate Truth: Forward and Reverse Order.

Puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Sabbattha puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Is a person found in the real and ultimate sense? Yes. Is a person found everywhere in the real and ultimate sense? It should not be said so.

Ājānāhi niggahaṃ – hañci puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, tena vata re vattabbe “sabbattha puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi “vattabbe kho ‘puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena’, no ca vattabbe ‘sabbattha puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti, micchā.

Acknowledge the refutation! If a person is found in the real and ultimate sense, then you must surely say, 'A person is found everywhere in the real and ultimate sense.' Your statement that one should say, 'A person is found in the real and ultimate sense,' but one should not say, 'A person is found everywhere in the real and ultimate sense,' is wrong.

No ce pana vattabbe “sabbattha puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti, no ca vata re vattabbe “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi “vattabbe kho ‘puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena’, no ca vattabbe ‘sabbattha puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti, micchā…pe….

But if it should not be said, 'A person is found everywhere in the real and ultimate sense,' then you surely should not say, 'A person is found in the real and ultimate sense.' Your statement that one should say, 'A person is found in the real and ultimate sense,' but one should not say, 'A person is found everywhere in the real and ultimate sense,' is wrong… and so on ….

Tatiyo niggaho.

Your statement that one should say, 'A person is found in the real and ultimate sense,' but one should not say, 'A person is always found in the real and ultimate sense,' is wrong… and so on ….

Catuttho niggaho.

The Fourth Refutation.

Avayavasaccikaṭṭhaanulomapaccanīkaṃ

Components and Ultimate Truth: Forward and Reverse Order.

Puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Sabbesu puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Pañcamo niggaho.

Chaṭṭho niggaho.

The Sixth Refutation.

Kālasaccikaṭṭhapaccanīkānulomaṃ

Time and Ultimate Truth: Reverse and Forward Order.

Puggalo [V 0.0035] nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Sabbadā puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

The Seventh Refutation.

Avayavasaccikaṭṭhapaccanīkānulomaṃ

Components and Ultimate Truth: Reverse and Forward Order.

Puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Sabbesu puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

6. Yamakamātikā

6. The Mātikā of the Yamaka

Mūlayamakaṃ

The Pair on Roots

Kusalapadanayacatukkaṃ

The Tetrad on the Method of the Wholesome Term

Ye [M 0.0041] keci kusalā dhammā (yama. 1.mūlayamaka.1 ādayo), sabbe te kusalamūlā. Ye vā pana kusalamūlā, sabbe te dhammā kusalā.

Whatever wholesome states there are (Yamaka 1, Mūlayamaka 1, etc.), all of them have wholesome roots. And whatever states have wholesome roots, all of those states are wholesome.

Ye keci kusalā dhammā, sabbe te kusalamūlena ekamūlā. Ye vā pana kusalamūlena ekamūlā, sabbe te dhammā kusalā.

Whatever wholesome states there are, they are all one-rooted with the wholesome root. And whatever states are one-rooted with the wholesome root, they are all wholesome states.

Ye keci kusalamūlena ekamūlā dhammā, sabbe te kusalamūlena aññamaññamūlā. Ye vā pana kusalamūlena aññamaññamūlā, sabbe te dhammā kusalā.

Whatever states are one-rooted with the wholesome root, they are all mutually rooted with the wholesome root. And whatever states are mutually rooted with the wholesome root, they are all wholesome states.

Ye keci kusalā dhammā, sabbe te kusalamūlamūlā. Ye vā pana kusalamūlamūlā, sabbe te dhammā kusalā.

Whatever wholesome states there are, they are all rooted in the wholesome root. And whatever states are rooted in the wholesome root, they are all wholesome states.

Ye [V 0.0037] keci kusalā dhammā, sabbe te kusalamūlena ekamūlamūlā. Ye vā pana kusalamūlena ekamūlamūlā, sabbe te dhammā kusalā.

Whatever wholesome states there are, they are all rooted in a single root with the wholesome root. And whatever states are rooted in a single root with the wholesome root, they are all wholesome states.

Ye keci kusalamūlena ekamūlamūlā dhammā, sabbe te kusalamūlena aññamaññamūlamūlā. Ye vā pana kusalamūlena aññamaññamūlamūlā, sabbe te dhammā kusalā.

Whatever states are rooted in a single root with the wholesome root, they are all rooted in a mutual root with the wholesome root. And whatever states are rooted in a mutual root with the wholesome root, they are all wholesome states.

Ye keci kusalā dhammā, sabbe te kusalamūlakā. Ye vā pana kusalamūlakā, sabbe te dhammā kusalā.

Whatever wholesome states there are, they all have a wholesome root. And whatever states have a wholesome root, they are all wholesome states.

Ye keci kusalā dhammā, sabbe te kusalamūlena ekamūlakā. Ye vā pana kusalamūlena ekamūlakā, sabbe te dhammā kusalā.

Whatever wholesome states there are, they all have a single root with the wholesome root. And whatever states have a single root with the wholesome root, they are all wholesome states.

Ye [M 0.0042] keci kusalamūlena ekamūlakā dhammā, sabbe te kusalamūlena aññamaññamūlakā. Ye vā pana kusalamūlena aññamaññamūlakā, sabbe te dhammā kusalā.

Whatever states have a single root with the wholesome root, they all have mutual roots with the wholesome root. And whatever states have mutual roots with the wholesome root, they are all wholesome states.

Ye keci kusalā dhammā, sabbe te kusalamūlamūlakā. Ye vā pana kusalamūlamūlakā, sabbe te dhammā kusalā.

Whatever wholesome states there are, they all have the wholesome root as their root. And whatever states have the wholesome root as their root, they are all wholesome states.

Ye keci kusalā dhammā, sabbe te kusalamūlena ekamūlamūlakā. Ye vā pana kusalamūlena ekamūlamūlakā, sabbe te dhammā kusalā.

Whatever wholesome states there are, they all have a single root as their root along with the wholesome root. And whatever states have a single root as their root along with the wholesome root, they are all wholesome states.

Ye keci kusalamūlena ekamūlamūlakā dhammā, sabbe te kusalamūlena aññamaññamūlamūlakā. Ye vā pana kusalamūlena aññamaññamūlamūlakā, sabbe te dhammā kusalā.

Whatever states have a single root as their root along with the wholesome root, they all have a mutual root as their root along with the wholesome root. And whatever states have a mutual root as their root along with the wholesome root, they are all wholesome states.

Akusalapadanayacatukkaṃ

The Tetrad on the Method of the Unwholesome Term

Ye keci akusalā dhammā, sabbe te akusalamūlā. Ye vā pana akusalamūlā, sabbe te dhammā akusalā.

Whatever unwholesome states there are, all of them have unwholesome roots. And whatever states have unwholesome roots, all those states are unwholesome.

Ye [V 0.0038] keci akusalā dhammā, sabbe te akusalamūlena ekamūlā. Ye vā pana akusalamūlena ekamūlā, sabbe te dhammā akusalā.

Whatever unwholesome states there are, they are all one-rooted with the unwholesome root. And whatever states are one-rooted with the unwholesome root, all those states are unwholesome.

Ye keci akusalamūlena ekamūlā dhammā, sabbe te akusalamūlena aññamaññamūlā. Ye vā pana akusalamūlena aññamaññamūlā, sabbe te dhammā akusalā.

Whatever states are one-rooted with the unwholesome root, they are all mutually rooted with the unwholesome root. And whatever states are mutually rooted with the unwholesome root, all those states are unwholesome.

Ye keci akusalā dhammā, sabbe te akusalamūlamūlā. Ye vā pana akusalamūlamūlā, sabbe te dhammā akusalā.
