Mātikāpadāni nikkhipitvā vibhattā. Ettha ca manojīvitaupekkhindriyāni, saddhādīni pañcāti [V 0.0243] aṭṭhindriyāni veditabbāni. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva. Evaṃ catūhi koṭṭhāsehi catuttho vāro veditabbo.

The matrix items have been laid down and analyzed. And here, the eight faculties are to be understood as the mind faculty, the life faculty, and the equanimity faculty, along with the five beginning with faith. The rest is easily understood. Thus, the fourth round is to be understood through these four sections.

Pañcamo pana vāro tesaṃ dhammānaṃ bhūmantaravasena “kāmāvacaradhammā, na kāmāvacarā…pe… pariyāpannā”ti cattāro duke mātikāvasena nikkhipitvā vibhajanavasena pavatto, so heṭṭhā vuttatthova.

The fifth round, however, proceeds by way of analysis, having laid down four dyads according to the matrix by classifying those phenomena according to their planes: 'sense-sphere phenomena, not sense-sphere phenomena…pe…included.' Its meaning is as stated previously.

Chaṭṭho pana vāro sammutidevaupapattidevavisuddhideve niddisitvā manussadevagatīsu uppādakakammaāyuppamāṇadassanavasena vutto. Tatthāyaṃ saṅkhepattho – sattā hi dānasīlādikāmāvacarakusalaṃ katvā manussaloke khattiyamahāsālādikulesu ceva cātumahārājikatāvatiṃsayāmatusitanimmānaratiparanimmitavasavattisaṅkhātesu chasu devalokesu ca uppajjanti, tattha sinerupabbatavemajjhaparibhaṇḍapabbatato paṭṭhāya heṭṭhā yāva bhūmi tiriyaṃ cakkavāḷapabbataṃ āhacca etthantare pabbataākāsarukkhapathavinissitā cātumahārājacandasūriyā sabbe cātumahārājikā. Tato uddhaṃ cakkavāḷapariyantaṃ tāvatiṃsādayo yathākkamaṃ uparūpari ṭhitāti veditabbā. Devalokopi paramparacakkavāḷapabbataṃ appatto nāma natthi.

The sixth round, after indicating conventional devas, devas by rebirth, and devas by purification, is explained by way of the kamma that produces rebirth in human and deva destinations, the measure of the lifespan, and the vision thereof. Here is the summary: beings who perform wholesome actions in the sense-sphere, such as generosity and virtue, are reborn in the human world in families of noble warriors, great householders, and so on, or in the six deva worlds known as the realms of the Four Great Kings, the Tāvatiṃsa, the Yāma, the Tusita, the Nimmānarati, and the Paranimmitavasavatti. There, starting from the middle circumference of Mount Sineru, extending downward to the earth and horizontally up to the Cakkavāḷa Mountain, within this space, situated on mountains, in the sky, on trees, or on the earth, are the Four Great Kings, the moon, and the sun—all are of the Cātumahārājika realm. Above that, up to the limit of the Cakkavāḷa, the Tāvatiṃsa and other realms are located successively one above the other. It should be understood that there is no deva world that does not reach the surrounding Cakkavāḷa mountain range.

Paṭhamajjhānaṃ pana parittaṃ bhāvetvā brahmapārisajjesu uppajjanti, majjhimaṃ bhāvetvā brahmapurohitesu, paṇītaṃ bhāvetvā mahābrahmesu, ime tayopi janā paṭhamajjhānabhūmiyaṃ ekatale [M 0.0319] vasanti. Āyuābhādibhedena panesaṃ bhedo, evaṃ uparipi.

Having developed the first jhāna to a limited extent, they are reborn among the Brahmā’s Retinue. Having developed it to a medium extent, they are reborn among the Brahmā’s Ministers. Having developed it to a superior extent, they are reborn among the Great Brahmās. These three kinds of beings dwell on the same plane, the first jhāna realm. However, they differ in lifespan, radiance, and so on; and this also applies to the realms above.

Catukkanaye pana dutiyajjhānaṃ, pañcakanaye dutiyatatiyajjhānañca parittaṃ, majjhimaṃ, paṇītañca bhāvetvā parittābhāappamāṇābhāābhassaresu uppajjanti. Tatiyajjhānaṃ parittādivasena bhāvetvā parittasubhaappamāṇasubhasubhakiṇhesu. Catutthajjhānaṃ pana bhāvetvā ārammaṇamanasikārachandādhimuttiādinānattato keci asaññīsu, keci vehapphalesu, keci avihesu, atappesu, sudassesu, sudassīsu, keci akaniṭṭhesu, ākāsānañcāyatanādīsu catūsu ca yathākkamaṃ uppajjanti. Tattha hi ekacce titthiyā “cittaṃ nissāya rajjanadussanādayo, tannidānāni ca dukkhāni samuppajjantī”ti citte dosaṃ disvā “diṭṭhadhammanibbānameta”nti saññāvirāgaṃ [V 0.0244] janetvā tatrūpapattiyā jhānaṃ bhāvetvā rūpakāyamattā ṭhitā vā nisinnā vā nipannā vā hutvā nibbattitvā tattheva pañcakappasatāni tiṭṭhantīti veditabbā.

In the fourfold method, having developed the second jhāna, and in the fivefold method, having developed the second and third jhānas as limited, medium, and sublime, they are reborn in the realms of Limited Radiance, Immeasurable Radiance, and Streaming Radiance. Having developed the third jhāna as limited, etc., they are reborn in the realms of Limited Beauty, Immeasurable Beauty, and Refulgent Glory. Having developed the fourth jhāna, due to diversity of object, attention, zeal, resolve, etc., some are reborn among the non-percipient beings, some among the Vehapphala devas, some among the Aviha, Atappa, Sudassa, Sudassī, and Akaniṭṭha devas, and some in the four formless attainments—beginning with the base of infinite space—in due order. Here, some adherents of other teachings, seeing a fault in consciousness and thinking, 'Lust, aversion, and the sufferings caused by them arise in dependence on consciousness,' generate dispassion toward perception, believing, 'This is Nibbāna in this very life.' It should be understood that having developed jhāna for rebirth there, they are reborn with only a material body and remain there for five hundred aeons, whether standing, sitting, or lying down.

Aṭṭhasamāpattilābhīnaṃ kataraṃ jhānaṃ vipaccatīti? Paguṇaṃ, sabbesu paguṇesu yassa vipākabhūmiṃ pattheti, taṃpatthanāya ca asati yaṃ maraṇasamaye samāpajjati, taṃ, tasmimpi asati uttamavasena nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ vipaccati. Suddhāvāsesu ca avihādīsu anāgāmivajjitā sattā na uppajjanti, anāgāmino pana asaññīvajjitabrahmalokesu sabbattha uppajjituṃ labhanti. Sabbesampi ca ariyānaṃ tatrūpapattito uparūpapattipi, na heṭṭhūpapatti. Te hi paṭhamajjhānabhūmiyaṃ nibbattā anāgāmino nava brahmaloke sodhetvā matthake vehapphalesu ṭhitā parinibbanti, na nivattanti ariyānaṃ heṭṭhūpapattiabhāvā. Vehapphalaakaniṭṭhanevasaññānāsaññāyatanabhavā tayopi seṭṭhabhavā nāma. Imesu tīsu ṭhānesu nibbattā anāgāmino neva uddhaṃ gacchanti, na adho. Tattheva parinibbāyanti[M 0.0320]. Manussaloke ca sekhā gihibhāve yāvajīvaṃ tiṭṭhanti, na asekhā. Te hi arahattaṃ pattadivase pabbajanti vā, parinibbanti vā. Bhummadevesu pana khīṇāsavāpi yāvajīvaṃ tiṭṭhanti. Chasu kāmāvacaradevesu sotāpannasakadāgāminova tiṭṭhanti, anāgāmino pana tadaheva rūpabhavaṃ gantuṃ vaṭṭati khīṇāsavena parinibbātunti gahetabbaṃ. Evaṃ imāsu sattavīsatiyā bhūmīsu pariyāpannamanussadevabrahmalokesu nibbattasattesu manussānaṃ tāva imasmiṃ buddhuppādeva vassasataṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ, appaṃ vā bhiyyo. Āpāyikānaṃ, bhummadevānañca kadāci āyuparicchedo natthi, kammameva pamāṇaṃ. Te hi sattāhenapi maranti, kappampi tiṭṭhantīti.

For those who have obtained the eight attainments, which jhāna ripens? The one in which one is proficient. Among all the proficient jhānas, the one for which they aspire to the plane of its result ripens. If there is no such aspiration, the one they attain at the time of death ripens. If that too is absent, the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception ripens by way of being the highest. In the Pure Abodes, beginning with Avihā, beings other than non-returners are not reborn. Non-returners, however, can be reborn in all brahma worlds except the realm of non-percipient beings. For all noble ones, after being reborn there, there is rebirth in a higher plane, but not in a lower one. For those non-returners who are reborn in the first jhāna plane, after purifying the nine brahma worlds, they attain final Nibbāna while established in the Vehapphala realm at the summit; they do not return, because there is no rebirth in a lower plane for noble ones. The Vehapphala, Akaniṭṭha, and the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception existences are called the three supreme existences. Non-returners reborn in these three places go neither higher nor lower. They attain final Nibbāna right there. In the human world, trainees may remain as householders for life, but adepts do not. On the very day they attain arahantship, they either go forth or attain final Nibbāna. Among the earth-devas, however, even those whose taints are destroyed remain for their full lifespan. In the six sense-sphere celestial worlds, only stream-enterers and once-returners remain. It should be understood, however, that it is fitting for a non-returner to go to the form existence on that very day, and for one whose taints are destroyed to attain final Nibbāna. Thus, among the beings reborn in these twenty-seven planes, which comprise the human, deva, and brahma worlds, for humans in this Buddha-dispensation the lifespan is a hundred years, more or less. For beings in the planes of misery and for the earth-devas, there is no definite lifespan; kamma alone is the measure. For they may die in seven days or they may live for a kappa.

Cātumahārājikānaṃ pana mānusakāni paññāsa vassāni ekaṃ rattindivaṃ, tāya rattiyā tiṃsa rattiyo māso, tena māsena dvādasamāsiyo saṃvaccharo, tena saṃvaccharena dibbāni pañcavassasatāni āyuppamāṇaṃ. Tāni manussagaṇanāya navutivassasatasahassāni honti. Tāvatiṃsānaṃ mānusakaṃ vassasataṃ ekaṃ rattindivaṃ katvā evamāgataṃ dibbaṃ vassasahassaṃ. Evaṃ yāmādīnaṃ vassagaṇanañca diguṇaṃ katvā heṭṭhimato diguṇacatugguṇaṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ veditabbaṃ.

For the devas of the Four Great Kings, fifty human years are one day and night. Thirty such nights make a month, twelve such months make a year, and five hundred such divine years is the measure of their lifespan. By human calculation, this amounts to nine million years. For the Tāvatiṃsa devas, one hundred human years make one day and night, and thus their lifespan is a thousand divine years. Similarly, for the Yāma devas and so on, by doubling the number of years, the lifespan should be understood as double, quadruple, and so on, in relation to the one below.

Brahmesu pana brahmapārisajjānaṃ kappassa tatiyo bhāgo āyuppamāṇaṃ, brahmapurohitānaṃ upaḍḍhakappo[V 0.0245], mahābrahmānaṃ eko kappo, parittābhānaṃ dve kappāti evaṃ uparūpari diguṇaṃ katvā yāva subhakiṇhā yojetabbaṃ. Subhakiṇhānaṃ hi catusaṭṭhikappaṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ, asaññīnaṃ, vehapphalānañca pañcakappasatāni, avihānaṃ kappasahassanti uparūpari diguṇavasena yāva akaniṭṭhā yojetabbaṃ. Akaniṭṭhānaṃ hi soḷasakappasahassāni, arūpānaṃ catunnaṃ yathākkamaṃ vīsati, cattāri, saṭṭhi, caturāsīti kappasahassāni āyuppamāṇanti.

Among the Brahmās, the measure of the lifespan for the Brahmā's Retinue is one-third of a kappa; for the Brahmā's Ministers, half a kappa; for the Great Brahmās, one kappa. For the devas of Limited Radiance, it is two kappas. Thus it should be applied by successively doubling up to the devas of Refulgent Glory. For the devas of Refulgent Glory, the lifespan is sixty-four kappas. For the non-percipient beings and the Vehapphala devas, it is five hundred kappas. For the Avihā devas, it is one thousand kappas, and this should be applied by successively doubling up to the Akaniṭṭha devas. For the Akaniṭṭha devas, the lifespan is sixteen thousand kappas. For the four formless beings, the measures of the lifespan are, respectively, twenty thousand, forty thousand, sixty thousand, and eighty-four thousand kappas.

Ukkhittā [M 0.0321] puññatejena, kāmarūpagatiṃ gatā;

Bhavaggatampi sampattā, punāgacchanti duggatiṃ.

Uplifted by the power of merit, having gone to a destination in the sense sphere or the form sphere, even having reached the peak of existence, they come again to a woeful state.

Tāva dīghāyukā sattā, cavanti āyusaṅkhayā;

Natthi koci bhavo nicco, iti vuttaṃ mahesinā.

Beings are so long-lived, yet they pass away at the exhaustion of their lifespan. There is no existence whatsoever that is permanent: so it has been said by the Great Sage.

Tasmā hi dhīrā nipakā, nipuṇā atthacintakā;

Jarāmaraṇamokkhāya, bhāventi maggamuttamaṃ.

Therefore the wise, prudent, and skillful, who reflect on the goal, develop the supreme path for the sake of release from aging and death.

Bhāvayitvā suciṃ maggaṃ, nibbānogadhagāminaṃ;

Sabbāsave pariññāya, parinibbanti anāsavāti. (vibha. 1029);

Having developed the pure path that leads to the plunge into Nibbāna, having fully understood all the taints, they attain final Nibbāna, free from taints.

Ayaṃ chaṭṭhavāre nayo.

This is the method in the sixth section.

Sattamo pana vāro tesaṃ khandhādīnaṃ abhiññeyyādibhāvavibhāvanavasena pavatto. Tattha hi –

The seventh section, however, proceeds by way of explaining the state of the aggregates and so forth as things to be directly known, and so on. Therein:

“Rūpakkhandho abhiññeyyo, pariññeyyo, na pahātabbo, na bhāvetabbo, na sacchikātabbo. Cattāro khandhā abhiññeyyā pariññeyyā, siyā pahātabbā, siyā bhāvetabbā, siyā sacchikātabbā, siyā na pahātabbā na bhāvetabbā na sacchikātabbā”tiādinā –

“The form aggregate is to be directly known and to be fully understood, but not to be abandoned, not to be developed, and not to be realized. The four aggregates are to be directly known and to be fully understood; they may be things to be abandoned, or to be developed, or to be realized; or they may be things not to be abandoned, not to be developed, and not to be realized,” and so on.

Dvādasapi koṭṭhāsā vitthārato vibhattā. Tattha lakkhaṇapariggāhikāya paññāya khandhādayo sabbe dhammā [V 0.0246] abhiññeyyā. Ñātatīraṇapahānapariññāsu yathāyogaṃ yāya kāyaci pariññāya vasena sabbepi dhammā pariññeyyā. Lokuttaradhammāpi ñātapariññeyyāva. Akusalā pana pahātabbā. Maggo bhāvetabbo, phalaṃ, nibbānañca sacchikātabbaṃ. Tattha rūpakkhandho ñātatīraṇavasena pariññeyyo. Vipassanāvisaye hi sabbaṃ tīraṇapariññāya pariññeyyanti. Iminā nayena sabbattha abhiññeyyādibhāvo veditabbo.

The twelve parts have been analyzed in detail. Therein, by the wisdom that comprehends their characteristics, all dhammas—the aggregates and so forth—are to be directly known. By way of any kind of full understanding, as is appropriate in the case of full understanding as knowing, as investigating, and as abandoning, all dhammas are to be fully understood. Even supramundane dhammas are to be fully understood only by the full understanding as knowing. Unwholesome states, however, are to be abandoned. The path is to be developed; the fruit and Nibbāna are to be realized. Therein, the form aggregate is to be fully understood by way of knowing and investigating. For in the domain of insight meditation, everything is to be fully understood by the full understanding as investigating. By this method, the state of being something to be directly known, and so on, should be understood in all cases.

Aṭṭhamo [M 0.0322] pana vāro tesaṃ sārammaṇatāvibhāvanavasena pavatto, navamo panesaṃ diṭṭhasutamutaviññātesu saṅgahadassanavasena. Dasamo kusalattikādīhi saraṇadukapariyosānehi tikadukehi vibhāgadassanavasena pavatto, tepi heṭṭhā vuttanayāvāti ayamettha saṅkhepo, vitthāro panettha heṭṭhā vuttoyeva. Ādito paṭṭhāya sabbattha vibhaṅgapāḷiaṭṭhakathāsu (vibha. 978 ādayo; vibha. aṭṭha. 978 ādayo) gahetabboti.

The eighth section, however, proceeds by way of explaining their nature of having an object. The ninth proceeds by way of showing their inclusion in the seen, heard, sensed, and cognized. The tenth proceeds by way of showing the division by the triads and dyads, beginning with the wholesome triad and ending with the dyad on refuges. These too are in accordance with the method stated above. This is the summary here; the detailed explanation has already been stated above. From the beginning, in all cases, this should be understood from the Vibhaṅga Pāḷi and its commentary (Vibh. 978ff.; Vibh-a 978ff.).

Dhammahadayavibhaṅgamātikatthavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Meaning of the Matrix of the Dhammahadayavibhaṅga is finished.

Mohavicchedaniyā abhidhammamātikatthavaṇṇanāya

The Dispeller of Delusion: An Explanation of the Meaning of the Abhidhamma Matrix.

Vibhaṅgamātikatthavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Meaning of the Vibhaṅga Matrix is finished.

3. Dhātukathāmātikā

3. The Matrix of the Dhātukathā

Idāni [M 0.0323][V 0.0247] vibhaṅgamātikānantaraṃ –

Now, following the Vibhaṅga Matrix—

Ayaṃ dhātukathādīnaṃ, sampattā atthavaṇṇanā;

Mātikānaṃ yato tasmā, pañcannampi yathārahaṃ.

This exposition of the meaning of the Dhātukathā and so forth has now arrived, since it pertains, as is fitting, to all five matrices.

Anuttānatthato ceva, saṅkhepenatthanicchayā;

Vibhaṅganayato ceva, hoti saṃvaṇṇanānayo.

The method of this exposition is by way of the non-obvious meaning, by a concise determination of the meaning, and by the method of the Vibhaṅga.

Tattha dhātukathāmātikāya tāva saṃvaṇṇanā hoti. Sā panesā nikkhepato pañcadhā ṭhitā – nayamātikā abbhantaramātikā nayamukhamātikā lakkhaṇamātikā bāhiramātikāti. Tattha “saṅgaho, asaṅgaho…pe… vippayuttena saṅgahitaṃ asaṅgahita”nti ayaṃ cuddasahi padehi nikkhittā saṅgahādikena nayena dhātukathāya dhammā vibhattāti dassetuṃ ṭhapitattā nayamātikā nāma, yā “mūlamātikā”tipi vuccati.

Here, first, is the explanation of the Dhātukathā Matrix. This, by way of enumeration, is established in five ways: the method matrix, the internal matrix, the method-introduction matrix, the characteristic matrix, and the external matrix. Among these, the one laid out in fourteen terms – “inclusion, non-inclusion… included by what is dissociated, not included” – is called the method matrix because it is established to show that the phenomena of the Dhātukathā are distinguished by the method of inclusion and so forth. It is also called the “root matrix.”

“Pañcakkhandhā…pe… manasikāro”ti ayaṃ pañcavīsādhikena padasatena nikkhittā saṅgahādinayena vibhajitabbabhāvena dhātukathāya abbhantare eva ṭhapitattā abbhantaramātikā nāma, yā “dhātukathāmātikā”tipi vuccati.

“The five aggregates… up to attention”—this, laid out in one hundred and twenty-five terms, is called the internal matrix because it is placed within the Dhātukathā itself, having the nature of being analyzed by the method of inclusion and so forth. It is also called the “Dhātukathā matrix.”

“Tīhi saṅgaho, tīhi asaṅgaho, catūhi sampayogo, catūhi vippayogo”ti ayaṃ catūhi padehi nikkhittā khandhādīsu ca kusalattikādīsu ca mātikādhammesu tīhi khandhāyatanadhātupadeheva [V 0.0248] saṅgaho asaṅgaho ca, tathā catūhi arūpakkhandhehi sampayogo, vippayogo cāti imesaṃ saṅgahāsaṅgahādīnaṃ nayānaṃ mukhānīti dassetuṃ ṭhapitattā nayamukhamātikā nāma.

"Inclusion by three, non-inclusion by three, association by four, dissociation by four"—this is laid out in four terms. Among the matrix principles concerning the aggregates and so on, and the wholesome triad and so on, inclusion and non-inclusion are only by means of the three terms of aggregates, sense bases, and elements. Likewise, association and dissociation are with the four immaterial aggregates. This is called the method-introduction matrix because it is established to show that these are the openings for the methods of inclusion, non-inclusion, and so on.

“Sabhāgo [M 0.0324] visabhāgo”ti ayaṃ dvīhi padehi nikkhittā sabhāgavisabhāgalakkhaṇavaseneva saṅgahāsaṅgahanayā ceva sampayogavippayoganayā ca hontīti dassetuṃ ṭhapitattā lakkhaṇamātikā nāma. Sabbāpi dhammasaṅgaṇī dhātukathāya mātikāti ayaṃ chasaṭṭhi tikapadāni, dve ca dukapadasatāni saṅkhipitvā nikkhittā dhātukathā mātikāto bahi ṭhapitattā bāhiramātikā nāma. Evametissā pañcavidhāya mātikāya ayamanuttānatthavaṇṇanā.

"Similar and dissimilar"—this is laid out in two terms. It is called the characteristic matrix because it is established to show that the methods of inclusion and non-inclusion, and of association and dissociation, arise precisely by way of the characteristics of similarity and dissimilarity. The entire Dhammasaṅgaṇī is the matrix for the Dhātukathā. This matrix, which summarizes and lays out sixty-six triad terms and two hundred dyad terms, is called the external matrix because it is placed outside the Dhātukathā matrix. Thus, this is the explanation of the non-obvious meaning of this fivefold matrix.

Saṅgahotiādīsu hi saṅgaho tāva jātisañjātikiriyāgaṇanavasena catubbidho. Tattha “sabbe khattiyā āgacchantu, yā cāvuso visākha, sammāvācā, yo ca sammākammanto, yo ca sammāājīvo, ime dhammā sīlakkhandhe saṅgahitā”ti (ma. ni. 1.462) ayaṃ jātisaṅgaho nāma. “Sabbe kosalakā āgacchantu, yo cāvuso visākha, sammāvāyāmo, yā ca sammāsati, yo ca sammāsamādhi, ime dhammā samādhikkhandhe saṅgahitā”ti (ma. ni. 1.462) ayaṃ sañjātisaṅgaho nāma, ekaṭṭhāne jātisambandhabhāvena saṅgahoti attho. “Sabbe hatthārohā āgacchantu, yā cāvuso visākha, sammādiṭṭhi, yo ca sammāsaṅkappo, ime dhammā paññākkhandhe saṅgahitā”ti (ma. ni. 1.462) ayaṃ kiriyāsaṅgaho nāma. “Hañci cakkhāyatanaṃ rūpakkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchati, tena vata re vattabbe ‘cakkhāyatanaṃ rūpakkhandhena saṅgahita’”nti (kathā. 471) ayaṃ gaṇanasaṅgaho nāma, ayamidha adhippeto. Tappaṭipakkhena asaṅgaho veditabbo. Tesaṃ vikappato saṅgahitena asaṅgahitādīni, ekuppādekanirodhaekavatthukaekārammaṇatāvasena sampayogo, tappaṭipakkhato vippayogo, tesaṃ vikappato sampayuttena vippayuttādīni, tadubhayasaṃsaggavikappato saṅgahitena sampayuttaṃ vippayuttantiādīni ca [M 0.0325] veditabbāni. Sesaṃ vuttatthameva. Ayaṃ tāvettha anuttānapadattho.

In the terms such as 'inclusion,' first, inclusion is fourfold by way of birth, origin, action, and enumeration. Herein, the phrase, “Let all the Khattiyas come, and, friend Visākha, right speech, right action, and right livelihood—these qualities are included in the aggregate of virtue” (MN 1.462), is called birth-inclusion. The phrase, “Let all the Kosalans come, and, friend Visākha, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration—these qualities are included in the aggregate of concentration” (MN 1.462), is called origin-inclusion, meaning inclusion by connection to birth in the same place. The phrase, “Let all the elephant-riders come, and, friend Visākha, right view and right intention—these qualities are included in the aggregate of wisdom” (MN 1.462), is called action-inclusion. The statement, “If the eye-base is counted under the aggregate of form, then it should be said, ‘The eye-base is included in the aggregate of form’” (Kv 471), is called enumeration-inclusion, and this is the intended meaning here. Its opposite should be understood as non-inclusion. From the variations of these, what is not included in relation to what is included, and so on, are to be understood. Association is by way of having a common arising, a common ceasing, a common basis, and a common object. Its opposite is dissociation. From the variations of these, what is dissociated in relation to what is associated, and so on, are to be understood. From the variations of the combination of both, what is associated with the included, what is dissociated, and so on, are to be understood. The rest has the meaning as stated. This, then, is the explanation here of the words whose meaning is not obvious.

Saṅgahāsaṅgahapadatthavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Meaning of the Terms 'Inclusion' and 'Non-inclusion'

Atthavinicchayato pana yasmā abbhantaramātikāya rūpakkhandhādīni, bāhiramātikāya kusalādīni ca “saṅgaho asaṅgaho”tiādikehi nayamātikāpadehi “tīhi saṅgaho, tīhi asaṅgaho”tiādinayamukhamātikāvasena [V 0.0249] yathārahaṃ niddesatthāya bhagavatā ṭhapitāni, tasmā khandhādīnaṃ saṅgahādīnaṃ pāḷiyaṃ vuttānusāreneva saṅkhepato atthavinicchayo hoti. Iminā nayena vibhaṅganayo sakkā ñātunti taṃ visuṃ na vakkhāma.

However, regarding the determination of meaning, because the aggregates, such as the form aggregate in the internal matrix, and the wholesome and so on in the external matrix, were established by the Blessed One for the purpose of appropriate exposition by way of the method-matrix terms such as 'inclusion, non-inclusion,' and by way of the method-introduction matrix such as 'inclusion by three, non-inclusion by three,' therefore the determination of meaning for the aggregates, inclusions, and so on is briefly made in accordance with what is stated in the Pāli text. By this method, the approach of the Vibhaṅga can be understood, so we will not explain it separately.

Tattha saṅgahāsaṅgahavāre khandhānaṃ tāva ayaṃ niddese nayo – rūpakkhandho ekena khandhena ekādasahi āyatanehi ekādasahi dhātūhi saṅgahito. Catūhi khandhehi ekenāyatanena sattahi dhātūhi asaṅgahito. Tattha ekādasahīti manāyatanavajjehi. Dhammāyatanenāpi hi keci rūpadhammā saṅgahitā. Ekādasahīti sattaviññāṇadhātuvajjāhi. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva.

Here, in the section on inclusion and non-inclusion, this is the method of exposition for the aggregates: the form aggregate is included by one aggregate, eleven sense bases, and eleven elements. It is not included by four aggregates, one sense base, and seven elements. Here, 'by eleven [sense bases]' means excluding the mind base. For some material phenomena are indeed included by the mental-object base. 'By eleven [elements]' means excluding the seven consciousness-elements. The rest is easily understood.

Vedanādayo tayo khandhā yathāsakaṃ ekena khandhena ekenāyatanena ekāya dhātuyā saṅgahitā, catūhi khandhehi ekādasahi āyatanehi sattarasahi dhātūhi asaṅgahitā, tathā viññāṇakkhandhopi. Kevalaṃ panettha sattahi viññāṇadhātūhi saṅgahito, ekādasahi dhātūhi asaṅgahitoti ettakameva viseso. Tattha hi vedanādīnaṃ tiṇṇaṃ khandhānaṃ ekena dhammāyatanena ca ekāya dhammadhātuyā ca saṅgahitatā veditabbā. Pāḷiyaṃ panettha khandhapadaniddese, upari āyatanādiniddesesu ca “rūpakkhandho ca vedanākkhandho ca dvīhi khandhehi ekādasahāyatanehi ekādasahi [M 0.0326] dhātūhi saṅgahitā”tiādinā (dhātu. 15) dvimūlakādinayenāpi vitthāranayo vibhatto, sopi iminā ekamūlanayānusārena sabbattha suviññeyyoti na vitthārayimhā. Ayaṃ khandhapadaniddesanayo.

The three aggregates—feeling and so on—are each included by one aggregate, one sense base, and one element, and are not included by four aggregates, eleven sense bases, and seventeen elements. The consciousness aggregate is likewise, with this one difference: it is included by seven consciousness-elements and not included by eleven elements. For here, it should be understood that the three aggregates—feeling and so on—are included by the one mental-object base and the one mental-object element. In the Pāli text, however, in the exposition of the aggregate terms, and further on in the expositions of the sense bases and so on, the detailed method is also analyzed by way of the two-rooted method and so on, as in: “The form aggregate and the feeling aggregate are included by two aggregates, eleven sense bases, and eleven elements,” etc. (Dhātu. 15). Since that too can be easily understood everywhere by following this single-rooted method, we have not elaborated. This is the method of exposition for the aggregate terms.

Āyatanadhātupadānampi khandhapade vuttānusāreneva tīhi saṅgaho, tīhi asaṅgaho ca yathāyogaṃ yojetvā ñātabbo. Kevalaṃ panettha dhammāyatanadhammadhātūsu asaṅkhatassa khandhasaṅgahābhāvā taṃ ṭhapetvā sesānaṃ khandhesu saṅgaho veditabbo.

For the terms for the sense bases and elements also, inclusion by three and non-inclusion by three should be understood by applying them appropriately, in accordance with what was stated for the aggregate terms. However, here, in the case of the mental-object base and the mental-object element, since the unconditioned has no inclusion in the aggregates, that should be set aside, and the inclusion of the remainder in the aggregates should be understood.

Saccesu dukkhasaccaṃ sabbehi khandhāyatanadhātūhi. Samudayamaggasaccāni saṅkhārakkhandhena, dhammāyatanadhammadhātūhi ca saṅgahitāni. Nirodhasaccaṃ khandhena asaṅgahitaṃ, dhammāyatanadhammadhātūhi eva saṅgahitaṃ.

Among the truths, the truth of suffering is included by all aggregates, sense bases, and elements. The truths of origin and the path are included by the formations aggregate, and by the mental-object base and the mental-object element. The truth of cessation is not included by any aggregate but is included only by the mental-object base and the mental-object element.

Indriyesu jīvitindriyaṃ dvīhi rūpakkhandhasaṅkhārakkhandhehi. Sukhindriyādīni pañca vedanākkhandhena[V 0.0250], saddhādīni saṅkhārakkhandhena, sabbāni cetāni jīvitindriyādīni, itthindriyapurisindriyādīnipi dhammāyatanadhammadhātūhi saṅgahitāni. Sesindriyāni suviññeyyāni.

Among the faculties, the life faculty is included by the two aggregates of form and formations. The five faculties of pleasure and so on are included by the aggregate of feeling; the faculties of faith and so on, by the aggregate of formations. All these faculties—the life faculty and so on, and also the faculties of femininity, masculinity, and so on—are included by the mental-object base and the mental-object element. The remaining faculties are easily understood.

Paṭiccasamuppādesu nāmarūpaṃ viññāṇavajjitehi catūhi khandhehi, ekādasahi āyatanadhātūhi ca saṅgahitaṃ. Ettha hi pavattiyaṃ nāmarūpassāpi gahitattā saddāyatanampi gahitanti veditabbaṃ. Saḷāyatanaṃ dvīhi khandhehi, pasādaviññāṇabhūtehi chahi āyatanehi, dvādasahi dhātūhi saṅgahitaṃ. Upapattibhavo pana kāmabhavabhūto pañcahi khandhehi, saddāyatanavajjitehi ekādasahi āyatanehi, sattarasahi dhātūhi. Rūpabhavo pañcahi khandhehi, saddādicatukkaghānādittayatabbiññāṇavajjehi pañcahāyatanehi, aṭṭhahi dhātūhi [M 0.0327] saṅgahito. Asaññībhavo ekena rūpakkhandhena, rūpadhammavasena dvīhi āyatanadhātūhi saṅgahito. Ghānādittayaṃ panettha āyatanādikiccākaraṇato āyatanadhātūhi asaṅgahitampi rūpakkhandhena saṅgahitanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Bhavassa ca ekantamupādinnattā pavattivipākānaṃ cakkhuviññāṇādīnaṃ gahaṇepi anupādinnasaddāyatanassa idha aggahaṇaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Arūpabhavo catūhi khandhehi dvīhi āyatanadhātūhi. Jātijarāmaraṇāni nāmarūpadhammānaṃ lakkhaṇattā dvīhi rūpakkhandhasaṅkhārakkhandhehi. Sokadukkhadomanassāni vedanākkhandhena. Upāyāso saṅkhārakkhandhena, dhammāyatanadhammadhātūhi ca saṅgahito. Paridevo rūpakkhandhasaddāyatanasaddadhātūhi. Sesāni panettha paṭiccasamuppādaṅgāni, satipaṭṭhānasammappadhānā ca suviññeyyāva.

In dependent origination, name-and-form is included by the four aggregates exclusive of consciousness, and by eleven bases and eleven elements. Here, since name-and-form is also taken in the course of existence, the sound base too should be understood as included. The sixfold base is included by two aggregates, by the six bases which are the sensitive faculties and consciousness, and by twelve elements. The rebirth-becoming, which is the sense-sphere becoming, is included by the five aggregates, by the eleven bases exclusive of the sound base, and by seventeen elements. The form-sphere becoming is included by the five aggregates; by five bases, exclusive of the four beginning with sound and the triad beginning with the nose faculty along with their consciousnesses; and by eight elements. The non-percipient becoming is included by the one aggregate of form, and by two bases and elements by way of form-phenomena. Here, the triad beginning with the nose faculty, though not included by the bases and elements because they do not perform the function of a base, etc., should be seen as included by the aggregate of form. And since becoming is entirely clung-to, even though eye-consciousness and so on are taken as resultants in the course of existence, it should be seen that the non-clung-to sound base is not taken here. The formless becoming is included by four aggregates and by two bases and elements. Birth, aging, and death, being characteristics of name-and-form phenomena, are included by the two aggregates: the aggregate of form and the aggregate of formations. Sorrow, pain, and displeasure are included by the aggregate of feeling. Distress is included by the aggregate of formations, and by the mind-object base and mind-object element. Lamentation is included by the aggregate of form, the sound base, and the sound element. The remaining links of dependent origination here, as well as the foundations of mindfulness and the right strivings, are quite easy to understand.

Iddhipādā dvīhi khandhehi, āyatanehi, dhātūhi saṅgahitā. Ettha ca cittiddhipādassa dhammadhātumanoviññāṇadhātuniyamato soḷasahi dhātūhi asaṅgaho veditabbo. Jhānāni dvīhi vedanāsaṅkhārakkhandhehi, ekenāyatanena, ekāya dhātuyā ca saṅgahitāni. Appamaññā ekena khandhena, ekena āyatanena, ekāya dhātuyā saṅgahitā. Evaṃ pañcindriyādīnipi. Kevalaṃ pana cittaṃ sattahi viññāṇadhātūhi saṅgahitanti ettakameva viseso. Sabbesampi cesa vuttāvasesehi khandhāyatanadhātūhi asaṅgahitabhāvo veditabbo.

The bases of spiritual power are included by two aggregates, two bases, and two elements. Here, it should be understood that in the case of the basis of spiritual power consisting of concentration, there is non-inclusion by sixteen elements because of its restriction to the mind-object element and the mind-consciousness element. The jhānas are included by the two aggregates of feeling and formations, by one base, and by one element. The immeasurables are included by one aggregate, by one base, and by one element. Similarly, the five faculties and so on. However, consciousness alone is included by the seven consciousness elements—this much is the distinction. And for all of these, their state of not being included by the remaining aggregates, bases, and elements should be understood.

Iminā nayena bāhiramātikāyapi “kusalā dhammā, akusalā dhammā catūhi khandhehi, dvīhi āyatanehi, dhātūhi saṅgahitā. Abyākatā pana asaṅkhataṃ khandhato ṭhapetvā pañcahi khandhehi dvādasahi āyatanehi aṭṭhārasahi dhātūhi saṅgahitā”tiādinā yojetvā saṅgahāsaṅgaho ñātabboti [M 0.0328][V 0.0251] ayamettha saṅkhepo, vitthāro pana dhātukathāpāḷiaṭṭhakathāsu (dhātu. 77 ādayo; dhātu. aṭṭha. 77) gahetabboti.

In this way, in the external matrix too, the inclusion and non-inclusion should be known by applying the method beginning: 'Wholesome phenomena and unwholesome phenomena are included by four aggregates, two bases, and two elements. But indeterminate phenomena, setting aside the unconditioned from the aggregates, are included by five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.' This is the summary here; the detailed account, however, should be taken from the Dhātukathā Pāḷi and its commentary (Dhātu. 77 ff.; Dhātu. Aṭṭha. 77).

Niṭṭhito “saṅgaho asaṅgaho”ti padassa

Here ends the section on 'Inclusion and Non-inclusion'.

Atthavinicchayo.

The Determination of Meaning

Saṅgahitenaasaṅgahitapadatthavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Meaning of the Term 'Not Included by the Included'

Saṅgahitenaasaṅgahitapade sabbesaṃ rūpakkhandhādipadānaṃ niddeso na sambhavati. Yāni panettha padāni rūpekadesaṃ, arūpena asammissaṃ viññāṇekadesañca aññena asammissaṃ dīpenti, tesamidha niddeso. Tāni pana manāyatanadhammāyatanavajjitānaṃ dasāyatanānaṃ, dhammadhātuvajjitānaṃ sattarasannaṃ dhātūnaṃ, sattarūpindriyānañca vasena veditabbāni, na rūpakkhandhādīnaṃ. Teneva pāḷiyaṃ –

In the term 'not included by the included,' an exposition of all terms such as the aggregate of form is not possible. However, those terms here that indicate a portion of form unmixed with the formless, and a portion of consciousness unmixed with anything else—of these there is an exposition here. These, however, should be understood by way of the ten bases exclusive of the mind base and the mind-object base; the seventeen elements exclusive of the mind-object element; and the seven material faculties; not by way of the aggregate of form and so on. Therefore, in the Pāḷi text:

“Dasāyatanā sattarasa dhātuyo,

Sattindriyā asaññābhavo ekavokārabhavo;

Paridevo sanidassanasappaṭighaṃ,

Anidassanaṃ punadeva sappaṭighaṃ upādā”ti. (dhātu. 178) –

"Ten bases, seventeen elements, seven faculties, non-percipient becoming, one-constituent becoming; lamentation, the visible-and-resistant, and again the invisible-and-resistant, and derived form."

Evaṃ uddānagāthā vuttā. Rūpakkhandhena hi rūpakkhandhova saṅgahito, evaṃ vedanākkhandhādīhi ca vedanākkhandhādayova. Tepi ca yehi kehici āyatanadhātūhi asaṅgahitā nāma natthīti tesaṃ saṅgahitena asaṅgahitattābhāvā yathāvuttāyatanānaṃ vasenevettha atthavinicchayo hoti. Idaṃ hettha lakkhaṇaṃ – yaṃ khandhapadena saṅgahitaṃ hutvā āyatanadhātupadehi asaṅgahitaṃ, khandhāyatanapadehi vā saṅgahitaṃ hutvā dhātupadena asaṅgahitaṃ, tassa khandhāyatanadhātūhi asaṅgaho [M 0.0329] vuccati. Kathaṃ? Cakkhāyatanena ye dhammā khandhasaṅgahena saṅgahitā, āyatanasaṅgahena, dhātusaṅgahena ca asaṅgahitā, te dhammā katihi khandhehi, āyatanehi, dhātūhi asaṅgahitā? Te dhammā catūhi khandhehi dvīhi āyatanehi [V 0.0252] aṭṭhahi dhātūhi asaṅgahitā. Evaṃ rūpāyatanādīsupi pasādavisayabhūtesu dhātūsu, rūpindriyādīsu ca yojanakkamo veditabbo.

Thus the summary verse has been stated. For the aggregate of form is included only by the aggregate of form, and similarly the aggregate of feeling and so on are included only by the aggregate of feeling and so on. And since these do not exist as things not included by any bases and elements whatsoever, because for them there is no state of being 'not included by the included,' the determination of meaning here proceeds by way of the aforesaid bases. This is the characteristic here: what, being included by the term 'aggregate,' is not included by the terms 'base' and 'element'; or what, being included by the terms 'aggregate' and 'base,' is not included by the term 'element'—that is called 'not included by the aggregates, bases, and elements.' How so? The phenomena that are included by the eye base by way of aggregate-inclusion, but not included by way of base-inclusion and element-inclusion—by how many aggregates, bases, and elements are those phenomena not included? Those phenomena are not included by four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements. Similarly, the method of application should be understood in regard to the form base and so on among the elements that are sensitive matter and sense objects, and in regard to the material faculties such as the eye faculty.

Tatrāyaṃ nayo – cakkhāyatanena ye rūpadhammā khandhasaṅgahena rūpakkhandhoti saṅgahitā, āyatanadhātusaṅgahena cakkhāyatanena asaṅgahitā, cakkhudhātuyā asaṅgahitā, cakkhāyatanacakkhudhātūhi ekassevetassa cakkhussa visuṃ āyatanadhātūsu saṅgahitattā te cakkhāyatanavirahitā sabbe rūpadhammā catūhi arūpakkhandhehi cakkhāyatanaṃ manāyatananti dvīhi āyatanehi cakkhudhātu sattaviññāṇadhātūti aṭṭhahi dhātūhi asaṅgahitā. Upari rūpāyatanādīsupi eseva nayo. Imasmiṃ hi vāre cakkhāyatanassa attano tīhipi khandhāyatanadhātusaṅgahehi saṅgahitatāya asaṅgahitattābhāvā khandhasaṅgahena saṅgahitaṃ, āyatanasaṅgahena asaṅgahitaṃ, dhātusaṅgahena asaṅgahitanti evaṃ tīhipi saṅgahitāsaṅgahitavisesanehi visiṭṭhasseva “katihi khandhehī”tiādinā khandhādīhi asaṅgahassa vuccamānattā ca arūpakkhandhehi saha bahibhūtatā veditabbā. Yathā cettha cakkhāyatanena upalakkhitānaṃ rūpadhammānaṃyeva saṅgahitena asaṅgahitatā, na cakkhāyatanassa, evaṃ upari rūpāyatanādīhi upalakkhitavārepi yathārahaṃ ñātabbā.

Herein, this is the method. Those material phenomena which, in relation to the eye base, are included by aggregate-inclusion as the aggregate of form, are not included by base-inclusion as the eye base, and are not included by element-inclusion as the eye element—because this one eye itself is included separately by the eye base and the eye element among the bases and elements—all those material phenomena apart from the eye base are not included by the four immaterial aggregates, by two bases (the eye base and the mind base), and by eight elements (the eye element and the seven consciousness elements). The same method applies above to the form base and so on. For in this section, since the eye base itself is included by its own three inclusions—aggregate, base, and element—it has no state of non-inclusion. And since the non-inclusion by aggregates, etc., is stated by asking 'By how many aggregates?' etc., only for what is specified by the three qualifiers—'included by aggregate-inclusion, not included by base-inclusion, not included by element-inclusion'—it should be understood that this is external along with the immaterial aggregates. And just as here the state of being 'not included by the included' pertains only to the material phenomena specified by the eye base, not to the eye base itself, so too it should be known accordingly in the sections specified above by the form base and so on.

Sesesu pana cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā ye dhammā khandhasaṅgahena saṅgahitā, āyatanasaṅgahena saṅgahitā, dhātusaṅgahena asaṅgahitā, te dhammā catūhi khandhehi ekādasahi āyatanehi [M 0.0330] dvādasahi dhātūhi asaṅgahitā. Evaṃ sesaviññāṇadhātūsupi. Paṭiccasamuppādaṅgesu asaññībhavena ye dhammā…pe… te dhammā catūhi khandhehi dasahāyatanehi soḷasahi dhātūhi asaṅgahitā. Upādādhammehi ye dhammā…pe… te dhammā catūhi khandhehi ekādasahāyatanehi sattarasahi dhātūhi asaṅgahitāti ime cattāro vārā apubbavisesā samāyeva. Tattha cakkhuviññāṇavāre dvādasahīti cha viññāṇadhātuyo vajjetvā avasesāhi dhātūhi sesā cha viññāṇadhātuyova khandhāyatanasaṅgahehi saṅgahitā, dhātusaṅgaheneva asaṅgahitā. Avasesāhi dvādasahi dhātūhi asaṅgahitāti. Esa nayo sesaviññāṇadhātūsupi.

But among the remaining, in the case of the eye-consciousness element, those phenomena that are included by aggregate-inclusion and by base-inclusion, but not included by element-inclusion—those phenomena are not included by four aggregates, eleven bases, and twelve elements. The same applies to the remaining consciousness elements. Among the links of dependent origination, in the case of non-percipient becoming, those phenomena... (etc.) ... are not included by four aggregates, ten bases, and sixteen elements. In the case of derived phenomena, those phenomena... (etc.) ... are not included by four aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements. These four sections are exactly the same, without any new distinction. Therein, in the section on eye-consciousness, 'by twelve' means by the remaining elements after excluding the six consciousness elements. The other six consciousness elements are included by aggregate- and base-inclusion, but not included by element-inclusion. They are not included by the remaining twelve elements. This method applies to the remaining consciousness elements as well.

Dutiye tīhāyatanehīti rūpāyatanadhammāyatanamanāyatanehi. Asaññibrahmaloke hi rūpāyatanadhammāyatanavasena dve āyatanāni upapattibhavabhāvena pāḷiyaṃ āgatāni, te pana khandhehi saṅgahitāni, āyatanadhātūsu asaṅgahitāni. Tadavasesāni nava rūpāyatanāni, tāni teheva [V 0.0253] ca dvīhi manāyatanadhammāyatanehi ca asaṅgahitāni nāma honti. Navahi dhātūhīti rūpadhātudhammadhātūhi saddhiṃ sattahi viññāṇadhātūhi.

In the second case, 'by three bases' means by the form-base, the dhamma-base, and the mind-base. For in the non-percipient brahma-world, two bases—the form-base and the dhamma-base—are given in the Pāḷi text as being present by way of rebirth-becoming. These, however, are included by the aggregates but not included among the bases and elements. The remaining nine material bases are thus considered not included by those very two, nor by the mind-base and the dhamma-base. 'By nine elements' means the form-element and the dhamma-element, together with the seven consciousness elements.

Tatiye dasahīti rūpāyatanadhammāyatanavajjehi. Soḷasahīti rūpadhātudhammadhātuvajjāhi. Anidassanasappaṭighāni nāma nava oḷārikāyatanāni, tāni tehi khandhasaṅgahena saṅgahitāni, āyatanadhātusaṅgahehi ca asaṅgahitāni, rūpāyatanadhammāyatanāni dvepi sesehi āyatanadhātūhi asaṅgahitāni nāma honti.

In the third case, 'by ten' means exclusive of the form-base and the dhamma-base. 'By sixteen' means exclusive of the form-element and the dhamma-element. The nine gross bases called 'invisible and resistant' are included by themselves by way of aggregate-inclusion, but are not included by way of base-and-element-inclusion; and the two bases, the form-base and the dhamma-base, are considered not included by the remaining bases and elements.

Catutthe ekādasahīti phoṭṭhabbāyatanavajjehi phoṭṭhabbāyatanassa upādādhammehi āyatanādīsu asaṅgahitattā. Sesaṃ [M 0.0331] suviññeyyameva. Ayaṃ saṅgahitenaasaṅgahitapade nayo.

In the fourth case, it is by eleven bases, excluding the tangible base, because the derived phenomena are not included in the tangible base among the bases, etc. The rest is easily understood. This is the method in the section 'Unincluded by the Included'.

Asaṅgahitenasaṅgahitapadatthavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Meaning of the Section 'Included by the Unincluded'

Asaṅgahitenasaṅgahitapade pana yāni padāni viññāṇena vā oḷārikarūpena vā asammissaṃ dhammāyatanekadesaṃ dīpenti, tāneva niddisīyanti, tāni pana vedanādīnaṃ tiṇṇaṃ khandhānaṃ, dukkhasaccavajjitānaṃ tiṇṇaṃ saccānaṃ, pasādamanovajjitānaṃ soḷasannaṃ indriyānaṃ, avijjāsaṅkhāraphassavedanātaṇhupādānakammabhavajātijarāmaraṇasokadukkhadomanassupāyāsavasena cuddasapaccayākārapadānañca vasena veditabbāni, na rūpakkhandhādīnaṃ. Teneva aṭṭhakathāyaṃ –

However, in the section 'Included by the Unincluded,' only those terms are specified that indicate a portion of the dhamma-base unmixed with either consciousness or gross form. These, however, should be understood in terms of: the three aggregates beginning with feeling; the three truths excluding the truth of suffering; the sixteen faculties excluding the sensitive matter of the sense faculties and the mind faculty; and the fourteen terms of the conditional structure, namely: ignorance, formations, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, kamma-becoming, birth, aging-and-death, sorrow, pain, grief, and despair—but not in terms of the form aggregate, etc. Thus it is said in the commentary:

“Tayo khandhā tathā saccā, indriyāni ca soḷasa;

Padāni paccayākāre, cuddasūpari cuddasa.

“Three aggregates and likewise the truths, and sixteen faculties; fourteen terms in the conditional structure, and fourteen more.

“Samatiṃsa padā honti, gocchakesu dasasvatha;

Duve cūḷantaradukā, aṭṭha honti mahantarā”ti. (dhātu. aṭṭha. 179) –

“Thirty terms there are in ten clusters; two are the small intermediate pairs, and eight are the great intermediate pairs.” (Dhātu. Aṭṭha. 179)

Evaṃ uddānagāthā vuttā. Idaṃ hettha lakkhaṇaṃ – yaṃ khandhapadena asaṅgahitaṃ, āyatanadhātupadehi saṅgahitaṃ, tasseva tīhi visesanehi visiṭṭhassa khandhādīhi saṅgaho vuccati. Kathaṃ? Vedanākkhandhena ye dhammā khandhasaṅgahena asaṅgahitā, āyatanadhātusaṅgahehi saṅgahitā, te dhammā katihi [V 0.0254] khandhehi, āyatanehi, dhātūhi saṅgahitā? Te dhammā asaṅkhataṃ khandhato ṭhapetvā tīhi khandhehi ekenāyatanena ekāya dhātuyā saṅgahitāti.

Thus the summary verses have been stated. Herein, this is the characteristic feature: when something is unincluded by the term 'aggregate' but included by the terms 'base' and 'element,' its inclusion by the aggregates, etc.—as qualified by these three distinctions—is spoken of. How so? Those phenomena that are unincluded by aggregate-inclusion with reference to the feeling aggregate, but are included by base- and element-inclusion—by how many aggregates, bases, and elements are those phenomena included? Those phenomena, setting aside the unconditioned from the aggregate-inclusion, are included by three aggregates, one base, and one element.

Tatrāyaṃ nayo – vedanākkhandhena hi nibbānaṃ, sukhumarūpaṃ, saññāsaṅkhārā ca khandhasaṅgahena asaṅgahitā hutvā dhammāyatanadhammadhātusaṅgahena saṅgahitā. Tesu nibbānaṃ khandhasaṅgahaṃ na [M 0.0332] gacchati, sesā tīhi rūpasaññāsaṅkhārakkhandhehi saṅgahaṃ gacchanti, āyatanadhātuyo panettha dhammāyatanadhammadhātūnaṃ vaseneva sabbattha veditabbā itarāsaṃ asambhavā, imesu ca nibbānampi saṅgahaṃ gacchati. Teneva hi “asaṅkhataṃ khandhato ṭhapetvā”ti vuttaṃ. Tassāyamattho – khandhasaṅgahe eva asaṅkhataṃ ṭhapetvā, na itarasaṅgahesūti evaṃ saññākkhandhādīsupi yojanā veditabbā. Ayaṃ pana viseso – jīvitindriyena ye dhammā…pe… te dhammā dvīhi vedanāsaññākkhandhehi saṅgahitā, rūpārūpajīvitindriyehi nibbānavedanāsaññāviññāṇakkhandhā khandhasaṅgahena asaṅgahitā, tesu ca nibbānavedanāsaññāva āyatanadhātusaṅgahena saṅgahitāti. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva. Ayaṃ asaṅgahitenasaṅgahitapade nayo.

Herein, this is the method. With reference to the feeling aggregate, Nibbāna, subtle form, perception, and formations are unincluded by aggregate-inclusion but are included by inclusion in the dhamma-base and dhamma-element. Among these, Nibbāna is not included in any aggregate, while the others are included by the three aggregates of form, perception, and formations. Here, the bases and elements should be understood everywhere only in terms of the dhamma-base and dhamma-element, since the others are impossible; and in this inclusion, Nibbāna too is included. For this reason it was said, 'setting aside the unconditioned from the aggregate-inclusion.' This is its meaning: one sets aside the unconditioned only in the aggregate-inclusion, not in the other inclusions. The application should be understood in the same way for the perception aggregate and so on. This, however, is a special case: with reference to the life faculty, those phenomena ...pe... are included by the two aggregates of feeling and perception. With reference to the material and immaterial life faculties, Nibbāna and the aggregates of feeling, perception, and consciousness are unincluded by aggregate-inclusion; and among these, only Nibbāna, feeling, and perception are included by base- and element-inclusion. The rest is easily understood. This is the method in the section 'Included by the Unincluded'.

Saṅgahitenasaṅgahitapadatthavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Meaning of the Section 'Included by the Included'

Saṅgahitenasaṅgahitapade pana yāni padāni saṅkhārekadesaṃ aññena asammissaṃ dīpenti vedanekadesaṃ vā sukhumarūpaṃ vā saddekadesaṃ vā, tāneva niddisīyanti. Khandhāyatanadhātūsu ekampi koṭṭhāsaṃ sakalena gahetvā ṭhitapadāni na yujjanti. Tāni pana dvinnaṃ samudayamaggasaccānaṃ, pannarasindriyānaṃ, ekādasapaṭiccapadādīnañca vasena veditabbāni. Idaṃ hettha lakkhaṇaṃ – yaṃ attanā khandhādivasena saṅgahitehi khandhādito saṅgahitaṃ, tasseva paṭhamaṃ uddhaṭapadassa puna khandhādīhi saṅgaho vuccati.

However, in the section 'Included by the Included,' only those terms are specified that indicate a portion of formations unmixed with anything else, or a portion of feeling, or subtle form, or a portion of sound. Terms that stand for an entire division of the aggregates, bases, and elements are not appropriate. These, however, should be understood in terms of the two truths of origination and path, the fifteen faculties, the eleven terms of dependent origination, and so on. Herein, this is the characteristic feature: when something is included by those things that are themselves included in terms of aggregates, etc., the inclusion of that very term, first extracted, by the aggregates, etc., is again spoken of.

Tatrāyaṃ ādipade nayo – samudayasaccena ye dhammā khandhādīhi tīhi saṅgahehipi saṅgahitā, tehi dhammehi ye dhammā khandhādīhi tīhipi saṅgahitā, te dhammā [M 0.0333] ekena khandhena ekenāyatanena ekāya dhātuyā saṅgahitāti. Samudayasaccena hi taṇhāvajjā sesā saṅkhārā khandhādīhi saṅgahehi saṅgahitā, puna tehi ca taṇhāva saṅgahitā, sā ca puna saṅkhārakkhandhadhammāyatanadhammadhātūhi [V 0.0255] saṅgahitā. Sesesupi eseva nayo. Ayaṃ saṅgahitenasaṅgahitapade nayo.

Herein, this is the method for the first term. With reference to the truth of origination, the phenomena included by it under the three inclusions of aggregates, etc., and the phenomena included by those phenomena under the three inclusions, are included by one aggregate, one base, and one element. For, with reference to the truth of origination, the remaining formations apart from craving are included by the inclusions of aggregates, etc.; and by these, in turn, craving itself is included. That craving is again included by the formations aggregate, the dhamma-base, and the dhamma-element. This same method applies to the remaining cases. This is the method in the section 'Included by the Included'.

Asaṅgahitenaasaṅgahitapadatthavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Meaning of the Section 'Unincluded by the Unincluded'

Asaṅgahitenaasaṅgahitapade pana yāni padāni pañcakkhandhagāhakehi dukkhasaccādīhi, viññāṇena saddhiṃ sukhumarūpagāhakehi acetasikādīhi ca padehi vivajjitāni rūpakkhandhādīni, tāneva niddisīyanti. Idaṃ hettha lakkhaṇaṃ – yaṃ paṭhamaṃ uddhaṭena rūpakkhandhādipadena khandhādito asaṅgahitaṃ, yaṃ tehi asaṅgahitaṃ, tasseva puna khandhādīhi asaṅgaho vuccati.

Moreover, in the section 'Unincluded by the Unincluded,' only those terms are indicated, such as the aggregate of form, etc., that are excluded by terms that grasp the five aggregates, such as the truth of suffering, etc., and by terms such as non-cetasikas, etc., that grasp subtle form along with consciousness. This is the characteristic here: that which is unincluded from the aggregates, etc., by the first-stated term, such as 'the aggregate of form'; and that which is unincluded by those unincluded phenomena—it is the non-inclusion of this very thing by the aggregates, etc., that is again stated.

Tatrāyaṃ ekapadayojanā – rūpakkhandhena ye dhammā khandhādīhi tīhipi asaṅgahehi asaṅgahitā, tehi dhammehi ye dhammā khandhādīhi tīhi asaṅgahitā, te dhammā ekena khandhena ekenāyatanena sattahi dhātūhi asaṅgahitā. Rūpakkhandhena hi cattāro khandhā, nibbānañca khandhasaṅgahena asaṅgahitā, āyatanādīhi pana viññāṇameva ṭhapetvā vedanādayo dhammāyatanena rūpakkhandhekadesena saṅgahitāti viññāṇameva tīhipi khandhasaṅgahādīhi rūpakkhandhena asaṅgahitaṃ nāma. Tena puna viññāṇena saddhiṃ sanibbānā cattāro khandhā khandhādīhi asaṅgahitā, te sabbepi puna viññāṇabhūtena ekena khandhena ekenāyatanena sattahi dhātūhi asaṅgahitāti. Ayaṃ asaṅgahitenaasaṅgahitapade nayo.

Herein is the application for a single term: those phenomena not included by the aggregate of form according to the three classifications (aggregates, etc.), and those phenomena not included by those phenomena according to the three classifications—those phenomena are not included by one aggregate, one base, and seven elements. For, with respect to the aggregate of form, the four aggregates and Nibbāna are not included by aggregate-inclusion; but concerning bases, etc., setting aside consciousness, feeling and the others are included by the dhamma-base and by a part of the aggregate of form. Thus, only consciousness is what is called 'not included by the aggregate of form' according to the three classifications of aggregates, etc. Then again, with that consciousness, the four aggregates together with Nibbāna are not included by aggregates, etc., and all of those are again not included by the one aggregate, one base, and seven elements that constitute consciousness. This is the method for the term 'not-included by the not-included'.

Sampayogavippayogapadatthavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Meaning of the Terms 'Association and Dissociation'

Sampayogavippayogapade [M 0.0334] pana yāni padāni nibbānena, rūpena vā missesu sattasu viññāṇadhātūsu ekāyapi avippayutte arūpadhamme pakāsenti, tesaṃ dhammāyatanadukkhasaccādīnaṃ niddeso na sambhavati. Kāhici pana viññāṇadhātūhi vippayuttānaṃ rūpamissārūpadhammānaṃ, kevalānārammaṇānaṃ vā sakalarūpakkhandhānaṃ vā pakāsakānaṃ rūpabhavarūpakkhandhakusalādipadānaṃ sampayogapade eva niddeso na sambhavati, vippayogapade pana sambhavati. Arūpakkhandhānaṃ pana paccekaṃ, dvinnaṃ, tiṇṇaṃ, tadekadesānaṃ vā tadubhayepi sambhavati. “Catūhi sampayogo, catūhi vippayogo, sabhāgo visabhāgo”ti hi vacanato catūhi arūpakkhandheheva sabhāgānaṃ ekasantāne ekakkhaṇeva uppannānaṃ arūpakkhandhānaṃ eva aññamaññaṃ sampayogo labbhati. Rūpadhammānaṃ [V 0.0256] pana rūpena, nibbānena vā, nibbānassa ca rūpena saddhiṃ sampayogo nāma natthi, tathā rūpanibbānānaṃ arūpakkhandhehi. Visabhāgā hi te tesaṃ yathā arūpakkhandhānaṃ rūpanibbānehi, evaṃ bhinnasantānikehi nānakkhaṇikehi arūpadhammehipi saddhiṃ natthiyeva. Tepi hi tesaṃ santānakkhaṇavisabhāgatāya visabhāgā eva. Ayaṃ pana visabhāgatā idha sāmaññato na gahitā tesaṃ avisesena sampayogassāpi sambhavā. Yattha pana visesetvā cakkhuviññāṇataṃsampayuttādayo nikkhittā, tatthāyampi visabhāgatā gahitā. Yattha pana ye aniddhāritavisesanā, tatthāpi sabbathā sampayogalakkhaṇaṃ na sambhavati. So ca tassa ekantena visabhāgoti idha gayhati.

Moreover, in the section on association and dissociation, an exposition of such terms as the dhamma-base and the truth of suffering is not possible for terms that express immaterial dhammas that are not dissociated from even one of the seven consciousness elements mixed with Nibbāna or with form. However, for terms that express immaterial dhammas mixed with form and dissociated from certain consciousness elements, or what is entirely without an object, or the entire aggregate of form—such as 'form-existence,' 'the aggregate of form,' 'wholesome,' etc.—an exposition is not possible in the association section, but it is possible in the dissociation section. For the immaterial aggregates, however, whether taken singly, in pairs, in threes, or partially, both are possible. For it is said: 'Association is with four, dissociation is with four; homogeneous and heterogeneous.' Thus, mutual association is obtained only among the four immaterial aggregates themselves when they are homogeneous and arise in a single continuum at a single moment. For material dhammas, however, there is no such thing as association with form or with Nibbāna, nor of Nibbāna with form; likewise, there is no association of form and Nibbāna with the immaterial aggregates. For these are heterogeneous to them, just as the immaterial aggregates are heterogeneous to form and Nibbāna. Similarly, there is no association at all with immaterial dhammas belonging to different continuums or different moments, for they too are heterogeneous due to their difference in continuum and moment. However, this heterogeneity is not generally taken into account here, since their association is also possible without distinction. But where eye-consciousness and its associated factors, etc., are set down with specification, there this heterogeneity is also taken into account. And where there are those with unspecified distinctions, there too the characteristic of association is in no way possible, and this is understood here as being entirely heterogeneous.

Tatrāyaṃ nayo – rūpakkhandho kenaci sampayuttoti? Natthi. Katihi vippayutto? Catūhi khandhehi ekenāyatanena sattahi [M 0.0335] dhātūhi vippayutto, ekenāyatanena ekāya dhātuyā kehici vippayutto. Esa nayo cakkhāyatanādianārammaṇesupi. Sārammaṇesu pana vedanākkhandho tīhi khandhehi ekenāyatanena sattahi dhātūhi sampayutto, ekenāyatanena ekāya dhātuyā kehici sampayutto. Ekena khandhena dasahi āyatanehi dasahi dhātūhi vippayutto, ekenāyatanena ekāya dhātuyā kehici vippayutto. Esa nayo saññākkhandhādīsupi.

Herein is the method: Is the aggregate of form associated with anything? No. With how many is it dissociated? It is dissociated from four aggregates, one base, and seven elements; from one base and one element, it is dissociated in some respects. This method also applies to the eye-base and other objectless phenomena. But regarding phenomena with an object, the feeling aggregate is associated with three aggregates, one base, and seven elements; with one base and one element, it is associated in some respects. It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements; from one base and one element, it is dissociated in some respects. This method also applies to the perception aggregate and the others.

Tattha ekenāti manāyatanena. Sattahīti viññāṇadhātūhi. Kehicīti dhammāyatanadhammadhātupariyāpannehi vedanāsaññāsaṅkhārehi. Dutiyanaye tīhīti attānaṃ ṭhapetvā sesehi arūpakkhandhehi. Kehici vippayuttoti dhammāyatanadhammadhātūsu saññāsaṅkhārehi. Kehici vippayuttoti rūpanibbānehi. Evaṃ uparipi sabbattha yathānurūpaṃ ñātabbaṃ. Sesaṃ vuttanayameva. Ayaṃ pana viseso “samudayamaggasaccādayo ekāya manoviññāṇadhātuyā sampayuttā, adhimokkho pana manodhātumanoviññāṇadhātūhi dvīhevā”ti. Ayaṃ sampayogavippayogapade nayo.

Herein, 'by one' means by the mind-base. 'By seven' means by the consciousness-elements. 'In some respects' refers to feeling, perception, and formations included in the dhamma-base and dhamma-element. In the second method, 'by three' means by the remaining immaterial aggregates, excluding itself. 'Dissociated in some respects' refers to dissociation from perception and formations in the dhamma-base and dhamma-element. 'Dissociated in some respects' refers to dissociation from form and Nibbāna. Thus above also, it should be understood everywhere accordingly. The rest is just as stated in the method. But this is the distinction: 'The truth of origin, the truth of the path, etc., are associated with the one mind-consciousness-element, while resolution is associated with just two—the mind-element and the mind-consciousness-element.' This is the method in the section on association and dissociation.

Sampayuttenavippayuttapadatthavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Meaning of the Term 'Dissociated from the Associated'

Sampayuttenavippayuttapade pana sampayogārahapadesu yāni padāni dhammadhātuyā sampayutte dhamme, viññāṇañca aññena asammissaṃ dīpenti, tesameva niddeso. Tāni pana catunnaṃ arūpakkhandhapadānaṃ, manāyatanassa, sattannaṃ viññāṇadhātūnaṃ, manopekkhāvasena dvinnaṃ indriyānaṃ, viññāṇaphassavedanānaṃ [V 0.0257] tiṇṇaṃ paṭiccasamuppādapadānaṃ, phassasattakassa, adukkhamasukhasavitakkasavicāraupekkhāsahagatānaṃ vasena tiṇṇaṃ tikapadānaṃ, sattamahantaradukapadādīnañca vasena veditabbāni, na itaresaṃ asambhavā. Teneva aṭṭhakathāyaṃ –

In the term 'dissociated from the associated,' the exposition refers only to those terms, among those suitable for association, that illuminate phenomena associated with the dhamma-element, and consciousness unmixed with anything else. These should be understood as applying to the terms for the four immaterial aggregates, the mind-base, the seven consciousness-elements, the two faculties (mind and equanimity), the three dependent-origination terms (consciousness, contact, and feeling), the group of seven contacts, the three terms from the triplets (namely, that which is accompanied by neither-pain-nor-pleasure, that which is accompanied by applied and sustained thought, and that which is accompanied by equanimity), and the seven major intermediate dyads, etc., because it is not possible for others. Therefore, in the commentary:

“Cattāro [M 0.0336] khandhāyatanañca ekaṃ,

Dve indriyā dhātupadāni satta;

Tayo paṭiccā atha phassasattakaṃ,

Tike tayo satta mahantare ca;

Ekaṃ savitakkaṃ savicāramekaṃ,

Yuttaṃ upekkhāya ca ekamevā”ti. (dhātu. aṭṭha. 306) –

“Four aggregates and one base,

Two faculties, seven element terms;

Three of dependent origination, then the group of seven contacts,

Three in the triplets, and seven among the major intermediates;

One term is 'with applied and sustained thought',

And one is 'associated with equanimity' alone.”

Uddānagāthā vuttā. Idaṃ hettha lakkhaṇaṃ – ye dhammā paṭhamaṃ uddhaṭapadena sampayuttā, tehi ye dhammā vippayuttā, tesaṃ khandhādīhi vippayogo vuccati.

A summary verse has been stated. Herein is the characteristic: The dissociation from aggregates, etc., is stated for those phenomena that are dissociated from the phenomena associated with the term first stated.

Tatrāyaṃ nayo – vedanākkhandhena ye dhammā sampayuttā, tehi dhammehi ye dhammā vippayuttā, te dhammā catūhi khandhehi ekenāyatanena sattahi dhātūhi vippayuttā, ekenāyatanena ekāya dhātuyā kehici vippayuttā. Cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā ye dhammā sampayuttā, tehi dhammehi ye dhammā vippayuttā, te dhammā na kehici khandhāyatanehi vippayuttā, ekāya pana dhātuyā vippayuttāti evaṃ sabbattha yojanā veditabbā.

Herein is the method: Whatever phenomena are associated with the feeling aggregate, the phenomena dissociated from these phenomena are dissociated from four aggregates, one base, and seven elements; and from one base and one element, they are dissociated in some respects. Whatever phenomena are associated with the eye-consciousness element, the phenomena dissociated from these phenomena are not dissociated from any aggregates or bases, but are dissociated from one element. Thus, the application should be understood everywhere.

Tattha te dhammāti rūpanibbānadhammā, te vedanāya sampayuttehi vippayuttā. Ekenāti manāyatanena. Dutiyanaye te dhammāti sappītikā te dhammā. Na kehicīti paṭhamaṃ uddhaṭaṃ cakkhuviññāṇadhātuṃ ṭhapetvā sesā chaviññāṇadhātū, taṃsampayuttā, rūpaṃ, nibbānañca. Tehi sabbesaṃ khandhāyatanānaṃ saṅgahitattā na kehici khandhehi, āyatanehi vā vippayuttā. Na hi sayaṃ attanā vippayujjati, sampayujjati vāti. Ekāyāti cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva. Ayaṃ sampayuttenavippayuttapade nayo.

Herein, 'those phenomena' refers to the dhammas of form and Nibbāna; they are dissociated from what is associated with feeling. 'By one' means by the mind-base. In the second method, 'those phenomena' refers to those phenomena accompanied by joy. 'Not by any' means, excluding the eye-consciousness element first stated, the remaining six consciousness elements, the dhammas associated with them, form, and Nibbāna. Since all aggregates and bases are included by these, they are not dissociated from any aggregates or bases. For a thing does not dissociate from or associate with itself. 'By one' refers to the eye-consciousness element. The rest is easily understood. This is the method for the term 'dissociated from the associated'.

Vippayuttenasampayuttapadatthavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Meaning of the Term 'Associated with the Dissociated'

Vippayuttenasampayuttapade [M 0.0337][V 0.0258] pana vippayuttena sampayutto nāma dhammo natthi, desanāsampadamattāya pana moghampetaṃ padaṃ uddhaṭaṃ, teneva pāḷiyaṃ sabbavāresupi “natthi natthi” icceva vuttaṃ. Rūpakkhandhādianārammaṇadhammehi vippayuttā cattāro khandhā, tesañca aññehi sampayogo natthi. Vedanādīhipi rūpanibbānādīni vippayuttāni, tesañca kenaci sampayogova natthīti. Ayaṃ vippayuttenasampayuttapade nayo.

In the term 'associated with the dissociated,' there is no phenomenon that is associated with what is dissociated; this term is merely stated in vain for the sake of completeness in the teaching. For that reason, in all instances in the Pāli, it is simply stated, 'There is none, there is none.' The four aggregates are dissociated from non-cognizing phenomena such as the form aggregate, etc., and they have no association with other such phenomena. Feeling, etc., are also dissociated from form, Nibbāna, etc., and they have no association with anything whatsoever. This is the method regarding the term 'associated with the dissociated.'

Sampayuttenasampayuttapadatthavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Meaning of the Term 'Associated with the Associated'

Sampayuttenasampayuttapade pana yāni padāni rūpena asammissaṃ arūpakkhandhekadesameva dīpenti, tesameva niddeso, na rūpārūpasammissānaṃ, sabbarūpakkhandhadīpakānaṃ tesaṃ sampayuttatāyogābhāvā. Sabbārūpakkhandhenāpi hi kusalādinā añño sampayutto nāma natthi. Idaṃ hettha lakkhaṇaṃ – ye dhammā paṭhamaṃ uddhaṭā, attanā sampayuttena puna sampayuttā, tesaññeva khandhādīhi sampayogo vuccati.

In the term 'associated with the associated,' the exposition is only of those terms that indicate a portion of the immaterial aggregates, being unmixed with form. It does not apply to those mixed with form and the immaterial, nor to those that indicate the entire form aggregate, for there is no possibility of their being associated. Indeed, there is no other phenomenon associated with the entire immaterial aggregate, such as the wholesome, etc. Herein is the characteristic: The association with aggregates, etc., is stated only for those phenomena that are first stated and are again associated with that which is associated with them.

Tatrāyaṃ nayo – vedanākkhandhena ye dhammā sampayuttā, tehi dhammehi ye dhammā sampayuttā, te dhammā tīhi khandhehi ekenāyatanena sattahi dhātūhi sampayuttā, ekenāyatanena…pe… kehici sampayuttā. Samudayasaccena ye dhammā sampayuttā, tehi dhammehi ye dhammā sampayuttā, te dhammā tīhi khandhehi ekenāyatanena ekāya manoviññāṇadhātuyā sampayuttā, ekena khandhena ekenāyatanena ekāya dhātuyā kehici sampayuttāti. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva. Ayaṃ sampayuttenasampayuttapade nayo.

Herein is the method: Those phenomena associated with the feeling aggregate, and those phenomena associated with those phenomena, are associated with three aggregates, one base, and seven elements; with one base…and so on… associated with some. Those phenomena associated with the truth of origin, and those phenomena associated with those phenomena, are associated with three aggregates, one base, and one mind-consciousness element; with one aggregate, one base, and one element, associated with some. The rest is easily understood. This is the method regarding the term 'associated with the associated.'

Vippayuttenavippayuttapadatthavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Meaning of the Term 'Dissociated from the Dissociated'

Vippayuttenavippayuttapade [M 0.0338] pana sampayogapade vuttapadāneva niddisīyanti. Idaṃ hettha lakkhaṇaṃ – ye dhammā paṭhamaṃ uddhaṭapadena vippayuttehi puna vippayuttā, tesaṃ khandhādīhi vippayogo vuccati.

However, in the term 'dissociated from the dissociated,' only those terms stated in the 'associated' term are indicated. Herein is the characteristic: The dissociation from the aggregates, etc., is spoken of for those phenomena that are again dissociated from those that are dissociated from the initially stated term.

Tatrāyaṃ [V 0.0259] nayo – rūpakkhandhena ye dhammā vippayuttā, tehi dhammehi ye dhammā vippayuttā, te dhammā catūhi khandhehi ekenāyatanena sattahi dhātūhi vippayuttā, ekenāyatanena…pe… kehici vippayuttā. Vedanākkhandhena ye dhammā vippayuttā, tehi dhammehi ye dhammā vippayuttā, te dhammā ekena khandhena dasahāyatanehi dasahi dhātūhi vippayuttā, ekena…pe… kehici vippayuttāti. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva. Ayaṃ vippayuttenavippayuttapade nayo.

Herein is the method: Those phenomena that are dissociated from the form aggregate, and those phenomena that are dissociated from them, are dissociated from the four aggregates, one base, and seven elements; from one base... and so on... dissociated from some. Those phenomena that are dissociated from the feeling aggregate, and those phenomena that are dissociated from them, are dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements; from one... and so on... dissociated from some. The rest is easily understood. This is the method regarding the term 'dissociated from the dissociated.'

Saṅgahitenasampayuttavippayuttapadatthavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Meaning of the Term 'Associated and Dissociated with the Included'

Saṅgahitenasampayuttavippayuttapade pana saṅgahitenasaṅgahitapade niddiṭṭhāni samudayasaccādipadāneva niddisīyanti. Idaṃ hettha lakkhaṇaṃ – ye dhammā paṭhamaṃ uddhaṭapadena khandhādīhi tīhipi saṅgahitā, tesaṃ khandhādīhi sampayogo, vippayogo ca vuccati.

However, in the term 'associated and dissociated with the included,' only those terms such as the truth of origin, etc., that are specified in the term 'included with the included' are indicated. Herein is the characteristic: The association and dissociation with the aggregates, etc., are spoken of for those phenomena which are first included by the stated term with the aggregates, etc., in all three ways.

Tatrāyaṃ nayo – samudayasaccena ye dhammā khandhādīhi tīhipi saṅgahehi saṅgahitā, te dhammā tīhi khandhehi ekenāyatanena sattahi dhātūhi sampayuttā, ekena khandhena ekenāyatanena ekāya dhātuyā kehici sampayuttā. Ekena khandhena dasahāyatanadhātūhi vippayuttā, ekenāyatanena ekāya dhātuyā kehici vippayuttā. Itthindriyena ye dhammā khandhādīhi tīhipi saṅgahitā, te dhammā [M 0.0339] na kehici sampayuttā, catūhi khandhehi ekenāyatanena sattahi dhātūhi vippayuttā, ekena…pe… kehici vippayuttāti.

Herein is the method: Those phenomena which are included by the truth of origin in all three ways with the aggregates, etc., are associated with three aggregates, one base, and seven elements; with one aggregate, one base, and one element, associated with some. They are dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases and elements; from one base and one element, dissociated from some. Those phenomena which are included by the female faculty in all three ways with the aggregates, etc., are not associated with any; they are dissociated from four aggregates, one base, and seven elements; from one... and so on... dissociated from some.

Tattha ekenāti manāyatanena. Ekena khandhenāti saṅkhārakkhandhena. Kehicīti saṅkhārakkhandhe taṇhāya dhammāyatanadhammadhātūsu taṇhāvedanāsaññāhi. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva. Ayaṃ saṅgahitenasampayuttavippayuttapade nayo.

Herein, 'by one' means by the mind base. 'By one aggregate' means by the formations aggregate. 'By some' means: in the formations aggregate, by craving; and in the phenomena base and phenomena element, by craving, feeling, and perception. The rest is easily understood. This is the method regarding the term 'associated and dissociated with the included.'

Sampayuttenasaṅgahitāsaṅgahitapadatthavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Meaning of the Term 'Included and Not Included by the Associated'

Sampayuttenasaṅgahitāsaṅgahitapade pana sampayuttenasampayuttapade niddiṭṭhāni vedanākkhandhādipadāneva niddisīyanti. Idaṃ hettha lakkhaṇaṃ – ye dhammā paṭhamaṃ uddhaṭapadena sampayuttā, tesaṃ khandhādīhi saṅgaho, asaṅgaho ca vuccati.

However, in the term 'included and not included by the associated,' only those terms such as the feeling aggregate, etc., that are specified in the term 'associated with the associated' are indicated. Herein is the characteristic: The inclusion and non-inclusion with the aggregates, etc., are spoken of for those phenomena which are first associated with the stated term.

Tatrāyaṃ [V 0.0260] nayo – vedanākkhandhena ye dhammā sampayuttā, te dhammā tīhi khandhehi dvīhi āyatanehi aṭṭhahi dhātūhi saṅgahitā, sesehi asaṅgahitā. Viññāṇakkhandhena ye dhammā sampayuttā, te dhammā tīhi khandhehi ekenāyatanena ekāya dhātuyā saṅgahitā, sesehi asaṅgahitāti.

Herein is the method: Those phenomena which are associated with the feeling aggregate are included by three aggregates, two bases, and eight elements, and not included by the remainder. Those phenomena which are associated with the consciousness aggregate are included by three aggregates, one base, and one element, and not included by the remainder.

Tattha tīhīti saññākkhandhādīhi tīhi. Tehi vedanāya sampayuttā. Dvīhīti dhammāyatanamanāyatanehi. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva. Ayaṃ sampayuttenasaṅgahitāsaṅgahitapade nayo.

Herein, 'by three' means by the three, namely, the aggregate of perception and so forth. By these, they are associated with feeling. 'By two' means by the phenomena base and the mind base. The rest is easily understood. This is the method regarding the term 'included and not included by the associated.'

Asaṅgahitenasampayuttavippayuttapadatthavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Meaning of the Term 'Associated and Dissociated with the Not Included'

Asaṅgahitenasampayuttavippayuttapade pana yāni padāni sukhumarūpaṃ aviññāṇaṃ, arūpaṃ saviññāṇaṃ vā, kevalaṃ arūpaṃ vā thūlarūpassapi kevalaṃ vā, sukhumarūpaṃ dīpenti, tesameva niddeso[M 0.0340]. Idaṃ hettha lakkhaṇaṃ – ye dhammā paṭhamaṃ uddhaṭadhammehi khandhādīhi tīhipi asaṅgahitā, tesaṃ khandhādīhi sampayogo, vippayogo ca vuccati.

However, in the term 'associated and dissociated with the not included,' the exposition is only of those terms which denote subtle form, that which is non-conscious; or formless with consciousness; or purely formless; or even purely gross form; or subtle form. Herein is the characteristic: The association and dissociation with the aggregates, etc., are spoken of for those phenomena which are first not included by the stated phenomena with the aggregates, etc., in all three ways.

Tatrāyaṃ nayo – rūpakkhandhena ye dhammā khandhādīhi asaṅgahitā, te dhammā tīhi khandhehi sampayuttā, ekenāyatanena ekāya dhātuyā kehici sampayuttā, ekena khandhena dasahi āyatanadhātūhi vippayuttā, ekenāyatanena ekāya dhātuyā kehici vippayuttā. Evaṃ dhammāyatanaitthindriyādīsupi yojanā.

Herein is the method: Those phenomena which are not included by the form aggregate with the aggregates, etc., are associated with three aggregates; with one base and one element, associated with some. They are dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases and elements; from one base and one element, dissociated from some. Similarly, this application extends to the phenomena base, the female faculty, and so forth.

Arūpabhavena ye dhammā khandhādīhi asaṅgahitā, te sampayuttāti natthi. Te catūhi khandhehi ekenāyatanena sattahi dhātūhi vippayuttā, ekenāyatanena ekāya dhātuyā kehici vippayuttā. Evaṃ iddhipādakusalādipadesupi yojanā.

Those phenomena which are not included by the formless state with the aggregates, etc., have no association. They are dissociated from four aggregates, one base, and seven elements; from one base and one element, dissociated from some. Similarly, this application extends to terms such as the bases of psychic power, the wholesome, and so forth.

Tattha rūpakkhandhena viññāṇasseva tīhipi asaṅgahitattā tassa tīhi vedanādīhi sampayogo, itarehi ca vippayogo ñātabbo. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva. Ayaṃ asaṅgahitenasampayuttavippayuttapade nayo.

Herein, since consciousness alone is not included by the form aggregate in any of the three ways, its association with the three—feeling and so forth—and its dissociation from the others should be understood. The rest is easily understood. This is the method regarding the term 'associated and dissociated with the not included.'

Vippayuttenasaṅgahitāsaṅgahitapadatthavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Meaning of the Term 'Included and Not Included by the Dissociated'

Vippayuttenasaṅgahitāsaṅgahitapade [V 0.0261] pana yāni padāni kevalānaṃ sārammaṇānaṃ, anārammaṇānaṃ vā dhammānaṃ pakāsakāni ca sabhāvajātibhūmikālasantānavasena bhinnatāya kehici arūpakkhandhehi vippayuttānaṃ anārammaṇadhammamissārūpakkhandhānaṃ pakāsakāni dukkhasaccaabyākataparittaatītaajjhattādipadāni, tesameva niddeso itaresaṃ dhammāyatanajīvitindriyanāmarūpasaḷāyatanajātijarāmaraṇaajjhattabahiddhāanidassanaappaṭighanahetuādīnaṃ tesaṃ kenaci vippayogāsambhavā. Idaṃ hettha lakkhaṇaṃ – ye dhammā paṭhamaṃ uddhaṭapadena [M 0.0341] vippayuttā, tesaṃ khandhādīhi saṅgaho, asaṅgaho ca vuccati.

Now, in the section on what is included and not included by the dissociated, the exposition concerns only certain terms. These are: terms that indicate phenomena that are exclusively with an object or without an object; terms that indicate formless aggregates mixed with phenomena without an object, which are dissociated from certain other formless aggregates because they are distinct in terms of intrinsic nature, kind, plane, time, and continuity; and terms such as the truth of suffering, the indeterminate, the limited, the past, and the internal. The exposition is limited to these because for the other phenomena—such as the mental-object base, the life faculty, name-and-form, the six sense bases, birth, aging, death, internal and external, non-manifestative and non-resistant, not-a-cause, etc.—dissociation from them by anything is impossible. This is the characteristic here: for phenomena that are dissociated from a term first cited, it is stated whether they are included or not included by the aggregates, etc.

Tatrāyaṃ nayo – rūpakkhandhena ye dhammā vippayuttā, te dhammā catūhi khandhehi dvīhāyatanehi aṭṭhahi dhātūhi saṅgahitā, ekena khandhena dasahi āyatanadhātūhi asaṅgahitā. Dukkhasaccena ye dhammā vippayuttā, te dhammā catūhi khandhehi dvīhāyatanehi dvīhi dhātūhi saṅgahitā. Tattha dukkhasaccena vippayuttā nāma lokuttaracittacetasikāni, te ca dhammā vedanākkhandhādicatukkhandhehi manoviññāṇadhammadhātuvasena dvīhi dhātūhi saṅgahitāti. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva.
