There is realization of the Dhamma in the womb, there is attainment of arahantship in the womb; there is realization of the Dhamma in a dream, and attainment of arahantship in a dream—thus are these three discourses. All dream consciousness is indeterminate—thus is the discourse. Due to the momentary nature of consciousnesses, there is no condition of repetition—thus is the discourse. All conditioned things last for a single moment of consciousness—thus is the discourse on momentariness.

Itthiyā saddhiṃ ekato sampattiṃ anubhavissāmāti pūjādiṃ katvā ekādhippāyappattassa bhikkhuno methuno dhammo paṭisevitabboti pavattā ekādhippāyakathā. Pāpabhikkhūsu methunaṃ paṭisevantesu arahantānaṃ vaṇṇena amanussā methunaṃ paṭisevantīti pavattā arahantavaṇṇakathā. Keci sattā attano issariyena kāmakārikāvasena vinipātaṃ gacchanti, na kammavasenāti pavattā issariyakāmakārikākathā. Na rāgo rāgapatirūpakotiādi patirūpakathā. Khandhāyatanādayo aparinipphannāti pavattā aparinipphannakathāti sādhikadvisatakathā. Pāḷiyaṃ aṭṭhamukhavādayuttivaseneva sammitiyādīnaṃ bhinnaladdhikānaṃ laddhibhedavasena nānāpakārato vibhattā, tā pana sabbakathā puggalakathāva. Tā taṃtaṃladdhibhedavasena saṅkhepatopi vuccamānā atibhāriyaṃ ganthaṃ karonti, tasmā na vitthāritā. Taṃ pana nayaṃ icchantehi pāḷiaṭṭhakathāsu (kathā. 1 ādayo; kathā. aṭṭha. nidānakathā) eva vitthārato gahetabboti ayamettha pāḷinayena saddhiṃ atthavinicchayo.

A monk who, having made offerings and so on with the thought, 'I will experience companionship together with a woman,' has attained a singular purpose, should indulge in sexual intercourse—thus is the discourse on singular purpose. When wicked monks indulge in sexual intercourse, non-human beings in the guise of arahants also indulge in sexual intercourse—thus is the discourse on the guise of arahants. Some beings, by their own power and acting as they please, fall into states of misery, not by the force of kamma—thus is the discourse on power and acting as one pleases. Lust is not a mere semblance of lust, and so on—thus is the discourse on semblances. The aggregates, sense-bases, and so on are not fully accomplished—thus is the discourse on the incomplete. Thus, there are more than two hundred discourses. In the Pāli, just as with the eight kinds of argument, the different views of the Sammitiyas and others are analyzed in various ways according to their differing tenets. Yet all these discourses are essentially about persons. Even when briefly explained according to their respective tenets, these discourses would make the text excessively heavy. Therefore, they are not elaborated upon here. For those who wish to study this method in detail, it should be taken extensively from the Pāli commentaries (such as Kathāvatthu 1 and so on; the Kathāvatthu Commentary, the Nidāna-kathā). This is the analysis of meaning here, along with the Pāli method.

Mohavicchedaniyā abhidhammamātikatthavaṇṇanāya

The Dispelling of Delusion: An Explanation of the Meaning of the Abhidhamma Matrix.

Kathāvatthumātikatthavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Kathāvatthu matrix is completed.

6. Yamakamātikā

6. The Matrix of the Yamaka

Mūlayamakamātikatthavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Meaning of the Matrix of the Root Yamaka

Idāni [M 0.0384][V 0.0294] yamakamātikāya saṃvaṇṇanānayo hoti. Sā panesā mūlayamakamātikā khandhaāyatanadhātusaccasaṅkhāraanusayacittadhammaindriyayamakamātikāti dasavidhā hoti. Kenaṭṭhena cettha yamakanti? Yugaḷaṭṭhena. Yugaḷaṃ hi “yamakapāṭihāriyaṃ”, “yamakasālā”tiādīsu “yamaka”nti vuccati, iti yugaḷasaṅkhātānaṃ yamakānaṃ vasena desitattā imesu dasasu ekekampi, etesaṃ vibhajanattā niddesopi, sabbesaṃ samūhattā pakaraṇampi yamakaṃ nāma. Idha panetā niddesayamakaṃ upādāya “yamakamātikā”tveva vuttā, tāsaṃ pana dasannaṃ yamakamātikānaṃ mūlayamakamātikā ādi. Tatthāpi “ye keci kusalā dhammā, sabbe te kusalamūlā. Ye vā pana kusalamūlā, sabbe te dhammā kusalā”ti idaṃ yamakaṃ ādi. Tassa kusalamūlasaṅkhātānaṃ dvinnaṃ atthānaṃ vasena atthayamakanti vā, tesaññeva atthānaṃ anulomato paṭilomato pavattapāḷidhammavasena dhammayamakanti vā, anulomapaṭilomato pavattapucchāvasena pucchāyamakanti vā tidhā yamakabhāvo veditabbo. Sesesupi eseva nayo.

Now, the method of explanation for the Yamaka matrix is as follows. This root Yamaka matrix is tenfold: the pairs concerning aggregates, sense bases, elements, truths, formations, latent tendencies, mind, phenomena, and faculties. What is the meaning of "Yamaka" here? It means "pair." For a pair is called "Yamaka" in such instances as "the twin miracle" (yamakapāṭihāriya) or "the twin sal tree" (yamakasālā), etc. Thus, because these teachings are taught by way of pairs (yamaka) that are reckoned as dualities (yugaḷa), each of these ten sections is called a Yamaka. Also, because of their distribution, the exposition (niddesa) is called a Yamaka, and because it is a collection of all of them, the treatise (pakaraṇa) is also called a Yamaka. Here, however, taking this Yamaka of exposition as the basis, it is simply called the "Yamaka matrix." Among these ten Yamaka matrices, the root Yamaka matrix comes first. In this regard, the first pair is: "Whatever wholesome phenomena there are, all of them are wholesome roots. And whatever are wholesome roots, all those phenomena are wholesome." This initial Yamaka is to be understood as threefold: (1) as the Yamaka of meaning (atthayamaka), based on the two meanings designated as "wholesome roots"; (2) as the Yamaka of Dhamma (dhammayamaka), based on the Pāli text which proceeds forward and in reverse order regarding those same meanings; and (3) as the Yamaka of questions (pucchāyamaka), based on the questions that proceed forward and in reverse order. The same method applies to the remaining pairs.

Idāni imesaṃ yamakānaṃ vasena desitāya imissā mūlayamakamātikāya tāva nayayamakapucchāatthavārappabhedavasena pāḷivavatthānaṃ evaṃ veditabbaṃ – kusalattikamātikāya hi “kusalā dhammā”ti idaṃ ādipadaṃ nissāya mūlanayo mūlamūlanayo mūlakanayo mūlamūlakanayoti ime cattāro nayā honti. Tesu ekekasmiṃ naye mūlayamakaṃ ekamūlayamakaṃ aññamaññamūlayamakanti tīṇi tīṇi yamakānīti [M 0.0385] dvādasa yamakāni. Ekekasmiṃ yamake anulomapaṭilomavasena [V 0.0295] dve dve pucchāti catuvīsati pucchā, ekekapucchāya sanniṭṭhānasaṃsayavasena dve dve atthāti aṭṭhacattālīsa atthā.

Now, regarding these pairs (yamaka) explained through this root-pair matrix (mūlayamakamātikā), the arrangement of the Pāli text according to the divisions of method, pair, question, meaning, and section should be understood as follows:—Based on the initial term "wholesome phenomena" (kusalā dhammā) of the wholesome triad matrix (kusalattikamātikā), there are four methods: the root method (mūlanayo), the root-root method (mūlamūlanayo), the rooted method (mūlakanayo), and the root-rooted method (mūlamūlakanayo). In each of these methods, there are three pairs: the root pair (mūlayamaka), the single-root pair (ekamūlayamaka), and the reciprocal-root pair (aññamaññamūlayamaka), thus twelve pairs in total. For each pair, there are two questions (pucchā) in forward and reverse order (anulomapaṭilomavasena), making twenty-four questions. For each question, there are two meanings (atthā) based on affirmation and doubt (sanniṭṭhānasaṃsayavasena), totaling forty-eight meanings.

Tattha ye keci kusalāti kusalesu “kusalā nu kho, na kusalā nu kho”ti sandehābhāvato imasmiṃ pade sanniṭṭhānattho veditabbo. Sabbe te kusalamūlāti “sabbe te kusalā dhammā kusalamūlā nu kho, na nu kho”ti evaṃ vimativasena pucchitattā imasmiṃ pade saṃsayattho veditabbo. So ca kho veneyyānaṃ saṃsayaṭṭhāne saṃsayaṃ dīpetvā taṃvinodanatthaṃ bhagavatā vutto, tathāgatassa pana saṃsayaṭṭhānaṃ nāma natthi. Ito paresupi pucchāpadesu eseva nayo. Yathā ca kusalapadaṃ nissāya ime catunayādayo honti, akusalapadaṃ nissāyapi tatheva, abyākatapadaṃ nissāyapi tatheva, kusalādīni tīṇipi padāni ekato katvā niddiṭṭhaṃ nāmapadaṃ nissāya tathevāti kusalattikamātikāya catūsu padesu sabbepi soḷasa nayā, aṭṭhacattālīsa yamakāni, channavuti pucchā, dvānavutisataṃ atthā ca uddesavasena vuttāti veditabbā. Ettāvatā mūlavāro hetuvāro nidānavāro sambhavavāro pabhavavāro samuṭṭhānavāro āhāravāro ārammaṇavāro paccayavāro samudayavāroti sabbepi dasa vārā honti. Tattha mūlavāre āgataparicchedeneva avasesesupi nayādayo veditabbā. Pāḷi panettha atisaṃkhittā. Iti sabbesupi dasasu vāresu saṭṭhisataṃ nayā, asītiadhikāni cattāri yamakasatāni, saṭṭhiadhikāni nava pucchāsatāni, vīsādhikāni ekūnavīsati atthasatāni ca uddiṭṭhānīti veditabbāni.

Herein, regarding 'whatever is wholesome'—since there is no doubt concerning wholesome states, such as "are they indeed wholesome or not?"—the meaning in this phrase should be understood as one of affirmation. Regarding 'all of them are wholesome roots'—since the question is posed by way of uncertainty, as in "are all those wholesome phenomena indeed wholesome roots or not?"—the meaning in this phrase should be understood as one of doubt. Yet, the Blessed One spoke this to dispel the doubt of those capable of being taught, having pointed out the basis of their doubt. For the Tathāgata, however, there is no ground for doubt. The same method applies to the other phrases of the questions. Just as these four methods and so on are based on the term "wholesome," the same applies when based on the term "unwholesome," and likewise when based on the term "indeterminate." When the three terms—wholesome, and so on—are combined into a single nominal phrase, the same method applies as well. Thus, in the four phrases of the wholesome triad matrix, all sixteen methods, forty-eight pairs, ninety-six questions, and one hundred and ninety-two meanings are stated by way of summary. By this much, the root section, the cause section, the source section, the origination section, the arising section, the uprising section, the nutriment section, the object section, the condition section, and the origin section—all ten sections are thus comprised. Here, in the root section, the remaining methods and so on should be understood by the same divisions already stated. The Pāli here is extremely condensed. Thus, it should be understood that in all ten sections, one hundred and sixty methods, four hundred and eighty pairs, nine hundred and sixty questions, and one thousand nine hundred and twenty meanings have been outlined.

Evamettha [M 0.0386] nayayamakapucchā atthavārappabhedavasena pāḷivavatthānaṃ viditvā idāni tassā anuttānapadatthānusāreneva vibhaṅganayasahito saṅkhepatthavaṇṇanānayo evaṃ veditabbo – tattha ye kecīti anavasesavacanaṃ. Kusalā dhammāti anavajjasukhavipākā nissattasabhāvā. Sabbe te kusalamūlāti kiṃ te sabbeyeva kusalamūlā hontīti pucchā. Imāni pana vissajjanamātikāya natthi. Yamakamātikāya hi sabbattha pucchāpadāneva uddhaṭāni, na vissajjanānīti. Vissajjanāni pana niddeseyeva vuttāni, tasmā sabbattha niddesanayeneva vissajjanamukhaṃ dassayissāma. Imissāva “ye keci kusalā dhammā, sabbe te kusalamūlā”ti pucchāya vibhaṅganayena idaṃ vissajjanamukhaṃ. “Tīṇeva kusalamūlāni, avasesā kusalā dhammā na kusalamūlā”ti tassā cāyamattho – na te sabbe kusalā dhammā kusalamūlāni honti, alobhādīni pana tīṇeva kusalamūlānīti. Ye vā pana kusalamūlā tayo alobhādayo kusalānaṃ [V 0.0296] mūlāti vuttā, sabbe te kusalā dhammāti kiṃ te sabbe tayopi dhammā kusalāti pucchā. Tassā niddese “āmantā”ti vissajjanaṃ. Tassa tesaṃ tiṇṇaṃ mūlānaṃ kusalabhāvampi sampaṭicchāmīti attho. Ayaṃ tāva mūlanaye mūlayamakanayo.

Thus, having understood the arrangement of the Pāli text according to its divisions of method, pair, question, meaning, and section, now the concise explanation of the meaning, together with the analytical method and following the sense of terms that are not obvious, should be understood as follows:—Therein, 'ye keci' (whatever) is an all-inclusive expression. 'Kusalā dhammā' (wholesome phenomena) refers to faultless states with pleasant results, which are phenomena devoid of a self. 'Sabbe te kusalamūlā' (all of them are wholesome roots) is the question: "Are all of them indeed wholesome roots?" These, however, are not found in the matrix of answers. For in the Yamaka matrix, only the phrases of the questions are extracted everywhere, not the answers. The answers, however, are stated in the exposition itself. Therefore, we will show the approach to the answer everywhere through the method of the exposition. For this very question—"Whatever wholesome phenomena there are, all of them are wholesome roots"—this is the approach to the answer by the analytical method: "There are only three wholesome roots; the remaining wholesome phenomena are not wholesome roots." And the meaning of this is: "Not all those wholesome phenomena are wholesome roots, but only the three, non-greed and so on." And as for 'whatever are wholesome roots'—the three, non-greed and so on, are said to be the roots of the wholesome. 'Sabbe te kusalā dhammā' (all those phenomena are wholesome) is the question: "Are all those three phenomena wholesome?" The answer to this in the exposition is "Āmantā" (Yes). The meaning of this is: "We accept that these three roots are also wholesome." This, for now, is the root-pair method in the root method.

Ekamūlayamake pana sabbe te kusalamūlena ekamūlāti gaṇanaṭṭhena ekamūlakaṃ aggahetvā samānatthena gahetabbā, ayaṃ hettha attho – “sabbe te kusalamūlena ekaṃ samānaṃ mūlaṃ etesanti ekamūlā”ti. Yaṃ phassassa mūlaṃ, kiṃ tadeva vedanādīnanti ayaṃ pucchā. Atha nesaṃ tathābhāvaṃ sampaṭicchanavasena “āmantā”ti vibhaṅge vissajjanaṃ. Ye vā pana kusalamūlena ekamūlā, sabbe te dhammā kusalāti pucchā. Tassā [M 0.0387] pana kusalacittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kusalamūlena ekamūlameva, na kusalaṃ, phassādidhammajātaṃ pana kusalamūlena ekamūlañceva kusalañcāti idaṃ vissajjanaṃ. Yatheva hi phassādīnaṃ alobhādayo suppatiṭṭhitabhāvasādhanena hetupaccayattā mūlaṃ, tathā taṃsamuṭṭhānarūpassāpīti taṃrūpampi arūpadhammehi saddhiṃ samānamūlanti vuccati, na pana kusalaṃ anavajjasukhavipākattābhāvā. Ekamūlayamakanayo.

In the single-root pair, however, the term 'single-rooted' (ekamūla) in 'all those are single-rooted by the wholesome root' should not be taken in the sense of counting as one root, but should be taken in the sense of similarity. This is the meaning here: 'All those have one similar root, namely, the wholesome root; hence they are single-rooted.' The question is: Is the root of contact the very same as that of feeling, and so on? Then, assenting to their being so, the reply in the analysis is “Yes.” Furthermore, the question is: Are all those phenomena that are single-rooted by the wholesome root also wholesome? The answer to this is: Material form arisen from wholesome consciousness is single-rooted by the wholesome root, but it is not wholesome; however, the collection of phenomena such as contact, and so on, are both single-rooted by the wholesome root and wholesome. For just as non-greed, and so on, are a root for contact, and so on, because they are the condition as root that establishes their well-founded nature, so too are they for the material form that arises from them. Thus, that material form is also said to have the same root as the immaterial phenomena, but it is not wholesome because it lacks the nature of having a faultless and pleasant result. This is the method of the single-root pair.

Aññamaññamūlayamake pana “ye keci kusalā”ti apucchitvā “ye keci kusalamūlena ekamūlā”ti pucchā katā. Kasmā? Imināpi byañjanena tassevatthassa sambhavadassanatthaṃ, kusalasamuṭṭhānarūpassāpi sampiṇḍanatthañca. Aññamaññamūlāti sabbeva te kiṃ aññamaññassa hetupaccayaṭṭhena mūlāni hontīti pucchā. Tassā yāni dve tīṇi mūlāni ekato uppajjanti, tāneva ekamūlāni ceva aññamaññamūlāni ca, avasesā kusalamūlasahajātā rūpārūpadhammā kusalamūlena ekamūlāva, na ca aññamaññamūlāti vissajjanaṃ. Tasseva paṭilomanaye sabbe te aññamaññamūlā alobhādayo kusalāti pucchā. Āmantāti vissajjanaṃ. Mūlanayo.

In the mutual-root pair, the question was not asked as, “Whatever states are wholesome,” but rather as, “Whatever states are single-rooted by a wholesome root.” Why? This phrasing is to show the possibility of that meaning and also for the inclusion of the forms arising from wholesome states. As to ‘mutual roots,’ the question is: are all those states roots for each other in the sense of the root-condition? The answer is: those two or three roots that arise together are both single-rooted and mutually rooted. The remaining material and immaterial phenomena that are co-arisen with wholesome roots are only single-rooted by the wholesome root, but not mutually rooted. In the reverse method, the question is: Are all those that are mutually rooted, namely non-greed and so on, wholesome? The answer is: “Yes.” This is the method of roots.

Yathā ca mūlanaye mūlayamakaekamūlayamakaaññamaññamūlayamakavasena chabbidhā pucchāvissajjananayā vuttā, evaṃ mūlamūlanayādīsupi veditabbā. Ayaṃ panettha viseso – sabbe te kusalamūlamūlāti sabbe te kusalamūlasaṅkhātā mūlā, kusalamūlamūlātveva attho. Ekamūlamūlāti samānaṭṭhena ekameva mūlamūlaṃ etesanti ekamūlamūlā, samānamūlamūlātveva attho. Aññamaññamūlamūlāti aññamaññassa mūlaṃ aññamaññamūlaṃ, taṃ hetupaccayaṭṭhena mūlaṃ etesanti aññamaññamūlamūlā, aññamaññamūlamūlātveva attho. Sesaṃ tādisamevāti. Mūlamūlanayo.

Just as in the root method, the sixfold method of question and answer was stated by way of the root-pair, the single-root-pair, and the mutual-root-pair, so too should it be understood in the root-of-a-root method and others. Herein, this is the distinction: ‘All those are rooted-in-a-wholesome-root’ means all those roots are designated as wholesome roots; the meaning is simply that they are rooted-in-a-wholesome-root. ‘Rooted-in-a-single-root’ means they have one and the same root-of-a-root in a common sense; the meaning is simply that they are rooted-in-a-common-root. ‘Rooted-in-a-mutual-root’ means a mutual root is a root for one another, and they have that as their root in the sense of the root-condition; the meaning is simply that they are rooted-in-a-mutual-root. The rest is just the same. This is the root-of-a-root method.

Mūlakanaye [M 0.0388][V 0.0297] pana sabbe te kusalamūlakāti sabbe te kusalā hetupaccayaṭṭhena kusalabhūtaṃ mūlaṃ etesanti kusalamūlakāti pucchā. Āmantāti vissajjanaṃ. “Ye vā pana kusalamūlakā, sabbe te dhammā kusalā”ti pucchā. Yaṃ rūpaṃ, taṃ ṭhapetvā sesaṃ kusalanti vissajjanaṃ, sesaṃ tādisamevāti. Mūlakanayo.

In the Mūlaka method, however, the question is: ‘Are all those states wholesome-rooted?’—meaning, do they have a root that is wholesome in the sense of the root-condition, and are thus wholesome-rooted? The answer is: ‘Yes.’ The question is: ‘Or are all those phenomena that are wholesome-rooted wholesome?’ The answer is: ‘Setting aside material form, the remainder is wholesome.’ The rest is just the same. Such is the Mūlaka method.

Mūlamūlakanaye pana kusalamūlamūlakāti kusalamūlasaṅkhātaṃ mūlaṃ etesanti kusalamūlamūlakā. Sesaṃ tādisamevāti.

In the Mūlamūlaka method, however, ‘rooted-in-a-wholesome-root’ means: they have as their root a root designated as a wholesome root, and thus they are rooted-in-a-wholesome-root. The rest is just the same.

Ayaṃ tāva kusalapadesu pucchāvissajjananayo. Akusalapadādīsupi eseva nayo. Ayaṃ pana viseso – akusalapadamūlesu ekamūlayamake “ye keci akusalā dhammā, sabbe te akusalamūlena ekamūlā”ti paṭhamapucchāya “ahetukaṃ akusalaṃ akusalamūlena ekamūla”nti niddese vissajjanaṃ kataṃ. Tattha ahetukaṃ akusalanti dvīsu mohamūlacittesu mohaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, abyākatapadamūlesu ekamūlayamake “ye keci abyākatā dhammā, sabbe te abyākatamūlena ekamūlā”ti pucchāya “ahetukaṃ abyākataṃ ṭhapetvā sesā abyākatamūlena ekamūlakā”ti vissajjanaṃ. Tattha ahetukaṃ abyākatanti aṭṭhārasāhetukacittuppādā, rūpaṃ, nibbānañca. Ettha ca kiñcāpi sahetukaabyākatacittasamuṭṭhānarūpampi abyākatamūlena ekamūlameva, taṃ pana abbohārikaṃ katvā niddese ekato labbhamānakavasenapetaṃ vissajjanaṃ katanti veditabbaṃ.

This, then, is the method of question and answer regarding wholesome terms. The same method applies to unwholesome terms and so forth. But there is this distinction: In the single-root dyad concerning unwholesome roots, to the first question, ‘Whatever unwholesome phenomena there are, are they all single-rooted with an unwholesome root?’ the answer given in the exposition is: ‘Rootless unwholesome is single-rooted with an unwholesome root.’ Here, ‘rootless unwholesome’ is stated with reference to delusion in the two consciousnesses rooted in delusion. In the single-root dyad concerning indeterminate roots, to the question, ‘Whatever indeterminate phenomena there are, are they all single-rooted with an indeterminate root?’ the answer is: ‘Setting aside rootless indeterminate, the rest are single-rooted with an indeterminate root.’ Here, ‘rootless indeterminate’ refers to the eighteen rootless consciousness-arisings, material form, and Nibbāna. And here, although material form produced by indeterminate consciousness with roots is also single-rooted with an indeterminate root, this is considered non-conventional; thus, it should be understood that the answer is given by way of what can be obtained together in the exposition.

Nāmapadamūlesu ca “ye keci nāmā dhammā, sabbe te nāmamūlā”ti pucchāya “naveva nāmamūlāni, avasesā nāmā dhammā, na nāmamūlā”ti vissajjanaṃ. Ekamūlanaye panettha “ye keci nāmā dhammā, sabbe te nāmamūlena ekamūlā”ti pucchā. “Ahetukaṃ nāmaṃ ṭhapetvā sesaṃ nāmamūlena ekamūla”nti [M 0.0389] vissajjanaṃ. Tattha ahetukacittuppādavicikicchuddhaccasampayuttamohanibbānavasena ahetukaṃ nāmaṃ veditabbaṃ. Sesaṃ sabbattha kusalapade vuttānusārena suviññeyyamevāti. Ayaṃ mūlavāre nayo.

And in the roots of the name section, to the question, ‘Whatever phenomena are name, are they all name-roots?’ the answer is: ‘There are only nine name-roots; the remaining name-phenomena are not name-roots.’ Here, in the single-root method, the question is: ‘Whatever phenomena are name, are they all single-rooted with a name-root?’ The answer is: ‘Setting aside rootless name, the rest are single-rooted with a name-root.’ Here, rootless name should be understood by way of the arisings of rootless consciousness, delusion associated with doubt and restlessness, and Nibbāna. The rest is easily understood everywhere according to what was stated in the wholesome section. Such is the method in the root chapter.

Ito paresu hetuvārādīsu navasu vāresu mūlavārasadisova sabbattha saṃvaṇṇanānayo. Hetuādipadamattameva hettha viseso, tāni ca mūla-saddapariyāyato alobhādihetukāneva. Alobhādayo hi sahajātadhammasaṅkhātassa attano phalassa patiṭṭhānaṭṭhena mūlaṃ. Tassa nipphādanatthaṃ hinoti [V 0.0298] pavattatīti hetu, “handa naṃ gaṇhathā”ti dassentaṃ viya attano phalaṃ nidetīti nidānaṃ. Etasmā phalaṃ sambhavatīti sambhavo. Pabhavatīti pabhavo. Samuṭṭhāti taṃ ettha, etenāti vā samuṭṭhānaṃ. Taṃ āharatīti āhāro. Apaṭikkhipitabbaṭṭhena tena ālambīyatīti ālambaṇaṃ. Etaṃ paṭicca taṃ etīti paccayo. Etasmā taṃ samudetīti samudayo. Sabbaṃ kāraṇapariyāyena vuttā “mūlaṃ hetu nidānañcā”ti gāthā dasannampi vārānaṃ uddānagāthā nāma. Ayaṃ mūlayamakamātikatthavaṇṇanānayo.

In the nine chapters that follow this, beginning with the cause chapter, the method of explanation is everywhere similar to that of the root chapter. Here, the only distinction is the terms ‘cause’ and so forth, and these are merely synonyms for the term ‘root,’ referring to non-greed and so on. For non-greed and so on are called ‘roots’ (mūla) because they serve as the foundation for their own fruit, which is reckoned as co-nascent phenomena. It is called ‘cause’ (hetu) because it impels or proceeds to produce its fruit. It is called ‘source’ (nidāna) because it points out its own fruit, as if saying, ‘Come, take this!’ It is called ‘arising’ (sambhava) because the fruit arises from it. It is called ‘origin’ (pabhava) because it proceeds from it. It is called ‘origination’ (samuṭṭhāna) because that arises here or by this. It is called ‘nutriment’ (āhāra) because it brings that forth. It is called ‘support’ (ālambana) because it is relied upon, being that which cannot be rejected. It is called ‘condition’ (paccaya) because that comes to be in dependence on this. It is called ‘origination’ (samudaya) because that arises from this. All these are stated by way of synonyms for cause. The verse, “Root, cause, source, and…” is the summary verse for all ten chapters. This is the method of explaining the meaning of the root-dyad matrix.

Khandhayamakamātikatthavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Meaning of the Aggregate-Dyad Matrix

Khandhayamakapāḷiyā pana pāḷivavatthānaṃ tāva evaṃ veditabbaṃ – “pañcakkhandhā”ti padaṃ ādiṃ katvā yāva “na khandhā na saṅkhārā”ti padaṃ, tāva pavattā ayaṃ khandhayamakamātikā nāma. Sā paṇṇattivārassa “uddesavāro”tipi “pucchāvāro”tipi vuccati. So ca padasodhanavāro padasodhanamūlacakkavāro suddhakhandhavāro suddhakhandhamūlacakkavāroti catūhi nayavārehi paṭimaṇḍito. Tattha “rūpaṃ rūpakkhandho, rūpakkhandho rūpa”ntiādinā nayena padameva sodhetvā gato padasodhanavāro nāma. So anulomapaṭilomavasena duvidho hoti[M 0.0390]. Tassa anulomavāre “rūpaṃ rūpakkhandho, rūpakkhandho rūpa”ntiādīni pañca yamakāni. Paṭilomavārepi “na rūpaṃ na rūpakkhandho, na rūpakkhandho na rūpa”ntiādinā pañca vārā.

Regarding the Pāli of the Aggregate-Dyad, the analysis of the text should first be understood thus: This, which extends from the phrase ‘the five aggregates’ up to the phrase ‘not aggregates, not formations,’ is called the Aggregate-Dyad matrix. In the chapter on designations, it is called the ‘exposition chapter’ or the ‘question chapter.’ And it is adorned with four methodical chapters: the word-purification chapter, the word-purification root-cycle chapter, the pure-aggregates chapter, and the pure-aggregates root-cycle chapter. Among these, the word-purification chapter is so called because it proceeds by purifying only the words, by the method beginning: ‘Material form is the material form aggregate, the material form aggregate is material form,’ and so on. It is twofold by way of direct order and reverse order. In its direct-order chapter, there are five dyads beginning: ‘Material form is the material form aggregate, the material form aggregate is material form,’ and so on. And in the reverse-order chapter, there are five chapters beginning: ‘Not material form, not the material form aggregate; not the material form aggregate, not material form,’ and so on.

Tato paraṃ tesaññeva padasodhanavāre sodhitānaṃ khandhānaṃ “rūpaṃ rūpakkhandho, khandhā vedanākkhandho”tiādinā nayena ekekakhandhamūlakāni cattāri cattāri cakkāni bandhitvā gato padasodhanamūlakānaṃ cakkānaṃ atthitāya padasodhanamūlacakkavāro nāma. Sopi anulomapaṭilomavasena duvidho hoti. Tassa anulomavāre “rūpaṃ rūpakkhandho, khandhā vedanākkhandho”tiādīni ekekakhandhamūlakāni cattāri cattāri katvā vīsati yamakāni. Paṭilomavārepi “na rūpaṃ na rūpakkhandho, na khandhā na vedanākkhandho”tiādīni vīsatimeva.

Then, regarding those very aggregates purified in the word-purification chapter, it proceeds by constructing four wheels each based on a single aggregate, by the method beginning: ‘Material form is the material form aggregate, aggregates are the feeling aggregate,’ and so on; and thus it is called the word-purification root-cycle chapter, due to the existence of cycles rooted in the word-purification. That too is twofold by way of direct order and reverse order. In its direct-order chapter, there are twenty dyads, having made four for each individual aggregate, beginning: ‘Material form is the material form aggregate, aggregates are the feeling aggregate,’ and so on. And in the reverse-order chapter, there are likewise twenty, beginning: ‘Not material form, not the material form aggregate; not aggregates, not the feeling aggregate,’ and so on.

Tato paraṃ “rūpaṃ khandho, khandhā rūpa”ntiādinā nayena suddhakhandhavaseneva gato suddhakhandhavāro nāma. Sopi anulomapaṭilomavasena duvidho hoti. Tassa anulomavāre “rūpaṃ khandho[V 0.0299], khandhā rūpa”ntiādīni pañca yamakāni. Paṭilomavārepi “na rūpaṃ na khandho, na khandhā na rūpa”ntiādīni pañceva.

Then, the Pure Aggregates Chapter is so called because it proceeds solely by way of the pure aggregates, by the method beginning: 'Material form is an aggregate, aggregates are material form,' and so on. That too is twofold by way of direct order and reverse order. In its direct-order chapter, there are five dyads beginning: 'Material form is an aggregate, aggregates are material form,' and so on. And in the reverse-order chapter, there are likewise five, beginning: 'Not material form, not an aggregate; not aggregates, not material form,' and so on.

Tato paraṃ tesaññeva suddhakhandhānaṃ “rūpaṃ khandho, khandhā vedanā”tiādinā nayena ekekakhandhamūlakāni cattāri cattāri cakkāni bandhitvā gato suddhakhandhamūlakānaṃ cakkānaṃ atthitāya suddhakhandhamūlacakkavāro nāma. Sopi anulomapaṭilomavasena duvidho hoti. Tassa anulomavāre “rūpaṃ khandho, khandhā vedanā”tiādīni ekekakhandhamūlakāni cattāri cattāri katvā vīsati yamakāni. Paṭilomavārepi “na rūpaṃ na khandho, na khandhā na vedanā”tiādīni vīsatimeva. Evamettha catūsu nayavāresu ekaṃ yamakasataṃ, dve pucchāsatāni, ekekapucchāya sanniṭṭhānasaṃsayavasena dve [M 0.0391] dve atthe katvā cattāri ca atthasatāni uddiṭṭhānīti veditabbāni.

Then, regarding those very pure aggregates, it proceeds by constructing four wheels based on each individual aggregate, by the method beginning: 'Material form is an aggregate, aggregates are feeling,' and so on; and thus it is called the Pure Aggregates Root-Cycle Chapter. That too is twofold by way of direct order and reverse order. In its direct-order chapter, there are twenty dyads, having made four for each individual aggregate, beginning: 'Material form is an aggregate, aggregates are feeling,' and so on. And in the reverse-order chapter, there are likewise twenty, beginning: 'Not material form, not an aggregate; not aggregates, not feeling,' and so on. Thus, in these four sections of method, one hundred dyads, two hundred questions, and for each question, by taking two meanings each by way of determination and doubt, four hundred meanings are to be understood as enumerated.

Evametissā pāḷivavatthānaṃ viditvā idāni anuttānapadatthānusārena vibhaṅganayasahitasaṅkhepatthavaṇṇanānayo evaṃ veditabbo. Pañcakkhandhāti ayaṃ yamakavasena pucchitabbānaṃ khandhānaṃ uddeso. Rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandhoti tesaññeva pabhedato nāmavavatthānaṃ. Tato paraṃ padasodhanavārādayo cattāro nayavārā. Tattha rūpaṃ rūpakkhandhoti yaṃ kiñci “rūpa”nti vuccati, sabbaṃ taṃ “rūpakkhandho”ti pucchatīti vacanasodhanatthaṃ pucchā. Tassā ca “piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ rūpaṃ na rūpakkhandho, rūpakkhandho rūpañceva rūpakkhandho cā”ti idaṃ niddesanayena vissajjanaṃ. Tattha piyarūpaṃ sātarūpantiādīsu yaṃ “rūpa”nti vuttaṃ, taṃ rūpameva na rūpakkhandho. Yo pana “rūpakkhandho”ti vutto, so “rūpa”ntipi “rūpakkhandho”tipi vattuṃ vaṭṭatīti attho. Rūpakkhandho rūpanti ettha pana “āmantā”ti vissajjanaṃ rūpakkhandhassa niyamena rūpanti vattabbattā. Vedanā vedanākkhandhoti pucchāya, vedanākkhandho vedanāti pucchāya ca “āmantā”ti vissajjanaṃ. Saññāsaññākkhandhoti pucchāya “papañcasaññā”tiādīsu āgatā diṭṭhisaññā saññā na saññākkhandho, saññākkhandho saññā ceva saññākkhandho cāti vissajjanaṃ. Saññākkhandho saññāti pucchāya ca “āmantā”ti vissajjanaṃ. Saṅkhārā saṅkhārakkhandhoti pucchāya “aniccā vata saṅkhārā”tiādīsu āgato saṅkhārakkhandho, tato avasesā saṅkhatadhammā saṅkhārā na saṅkhārakkhandhoti vissajjanaṃ. Saṅkhārakkhandho saṅkhārāti pucchāya “āmantā”ti vissajjanaṃ. Viññāṇaṃ [V 0.0300] viññāṇakkhandhoti pucchāya, viññāṇakkhandho viññāṇanti pucchāya ca “āmantā”ti vissajjanaṃ.

Having thus understood the arrangement of the Pāḷi, now the method of concise explanation together with the way of analysis should be understood in accordance with the meaning of the terms not made plain. 'The five aggregates': this is the statement of the aggregates to be questioned by way of pairs. 'The aggregate of form... the aggregate of consciousness': this is the arrangement of their names by way of division. After that are the four sections of method, beginning with the section on the clarification of terms. Herein, the question, 'Is form the aggregate of form?'—that is, whatever is called 'form,' is all that asked about as 'the aggregate of form?'—is for the purpose of clarifying the term. And its answer by way of exposition is this: 'Pleasing form, agreeable form is form but not the aggregate of form; the aggregate of form is both form and the aggregate of form.' Herein, in such cases as 'pleasing form, agreeable form,' what is called 'form' is just form, not the aggregate of form. But what is called 'the aggregate of form' may be spoken of as both 'form' and 'the aggregate of form'—this is the meaning. To the question, 'Is the aggregate of form form?' the answer is 'Yes,' because the aggregate of form must necessarily be called form. To the question, 'Is feeling the aggregate of feeling?' and to the question, 'Is the aggregate of feeling feeling?' the answer is 'Yes.' To the question, 'Is perception the aggregate of perception?' the answer is: 'The perception of views that occurs in such phrases as "the perception of proliferation" is perception but not the aggregate of perception; the aggregate of perception is both perception and the aggregate of perception.' And to the question, 'Is the aggregate of perception perception?' the answer is 'Yes.' To the question, 'Are formations the aggregate of formations?', the answer is that the aggregate of formations is what is found in phrases such as 'Alas, formations are impermanent,' while the remaining conditioned phenomena apart from that are formations but not the aggregate of formations. To the question, 'Is the aggregate of formations formations?' the answer is 'Yes.' To the question, 'Is consciousness the aggregate of consciousness?' and to the question, 'Is the aggregate of consciousness consciousness?' the answer is 'Yes.'

Paṭilomavāre na rūpaṃ na rūpakkhandhoti pucchāya “āmantā”ti vissajjanaṃ. Tassa rūpa-saddavacanīyā dhammā rūpakkhandho [M 0.0392] na hontīti attho. Na rūpakkhandho na rūpanti pucchāya rūpakkhandhavirahitā “piyarūpaṃ sātarūpa”nti vuttā dhammā na rūpakkhandho, rūpaṃ, piyarūpasātarūparūpakkhandhavirahitā pana dhammā na rūpakkhandho ceva na rūpañcāti vissajjanaṃ. Na vedanā na vedanākkhandhoti pucchāya, na vedanākkhandho na vedanāti pucchāya, na saññā na saññākkhandhoti pucchāya ca “āmantā”ti vissajjanaṃ. Na saṅkhārā na saṅkhārakkhandhoti pucchāya “āmantā”ti vissajjanaṃ. Na saññākkhandho na saññāti pucchāya pana diṭṭhisaññā na saññākkhandho, saññā, taṃ diṭṭhisaññaṃ, saññākkhandhañca ṭhapetvā avasesā na ceva saññā na ca saññākkhandhoti vissajjanaṃ. Na saṅkhārā na saṅkhārakkhandhoti pucchāya “āmantā”ti vissajjanaṃ. Na saṅkhārakkhandho na saṅkhārāti pucchāya saṅkhārakkhandhaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesasaṅkhatadhammā na saṅkhārakkhandho, saṅkhārā, asaṅkhatā pana dhātu na ceva saṅkhārā na ca saṅkhārakkhandhoti vissajjanaṃ. Na viññāṇaṃ na viññāṇakkhandhoti pucchāya, na viññāṇakkhandho na viññāṇanti pucchāya ca “āmantā”ti vissajjanaṃ. Imināva nayena ito paresupi sabbattha vissajjananayo veditabbo, visesamattameva pana vakkhāma.

In the converse section, to the question, 'Is it not form and not the aggregate of form?' the answer is 'Yes.' The meaning is that phenomena not describable by the word 'form' are not the aggregate of form. To the question, 'Is it not the aggregate of form and not form?' the answer is: 'The phenomena called "pleasing form, agreeable form," which are apart from the aggregate of form, are not the aggregate of form, but they are form; however, phenomena apart from pleasing form, agreeable form, and the aggregate of form are neither the aggregate of form nor form.' To the questions, 'Is it not feeling and not the aggregate of feeling?,' 'Is it not the aggregate of feeling and not feeling?,' and 'Is it not perception and not the aggregate of perception?' the answer is 'Yes.' To the question, 'Is it not formations and not the aggregate of formations?' the answer is 'Yes.' But to the question, 'Is it not the aggregate of perception and not perception?' the answer is: 'The perception of views is not the aggregate of perception, but it is perception; setting aside that perception of views and the aggregate of perception, the remainder is neither perception nor the aggregate of perception.' To the question, 'Is it not formations and not the aggregate of formations?' the answer is 'Yes.' To the question, 'Is it not the aggregate of formations and not formations?' the answer is: 'Setting aside the aggregate of formations, the remaining conditioned phenomena are not the aggregate of formations, but they are formations; however, the unconditioned element is neither formations nor the aggregate of formations.' To the questions, 'Is it not consciousness and not the aggregate of consciousness?' and 'Is it not the aggregate of consciousness and not consciousness?' the answer is 'Yes.' By this same method, the way of answering should be understood everywhere in the subsequent sections; we will state only the specific points.

Padasodhanamūlacakkavāre pana ayaṃ viseso – khandhā vedanākkhandhoti ye keci khandhā, sabbe te vedanākkhandhoti pucchā. Tassā “vedanākkhandho khandho ceva vedanākkhandho ca, avasesā pana khandhā, na vedanākkhandho”ti vissajjanaṃ. Sesesupi eseva nayo. Paṭilome pana na khandhā na vedanākkhandhoti pucchāya “āmantā”ti vissajjanaṃ. Ettha ca ye paññattinibbānasaṅkhātā dhammā khandhāpi na honti, te yasmā vedanākkhandhopi na hoti, tasmā “āmantā”ti vissajjanaṃ, sesaṃ suviññeyyameva. Padasodhanamūlacakkavāro.

Now, in the Section of the Root-Cycle of the Clarification of Terms, this is the specific point: the question, 'Are the aggregates the aggregate of feeling?' means, 'Whatever aggregates there are, are they all the aggregate of feeling?' Its answer is: 'The aggregate of feeling is both an aggregate and the aggregate of feeling; but the remaining aggregates are aggregates, not the aggregate of feeling.' This same method applies in the remaining cases. In the converse, however, to the question, 'Is it not the aggregates and not the aggregate of feeling?' the answer is 'Yes.' And here, since those phenomena reckoned as concepts and Nibbāna are not aggregates, and they are also not the aggregate of feeling, therefore the answer is 'Yes.' The rest is easy to understand. The Section of the Root-Cycle of the Clarification of Terms.

Suddhakhandhavāre pana “rūpaṃ khandho”ti pucchāya “āmantā”ti vissajjanaṃ piyarūpādīnañca pañcasu khandhesu saṅgahitattā. “Khandhā rūpa”ntiādīsu [M 0.0393] ye keci khandhā, sabbe te rūpakkhandhotiādinā attho gahetabbo. Teneva hissa niddese “khandhā rūpa”ntiādinā padaṃ anuddharitvā [V 0.0301] “khandhā rūpakkhandho”tiādinā atthavaseneva padaṃ uddharitvā “rūpakkhandho khandho ceva rūpakkhandho ca, avasesā khandhā, na rūpakkhandho”ti vissajjanaṃ kataṃ. Teneva ca kāraṇena suddhakhandhavāroti vutto. Vacanasodhane viya hi ettha na vacanaṃ pamāṇaṃ, yathā pana suddhakhandhā labbhanti, tathā tathā atthova pamāṇaṃ. Parato āyatanayamakamātikādīsupi eseva nayo. Paṭilome “na rūpaṃ na khandho”ti yaṃ dhammajātaṃ rūpaṃ na hoti, taṃ khandhopi na hotīti pucchā, tassā “rūpakkhandhavirahitā khandhā, na rūpaṃ, tathā nibbānaṃ na pana rūpañceva na khandho cā”ti vissajjanaṃ. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva. Suddhakhandhavāro.

Now, in the section on the pure aggregates, to the question, 'Is form an aggregate?' the answer is 'Yes,' because pleasing forms and so on are included in the five aggregates. In such questions as 'Are the aggregates form?' the meaning should be taken as 'Whatever aggregates there are, are they all the aggregate of form?' and so on. For that reason, in its exposition, without citing the term as 'the aggregates are form,' the term is cited according to the meaning as 'are the aggregates the aggregate of form?,' and the answer is given: 'The aggregate of form is both an aggregate and the aggregate of form; the remaining aggregates are aggregates, but not the aggregate of form.' And for that very reason it is called the section on the pure aggregates. For here, unlike in the clarification of terms, the wording is not the authority; rather, just as the pure aggregates are obtained, so the meaning alone is the authority. Further on, in the sections on the matrix of the base-pairs and so on, this is the same method. In the converse, the question 'Is it not form and not an aggregate?' asks: 'That class of phenomena which is not form, is it also not an aggregate?' To this, the answer is: 'The aggregates devoid of the aggregate of form are not form, yet they are aggregates; Nibbāna is neither form nor an aggregate.' The rest is easy to understand. The Section on the Pure Aggregates.

Suddhakhandhamūlacakkavārepi “khandhā vedanākkhandho”tiādinā heṭṭhā vuttanayena attho veditabboti ayaṃ paṇṇattivāre nayo.

Also in the section of the root-cycle of the pure aggregates, the meaning of such questions as 'Are the aggregates the aggregate of feeling?' and so on should be understood by the method stated above. This is the method in the section on concepts.

Yasmā pana niddese imissā pana mātikāya paṇṇattivārasaṅkhātaṃ niddesaṃ vatvā tato imaṃ mātikākkamaṃ muñcitvā aparena pariyāyena aññepi uddesavāravirahitā “pavattivāro pariññāvāro”ti dve mahāvārā pucchāvissajjanavasena vuttā, tasmā tesaṃ dvinnampi vārānaṃ nayo dassetabbo. Tato pavattivāre tāva pāḷivavatthānapubbikā mukhamattappakāsanā – imasmiṃ hi uppādavāro nirodhavāro uppādanirodhavāroti tayo antaravārā honti. Tattha uppādavāre tāva tiṇṇaṃ addhānaṃ vasena cha kālabhedā honti paccuppanno, atīto, anāgato, paccuppannenātīto, paccuppannenānāgato, atītenānāgatoti. Evametesu chasu kālabhedesu yvāyaṃ paṭhamo [M 0.0394] paccuppanno, tattha puggalato okāsato puggalokāsatoti tayo vārā honti.

But since in the exposition, having stated the exposition of this matrix called the section on concepts, and then having abandoned this order of the matrix, two other great sections devoid of a recitation section—the 'section on occurrence' and the 'section on full understanding'—are stated in another way by means of questions and answers, therefore the method of both these two sections should be shown. Then, in the section on occurrence, there is first a brief indication preceded by the arrangement of the Pāḷi text: for in this there are three internal sections: the section on arising, the section on cessation, and the section on arising and cessation. Therein, in the section on arising, there are six divisions of time by way of the three time periods: present, past, future, present-and-past, present-and-future, and past-and-future. Thus, in these six divisions of time, in the first, the present, there are three sections: concerning the person, concerning the location, and concerning the person and location.

Tattha “yassa rūpakkhandho uppajjati, tassa vedanākkhandho uppajjatīti? Asaññasattaṃ upapajjantānaṃ tesaṃ rūpakkhandho uppajjati, no ca tesaṃ vedanākkhandho uppajjati. Pañcavokāraṃ upapajjantānaṃ tesaṃ rūpakkhandho ca uppajjati, vedanākkhandho ca uppajjati. Yassa vā pana vedanākkhandho uppajjati, tassa rūpakkhandho uppajjatīti? Arūpaṃ upapajjantānaṃ tesaṃ vedanākkhandho uppajjati, no ca tesaṃ rūpakkhandho uppajjati. Pañcavokāraṃ upapajjantānaṃ tesaṃ vedanākkhandho ca uppajjati, rūpakkhandho ca uppajjati. Yassa rūpakkhandho uppajjati…pe… tassa viññāṇakkhandho uppajjati…pe… yassa vā pana viññāṇakkhandho uppajjati, tassa rūpakkhandho uppajjatīti…pe… pañcavokāraṃ [V 0.0302] …pe… uppajjatī”ti evaṃ rūpakkhandhamūlakāni cattāri, “yassa vedanākkhandho uppajjati, tassa saññākkhandho uppajjatī”tiādinā ca vedanākkhandhamūlakāni tīṇi, saññākkhandhamūlakāni dve, saṅkhārakkhandhamūlakaṃ ekanti evametāni paccuppannakāle puggalavāre anulomanaye dasa yamakāni honti. Tattha rūpakkhandhamūlakesu catūsu ādito ekameva pāḷiyaṃ vissajjitaṃ, sesāni tena sadisavissajjanānīti tantiyā lahubhāvatthaṃ saṃkhittāni.

Herein: ‘For one for whom the form aggregate arises, does the feeling aggregate arise for him?’ For those being reborn into the realm of non-percipient beings, the form aggregate arises for them, but the feeling aggregate does not arise for them. For those being reborn into the five-constituent existence, the form aggregate arises for them and the feeling aggregate also arises for them. ‘Or for one for whom the feeling aggregate arises, does the form aggregate arise for him?’ For those being reborn into the formless realm, the feeling aggregate arises for them, but the form aggregate does not arise for them. For those being reborn into the five-constituent existence, the feeling aggregate arises for them and the form aggregate also arises for them. ‘For one for whom the form aggregate arises… does the consciousness aggregate arise for him?… Or for one for whom the consciousness aggregate arises, does the form aggregate arise for him?… into the five-constituent existence… it arises.’ Thus there are four rooted in the form aggregate. And by the passage beginning, ‘For one for whom the feeling aggregate arises, does the perception aggregate arise for him?,’ there are three rooted in the feeling aggregate, two rooted in the perception aggregate, and one rooted in the formations aggregate. In this way, there are these ten couplets in the present time, in the section on individuals, in the positive series. Herein, among the four rooted in the form aggregate, only the first is answered in full in the Pāḷi text; the others, having similar answers, are abbreviated for the sake of textual brevity.

Vedanākkhandhamūlake pana sabbattha “āmantā”ti ekasadisameva vissajjanaṃ. Vedanādīsu uppannesu niyamena saññādīnaṃ uppajjanato tattha sabbāni saṃkhittāni. Yathā ca puggalavāre dasa yamakāni, evaṃ okāsavārepi “yattha rūpakkhandho uppajjati, tattha vedanākkhandho uppajjatīti? Asaññasatte tattha…pe… pañcavokāre tattha…pe… uppajjatī”tiādinā, puggalokāsavārepi “yassa yattha rūpakkhandho uppajjati, tassa tattha vedanākkhandho uppajjatīti? Asaññasattaṃ…pe… pañcavokāraṃ…pe… uppajjatī”tiādinā. Paccuppannakāle tīsu vāresu [M 0.0395] anulomanaye tiṃsa yamakā honti. Yathā anulomanaye tiṃsa, evaṃ paṭilomanayepi “yassa rūpakkhandho nuppajjati, tassa vedanākkhandho nuppajjatīti? Arūpaṃ upapajjantānaṃ tesaṃ rūpakkhandho nuppajjati, no ca tesaṃ vedanākkhandho nuppajjati. Sabbesaṃ cavantānaṃ tesaṃ rūpakkhandho ca nuppajjati vedanākkhandho ca nuppajjati. Yassa vā pana vedanākkhandho nuppajjati, tassa rūpakkhandho nuppajjatīti? Asaññasattaṃ upapajjantānaṃ tesaṃ vedanākkhandho nuppajjati, no ca tesaṃ rūpakkhandho nuppajjati. Sabbesaṃ cavantānaṃ tesaṃ vedanākkhandho ca nuppajjati rūpakkhandho ca nuppajjatī”tiādinā, “yattha rūpakkhandho nuppajjati, tattha vedanākkhandho nuppajjatīti? Uppajjati. Yattha vā pana…pe… nuppajjatīti? Uppajjatī”tiādinā ca, “yassa yattha rūpakkhandho nuppajjati, tassa tattha vedanākkhandho nuppajjatīti…pe… sabbesaṃ cavantānaṃ tadubhayaṃ nuppajjatī”tiādinā cāti tiṃsa yamakā. Evaṃ paccuppannakāle saṭṭhi yamakāni, taddiguṇā pucchā, taddiguṇā ca atthā veditabbā.

But in the case of those rooted in the feeling aggregate, the answer is uniformly ‘Yes’ everywhere. Because when feeling and so on have arisen, perception and so on necessarily arise, all of them are abbreviated there. Just as there are ten couplets in the section on individuals, so too in the section on location: ‘Where the form aggregate arises, does the feeling aggregate arise there? In the non-percipient existence… in the five-constituent existence… it arises,’ and so on. And also in the section on individuals and location: ‘For one for whom, where the form aggregate arises, does the feeling aggregate arise for him there? For those being reborn into the non-percipient existence… into the five-constituent existence… it arises,’ and so on. In the present time, in the three sections, there are thirty couplets in the positive series. Just as there are thirty in the positive series, so too in the negative series: ‘For one for whom the form aggregate does not arise, does the feeling aggregate not arise for him? For those being reborn into the formless realm, the form aggregate does not arise for them, but the feeling aggregate does arise for them. For all who are passing away, neither the form aggregate nor the feeling aggregate arises for them. Or for one for whom the feeling aggregate does not arise, does the form aggregate not arise for him? For those being reborn into the non-percipient existence, the feeling aggregate does not arise for them, but the form aggregate does arise for them. For all who are passing away, neither the feeling aggregate nor the form aggregate arises for them,’ and so on. And: ‘Where the form aggregate does not arise, does the feeling aggregate not arise there? It arises. Or where… does it not arise? It arises,’ and so on. And: ‘For one for whom, where the form aggregate does not arise, does the feeling aggregate not arise for him there?… For all who are passing away, both do not arise for them there,’ and so on. Thus there are thirty couplets. In this way, in the present time, there are sixty couplets; the questions are double that, and the meanings should be understood to be double that as well.

Tattha yassa rūpakkhandho uppajjatīti yassa puggalassa paṭisandhikkhaṇe rūpakkhandho uppajjati. Tassa vedanākkhandhoti vedanākkhandhopi tassa tasmiṃyeva khaṇe uppajjatīti attho imināva nayena. Tattha asaññasattanti asaññattabhavaṃ paṭisandhivasena upapajjantānaṃ tesaṃ uppajjanakkhaṇe rūpakkhandho uppajjati, no ca tesaṃ acittakattā vedanākkhandho uppajjatīti attho[V 0.0303]. Imināva nayena “yassa vā pana vedanākkhandho”tiādikesu pucchāvissajjanesu, tato paresupi sabbattha attho veditabbo.

Herein, the phrase ‘for one for whom the form aggregate arises’ means: for whichever individual the form aggregate arises at the moment of rebirth-linking. By this same method, the meaning of ‘for him the feeling aggregate’ is that the feeling aggregate also arises for him at that very same moment. Herein, ‘non-percipient beings’ means those being reborn into the non-percipient existence by way of rebirth-linking. The meaning is that for them, at the moment of arising, the form aggregate arises, but because they are without mind, the feeling aggregate does not arise for them. In this same way, the meaning should be understood everywhere in the subsequent questions and answers, such as ‘Or for one for whom the feeling aggregate arises?’ and so on.

Idaṃ panettha uppādanirodhesu niyamalakkhaṇaṃ – sakalepi hi imasmiṃ khandhayamake tattha tattha uppannānaṃ sattānaṃ pavatte yāva maraṇā vā khandhānaṃ apariyantesu uppādanirodhesu vijjamānesupi lahuparivattānaṃ dhammānaṃ vinibbhogaṃ katvā uppādanirodhe [M 0.0396] dassetuṃ na sukaranti pavattiyaṃ uppādanirodhe anāmasitvā paṭisandhiuppādavaseneva uppādavāro, nirodhamaraṇakāle nirodhavaseneva ca nirodhavāro kathito. Evamettha uppādanirodhesu niyamalakkhaṇaṃ viditvā paṭisandhiuppādameva ca cutinirodhameva ca gahetvā tesu tesu ṭhānesu āgatānaṃ pucchāvissajjanānaṃ atthavinicchayo veditabbo.

This, herein, is the fixed characteristic regarding arising and cessation: For in this entire Couplets on the Aggregates, even though for beings who have arisen here and there, during the course of existence up to death, there are limitless arisings and cessations of the aggregates, it is not easy to show the arising and cessation by making a distinction for phenomena that change rapidly. Therefore, without referring to arising and cessation during the course of life, the section on arising is taught only by way of the arising at rebirth-linking, and the section on cessation is taught only by way of the cessation at the time of death. Thus, having understood the fixed characteristic of arising and cessation here, and having taken only the arising at rebirth-linking and the cessation at death, the determination of the meaning of the questions and answers that occur in those respective places should be understood.

Paṭilomanaye pana sabbesaṃ cavantānanti maraṇacittassa bhaṅgakkhaṇasamannāgatānaṃ. Tesaṃ hi tattha rūpakkhandho nuppajjati, vedanākkhandho ca cuticittassa uppattikkhaṇe eva uppannattā. “Yattha rūpakkhandho nuppajjati, tattha vedanākkhandho nuppajjatī”ti pucchāya arūpabhavaṃ sandhāya “uppajjatī”ti idaṃ vissajjanaṃ kataṃ, anantarapucchāya asaññibhavaṃ sandhāya “uppajjatī”ti idaṃ vissajjananti veditabbaṃ. Sesaṃ suviññeyyamevāti ayaṃ paccuppannakāle nayo.

But in the negative series, ‘for all who are passing away’ means those endowed with the dissolution moment of the death-consciousness. For them, the form aggregate does not arise there, since the feeling aggregate arose at the very arising moment of the death-consciousness. To the question, ‘Where the form aggregate does not arise, does the feeling aggregate not arise there?,’ the answer ‘It arises’ is given with reference to the formless existence. It should be understood that to the immediately following question, the answer ‘It arises’ is given with reference to the non-percipient existence. The rest is easy to understand. This is the method concerning the present time.

Yathā ca paccuppannakāle saṭṭhi yamakādīni, evaṃ sesesupi pañcasu kālabhedesu paccekanti gahetabbaṃ. Pucchāvissajjanesu panettha kiñcāpi “yassa rūpakkhandho uppajjittha, tassa vedanākkhandho uppajjitthāti? Āmantā”tiādinā, “yattha rūpakkhandho uppajjittha, tattha vedanākkhandho uppajjitthāti? Pañcavokāre uppajjittha, nāññatthā”tiādinā ca, “yassa yattha rūpakkhandho uppajjittha, tassa tattha vedanākkhandho uppajjitthāti? Pañcavokārānaṃ tesaṃ tattha uppajjittha, nāññatthā”tiādinā ca atītakāle anulomanaye, “yassa rūpakkhandho nuppajjittha, tassa vedanākkhandho nuppajjitthāti? Natthī”tiādinā, “yattha rūpakkhandho nuppajjittha, tattha vedanākkhandho nuppajjitthāti? Uppajjitthā”tiādinā, “yassa yattha rūpakkhandho nuppajjittha, tassa tattha vedanākkhandho nuppajjitthāti? Arūpānaṃ tesaṃ tattha rūpakkhandho nuppajjittha, no ca tesaṃ…pe… suddhāvāsānaṃ [M 0.0397] tesaṃ tattha tadubhayaṃ nuppajjitthā”tiādinā tīsu vāresu paṭilomanaye ca,

And just as there are sixty couplets and so on in the present time, so it should be understood for each of the remaining five divisions of time. Herein, in the questions and answers, although in the positive series in the past time it is said: ‘For one for whom the form aggregate arose, did the feeling aggregate arise for him? Yes,’ and so on; ‘Where the form aggregate arose, did the feeling aggregate arise there? It arose in the five-constituent existence, not elsewhere,’ and so on; and ‘For one for whom, where the form aggregate arose, did the feeling aggregate arise for him there? It arose for those in the five-constituent existence there, not elsewhere,’ and so on; and in the negative series in the three sections in the past time: ‘For one for whom the form aggregate did not arise, did the feeling aggregate not arise for him? There is none,’ and so on; ‘Where the form aggregate did not arise, did the feeling aggregate not arise there? It arose,’ and so on; and ‘For one for whom, where the form aggregate did not arise, did the feeling aggregate not arise for him there? For those in the formless realms, the form aggregate did not arise for them there, but the feeling aggregate did arise for them… for those in the Pure Abodes, both did not arise for them there,’ and so on,

“Yassa [V 0.0304] rūpakkhandho uppajjissati, tassa vedanākkhandho uppajjissatīti? Āmantā”tiādinā, “yattha rūpakkhandho uppajjissati, tattha vedanākkhandho uppajjissatīti…pe… pañcavokāre uppajjissatī”tiādinā, “yassa yattha rūpakkhandho uppajjissati, tassa tattha vedanākkhandho uppajjissati…pe… pañcavokārānaṃ tesaṃ tattha uppajjissatī”tiādinā ca anāgatakāle anulomanaye, “yassa rūpakkhandho nuppajjissati, tassa vedanākkhandho nuppajjissatīti? Ye arūpaṃ upapajjitvā parinibbāyissanti, tesaṃ rūpakkhandho nuppajjissati, netaro, pacchimabhavikānaṃ tadubhayaṃ nuppajjissatī”tiādinā, “yattha rūpakkhandho nuppajjissati, tattha vedanākkhandho nuppajjissatī”tiādinā, “yassa yattha rūpakkhandho nuppajjissati, tassa tattha vedanākkhandho nuppajjissatīti? Arūpānaṃ tesaṃ tattha rūpakkhandho nuppajjissati, netaro, pacchimabhavikānaṃ tadubhayaṃ nuppajjissatī”tiādinā paṭilomanaye ca,

and in the positive series in the future time: ‘For one for whom the form aggregate will arise, will the feeling aggregate arise for him? Yes,’ and so on; ‘Where the form aggregate will arise, will the feeling aggregate arise there?… it will arise in the five-constituent existence,’ and so on; and ‘For one for whom, where the form aggregate will arise, will the feeling aggregate arise for him there?… it will arise for them in the five-constituent existence there,’ and so on; and in the negative series: ‘For one for whom the form aggregate will not arise, will the feeling aggregate not arise for him? For those who, after being reborn into the formless realm, will attain final Nibbāna, the form aggregate will not arise for them, but the other will; for those in their final existence, both will not arise for them,’ and so on; ‘Where the form aggregate will not arise, will the feeling aggregate not arise there?’ and so on; and ‘For one for whom, where the form aggregate will not arise, will the feeling aggregate not arise for him there? For those in the formless realms, the form aggregate will not arise for them there, but the other will; for those in their final existence, both will not arise for them there,’ and so on, in the negative series.

“Yassa rūpakkhandho uppajjati, tassa vedanākkhandho uppajjitthā”tiādinā, “yattha rūpakkhandho uppajjati, tattha vedanākkhandho uppajjitthāti…pe… pañcavokāre uppajjatī”tiādinā, “yassa yattha rūpakkhandho uppajjati, tassa tattha vedanākkhandho uppajjitthāti? Suddhāvāsaṃ asaññasattaṃ upapajjantānaṃ tesaṃ tattha rūpakkhandho uppajjati, no ca tesaṃ tattha vedanākkhandho uppajjittha, pañcavokāre pana uppajjitthā”tiādinā paccuppannena atītakāle anulomanaye, “yassa rūpakkhandho nuppajjati, tassa vedanākkhandho nuppajjitthā”tiādinā, “yattha rūpakkhandho nuppajjati, tattha vedanākkhandho nuppajjitthāti? Uppajjitthā”tiādinā, “yassa yattha rūpakkhandho nuppajjati[M 0.0398], tassa tattha vedanākkhandho nuppajjitthāti? Pañcavokārā cavantānaṃ arūpānañca tesaṃ tattha rūpakkhandho nuppajjati, no ca tesaṃ tattha vedanākkhandho nuppajjittha, suddhāvāse parinibbantānaṃ asaññasattā cavantānaṃ tesaṃ tattha rūpakkhandho ca nuppajjati vedanākkhandho ca nuppajjitthā”tiādinā paṭilomanaye ca,

“For one for whom the form aggregate arises, had the feeling aggregate arisen for them?” and so on; “Where the form aggregate arises, had the feeling aggregate arisen there? …pe… it arises in the five-constituent existence,” and so on; “For one for whom, and where, the form aggregate arises, had the feeling aggregate arisen for them there? For those being reborn into the Pure Abodes and as non-percipient beings, for them the form aggregate arises there, but for them the feeling aggregate had not arisen there; however, it had arisen in the five-constituent existence,” and so on—in the forward method with the present in relation to the past. And, “For one for whom the form aggregate does not arise, had the feeling aggregate not arisen for them?” and so on; “Where the form aggregate does not arise, had the feeling aggregate not arisen there? It had arisen,” and so on; “For one for whom, and where, the form aggregate does not arise, had the feeling aggregate not arisen for them there? For those passing away from the five-constituent existence and for formless beings, for them the form aggregate does not arise there, but for them the feeling aggregate had not failed to arise there. For those attaining final Nibbāna in the Pure Abodes and for those passing away from the non-percipient state, for them there the form aggregate does not arise and the feeling aggregate had not arisen,” and so on—in the reverse method.

“Yassa rūpakkhandho uppajjati, tassa vedanākkhandho uppajjissatīti? Pacchimabhavikānaṃ pañcavokāraṃ upapajjantānaṃ tesaṃ rūpakkhandho uppajjatī”tiādinā, “yattha rūpakkhandho uppajjati, tattha vedanākkhandho uppajjissatīti? Pañcavokāre…pe… uppajjissatī”tiādinā ca, “yassa yattha rūpakkhandho uppajjati, tassa tattha vedanākkhandho uppajjissatīti[V 0.0305]? Pacchimabhavikānaṃ pañcavokāre…pe… uppajjissatī”tiādinā ca paccuppannena anāgatakāle anulomanaye, “yassa rūpakkhandho nuppajjati, tassa vedanākkhandho nuppajjissatīti pañcavokāre parinibbantānaṃ arūpe pacchimabhavikānaṃ…pe… nuppajjissatī”tiādinā, “yattha rūpakkhandho nuppajjati, tattha vedanākkhandho nuppajjissatīti? Uppajjissatī”tiādinā, “yassa yattha rūpakkhandho nuppajjati, tassa tattha vedanākkhandho nuppajjissatīti…pe… pañcavokāre parinibbantānaṃ arūpe pacchimabhavikānaṃ asaññasattā cavantānaṃ tesaṃ tattha…pe… nuppajjissatī”tiādinā paṭilomanaye ca,

“For one for whom the form aggregate arises, will the feeling aggregate arise for them? For those in their last existence who are being reborn into the five-constituent existence, for them the form aggregate arises,” and so on; and “Where the form aggregate arises, will the feeling aggregate arise there? In the five-constituent existence…pe… it will arise,” and so on; and “For one for whom, and where, the form aggregate arises, will the feeling aggregate arise for them there? For those in their last existence in the five-constituent existence…pe… it will arise,” and so on—in the forward method with the present in relation to the future. And, “For one for whom the form aggregate does not arise, will the feeling aggregate not arise for them? For those attaining final Nibbāna in the five-constituent existence, for those in their last existence in the formless realm…pe… it will not arise,” and so on; “Where the form aggregate does not arise, will the feeling aggregate not arise there? It will arise,” and so on; “For one for whom, and where, the form aggregate does not arise, will the feeling aggregate not arise for them there? …pe… For those attaining final Nibbāna in the five-constituent existence, for those in their last existence in the formless realm, and for non-percipient beings passing away, for them there…pe… it will not arise,” and so on—in the reverse method.

“Yassa rūpakkhandho uppajjittha, tassa vedanākkhandho uppajjissatīti? Pacchimabhavikānaṃ uppajjissatī”tiādinā, “yattha rūpakkhandho uppajjittha, tattha vedanākkhandho uppajjissatīti…pe… pañcavokāre uppajjissatī”tiādinā, “yassa yattha rūpakkhandho uppajjittha, tassa tattha vedanākkhandho uppajjissatīti? Pañcavokāre pacchimabhavikānaṃ asaññasattānaṃ…pe… uppajjissatī”tiādinā atītena anāgatakāle anulomanaye, “yassa rūpakkhandho uppajjittha, tassa vedanākkhandho uppajjissatīti? Natthī”tiādinā, “yattha rūpakkhandho [M 0.0399] nuppajjittha, tattha vedanākkhandho nuppajjissatīti? Uppajjissatī”tiādinā, “yassa yattha rūpakkhandho nuppajjittha, tassa tattha vedanākkhandho nuppajjissatīti…pe… suddhāvāsānaṃ arūpe pacchimabhavikānaṃ tesaṃ tattha rūpakkhandho ca nuppajjittha vedanākkhandho ca nuppajjissatī”tiādinā paṭilomanaye ca suddhā atthavisesā upalabbhanti. Tathāpi ganthavitthārabhayena anavasesato na dassayissāma, dassitanayeneva sabbattha pucchāvissajjanaṃ sakkā paṇḍitena ñātunti ayaṃ uppādavāre nayo.

“For one for whom the form aggregate had arisen, will the feeling aggregate arise for them? For those in their final existence, it will arise,” and so on; “Where the form aggregate had arisen, will the feeling aggregate arise there? …pe… In the five-constituent existence, it will arise,” and so on; “For one for whom, and where, the form aggregate had arisen, will the feeling aggregate arise for them there? For those in their last existence in the five-constituent existence, for non-percipient beings…pe… it will arise,” and so on—in the forward method with the past in relation to the future. And in the reverse method: “For one for whom the form aggregate had arisen, will the feeling aggregate arise for them? No,” and so on; “Where the form aggregate had not arisen, will the feeling aggregate not arise there? It will arise,” and so on; “For one for whom, and where, the form aggregate had not arisen, will the feeling aggregate not arise for them there? …pe… For the beings of the Pure Abodes and for those in their last existence in the formless realm, for them there both the form aggregate had not arisen and the feeling aggregate will not arise,” and so on. In this way, clear distinctions of meaning are found. However, for fear of making the text too long, we will not present them exhaustively. A wise person can understand the questions and answers everywhere by the method that has been shown. This is the method in the Section on Arising.

Yathā ca uppādavāre chasu kālabhedesu paccekaṃ puggalādibhedato anulomapaṭilomanayubhayena cha cha vārā, ekekasmiṃ vāre dasa dasa katvā saṭṭhi saṭṭhi yamakāni, sabbānipi saṭṭhiadhikāni tīṇi yamakasatāni, tato dviguṇā pucchā, dviguṇā atthā ca honti, evaṃ nirodhavāre uppādanirodhavārepi veditabbā. Tattha ca “yassa rūpakkhandho nirujjhati, tassa vedanākkhandho nirujjhatīti…pe… pañcavokārā cavantānaṃ…pe… nirujjhatī”tiādinā, “yassa rūpakkhandho na nirujjhati, tassa vedanākkhandho na nirujjhatīti…pe… sabbesaṃ upapajjantānaṃ…pe… na nirujjhatī”tiādinā nirodhavāre, “yassa [V 0.0306] rūpakkhandho uppajjati, tassa vedanākkhandho nirujjhatīti? No. Yassa rūpakkhandho nuppajjati, tassa vedanākkhandho na nirujjhatīti…pe… arūpaṃ upapajjantānaṃ asaññasattā cavantānaṃ tesaṃ rūpakkhandho ca nuppajjati, vedanākkhandho ca na nirujjhatī”tiādinā uppādanirodhavāre ca heṭṭhā vuttānusārena sabbattha pucchāvissajjananayo ñātabboti ayaṃ pavattivāre nayo.

And just as in the Section on Arising, for the six divisions of time, each distinguished by person, etc., there are six sections for both the forward and reverse methods. In each of these sections there are ten couplets, making sixty couplets for each time division, and three hundred and sixty couplets in all. The questions are doubled, and the points of analysis are also doubled. The same should be understood for the Section on Cessation and the Section on Arising and Cessation. Therein, in the Section on Cessation: “For one for whom the form aggregate is ceasing, is the feeling aggregate ceasing for them? …pe… For those passing away from the five-constituent existence…pe… it is ceasing,” and so on. And: “For one for whom the form aggregate is not ceasing, is the feeling aggregate not ceasing for them? …pe… For all who are being reborn…pe… it is not ceasing,” and so on. And in the Section on Arising and Cessation: “For one for whom the form aggregate is arising, is the feeling aggregate ceasing for them? No. For one for whom the form aggregate is not arising, is the feeling aggregate not ceasing for them? …pe… For those being reborn into the formless realm and for non-percipient beings passing away, for them the form aggregate is not arising and the feeling aggregate is not ceasing,” and so on. In all cases, the method of question and answer should be understood according to what has been said above. This is the method in the Section on Occurrence.

Pariññāvāre pana puggalavārādīsu tīsu puggalavāro ekova labbhati, na okāsapuggalokāsavārā sadisavissajjanattā. Yo hi koci puggalo rūpādiṃ parijānantova[M 0.0400], yattha katthaci niruddhopi tādisova hoti, tasmā chasu kālabhedesu anulomato puggalavasena dve dve vārā, ekekasmiṃ vāre dasa dasa katvā vīsati vīsati yamakānīti vīsaṃ yamakasataṃ, taddiguṇā pucchā, taddiguṇā ca atthā veditabbā. Tattha ca “yo rūpakkhandhaṃ parijānāti, so vedanākkhandhaṃ parijānātīti? Āmantā”tiādinā ca, “yo rūpakkhandhaṃ na parijānāti, so vedanākkhandhaṃ na parijānātīti? Āmantā”ti ādinā ca anulomapaṭilomato ādito tīsu kālesu sabbapucchānaṃ “āmantā āmantā”tveva vissajjanaṃ. Itaresu pana tīsu missakakālesu “yo rūpakkhandhaṃ parijānāti, so vedanākkhandhaṃ parijānitthāti? No. Yo vā pana…pe… no”ti evaṃ itarakāladvayepi anulomanaye “no no”tveva vissajjanaṃ.

In the Section on Full Understanding, however, among the three sections beginning with the Person Section, only the Person Section is found, not the Location and Person-Location Sections, because their answers are similar. For any person who is fully understanding form, etc., is just the same even if they have ceased somewhere or other. Therefore, in the six divisions of time, by way of person, there are two sections for each time period, for the forward and reverse methods. In each section there are ten couplets, making twenty couplets for each time period, thus one hundred and twenty couplets in total. The questions should be understood as double that, and the meanings as double that. Therein: “Does one who fully understands the form aggregate also fully understand the feeling aggregate? Yes,” and so on; and “Does one who does not fully understand the form aggregate also not fully understand the feeling aggregate? Yes,” and so on. Thus, in the first three time periods, the answer to all questions in both the forward and reverse methods is just “Yes, yes.” But in the other three mixed time periods, for the forward method the answer is: “Does one who fully understands the form aggregate also have fully understood the feeling aggregate? No. Or alternatively…pe… no.” Thus in the other two mixed time periods as well, in the forward method, the answer is just “No, no.”

Paṭilomanaye pana “yo rūpakkhandhaṃ na parijānāti, so vedanākkhandhaṃ na parijānitthāti? Arahā rūpakkhandhaṃ na parijānāti, no ca so vedanākkhandhaṃ na parijānittha. Aggamaggasamaṅgiñca arahantañca ṭhapetvā avasesā puggalā rūpakkhandhañca na parijānanti, vedanākkhandhañca na parijāniṃsū”tiādinā, “yo rūpakkhandhaṃ na parijānāti, so vedanākkhandhaṃ na parijānissatīti? Ye maggaṃ paṭilabhissanti, te rūpakkhandhaṃ na parijānanti, no ca vedanākkhandhaṃ na parijānissanti. Arahā ye ca puthujjanā maggaṃ na paṭilabhissanti, te rūpakkhandhañca na parijānanti, vedanākkhandhañca na parijānissantī”tiādinā ca, “yo rūpakkhandhaṃ na parijānittha, so vedanākkhandhaṃ na parijānissantīti? Ye maggaṃ paṭilabhissanti, te rūpakkhandhaṃ na parijāniṃsu, no ca vedanākkhandhaṃ na parijānissanti. Aggamaggasamaṅgī ye ca puthujjanā maggaṃ na paṭilabhissanti, te [V 0.0307] rūpakkhandhañca na parijāniṃsu, vedanākkhandhañca na parijānissantī”tiādinā ca pucchāvissajjananayo veditabbo.

In the reverse method, however: “One who does not fully understand the form aggregate, had that one not fully understood the feeling aggregate? An arahant does not fully understand the form aggregate, but they had not failed to fully understand the feeling aggregate. Setting aside one endowed with the highest path and the arahant, the remaining persons both do not fully understand the form aggregate and had not fully understood the feeling aggregate,” and so on. And: “One who does not fully understand the form aggregate, will that one not fully understand the feeling aggregate? Those who will attain the path do not fully understand the form aggregate, but they will not fail to fully understand the feeling aggregate. The arahant and those worldlings who will not attain the path both do not fully understand the form aggregate and will not fully understand the feeling aggregate,” and so on. And: “One who had not fully understood the form aggregate, will that one not fully understand the feeling aggregate? Those who will attain the path had not fully understood the form aggregate, but they will not fail to fully understand the feeling aggregate. One endowed with the highest path and those worldlings who will not attain the path both had not fully understood the form aggregate and will not fully understand the feeling aggregate,” and so on. The method of question and answer should be understood in this way.

Ettha [M 0.0401] ca atītānāgatapaccuppannasaṅkhātā tayo addhā pavattivāre cutipaṭisandhivasena na labbhanti, pavatte cittakkhaṇavaseneva labbhanti. Lokuttaramaggakkhaṇasmiṃ hi nibbānārammaṇena cittena pañcasu khandhesu pariññākiccanipphattiyā yaṃ kañci ekaṃ khandhaṃ parijānanto itarampi “parijānātī”ti anulomapañhesu pariññākiccassa matthakappattaṃ aggamaggasamaṅgiṃ sandhāya “āmantā”ti vissajjanaṃ vuttaṃ. “Na parijānātī”ti paṭilomapañhesu puthujjanādayo sandhāya “āmantā”ti vissajjanaṃ vuttanti veditabbaṃ. “Parijānitthā”ti imasmiṃ pana atītakālavāre maggānantare aggaphale ṭhitopi pariññākiccassa niṭṭhitattā parijānitthayeva nāma. “Parijānātī”ti ca aggamaggasamaṅgī vuccati, “parijānissantī”ti puthujjanādayo, tasmā yo na parijānāti, so parijānitthāti vā, parijānissatītiādinā vā vattuṃ asakkuṇeyyatāya “āmantā”ti vissajjanaṃ kataṃ.

Here, the three times—past, future, and present—are not obtained in the Section on Occurrence by way of death and relinking, but are obtained only by way of moments of consciousness during the process of existence. For at the moment of the supramundane path, with a mind that has Nibbāna as its object, by accomplishing the function of fully understanding the five aggregates, when one fully understands any single aggregate, one is said to ‘fully understand’ the others too. In the forward questions, the answer ‘Yes’ was given with reference to one endowed with the highest path who has reached the culmination of the function of full understanding. In the reverse questions, it should be understood that the answer ‘Yes’ was given with reference to worldlings and others. Regarding ‘had fully understood,’ in this past-time section, even one established in the highest fruition immediately following the path is indeed said to ‘have fully understood,’ since the function of full understanding has been completed. And one endowed with the highest path is said to ‘fully understand,’ while worldlings and others are said to ‘will fully understand.’ Therefore, because it is impossible to say of one who does not fully understand that they ‘had fully understood’ or ‘will fully understand,’ and so on, the answer ‘Yes’ was given.

Paṭilomanaye pana “aggamaggasamaṅgiñca arahantañca ṭhapetvā”ti idaṃ aggamaggasamaṅgino “na parijānātī”ti vacanaṃ, arahato ca “na parijānitthā”ti vattuṃ asakkuṇeyyatāya vuttaṃ, “ye ca puthujjanā maggaṃ na paṭilabhissantī”ti iminā atīte viya anāgatepi anantakālaṃ amuccanakā sattā nāma atthīti dasseti, te ca arahatā niṭṭhitapariññākiccena, “na parijānissantī”ti vattabbataṃ vā āpannena samakā jātā, sabbattha ca ekaṃ khandhaṃ parijānanto sabbaṃ parijānāti, aparijānantopi ca sabbaṃ na parijānātīti veditabbanti ayaṃ khandhayamakamātikatthasaṃvaṇṇanānayo.

But in the reverse method, the statement 'except for one endowed with the highest path and the Arahant' is made because it is impossible to say of one endowed with the highest path that he 'does not fully understand,' or of an Arahant that he 'has not fully understood.' The phrase 'and those worldlings who will not attain the path' shows that, just as in the past, in the future too there are beings who will not be liberated for an endless time. And these beings are treated as similar to an Arahant—who has completed the function of full understanding—in that it can also be said of them, 'they will not fully understand.' And it should be understood that in all cases, one who fully understands one aggregate fully understands all, and one who does not fully understand one aggregate does not fully understand all. This is the method of the explanation of the meaning of the Mātikā to the Khandha Yamaka.

Āyatanayamakamātikatthavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Meaning of the Mātikā to the Āyatana Yamaka

Āyatanayamakamātikāya pana pāḷivavatthānādikaṃ sabbaṃ khandhayamakamātikāya vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ aññatra visesā[M 0.0402], tatrāyaṃ viseso – “dvādasāyatanānī”ti padaṃ ādiṃ katvā yāva “nāyatanā na mano”ti, tāva pavattā ayaṃ āyatanamātikā nāma. Tattha dvādasāyatanāni uddisitvā yamakavasena pucchāsu khandhapadaṃ ṭhapetvā cakkhādīni pañca ajjhattikāyatanāni [V 0.0308] paṭhamaṃ vuttāni, pacchā rūpādipañcabāhirāyatanāni, pariyosāne manāyatanadhammāyatanānīti evaṃ pāḷivavatthāne pañhe. Vissajjane pana “cakkhu cakkhāyatananti? Dibbacakkhu paññācakkhu cakkhumeva, na cakkhāyatanaṃ, cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhu ceva cakkhāyatanañca. Sotaṃ sotāyatananti? Dibbasotaṃ taṇhāsotaṃ sotameva, na sotāyatanaṃ. Ghānaṃ ghānāyatananti? Āmantā…pe… kāyo kāyāyatananti? Nāmakāyo cittakāyotiādi kāyo, na kāyāyatanaṃ. Rūpaṃ rūpāyatananti? Bhūtādi, piyarūpādi ca rūpaṃva, na rūpāyatanaṃ. Saddo saddāyatananti? Āmantā. Gandho gandhāyatananti? Sīlagandhādayo gandhova, na gandhāyatanaṃ. Raso rasāyatananti? Attharasādayo rasova, na rasāyatanaṃ. Dhammo dhammāyatananti? Pariyattidhammādayo dhammova, na dhammāyatanaṃ. Dhammāyatanaṃ dhammoti? Āmantā”ti ayaṃ paṇṇattivāre viseso.

But regarding the Mātikā to the Āyatana Yamaka, the textual arrangement and so on should all be understood in the same way as explained for the Mātikā to the Khandha Yamaka, apart from the special points. Herein, this is the special point: this is called the Āyatana Mātikā, which proceeds from the term 'twelve bases' up to 'neither a base nor mind.' There, having set forth the twelve bases, in the questions by way of pairs, setting aside the term 'aggregate,' the five internal bases—eye, etc.—are stated first, followed by the five external bases—form, etc.—and concluding with the mind-base and the dhamma-base. Thus is the textual arrangement in the questions. In the answers, however, the special point is as follows: 'Is the eye the eye-base? The divine eye and the wisdom eye are merely "eye," not the eye-base. The eye-base is both "eye" and the eye-base. Is the ear the ear-base? The divine ear and the "ear of craving" are merely "ear," not the ear-base. Is the nose the nose-base? Yes… Is the body the body-base? The mental body, the body of consciousness, etc., are "body," not the body-base. Is form the form-base? Primary matter, agreeable form, etc., are merely "form," not the form-base. Is sound the sound-base? Yes. Is odour the odour-base? The odour of virtue, etc., are merely "odour," not the odour-base. Is taste the taste-base? The taste of the meaning, etc., are merely "taste," not the taste-base. Is a dhamma the dhamma-base? The Dhamma of the scriptures, etc., are merely "dhamma," not the dhamma-base. Is the dhamma-base a dhamma? Yes.' This is the special point in the designation section.

Pavattivāre pana “yassa cakkhāyatanaṃ uppajjati, tassa sotāyatanaṃ uppajjatīti? Sacakkhukānaṃ asotakānaṃ upapajjantānaṃ tesaṃ cakkhāyatanaṃ uppajjati, no ca tesaṃ sotāyatanaṃ uppajjati. Sacakkhukānaṃ sasotakānaṃ upapajjantānaṃ tesaṃ cakkhāyatanañca uppajjati, sotāyatanañca uppajjati…pe… yassa rūpāyatanaṃ uppajjati, tassa manāyatanaṃ uppajjatīti? Acittakānaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ uppajjati, no ca tesaṃ manāyatanaṃ uppajjati. Pañcavokāre uppādakkhaṇe tadubhayaṃ uppajjati. Yassa vā pana manāyatanaṃ uppajjati, tassa rūpāyatanaṃ uppajjatīti? Arūpabhavavajjite saññābhave upapajjantānaṃ…pe… uppajjati[M 0.0403]. Yassa rūpāyatanaṃ uppajjati, tassa dhammāyatanaṃ uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Yassa vā pana…pe… uppajjatīti? Arūpabhavavajjite sabbattha uppajjati. Yassa manāyatanaṃ uppajjati, tassa dhammāyatanaṃ uppajjatīti? Āmantā, yassa vā pana…pe… uppajjatīti? Asaññabhavavajjite sabbattha uppajjatī”ti evaṃ saddāyatanavajjitā sesāyatanamātikāyamakayojanā yathānurūpaṃ veditabbā. Saddāyatanaṃ hi paṭisandhikkhaṇe na labbhati, ayaṃ uppādavāre viseso, iminā nayena nirodhavārādīsu, pariññāvāre ca yojanāviseso veditabbo, sabbattha ca khandhato āyatanānaṃ bahutā ca yamakavārabahutā ca veditabbā. Sesaṃ tādisamevāti ayaṃ āyatanayamakamātikatthasaṃvaṇṇanānayo.

In the Process Section: 'For one for whom the eye-base arises, does the ear-base arise?' For those being reborn who have an eye but lack an ear, the eye-base arises for them, but the ear-base does not arise for them. For those being reborn who have an eye and an ear, both the eye-base and the ear-base arise for them… 'For one for whom the form-base arises, does the mind-base arise?'
