For mindless beings, the form-base arises, but the mind-base does not arise for them. In the five-constituent existence, at the moment of arising, both arise. 'Or for one for whom the mind-base arises, does the form-base arise?' For those being reborn in percipient existence, excluding the formless existence… it arises. 'For one for whom the form-base arises, does the dhamma-base arise?' Yes. 'Or for one for whom the dhamma-base arises, does the form-base arise?' It arises everywhere except in the formless existence. 'For one for whom the mind-base arises, does the dhamma-base arise?' Yes. 'Or for one for whom the dhamma-base arises, does the mind-base arise?' It arises everywhere except in the non-percipient existence.' Thus, the application of the Yamaka to the remaining Mātikās on the bases, excluding the sound-base, should be understood accordingly. For the sound-base is not found at the moment of relinking—this is the special point in the Arising Section. In this way, the special application in the Cessation Section, etc., and in the Full Understanding Section should be understood. And everywhere, the greater number of bases than aggregates, and the greater number of Yamaka sections, should be understood. The rest is just the same. This is the method of the explanation of the meaning of the Mātikā to the Āyatana Yamaka.

Dhātuyamakamātikatthavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Meaning of the Mātikā to the Dhātu Yamaka

Dhātuyamakamātikāya [V 0.0309] pana pāḷivavatthānaṃ sabbaṃ āyatanayamakamātikāya vuttanayeneva veditabbanti ayaṃ dhātuyamakamātikatthasaṃvaṇṇanānayo.

However, in the Mātikā to the Dhātu Yamaka, the entire structure of the Pāḷi text should be understood in the same way as was explained in the Mātikā to the Āyatana Yamaka. This is the method for the explanation of the meaning of the Mātikā to the Dhātu Yamaka.

Saccayamakamātikatthavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Meaning of the Mātikā to the Sacca Yamaka

Saccayamakamātikāya pana khandhayamake vuttanayena vārabhedā, kālādibhedā ca veditabbā, pāḷivavatthāne panettha catunnaṃ saccānaṃ vasena padasodhanavāro padasodhanamūlacakkavāro suddhasaccavāro suddhasaccamūlacakkavāroti imesu catūsu vāresu yamakagaṇanā veditabbā. Pucchāvissajjanesu pana “dukkhaṃ dukkhasaccanti? Āmantā. Dukkhasaccaṃ dukkhanti? Kāyikacetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesaṃ dukkhasaccaṃ, na dukkhaṃ. Kāyikacetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ pana dukkhañceva dukkhasaccañca. Samudayo samudayasaccanti? Taṇhaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā saccavibhaṅge niddiṭṭhā kusalādidhammā samudayo, na samudayasaccaṃ. Taṇhā [M 0.0404] pana samudayo ceva samudayasaccañca. Samudayasaccaṃ samudayoti? Āmantā. Nirodho nirodhasaccanti? Tadaṅganirodhādayo, khaṇikanirodho ca nirodhova, na nirodhasaccaṃ. Nibbānaṃ pana nirodho ceva nirodhasaccañca. Nirodhasaccaṃ nirodhoti? Āmantā. Maggo maggasaccanti? Micchāmaggaṅgādayo maggo, na maggasaccaṃ. Ariyamaggo pana maggo ceva maggasaccañca. Maggasaccaṃ maggoti? Āmantā”tiādinā paṇṇattivāre nayo veditabbo.

In the Mātikā to the Sacca Yamaka, however, the divisions into sections and the divisions by time, etc., should be understood as explained in the Khandha Yamaka. Regarding the structure of the Pāḷi text here, the counting of pairs in these four sections should be understood based on the four truths: the section on word-clarification, the section on the wheel of roots of word-clarification, the section on the pure truths, and the section on the wheel of roots of the pure truths. In the questions and answers, however, the method in the section on designation should be understood as follows: 'Is suffering the truth of suffering?' 'Yes.' 'Is the truth of suffering suffering?' 'Excluding bodily and mental suffering, the remaining truth of suffering is not suffering. But bodily and mental suffering are both suffering and the truth of suffering.' 'Is the origin the truth of origin?' 'Excluding craving, the remaining wholesome states, etc., mentioned in the Analysis of the Truths are the origin, but not the truth of origin. Craving, however, is both the origin and the truth of origin.' 'Is the truth of origin the origin?' 'Yes.' 'Is cessation the truth of cessation?' 'Cessation by substitution of opposites, etc., and momentary cessation are just cessation, not the truth of cessation. Nibbāna, however, is both cessation and the truth of cessation.' 'Is the truth of cessation cessation?' 'Yes.' 'Is the path the truth of the path?' 'The factors of the wrong path, etc., are the path, but not the truth of the path. The Noble Path, however, is both the path and the truth of the path.' 'Is the truth of the path the path?' 'Yes.' And so on.

Pavattivāre pana “yassa dukkhasaccaṃ uppajjati, tassa samudayasaccaṃ uppajjatīti? Sabbesaṃ upapajjantānaṃ pavatte taṇhāvippayuttacittassa uppādakkhaṇe tesaṃ dukkhasaccaṃ uppajjati, no ca tesaṃ samudayasaccaṃ uppajjati. Taṇhāya uppādakkhaṇe tadubhayaṃ uppajjati. Yassa dukkhasaccaṃ uppajjati, tassa maggasaccaṃ uppajjatīti…pe… pañcavokāre maggassa uppādakkhaṇe tadubhayaṃ uppajjati. Yassa vā pana…pe… uppajjatīti? Arūpe maggassa uppādakkhaṇe tesaṃ maggasaccaṃ uppajjati, no ca tesaṃ dukkhasaccaṃ uppajjati. Pañcavokāre tadubhayaṃ uppajjati. Yassa samudayasaccaṃ uppajjati, tassa maggasaccaṃ uppajjatīti? No, yassa vā pana…pe… no”tiādinā puggalavāre, “yattha dukkhasaccaṃ uppajjati, tattha samudayasaccaṃ uppajjatīti? Asaññasatte tattha dukkhasaccaṃ uppajjati, no ca tattha tadaññaṃ, aññattha [V 0.0310] tadubhayampi. Yattha dukkhasaccaṃ uppajjati, tattha maggasaccaṃ uppajjatīti? Apāye, asaññasatte ca dukkhameva, no ca tattha tadaññaṃ, aññattha tadubhayampī”tiādinā okāsavāre, puggalokāsavārepīti evaṃ anulomanaye,

However, in the section on occurrence: 'For whom does the truth of suffering arise, for them does the truth of origin arise?' For all beings who are being reborn, in the course of existence, at the moment of the arising of a mind dissociated from craving, the truth of suffering arises for them, but the truth of origin does not arise for them. At the moment of the arising of craving, both arise. 'For whom does the truth of suffering arise, for them does the truth of the path arise?'…pe… In the five-constituent existence, at the moment of the arising of the path, both arise. 'Or for whom…pe… does it arise?' In the formless realm, at the moment of the arising of the path, the truth of the path arises for them, but the truth of suffering does not arise for them. In the five-constituent existence, both arise. 'For whom does the truth of origin arise, for them does the truth of the path arise?' No. 'Or for whom…pe…?' No. And so on in the section on persons. 'Where does the truth of suffering arise, there does the truth of origin arise?' In the realm of non-percipient beings, the truth of suffering arises there, but the other does not arise there; elsewhere, both arise. 'Where does the truth of suffering arise, there does the truth of the path arise?' In the states of deprivation and in the realm of non-percipient beings, only suffering arises, but the other does not arise there; elsewhere, both arise. And so on in the section on location, and also in the section on persons and locations, thus in the positive method,

“Yassa dukkhasaccaṃ nuppajjati, tassa samudayasaccaṃ nuppajjatīti? Āmantā. Yassa vā pana…pe… nuppajjatīti? Sabbesaṃ upapajjantānaṃ pavatte taṇhāvippayuttacittassa uppādakkhaṇe samudayasaccaṃ nuppajjati, no ca tesaṃ dukkhasaccaṃ nuppajjati. Sabbesaṃ [M 0.0405] cavantānaṃ pavatte cittassa bhaṅgakkhaṇe arūpe maggassa ca phalassa ca uppādakkhaṇe tesaṃ samudayasaccañca nuppajjati, dukkhasaccañca nuppajjatī”tiādinā, “yattha dukkhasaccaṃ nuppajjati, tattha samudayasaccaṃ nuppajjatīti? Natthi. Yattha vā pana samudayasaccaṃ nuppajjati, tattha dukkhasaccaṃ nuppajjatīti? Uppajjatī”tiādinā ca, “yassa yattha dukkhasaccaṃ nuppajjati, tassa tattha samudayasaccaṃ nuppajjatīti? Āmantā. Yassa vā pana yattha samudayasaccaṃ nuppajjati, tassa tattha dukkhasaccaṃ nuppajjatīti? Sabbesaṃ upapajjantānaṃ pavatte taṇhāvippayuttacittassa uppādakkhaṇe tesaṃ tattha samudayasaccaṃ eva nuppajjati, netaraṃ, sabbesaṃ pana cavantānaṃ pavatte cittassa bhaṅgakkhaṇe arūpe maggassa ca phalassa ca uppādakkhaṇe tesaṃ tattha tadubhayampi nuppajjatī”tiādinā ca sabbattha paṭilomanaye ca,

'For whom does the truth of suffering not arise, for them does the truth of origin not arise?' 'Yes.' 'Or for whom…pe… does it not arise?' 'For all those who are being reborn, in the course of existence, at the moment of the arising of a mind dissociated from craving, the truth of origin does not arise, but the truth of suffering does arise for them. For all those who are passing away, in the course of existence, at the moment of dissolution of a mind, and in the formless realm at the moment of arising of the path and of the fruit, for them both the truth of origin and the truth of suffering do not arise.' And so on. 'Where does the truth of suffering not arise, there does the truth of origin not arise?' 'There is no such case.' 'Or where does the truth of origin not arise, there does the truth of suffering not arise?' 'It arises.' And so on. 'For whom, where the truth of suffering does not arise, for them there does the truth of origin not arise?' 'Yes.' 'Or for whom, where the truth of origin does not arise, for them there does the truth of suffering not arise?' 'For all those who are being reborn, in the course of existence, at the moment of the arising of a mind dissociated from craving, for them there only the truth of origin does not arise, while the truth of suffering does arise. However, for all those who are passing away, in the course of existence, at the moment of dissolution of a mind, and in the formless realm at the moment of arising of the path and of the fruit, for them there both do not arise.' And so on, and in the negative method everywhere,

“Yassa dukkhasaccaṃ uppajjittha, tassa samudayasaccaṃ uppajjitthāti? Āmantā. Yassa dukkhasaccaṃ uppajjittha, tassa maggasaccaṃ uppajjitthāti? Abhisametāvīnaṃ uppajjittha, na itaresa”ntiādinā, “yassa yattha dukkhasaccaṃ uppajjittha, tassa tattha samudayasaccaṃ uppajjitthāti? Suddhāvāsānaṃ dutiye citte vattamāne asaññasattānaṃ tattha dukkhasaccaṃ uppajjittha, netaraṃ, itaresaṃ tadubhayaṃ uppajjitthā”tiādinā, “yassa dukkhasaccaṃ uppajjissati, tassa samudayasaccaṃ uppajjissatīti? Aggamaggasamaṅgīnaṃ arahantānaṃ yassa cittassa anantarā aggamaggaṃ paṭilabhissanti, tesaṃ dukkhasaccaṃ uppajjissati, netaraṃ, itaresaṃ tadubhayaṃ uppajjissatī”tiādinā ca, “yassa dukkhasaccaṃ uppajjati, tassa samudayasaccaṃ uppajjitthāti? Āmantā, yassa vā pana…pe… uppajjatīti? Sabbesaṃ cavantānaṃ pavatte cittassa bhaṅgakkhaṇe arūpe maggaphaluppattikkhaṇe tesaṃ samudayasaccaṃ uppajjittha, no ca tesaṃ dukkhasaccaṃ uppajjati. Sabbesaṃ upapajjantānaṃ pavatte cittassa uppādakkhaṇe samudayasaccañca uppajjittha[V 0.0311], dukkhasaccañca uppajjatī”tiādinā ca sesakālabhedesu [M 0.0406] ca anulomapaṭilomādīsu ca vuttānusārena uppādavāre sabbattha vissajjananayo yathānurūpaṃ ñātabbo. “Yassa dukkhasaccaṃ nirujjhati, tassa samudayasaccaṃ nirujjhatīti…pe… taṇhāya bhaṅgakkhaṇe tesaṃ tadubhayaṃ nirujjhatī”tiādinā nirodhavāre, uppādanirodhavārepīti evaṃ pavattivāre sabbattha yathānurūpato yojanā veditabbā.

'For whom has the truth of suffering arisen, for them has the truth of origin arisen?' 'Yes.' 'For whom has the truth of suffering arisen, for them has the truth of the path arisen?' 'For those who have realized, it has arisen; not for others.' And so on. 'For whom, where the truth of suffering has arisen, for them there has the truth of origin arisen?' 'For beings in the Pure Abodes when the second consciousness is occurring, and for non-percipient beings, the truth of suffering has arisen there, but not the other; for others, both have arisen.' And so on. 'For whom will the truth of suffering arise, for them will the truth of origin arise?' 'For those endowed with the highest path, for whom immediately after this consciousness they will attain the highest path, and for arahants, for them the truth of suffering will arise, but not the other; for others, both will arise.' And so on. 'For whom is the truth of suffering arising, for them has the truth of origin arisen?' 'Yes.' 'Or for whom…pe… is it arising?' 'For all those who are passing away, in the course of existence, at the moment of dissolution of a mind, and in the formless realm at the moment of the path and fruition arising, for them the truth of origin has arisen, but the truth of suffering is not arising. For all those who are being reborn, in the course of existence, at the moment of the arising of a mind, both the truth of origin has arisen and the truth of suffering is arising.' And so on. In the remaining time-divisions and in the positive, negative, and other methods, in accordance with what has been said, the method of answering should be known appropriately everywhere in the section on arising. 'For whom is the truth of suffering ceasing, for them is the truth of origin ceasing?'…pe… 'At the moment of the dissolution of craving, both cease for them.' And so on in the section on cessation, and in the section on arising-and-cessation. Thus, in the section on occurrence, the application should be understood appropriately everywhere.

Tathā “yo dukkhasaccaṃ parijānāti, so samudayasaccaṃ pajahatīti? Āmantā”tiādinā pariññāvārepīti evamettha pāḷinayo ñātabbo.

Likewise, in the section on full understanding: 'Does one who fully understands the truth of suffering abandon the truth of origin?' 'Yes.' And so on. Thus the method of the Pāli text should be understood here.

Atthavinicchaye panettha idaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ – pavatti vāre tāvettha nirodhasaccaṃ na labbhateva, sesesu pana tīsu saccesu samudayamaggasaccāni ekantena pavattiyaṃ eva labbhanti. Dukkhasaccaṃ cutipaṭisandhīsupi pavattepīti evamettha yaṃ yaṃ sabbattha labbhati, tassa tassa vasena atthavinicchayo veditabbo. Tatridaṃ nayamukhaṃ – sabbesaṃ upapajjantānanti antamaso suddhāvāsānampi. Tepi hi dukkhasacceneva uppajjanti. Taṇhāvippayuttacittassāti idaṃ dukkhasaccasamudayasaccesu ekakoṭṭhāsassa uppattidassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ, tasmā pañcavokāravaseneva gahetabbaṃ. Catuvokāre pana taṇhāvippayuttaphalasamāpattiyā uppādakkhaṇe ekampi saccaṃ nuppajjati. Tadubhayanti dukkhasamudayasaccadvayaṃ. Tasmiṃ hi khaṇe taṇhaṃ ṭhapetvā sesaṃ dukkhasaccaṃ nāma hotīti taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Maggassa uppādakkhaṇe pana rūpameva dukkhasaccaṃ nāma, sesā maggasahajātā dhammā saccavinimuttāva. Teneva kāraṇena “arūpe maggassa uppādakkhaṇe tesaṃ maggasaccaṃ uppajjati, no ca tesaṃ dukkhasaccaṃ uppajjatī”ti vuttaṃ. Sabbesaṃ upapajjantānaṃ pavatte taṇhāvippayuttacittassa uppādakkhaṇe. Tesaṃ tatthāti tesaṃ tasmiṃ upapattikkhaṇe taṇhāvippayuttacittuppattikkhaṇe cāti evamettha khaṇavasena okāso veditabbo. Aññesupi evarūpesu eseva nayo. Anabhisametāvīnanti [M 0.0407] anabhisamitasaccānanti iminā nayamukhena sabbattha atthavinicchayo veditabbo.

In the analysis of meaning here, this is the characteristic: in the section on occurrence, the truth of cessation is not found at all, but among the remaining three truths, the truths of origin and path are found exclusively in the course of existence. The truth of suffering is found at decease and rebirth-linking, and also in the course of existence; thus, here, the analysis of meaning should be understood by way of whatever is found everywhere. Here is the method of approach: 'for all beings who are reborn' means even the inhabitants of the Pure Abodes. For they too arise only with the truth of suffering. 'Of a mind dissociated from craving'—this is stated to show the arising of one part of the truths of suffering and origin; therefore, it should be taken only in terms of the five-constituent existence. In the four-constituent existence, however, at the moment of arising of fruition attainment dissociated from craving, not even one truth arises. 'Both' means the pair of truths: suffering and origin. For at that moment, apart from craving, the remainder is called the truth of suffering—this is stated in reference to that. At the moment of the path's arising, however, only material form is called the truth of suffering; the other phenomena co-nascent with the path are entirely free from the truths. For this reason, it is said: 'In the formless realm, at the moment of the path's arising, the truth of the path arises for them, but the truth of suffering does not arise for them.' 'For all beings who are reborn, in the course of existence, at the moment of arising of a mind dissociated from craving.' 'For them, there' means for them at that moment of rebirth and at the moment of the arising of a mind dissociated from craving; thus, here, the location should be understood in terms of moments. The same method applies to other similar cases. 'For those who have not realized' means 'for those who have not realized the truths'; through this method of approach, the analysis of meaning should be understood everywhere.

Pariññāvāre pana ñātatīraṇapahānavasena tissopi pariññāyo labbhanti. Yasmā pana lokuttaradhammesu pariññānāma natthi, tasmā idha dve eva saccāni gahitāni. Tattha “dukkhasaccaṃ parijānātī”ti ñātatīraṇapariññāvasena vuttaṃ, “samudayasaccaṃ pajahatī”ti ñātapahānapariññāvasena[V 0.0312], iti imāsaṃ pariññānaṃ vasena sabbattha attho veditabbo. Ayaṃ saccayamakamātikatthasaṃvaṇṇanānayo.

In the section on full comprehension, however, three kinds of full comprehension are obtained by way of knowing, scrutinizing, and abandoning. But because there is no such thing as full comprehension in supramundane states, here only two truths are taken. Therein, "one fully comprehends the truth of suffering" is stated by way of full comprehension as knowing and scrutinizing; "one abandons the truth of origin" is stated by way of full comprehension as knowing and abandoning. Thus, the meaning should be understood everywhere in terms of these full comprehensions. This is the method of explaining the meaning of the matrix of the Yamaka on the Truths.

Saṅkhārayamakamātikatthavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Meaning of the Matrix of the Yamaka on Formations

Saṅkhārayamakamātikāya pana heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva mahāvārantarādibhedā veditabbā. Ayaṃ panettha viseso – mātikāya tāva yathā heṭṭhā khandhādayo dhamme uddisitvā “rūpaṃ rūpakkhandho”tiādinā padasodhanavāro āraddho, tathā anārabhitvā “assāsapassāsā kāyasaṅkhāro”tiādinā paṭhamaṃ tayopi saṅkhārā vibhajitvā dassitā. Tattha kāyassa saṅkhāro kāyasaṅkhāro, assāsapassāsā. “Kāyikā ete dhammā kāyapaṭibaddhā”ti (ma. ni. 1.463; saṃ. ni. 4.348) vacanato kāraṇabhūtassa karajakāyassa phalabhūto esa saṅkhāroti kāyasaṅkhāro. Aparo nayo – saṅkharīyatīti saṅkhāro. Kena saṅkharīyati? Kāyena. Ayaṃ hi vāto viya bhastāya karajakāyena saṅkharīyati, evampi kāyassa saṅkhāroti kāyasaṅkhāro, kāyena kato assāsapassāsavātoti attho. Cetasā vitakketvā vicāretvā pacchā vācaṃ bhindati, tasmā “vitakkavicārā vacīsaṅkhāro”ti (ma. ni. 1.463) vacanato pana saṅkharotīti saṅkhāro, kiṃ saṅkharoti? Vaciṃ. Vaciyā saṅkhāroti vacīsaṅkhāro, vacībhedasamuṭṭhāpakassa [M 0.0408] vitakkavicāradvayassetaṃ nāmaṃ. “Saññā ca vedanā ca cetasikā ete dhammā cittapaṭibaddhā”ti (ma. ni. 1.463; saṃ. ni. 4.348) vacanatoyeva pana tatiyapade saṅkharīyatīti saṅkhāro, kena saṅkharīyati? Cittena, iti cittassa saṅkhāroti cittasaṅkhāro, sabbesampi cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ cetasikānaṃ dhammānaṃ etaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Vitakkavicārānaṃ pana vacīsaṅkhārabhāvena visuṃ gahitattā “ṭhapetvā vitakkavicāre”ti vuttaṃ.

Regarding the Matrix of the Yamaka on Formations, however, the divisions such as the great sections, intermediate sections, and so on should be understood in the same way as explained previously. The difference here is this: in the matrix, whereas previously the aggregates and other phenomena were listed and then the section on the clarification of terms, such as 'form is the form aggregate,' was begun, here, without beginning in that way, the three types of formations are first analyzed and presented as 'in-breath and out-breath are bodily formation.' Here, 'formation of the body' is bodily formation, namely, in-breaths and out-breaths. Because it is said, 'These phenomena are bodily, connected to the body' (MN 1.463; SN 4.348), this formation is the result of the causal physical body; hence it is bodily formation. Another explanation: that which is formed is a formation. By what is it formed? By the body. For this is formed by the physical body, like wind by a bellows; thus, it is also the 'formation of the body,' meaning the wind of in-and-out breaths made by the body. One first thinks and examines with the mind, then breaks forth into speech. Therefore, it is said, 'applied thought and sustained thought are verbal formation' (MN 1.463). That which forms is a formation. What does it form? Speech. The 'formation of speech' is verbal formation. This is the name for the pair of applied and sustained thought, which gives rise to verbal expression. Further, because it is said, 'perception and feeling are mental; these phenomena are connected to the mind' (MN 1.463; SN 4.348), in the third case, that which is formed is a formation. By what is it formed? By the mind. Thus, the 'formation of the mind' is mental formation. This is a designation for all mental factors arising from the mind. However, because applied thought and sustained thought are taken separately as verbal formation, it is said, 'excluding applied thought and sustained thought.'

Idāni “kāyo kāyasaṅkhāro”ti padasodhanavāro āraddho, tassa anulomanaye tīṇi, paṭilomanaye tīṇīti cha yamakāni. Padasodhanamūlacakkavāre ekekasaṅkhāramūlakāni dve dve katvā anulomanaye cha, paṭilomanaye chāti dvādasa yamakāni. Suddhasaṅkhāravāre pana yathā suddhakhandhavārādīsu “rūpaṃ khandho, khandhā rūpa”ntiādinā nayena yamakānivuttāni, evaṃ “kāyo saṅkhāro, saṅkhārā kāyo”ti avatvā “kāyasaṅkhāro vacīsaṅkhāro”tiādinā nayena kāyasaṅkhāramūlakāni dve, vacīsaṅkhāramūlakaṃ ekanti anulome tīṇi, paṭilome tīṇīti cha yamakāni [V 0.0313] vuttāni. Kiṃ kāraṇā? Suddhikaekekapadavasena atthabhedābhāvato, kāyasaṅkhāroti pana dvīhipi padehi ekova attho labbhatīti ayaṃ visesova, tasmā ekekapadavasena na vuttaṃ, “kāyo kāyasaṅkhāro”tiādi pana vattabbaṃ siyā, sopi nayo padasodhanavāre vināpi atthena vacanaṃ yujjatīti tattheva vutto, idha pana kāyasaṅkhārādīnaṃ vacīsaṅkhārādīhi aññattā “kāyasaṅkhāro vacīsaṅkhāro”tiādināpi yamakāni vuttāni. Suddhasaṅkhāramūlacakkavāro panettha na gahitoti ayaṃ tāvettha pāḷivavatthāne viseso.

Now, the section on the clarification of terms, 'the body is bodily formation,' has begun. In its forward sequence, there are three pairs; in the reverse sequence, three—making six pairs in total. In the root cycle of the clarification of terms, taking each formation as a root, there are two pairs each, making six in the forward sequence and six in the reverse, totaling twelve pairs. However, in the section on pure formations, just as in the sections on pure aggregates, etc., pairs are stated in the manner of 'form is an aggregate, aggregates are form,' here it is not stated as 'the body is a formation, formations are the body,' but rather in the manner of 'bodily formation, verbal formation,' etc. Thus, with bodily formation as the root, there are two pairs; with verbal formation as the root, one—making three in the forward sequence and three in the reverse, totaling six pairs. Why is this? Because when taken purely as single terms, there is no difference in meaning. But with 'bodily formation,' one and the same meaning is obtained from both terms—this is the distinction. Therefore, it is not stated by way of single terms. However, phrases like 'the body is bodily formation' could be stated, and that method is also stated in the section on the clarification of terms, as the statement is suitable even without a literal meaning. Here, though, because bodily formations, etc., are distinct from verbal formations, etc., pairs are also stated in the manner of 'bodily formation, verbal formation,' etc. The root cycle of pure formations, however, is not included here. This, then, is the distinction in the arrangement of the Pāli text.

Pañhavissajjanesu [M 0.0409] pana “kāyo kāyasaṅkhāroti? No, kāyasaṅkhāro kāyoti? No”ti vā evaṃ sabbattha paṭisedho. Vissajjanānaṃ kāyādīnaṃ eva kāyasaṅkhārādināmattā. Na hi kāyādayo viya kāyasaṅkhārādīnaṃ nāmaṃ hoti, paṭilome pana na kāyo na kāyasaṅkhāroti yo kāyo na hoti, so kāyasaṅkhāropi na hotīti pucchāya attho, tassā kāyasaṅkhāro na kāyo kāyasaṅkhāroti kāyasaṅkhāro kāyo na hoti, kāyasaṅkhāroyeva paneso hoti, kāyañca kāyasaṅkhārañca ṭhapetvā avasesaṃ saṅkhatāsaṅkhatādibhedaṃ sabbaṃ na ca kāyo, na ca kāyasaṅkhāroti vissajjanaṃ. Sesesupi eseva nayo, itaresu ca anulomapaṭilomesu “kāyo kāyasaṅkhāroti? No, saṅkhārā vacīsaṅkhāroti? Vacīsaṅkhāro saṅkhāro ceva vacīsaṅkhāro ca, avasesā saṅkhārā, na vacīsaṅkhāro, na saṅkhārā na vacīsaṅkhāroti? Āmantā”tiādinā sabbattha pucchāvissajjananayo veditabbo.

In the questions and answers, however, it is said: 'Is the body the bodily formation? No. Is the bodily formation the body? No.' Thus, denial is applied everywhere. The answers concern the fact that 'body' etc. and 'bodily formation' etc. are distinct designations. For 'body' and the like are not the same as the designation 'bodily formation' and the like. In the reverse, however, 'Is that which is not the body not the bodily formation?' means the question is: 'that which is not the body, is it also not the bodily formation?' The answer to that is: 'The bodily formation is not the body, but it is indeed the bodily formation. And having set aside the body and the bodily formation, all the rest, whether classified as conditioned or unconditioned, is neither the body nor the bodily formation.' The same method applies to the rest. In other cases, in both the forward and reverse sequences, the method of questioning and answering should be understood everywhere in this way: 'Is the body the bodily formation? No. Are formations the verbal formation? The verbal formation is both a formation and a verbal formation. The remaining formations are formations, but not verbal formations. Is that which is not a formation also not a verbal formation? Yes.' And so on.

Pavattivāre pana “yassa kāyasaṅkhāro uppajjati, tassa vacīsaṅkhāro uppajjatīti? Vinā vitakkavicārehi assāsapassāsānaṃ uppādakkhaṇe tesaṃ kāyasaṅkhāro uppajjati, netaro, savitakkasavicāracittasamaṅgīnaṃ pana kāmāvacarasattānaṃ tadubhayampi uppajjati. Yassa vā pana…pe… uppajjatīti? Rūpārūpabhavikānaṃ vitakkavicāruppādakkhaṇe vacīsaṅkhārova uppajjati, netaro…pe… yathāvuttakāmāvacarānaṃ pana tadubhayaṃ uppajjati. Yassa kāyasaṅkhāro uppajjati, tassa cittasaṅkhāro uppajjatīti? Āmantā…pe… yassa vā pana…pe… uppajjatīti…pe… assāsapassāsānaṃ uppādakkhaṇe tadubhayaṃ uppajjati. Yassa vacīsaṅkhāro uppajjati, tassa cittasaṅkhāro uppajjatīti? Āmantā…pe… yattha kāyasaṅkhāro uppajjati, tattha vacīsaṅkhāro uppajjatīti[M 0.0410]? Kāmāvacarasattānaṃ dutiyajjhāne tatiyajjhāne tattha kāyasaṅkhārova uppajjati, netaro, paṭhamajjhānādīsu pana tadubhayaṃ uppajjati. Yattha vā pana [V 0.0314] …pe… uppajjatīti? Kāmāvacare uppajjati, na rūpārūpabhavesu. Yattha kāyasaṅkhāro uppajjati, tattha cittasaṅkhāro uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Yattha vā pana…pe… uppajjatīti? Kāmāvacarasattānaṃ catutthajjhāne rūpārūpabhave ca tattha cittasaṅkhārova uppajjati, netaro, itarajjhānādīsu pana tadubhayaṃ uppajjatī”tiādinā,

In the section on occurrence, however: 'For whom the bodily formation arises, does the verbal formation arise for them? For those without applied thought and sustained thought, at the moment of the arising of in-and-out breathing, the bodily formation arises for them, but not the other. However, for beings in the sense-sphere realm possessing a mind accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, both arise. Or for whom does the verbal formation arise? For those existing in the form and formless realms, at the moment when applied thought and sustained thought arise, only the verbal formation arises, not the other... but for those in the sense-sphere realm as stated, both arise. For whom the bodily formation arises, does the mental formation arise for them? Yes... Or for whom does the mental formation arise?... At the moment of the arising of in-and-out breathing, both arise. For whom the verbal formation arises, does the mental formation arise for them? Yes... Where the bodily formation arises, does the verbal formation arise there? For beings in the sense-sphere realm, in the second and third jhānas, only the bodily formation arises there, not the other. But in the first jhāna and so on, both arise. Or where does the verbal formation arise? It arises in the sense-sphere realm, not in the form or formless existences. Where the bodily formation arises, does the mental formation arise there? Yes. Or where does the mental formation arise? For beings in the sense-sphere realm, in the fourth jhāna, and in the form and formless existences, only the mental formation arises there, not the other. But in the other jhānas and so on, both arise.' And so on.

“Yassa kāyasaṅkhāro nuppajjati, tassa vacīsaṅkhāro nuppajjatīti? Vinā assāsapassāsehi vitakkavicārānaṃ uppādakkhaṇe tesaṃ kāyasaṅkhārova nuppajjati, netaro, sabbesaṃ cittassa bhaṅgakkhaṇe vinā assāsapassāsehi avitakkaavicāracittassa uppādakkhaṇe nirodhasamāpannānaṃ asaññasattānañca tadubhayampi nuppajjati…pe… yassa kāyasaṅkhāro nuppajjati, tassa cittasaṅkhāro nuppajjatīti…pe… sabbacittānaṃ bhaṅgakkhaṇe nirodhasamāpannānaṃ asaññasattānañca nuppajjatī”tiādinā ca, “yattha kāyasaṅkhāro nuppajjati, tattha vacīsaṅkhāro nuppajjatīti…pe… catutthajjhānakkhaṇe rūpabhavādīsu nuppajjatī”tiādinā ca, “yassa kāyasaṅkhāro uppajjittha, tassa vacīsaṅkhāro uppajjitthāti? Āmantā”tiādinā, “yassa kāyasaṅkhāro nuppajjittha, tassa cittasaṅkhāro nuppajjitthāti? Natthī”tiādinā, “yassa yattha kāyasaṅkhāro nuppajjittha, tassa tattha vacīsaṅkhāro nuppajjitthāti…pe… catutthajjhānaṃ samāpannānaṃ suddhāvāsānaṃ dutiye citte vattamāne asaññasattānaṃ tesaṃ tattha kāyasaṅkhāro ca nuppajjittha vacīsaṅkhāro cā”tiādinā ca,

'For one for whom bodily formation does not arise, does verbal formation not arise for them? With the exception of in-breaths and out-breaths, at the moment of the arising of applied thought and sustained thought, only bodily formation does not arise for them, not the other. At the moment of the dissolution of all consciousness, at the moment of the arising of consciousness without applied thought and sustained thought (with the exception of in-breaths and out-breaths), and for those attained to cessation and for non-percipient beings, both do not arise… For one for whom bodily formation does not arise, does mental formation not arise for them?… At the moment of the dissolution of all consciousness, and for those attained to cessation and for non-percipient beings, it does not arise.' And also by such passages as, 'Where bodily formation does not arise, does verbal formation not arise there?… At the moment of the fourth jhāna, in the realms of form and so on, it does not arise.' And also, 'For one for whom bodily formation had arisen, had verbal formation arisen for them? Yes.' And, 'For one for whom bodily formation had not arisen, had mental formation not arisen for them? There is not.' And also, 'For one for whom bodily formation had not arisen in a certain place, had verbal formation not arisen there?… For those attained to the fourth jhāna, for the Pure Abode beings when the second consciousness is occurring, and for non-percipient beings, for them there bodily formation had not arisen and verbal formation also had not arisen,' and so on.

“Yassa kāyasaṅkhāro uppajjissati, tassa vacīsaṅkhāro uppajjissatīti? Āmantā. Yassa vā pana…pe… uppajjissatīti? Yassa cittassa anantarā kāmāvacarānaṃ pacchimacittaṃ uppajjissati, rūpārūpabhave pacchimabhavikānaṃ vacīsaṅkhārova uppajjissati, na kāyasaṅkhāro[M 0.0411], aññesaṃ pana tadubhayaṃ uppajjissatī”tiādinā ca, “yassa kāyasaṅkhāro nuppajjissati, tassa vacīsaṅkhāro nuppajjissatīti…pe… pacchimacittasamaṅgīnaṃ yassa cittassa anantarā avitakkaavicāraṃ pacchimacittaṃ uppajjissati, tesaṃ tadubhayaṃ nuppajjissatī”tiādinā sabbakālabhedesu yathānurūpato uppādavāre yojanānayo veditabbo. “Yassa kāyasaṅkhāro nirujjhati, tassa vacīsaṅkhāro nirujjhatīti…pe… paṭhamajjhānaṃ samāpannānaṃ kāmāvacarānaṃ assāsapassāsānaṃ bhaṅgakkhaṇe tadubhayaṃ nirujjhati. Yassa kāyasaṅkhāro nirujjhati, tassa cittasaṅkhāro nirujjhatīti? Āmantā”tiādinā nirodhavāre, “yassa [V 0.0315] kāyasaṅkhāro uppajjati, tassa vacīsaṅkhāro nirujjhatīti? No”tiādinā uppādanirodhavāre ca,

“For one for whom bodily formation will arise, will verbal formation arise? Yes. Or for one for whom… will it arise? For one whose consciousness is immediately followed by the final consciousness of the sense-sphere, for those in their final existence in the form and formless realms, only verbal formation will arise, not bodily formation; for others, both will arise.” And similarly, “For one for whom bodily formation will not arise, will verbal formation not arise?… For those endowed with the final consciousness, whose consciousness is immediately followed by the final consciousness without applied thought and sustained thought, for them, both will not arise.” And so on. In all divisions of time, the method of application in the arising section should be understood as is appropriate. “For one for whom bodily formation ceases, does verbal formation cease?… For those who have attained the first jhāna, for sense-sphere beings, at the moment of the dissolution of in-breaths and out-breaths, both cease. For one for whom bodily formation ceases, does mental formation cease? Yes.” And so on in the cessation section; and “For one for whom bodily formation arises, does verbal formation cease? No.” And so on in the arising-and-cessation section.

“Yo kāyasaṅkhāraṃ parijānāti, so vacīsaṅkhāraṃ parijānātīti? Āmantā”tiādinā pariññāvāre ca heṭṭhā vuttānusārena sabbattha pāḷinayo veditabbo.

“One who fully comprehends bodily formation, does one fully comprehend verbal formation? Yes.” And so on. In the full comprehension section, the method of the Pāli should be understood everywhere in accordance with what was stated before.

Pavattivāre panettha paccuppannakāle puggalavārassa anulomanaye kāyasaṅkhāramūlakāni dve, vacīsaṅkhāramūlakaṃ ekanti tīṇeva yamakāni labbhanti. Tassa paṭilomanayepi okāsavārādīsupi eseva nayo. Evamettha sabbavāresu tiṇṇaṃ tiṇṇaṃ yamakānaṃ vasena yamakagaṇanā veditabbā. Atthavinicchaye panettha idaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ – imasmiṃ hi saṅkhārayamake “assāsapassāsānaṃ uppādakkhaṇe, vitakkavicārānaṃ uppādakkhaṇe”tiādivacanato (yama. 2.saṅkhārayamaka.19) paccuppannādikālabhedo pavattivasenāpi gahetabbo, na cutipaṭisandhivaseneva. “Dutiyajjhāne tatiyajjhāne tattha kāyasaṅkhāro uppajjatī”tiādivacanato (yama. 2.saṅkhārayamaka.21) ca jhānampi okāsavasena gahitanti veditabbaṃ. Evamettha yaṃ yaṃ labbhati, tassa tassa vasena atthavinicchayo [M 0.0412] veditabbo. Tatridaṃ nayamukhaṃ – “vinā vitakkavicārehī”ti dutiyatatiyajjhānavasena vuttaṃ, na catutthajjhānavasena tattha assāsapassāsānaṃ abhāvato. “Cittassa bhaṅgakkhaṇe”ti idaṃ kāyasaṅkhārassa ekantacittasamuṭṭhānattā vuttaṃ, uppajjamānameva hi cittaṃ rūpaṃ, arūpaṃ vā samuṭṭhāpeti, na bhijjamānaṃ, ṭhitaṃ vā. “Pacchimacittasamaṅgīna”nti sabbapacchimena appaṭisandhikacittena samaṅgīnaṃ khīṇāsavānaṃ. “Avitakkaavicāraṃ pacchimacitta”nti ettha rūpāvacarānaṃ dutiyajjhānikādicuticittavasena, arūpāvacarānañca catutthajjhānikacuticittavasena attho gahetabbo.

Here, in the occurrence section, in the present time of the individual section, in the forward method, two dyads rooted in bodily formation and one dyad rooted in verbal formation are obtained, thus three dyads in total. This same method applies to the reverse method and to the location sections, etc. Thus, in all sections, the counting of dyads should be understood on the basis of three dyads each. Here, in the analysis of meaning, this is the characteristic: in this formation dyad, from statements such as “at the moment of the arising of in-breaths and out-breaths, at the moment of the arising of applied thought and sustained thought,” the distinction of present time, etc., should be understood as based on the mode of occurrence, not solely on the mode of death and rebirth-linking. And from statements such as “in the second jhāna, in the third jhāna, the bodily formation arises there,” it should be understood that jhāna is also taken on the basis of location. Here, for whatever is obtainable, the analysis of meaning should be understood on that basis. Herein, this is the method of exposition: “Without applied thought and sustained thought” is stated with reference to the second and third jhānas, not the fourth jhāna, because in-breaths and out-breaths are absent there. “At the moment of the breaking up of consciousness” is stated because bodily formation is exclusively mind-originated; for it is only arising consciousness that originates material or immaterial form, not consciousness that is breaking up or static. “Endowed with the final consciousness” refers to the destroyers of the taints, those endowed with the very last consciousness, which does not link to rebirth. “The final consciousness without applied thought and sustained thought”—here, the meaning should be taken with reference to the death-consciousness of the second jhāna and so on for those in the form realm, and the death-consciousness of the fourth jhāna for those in the formless realm.

“Yassa kāyasaṅkhāro nirujjhati, tassa cittasaṅkhāro nirujjhatī”ti ettha niyamato kāyasaṅkhārassa cittasaṅkhārena saddhiṃ ekakkhaṇe nirujjhanato “āmantā”ti paṭivacanaṃ dinnaṃ na ekacittakkhaṇikattā. Cittasaṅkhāro hi kāyasaṅkhārena vināpi uppajjati ca nirujjhati ca. Kāyasaṅkhāro pana cittasamuṭṭhānattā yena cittena saddhiṃ uppajjati, tato paṭṭhāya sattarasamena saddhiṃ nirujjhati, esā cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa dhammatā. Yaṃ pana vibhaṅgappakaraṇassa sīhaḷaṭṭhakathāya “cittasamuṭṭhānarūpaṃ sattarasamacittassa uppādakkhaṇe nirujjhatī”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ imāya [V 0.0316] pāḷiyā virujjhati. “Yassa kāyasaṅkhāro uppajjati, tassa vacīsaṅkhāro nirujjhatī”ti ettha yasmā kāyasaṅkhāro cittassa uppādakkhaṇe uppajjati, na ca tasmiṃ khaṇe vitakkavicārā nirujjhanti, tasmā “no”ti paṭisedho kato. Iminā nayamukhena sabbattha vinicchayo veditabbo. Ayaṃ saṅkhārayamakamātikatthasaṃvaṇṇanānayo.

Regarding: “For one for whom bodily formation ceases, does mental formation cease?”—here, the reply “Yes” is given because bodily formation necessarily ceases at the same moment as mental formation, not because they are phenomena lasting for a single consciousness-moment. For mental formation arises and ceases even without bodily formation. Bodily formation, however, being mind-originated, arises together with a certain consciousness and, starting from then, ceases together with the seventeenth consciousness; this is the nature of mind-originated matter. But what is stated in the Sinhala commentary to the Vibhaṅga, that “mind-originated matter ceases at the arising moment of the seventeenth consciousness,” contradicts this Pāli passage. Regarding: “For one for whom bodily formation arises, does verbal formation cease?”—here, because bodily formation arises at the arising moment of a consciousness, and applied thought and sustained thought do not cease at that moment, the denial “No” is made. By this method of exposition, the analysis should be understood in all cases. This is the method of explaining the meaning of the matrix of the formation dyad.

Anusayayamakamātikatthavaṇṇanā

The Exposition of the Meaning of the Mātikā to the Anusaya Yamaka

Anusayayamakamātikāya pana pāḷivavatthānaṃ tāva evaṃ veditabbaṃ. Anusayayamakepi khandhayamakamātikādīsu viya desanaṃ [M 0.0413] akatvā aññena nayena pāḷidesanā katā. Kathaṃ? Paṭhamaṃ tāva paricchedavāro paricchinnuddesavāroti dve vārā uddesavasena desitā, tato uppattiṭṭhānavāroti eko khuddakavāro. Tato anusayavāro sānusayavāro pajahanavāro pariññāvāro pahīnavāro uppajjanavāro dhātuvāroti anusaye yojetvā yamakavasena papañcato niddiṭṭhā satta mahāvārāti aṭṭhakaniddesavasena desitā, evaṃ dasahi vārehi anusayayamakadesanā katā. Tesu ye ime hi paricchedavārotiādinā dve vārā uddesavasena vuttā, te idha anusayayamakamātikāti gahetabbā.

Now, in the Mātikā to the Anusaya Yamaka, the arrangement of the Pāli text should first be understood as follows. In the Anusaya Yamaka, unlike in the Mātikā to the Khandha Yamaka and others, the teaching is not given in the same way; instead, the Pāli teaching is given in a different manner. How? First, the section on delimitation (paricchedavāra) and the section on the summary of what is delimited (paricchinnuddesavāra)—these two sections are taught by way of summary. Then there is the section on the place of arising (uppattiṭṭhānavāra), a minor section. After that, the section on underlying tendencies (anusayavāra), the section on things with underlying tendencies (sānusayavāra), the section on abandoning (pajahanavāra), the section on full comprehension (pariññāvāra), the section on what is abandoned (pahīnavāra), the section on arising (uppajjanavāra), and the section on elements (dhātuvāra)—these seven major sections are set forth in detail by way of the yamaka method, applying them to the underlying tendencies, and are taught by way of the ‘exposition of the octads.’ Thus, the teaching of the Anusaya Yamaka is given in ten sections. Among these, those two sections mentioned first by way of summary, beginning with the section on delimitation, are to be taken here as the Mātikā to the Anusaya Yamaka.

Tattha hi satta anusayāti ayaṃ gaṇanāya paricchinditvā anusayānaṃ desitattā paricchedavāro nāma. Kāmarāgānusayo…pe… avijjānusayoti ayaṃ paricchedavasena paricchinnānaṃ nāmamattaṃ uddisitvā “ime nāma te”ti desitattā paricchinnuddesavāro nāma. Tattha anuttānatthato tāva anusayāti kenaṭṭhena anusayā? Anusayanaṭṭhena. Ko esa anusayanaṭṭho nāmāti? Appahīnaṭṭho. Kāmarāgānusayādayo hi appahīnaṭṭhena tassa tassa santāne anusenti nāma, tasmā “anusayā”ti vuccanti, anusentīti ca taṃ taṃ anurūpaṃ kāraṇaṃ labhitvā uppajjantīti attho. Athāpi siyā – anusayanaṭṭho nāma appahīnākāro, appahīnākāro ca na uppajjati, tasmā anusayā na uppajjantīti. Tatridaṃ paṭivacanaṃ – appahīnākāro anusayo, anusayoti pana appahīnaṭṭhena thāmagatakileso vuccati, so cittasampayutto sārammaṇo sappaccayaṭṭhena sahetuko ekantākusalova hoti kathāvatthusmiṃ (kathā. 554 ādayo) anusayānaṃ cittavippayuttabhāvassa paṭisedhitattā[M 0.0414], so ca atītopi hoti, anāgatopi paccuppannopi, tasmā uppajjatīti vattuṃ yuttaṃ. Tathā hi dhammasaṅgahe mohassa padabhājane 317 “avijjānusayo avijjāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… ayaṃ tasmiṃ samaye moho hotī”ti (dha. sa. 390). Imasmiñca yamake uppajjanavāre “yassa kāmarāgānusayo uppajjati, tassa paṭighānusayo uppajjatī”tiādi vuttaṃ, tasmā “anusentīti taṃ taṃ anurūpaṃ kāraṇaṃ labhitvā uppajjantī”ti yaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ suvuttanti veditabbaṃ. Kāmarāgānusayoti kāmarāgo ca so appahīnaṭṭhena anusayo cāti kāmarāgānusayo. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo. Ayaṃ tāvettha anuttānattho. Atthavinicchayo panetthāpi niddesanayamukhadassanavaseneva hoti, niddeso cettha heṭṭhā vutto.

Here, since the seven underlying tendencies are taught by delimiting them through enumeration, this is called the section on delimitation. 'The underlying tendency of sensual desire… up to… the underlying tendency of ignorance'—this is called the section on the indication of the delimited, as it merely indicates the names of what has been delimited and teaches, 'These are their names.' Now, first, as to the unelaborated meaning of 'underlying tendency' (anusaya): In what sense are they underlying tendencies? In the sense of lying latent. And what is this sense of lying latent? It is the sense of not being abandoned. For the underlying tendencies, such as that of sensual desire, lie latent in the continuum of a being because they have not been abandoned; thus, they are called 'underlying tendencies,' and 'they lie latent' means that they arise upon obtaining a suitable cause. But one might argue: the sense of lying latent is the state of not being abandoned, and what is not abandoned does not arise; therefore, underlying tendencies do not arise. To this, the reply is: the state of not being abandoned is the underlying tendency, but 'underlying tendency' refers to a defilement that has become a persistent force due to not being abandoned. When associated with the mind, it has an object, has a condition, and has a root-cause, and is exclusively unwholesome, as the Kathāvatthu (e.g., Kathā. 554ff) denies that underlying tendencies can be dissociated from the mind. Moreover, it exists in the past, future, and present. Therefore, it is proper to say that it arises. Indeed, in the Dhammasaṅgaṇī, in the analysis of terms for delusion, it is said: 'The underlying tendency of ignorance, the obsession of ignorance… at that time, this is delusion' (Dhs. 390). And in this Yamaka, in the section on arising, it is said: 'For whom the underlying tendency of sensual desire arises, for him the underlying tendency of aversion arises,' and so on. Therefore, what was said—'they arise upon obtaining a suitable cause'—should be understood as well-stated. 'The underlying tendency of sensual desire': it is sensual desire and it is an underlying tendency in the sense of not being abandoned; thus, it is the underlying tendency of sensual desire. The same method applies to the remaining terms. This, then, is the unelaborated meaning here. As for the determination of the meaning, it should be understood here too only by way of showing the introduction to the method of exposition, for the exposition has already been stated below.

Uppattiṭṭhānavārādayo aṭṭha vārā ca, tatrāyaṃ pāḷivavatthānānupubbikāmukhamattappakāsanā. Tesaṃ hi paṭhamo anusayānaṃ uppattiṭṭhānavāro nāma. Tattha vārabhedo yamakayojanavāre natthi, itaresu pana sattasu mahāvāresu atthi. Tesu hi paṭhamo anusayavāro anulomapaṭilomanayavasena duvidho hoti. Tattha anulomanaye “yassa yattha…pe… anusetī”ti puggalokāsatadubhayanāmavasena tayo antaravārā honti, tesu ekekasmiṃ ekamūlakadvimūlakatimūlakacatumūlakapañcamūlakachamūlakānaṃ vasena yamakabhedā honti. Yathā ca anulomanaye, evaṃ paṭilomanayepi veditabbā. Yathā cettha anusayavāre, evaṃ sānusayavārapajahanavārapariññāvārapahīnavārauppajjanavāresu pañcasupi. Ayaṃ panettha purimesu tīsu vāresu viseso. Okāsavāre “yattha tatthā”ti avatvā “yato tato”ti nissakkavacanena desanā katā. Sesaṃ tādisameva[M 0.0415]. Yo panāyaṃ sabbapacchimo dhātuvāro nāma, so pucchāvāro vissajjanavāroti dvidhā ṭhito. Tattha pucchāvāro anulomapaṭilomavasena duvidho. Tassāvasāne pucchānukkamena vissajjanaṃ katanti. Evaṃ tāvettha pāḷivavatthānaṃ veditabbaṃ.

The eight sections beginning with the section on the place of origination, and here is a mere introductory exposition of the sequential arrangement of the Pali text. Among these, the first is called the section on the place of origination of underlying tendencies. There, a division of sections is not found in the section on the application of pairs, but it is present in the remaining seven major sections. Among these, the first section on underlying tendencies is twofold: in forward order and reverse order. There, in the forward order, the phrase "In whom, in what... the underlying tendency lies" is divided into three intermediate sections by way of the names of the individual, the location, and both. In each of these, there are divisions into pairs based on one root, two roots, three roots, four roots, five roots, and six roots. As in the forward order, so too should the reverse order be understood. And as here in the section on underlying tendencies, so too in the five sections: the section with underlying tendencies, the section on abandoning, the section on comprehension, the section on having abandoned, and the section on arising. Here, however, there is a distinction in the first three sections. In the section on location, instead of saying "where, there," the exposition is given with the expression "from where, thence," by means of the ablative case. The rest is similar. The very last section, called the section on elements, is twofold: the section of questions and the section of answers. There, the section of questions is twofold: in forward and reverse order. At its conclusion, the answers are given in accordance with the sequence of the questions. Thus far, the arrangement of the Pali text should be understood.

Tatridaṃ aṭṭhannaṃ vārānaṃ ādito paṭṭhāya mukhamattadassanaṃ. “Kattha kāmarāgānusayo anuseti? Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu ettha kāmarāgānusayo anuseti. Kattha paṭighānusayo anuseti? Dukkhāya vedanāya…pe… mānānusayo kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ca anuseti. Diṭṭhānusayo, vicikicchānusayo ca sabbasakkāyapariyāpannesu dhammesu, bhavarāgānusayo rūpārūpadhātūsu, avijjānusayo sabbasakkāyapariyāpannesu dhammesu anusetī”ti ayaṃ tāva paṭhamavāre pāḷinayo.

Here now is a brief overview of these eight sections, starting from the beginning. "Where does the underlying tendency of sensual desire lie? The underlying tendency of sensual desire lies in the two feelings in the sense-sphere. Where does the underlying tendency of aversion lie? In painful feeling... The underlying tendency of conceit lies in the two feelings in the sense-sphere, in the form-sphere, and in the formless-sphere. The underlying tendency of views and the underlying tendency of doubt lie in all phenomena included in the personality-view. The underlying tendency of craving for existence lies in the form-sphere and formless-sphere. The underlying tendency of ignorance lies in all phenomena included in the personality-view." This, for now, is the Pali method in the first section.

Tattha [V 0.0318] kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsūti kāmāvacarabhūmiyaṃ sukhāya ceva upekkhāya cāti dvīsu vedanāsu, kāmarāgānusayo pana sahajātavasena, ārammaṇavasena cāti dvīhākārehi anuseti uppajjati, tattha akusalāhi sukhaupekkhāhi sahajātopi hutvā tā ārammaṇaṃ katvāpi uppajjati. Avasesā pana kāmāvacarakusalavipākakiriyavedanā ārammaṇameva katvā uppajjati, imāsu vedanāsu anusayamāno cesa tāhi vedanāhi sampayuttesu saññāsaṅkhāraviññāṇesupi anusetiyeva. Imāsaṃ pana vedanānaṃ assādaṭṭhena kāmarāgānusayuppattiyā sesasampayuttehi padhānattā, oḷārikattena veneyyānaṃ subodhattā ca dvīsu vedanāsuyeva anusetīti vuttaṃ, evaṃ uparipi. Na kevalañcesa anusayamāno imāsu dvīsu vedanāsuyeva, vedanāsampayuttesu dhammesu ca anuseti, iṭṭhesu [M 0.0416] pana rūpādīsupi anuseti eva. Vuttampi cetaṃ vibhaṅgappakaraṇe “yaṃ loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ, ettha sattānaṃ kāmarāgānusayo anusetī”ti (vibha. 816), etthānusayayamakepi vuttaṃ “dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā ettha kāmarāgānusayo nānusetī”tiādi. Etena vuttāvasesarūpādīsu chasupi ārammaṇesu anusetīti vuttaṃ hoti. Idha pana taṃ sabbaṃ avatvā kiñcideva padhānattādinā kāraṇena vuttanti gahetabbaṃ.

Here, 'in the two feelings in the sense-sphere' means in the two feelings, namely, pleasant and neutral, in the plane of sensual existence. The underlying tendency of sensual desire, however, lies latent and arises in two ways: by way of co-arising and by way of object. There, it arises both co-arising with unwholesome pleasant and neutral feelings, and by taking them as its object. With respect to the remaining wholesome, resultant, and functional feelings of the sensual realm, it arises only by taking them as its object. While lying latent in these feelings, it also lies latent in the perceptions, formations, and consciousness associated with them. However, because the arising of the underlying tendency of sensual desire is primarily due to the enjoyment aspect of these feelings, and because they are prominent among the remaining associated factors, and because they are easily understood by those to be trained due to their grossness, it is said to lie latent in just these two feelings. The same applies in subsequent cases. Not only does it lie latent in these two feelings, but it also lies latent in the phenomena associated with feeling. Moreover, it also lies latent in desirable forms and so on. This is also stated in the Vibhaṅga: "Whatever in the world is agreeable and pleasing, therein the underlying tendency of sensual desire lies latent in beings" (Vibh. 816). And here in the Anusaya Yamaka, it is said: "In painful feeling and in the form realm, the underlying tendency of sensual desire does not lie latent," and so on. By this, it is shown that it lies latent in all six objects, including the remaining forms, etc., mentioned previously. Here, however, without stating all that, it is to be understood that only a part is mentioned due to reasons such as prominence.

Dukkhāyāti ettha paṭighacittasampayuttā dve domanassavedanā, kāyaviññāṇasampayuttā dukkhavedanā cāti tisso vedanā, taṃ sampayuttā ca dhammā, aniṭṭhā cha rūpādayo dhammā paṭighānusayasahajātavasena, ārammaṇavasena ca yathārahaṃ anusayanaṭṭhānaṃ. Kiṃ pana itarā dve vedanā iṭṭhārammaṇaṃ vā paṭighassa ārammaṇaṃ na hontīti? No na honti. Parihīnajjhānassa hi naṭṭhaṃ iṭṭhaṃ sasampayuttadhammaṃ jhānamārabbha domanassaṃ uppajjati, taṃ pana ārammaṇamattameva, nānusayanaṭṭhānaṃ iṭṭhattā. Aniṭṭhameva hi iṭṭhato paṭihanananimittaṃ, yaṃ pana tatthuppannaṃ, tassa paṭighamattameva hoti, na paṭighānusayoti. Paṭighānusayo hi aniṭṭhārammaṇe paṭihananavasena uppanno thāmagato kileso, itaro domanassena saddhiṃ uppannopi attano paṭihananakiccassa akaraṇato paṭighānusayo na hoti, abbohārikattaṃ gacchati. Yathā hi pāṇātipātacetanāya saddhiṃ uppannopi byāpādo manokammaṃ nāma na hoti, abbohārikattaṃ gacchati, evanti gahetabbaṃ. Teneva nekkhammassitaṃ domanassaṃ sevitabbaṃ vuttaṃ. Mānānusayassa pana dukkhadomanassavajjitā sabbe lokiyā dhammā anusayanaṭṭhānaṃ. “Dukkhāya vedanāya apariyāpanne ettha…pe… mānānusayo ca nānusetī”ti hi [M 0.0417] vuttaṃ. Diṭṭhānusayavicikicchānusayānaṃ pana lokuttaravajjitā sabbepi dhammā anusayanaṭṭhānaṃ. Tena vuttaṃ “sabbasakkāyapariyāpannesu [V 0.0319] dhammesū”ti. Tattha saṃsāravaṭṭanissitaṭṭhena sakkāyapariyāpannesu sabbadhammesūti attho. Evaṃ avijjānusayopi veditabbo. Sabbattha ca sahajātārammaṇabhedo heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva veditabbo.

Here, by 'painful' (dukkhāya) are meant three feelings: the two feelings of displeasure associated with aversion-consciousness, and the painful feeling associated with body-consciousness. Along with these, the states associated with them, and the six undesirable phenomena beginning with forms, are the grounds for the latent tendency of aversion, either by way of co-nascence or by way of object, as appropriate. But are the other two feelings—pleasant and neutral—not objects for aversion? It is not that they are not. For when a meditator has lost a desirable jhāna, displeasure arises regarding that desirable jhāna and its associated states, but that jhāna is merely an object and not a ground for the latent tendency because it is desirable. For only the undesirable is the basis for striking back; but what arises there is merely aversion, not the latent tendency of aversion. For the latent tendency of aversion is a defilement that has become strong, arisen by way of striking against an undesirable object; the other, even though arisen with displeasure, does not become the latent tendency of aversion because it does not perform its function of striking, and thus becomes insignificant. Just as ill-will, even though arisen with the intention to kill, is not called mental action (manokamma) and becomes insignificant, so too should this be understood. Therefore, it is said that displeasure rooted in renunciation should be cultivated. As for the latent tendency of conceit, all worldly phenomena, excluding painful and displeasurable feelings, are its grounds. For it is said: 'In what is not encompassed by painful feeling... the latent tendency of conceit does not lie dormant.' For the latent tendencies of wrong view and doubt, all phenomena, excluding the supramundane, are their grounds. Hence it is said: 'In all phenomena encompassed by identity.' Here, 'encompassed by identity' means all phenomena rooted in the cycle of existence. Similarly, the latent tendency of ignorance should be understood. And in all cases, the distinction between co-nascence and object should be understood in the manner stated above.

Bhavarāgānusayo pana kiñcāpi diṭṭhivippayuttesu catūsu cittesu uppajjanato sahajātavasena kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu anusetīti vattabbo bhaveyya, so pana yasmā rūpārūpāvacaramevārammaṇaṃ labhati, na kāmāvacarārammaṇameva, anusayānaṃ pana taṃ na anusayanaṭṭhānaṃ, tasmā ārammaṇavasena niyamaṃ akatvā “rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha bhavarāgānusayo anusetī”ti vuttaṃ. Taṃ rāgavasena so ca sabbopi rāgo kāmarāgānusayo gahetabboti ayaṃ uppattiṭṭhānavāre nayo.

However, although the latent tendency of craving for existence arises in the four types of consciousness dissociated from wrong view and, by way of co-nascence, it might be said to lie dormant in the two feelings of the sensuous sphere, yet because it obtains only objects of the form and formless spheres and not objects of the sensuous sphere—and a sensuous sphere object is not a ground for this latent tendency—therefore, without making a fixed rule based on the object, it is said: 'In the form sphere and the formless sphere, the latent tendency of craving for existence lies dormant.' As for craving, all such craving is to be taken as the latent tendency of sensual craving. This is the method in the section on the place of arising.

Itaresu pana sattasu mahāvāresu tāva “yassa kāmarāgānusayo anuseti, tassa paṭighānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā. Yassa vā pana paṭighānusayo anuseti, tassa kāmarāgānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā. Yassa kāmarāgānusayo anuseti, tassa mānānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā. Yassa vā pana mānānusayo anuseti, tassa kāmarāgānusayo anusetīti? Anāgāmissa mānānusayo anuseti, no ca tassa kāmarāgānusayo anuseti, tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ mānānusayo ca anuseti, kāmarāgānusayo ca anuseti. Yassa kāmarāgānusayo anuseti, tassa diṭṭhānusayo anusetīti? Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ kāmarāgānusayo anuseti, no ca…pe… diṭṭhānusayo ca anuseti, yassa vā pana…pe… āmantā. Yassa kāmarāgānusayo anuseti, tassa vicikicchānusayo [M 0.0418] anusetī”ti pucchāyapi diṭṭhānusayasadisameva vissajjanaṃ. Yassa kāmarāgānusayo anuseti, tassa bhavarāgānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā. Yassa vā pana…pe… anusetīti…pe… tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ bhavarāgānusayo ca anuseti, kāmarāgānusayo ca anuseti. Avijjānusayepi eseva nayo. Iminā nayena paṭighānusayādimūlikāsu pucchāsu vissajjananayo veditabbo. Ayaṃ ekamūlake nayo.

Now, among the remaining seven great sections, first: 'In whom the latent tendency of sensual craving lies dormant, does the latent tendency of aversion lie dormant? Yes. Or, in whom the latent tendency of aversion lies dormant, does the latent tendency of sensual craving lie dormant? Yes. In whom the latent tendency of sensual craving lies dormant, does the latent tendency of conceit lie dormant? Yes. Or, in whom the latent tendency of conceit lies dormant, does the latent tendency of sensual craving lie dormant? In a non-returner, the latent tendency of conceit lies dormant, but the latent tendency of sensual craving does not lie dormant in him. In three individuals, both the latent tendency of conceit and the latent tendency of sensual craving lie dormant. In whom the latent tendency of sensual craving lies dormant, does the latent tendency of wrong view lie dormant? In two individuals, the latent tendency of sensual craving lies dormant, but the latent tendency of wrong view does not lie dormant in them; in the ordinary person, both the latent tendency of sensual craving and the latent tendency of wrong view lie dormant. Or, in whom the latent tendency of wrong view lies dormant, does the latent tendency of sensual craving lie dormant? Yes. In whom the latent tendency of sensual craving lies dormant, does the latent tendency of doubt lie dormant?' In this question too, the answer is similar to that regarding the latent tendency of wrong view. 'In whom the latent tendency of sensual craving lies dormant, does the latent tendency of craving for existence lie dormant? Yes. Or, in whom the latent tendency of craving for existence lies dormant, does the latent tendency of sensual craving lie dormant? In a non-returner, the latent tendency of craving for existence lies dormant, but the latent tendency of sensual craving does not lie dormant in him. In three individuals, both the latent tendency of craving for existence and the latent tendency of sensual craving lie dormant.' The same method applies to the latent tendency of ignorance. By this method, the way of answering questions rooted in the latent tendency of aversion and so on should be understood. This is the method for the single-rooted section.

Yassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca anuseti, tassa mānānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā. Dvinnaṃ dvimūlikā…pe… pañcamūlikānaṃ pana ekamūle vuttānusārena vissajjananayo [V 0.0320] ñātabbo. Tatrāyaṃ pacchimānusaye yojanā – “yassa kāmarāgānusayo ca paṭighānusayo ca mānānusayo ca diṭṭhānusayo ca vicikicchānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca anuseti, tassa avijjānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā. Yassa vā pana avijjānusayo anuseti, tassa kāmarāgānusayo ca…pe… bhavarāgānusayo ca anusetīti? Anāgāmissa avijjānusayo ca mānānusayo ca bhavarāgānusayo ca anuseti, na itare, dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ avijjānusayo ca kāmarāgapaṭighamānabhavarāgānusayā ca anusenti, na diṭṭhivicikicchānusayā, puthujjanassa pana sabbepi anusentī”ti ayaṃ puggalavāre nayo.

In whom both the latent tendency of sensual craving and the latent tendency of aversion lie dormant, does the latent tendency of conceit lie dormant? Yes. However, for the two-rooted, three-rooted, four-rooted, and five-rooted questions, the method of answering should be understood according to what was stated in the single-rooted section. Here is the application to the last latent tendency: 'In whom the latent tendency of sensual craving, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of wrong view, the latent tendency of doubt, and the latent tendency of craving for existence all lie dormant, does the latent tendency of ignorance lie dormant? Yes. Or, in whom the latent tendency of ignorance lies dormant, do the latent tendency of sensual craving, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of wrong view, the latent tendency of doubt, and the latent tendency of craving for existence also lie dormant? In a non-returner, the latent tendency of ignorance, the latent tendency of conceit, and the latent tendency of craving for existence lie dormant, but not the others. In two individuals, the latent tendency of ignorance and the latent tendencies of sensual craving, aversion, conceit, and craving for existence lie dormant, but not the latent tendencies of wrong view and doubt. In an ordinary person, however, all the latent tendencies lie dormant.' This is the method in the section on individuals.

Okāsavāre pana “yattha kāmarāgānusayo anuseti, tattha paṭighānusayo anusetīti? No. Yattha vā pana…pe… anusetīti? No. Yattha kāmarāgānusayo anuseti, tattha mānānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā. Yattha vā pana mānānusayo anuseti, tattha kāmarāgānusayo anusetīti? Rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha mānānusayo anuseti[M 0.0419], na kāmarāgānusayo, kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tadubhayaṃ anuseti. Yattha kāmarāgānusayo…pe… anusetīti? Āmantā. Yattha vā pana…pe… anusetīti? Dukkhāya vedanāya rūpadhātuyā arūpadhātuyā ettha vicikicchānusayo anuseti, na kāmarāgānusayo, kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tadubhayaṃ anuseti. Yattha kāmarāgānusayo…pe… anuseti, tattha bhavarāgānusayo anusetīti? No. Yattha vā pana…pe… no. Yattha kāmarāgānusayo anuseti, tattha avijjānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā. Yattha vā pana…pe… anusetīti? Dukkhāya vedanāya rūpārūpadhātuyā ettha avijjānusayo anuseti, na kāmarāgānusayo, kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu tadubhayaṃ anuseti.

Regarding the section on occasions: 'Where the latent tendency of sensual craving lies dormant, does the latent tendency of aversion also lie dormant there? No. Or where the latent tendency of aversion lies dormant, does the latent tendency of sensual craving lie dormant? No. Where the latent tendency of sensual craving lies dormant, does the latent tendency of conceit lie dormant there? Yes. Or where the latent tendency of conceit lies dormant, does the latent tendency of sensual craving lie dormant there? In the form sphere and the formless sphere, the latent tendency of conceit lies dormant there, but not the latent tendency of sensual craving. In the two feelings of the sensuous sphere, both lie dormant. Where the latent tendency of sensual craving lies dormant, does the latent tendency of wrong view lie dormant? Yes. Or where the latent tendency of wrong view lies dormant, does the latent tendency of sensual craving lie dormant? In painful feeling, in the form sphere, and in the formless sphere, the latent tendency of wrong view lies dormant, but not the latent tendency of sensual craving. In the two feelings of the sensuous sphere, both lie dormant. Where the latent tendency of sensual craving lies dormant, does the latent tendency of craving for existence lie dormant? No. Or where the latent tendency of craving for existence lies dormant, does the latent tendency of sensual craving lie dormant? No. Where the latent tendency of sensual craving lies dormant, does the latent tendency of ignorance lie dormant? Yes. Or where the latent tendency of ignorance lies dormant, does the latent tendency of sensual craving lie dormant? In painful feeling, and in the form and formless spheres, the latent tendency of ignorance lies dormant, but not the latent tendency of sensual craving. In the two feelings of the sensuous sphere, both lie dormant.

Yattha paṭighānusayo anuseti, tattha mānānusayo anusetīti? No. Yattha vā pana…pe… no. Yattha paṭighānusayo anuseti, tattha diṭṭhānusayo vicikicchānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā. Yattha vā pana…pe… anusetīti? Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpārūpadhātuyā ettha vicikicchānusayo anuseti, na paṭighānusayo, dukkhāya pana vedanāya tadubhayaṃ anuseti. Yattha paṭighānusayo anuseti, tattha bhavarāgānusayo anusetīti? No. Yattha vā pana…pe… no. Yattha paṭighānusayo anuseti, tattha avijjānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā. Yattha vā pana…pe… anusetīti…pe… dukkhāya vedanāya tadubhayaṃ anuseti, aññattha avijjānusayo ca.

Where the latent tendency of aversion lies dormant, does the latent tendency of conceit lie dormant there? No. Or where the latent tendency of conceit lies dormant, does the latent tendency of aversion lie dormant there? No. Where the latent tendency of aversion lies dormant, do the latent tendencies of view and doubt lie dormant there? Yes. Or where the latent tendency of doubt lies dormant, does the latent tendency of aversion lie dormant there? In the two feelings of the sensuous sphere, and in the form and formless spheres, the latent tendency of doubt lies dormant, but not the latent tendency of aversion; however, in painful feeling, both lie dormant. Where the latent tendency of aversion lies dormant, does the latent tendency of craving for existence lie dormant there? No. Or where the latent tendency of craving for existence lies dormant, does the latent tendency of aversion lie dormant there? No. Where the latent tendency of aversion lies dormant, does the latent tendency of ignorance lie dormant there? Yes. Or where the latent tendency of ignorance lies dormant, does the latent tendency of aversion lie dormant there? In painful feeling, both lie dormant; elsewhere, only the latent tendency of ignorance.

Yattha [V 0.0321] mānānusayo anuseti, tattha diṭṭhānusayo vicikicchānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā. Yattha vā pana…pe… anusetīti? Dukkhāya vedanāya diṭṭhānusayova, netaro[M 0.0420], tadaññesu sabbattha anuseti. Yattha mānānusayo anuseti, tattha bhavarāgānusayo anusetīti? Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu mānānusayo, netaro, rūpārūpadhātuyā pana tadubhayaṃ anuseti. Yattha vā pana…pe… āmantā. Yattha mānānusayo anuseti, tattha avijjānusayo…pe… āmantā. Yattha vā pana…pe… anusetīti? Dukkhavedanaṃ ṭhapetvā tadaññāsu sabbattha tadubhayaṃ anuseti. Yattha diṭṭhānusayo, tattha vicikicchānusayo…pe… āmantā. Yattha diṭṭhānusayo, tattha bhavarāgānusayo anusetīti? Kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu diṭṭhānusayova, rūpārūpabhavesu tadubhayaṃ anuseti. Yattha vā pana…pe… āmantā. Yattha diṭṭhānusayo anuseti, tattha avijjānusayo…pe… āmantā. Yattha vā pana…pe… āmantā. Esa nayo vicikicchāmūlakesupi. Yattha bhavarāgānusayo, tattha avijjānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā. Yattha vā pana…pe… anuseti, tattha kāmadhātuyā tīsu vedanāsu avijjānusayova, rūpārūpabhavesu pana tadubhayaṃ anusetī”ti ayamettha ekamūlanayo.

Where the latent tendency of conceit lies dormant, do the latent tendencies of view and doubt lie dormant there? Yes. Or where the latent tendencies of view and doubt lie dormant, does the latent tendency of conceit lie dormant there? In painful feeling, only the latent tendency of view lies dormant, not the other; in all other cases, it lies dormant. Where the latent tendency of conceit lies dormant, does the latent tendency of craving for existence lie dormant there? In the sensuous sphere, in two feelings, the latent tendency of conceit lies dormant, not the other; but in the form and formless spheres, both lie dormant. Or where the latent tendency of craving for existence lies dormant, does the latent tendency of conceit lie dormant there? Yes. Where the latent tendency of conceit lies dormant, does the latent tendency of ignorance lie dormant there? Yes. Or where the latent tendency of ignorance lies dormant, does the latent tendency of conceit lie dormant there? Excluding painful feeling, in all other cases, both lie dormant. Where the latent tendency of view lies dormant, does the latent tendency of doubt lie dormant there? Yes. Where the latent tendency of view lies dormant, does the latent tendency of craving for existence lie dormant there? In the sensuous sphere, in three feelings, only the latent tendency of view lies dormant; in the form and formless existences, both lie dormant. Or where the latent tendency of craving for existence lies dormant, does the latent tendency of view lie dormant there? Yes. Where the latent tendency of view lies dormant, does the latent tendency of ignorance lie dormant there? Yes. Or where the latent tendency of ignorance lies dormant, does the latent tendency of view lie dormant there? Yes. This same method applies to cases rooted in doubt. Where the latent tendency of craving for existence lies dormant, does the latent tendency of ignorance lie dormant there? Yes. Or where the latent tendency of ignorance lies dormant, does the latent tendency of craving for existence lie dormant there? In the sensuous sphere, in three feelings, only the latent tendency of ignorance lies dormant; but in the form and formless existences, both lie dormant. This is the single-root method here.

“Yassa…pe… nānuseti. Yassa…pe… nānuseti mānānusayo, arahato pana tadubhayampi nānuseti. Yassa vā pana…pe… āmantā. Yassa kāmarāgānusayo nānuseti, tassa diṭṭhānusayo vicikicchānusayo nānusetīti? Āmantā. Yassa vā pana…pe… nānusetīti? Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ vicikicchānusayova nānuseti, netaro, anāgāmiarahantānaṃ tadubhayampi nānusetī”tiādinā nayena puggalavāre,

“In whom... does not lie dormant. In whom... the latent tendency of conceit does not lie dormant; but in an Arahant, both do not lie dormant. Or in whom... Yes. In whom the latent tendency of sensual craving does not lie dormant, do the latent tendencies of view and doubt not lie dormant in him? Yes. Or in whom the latent tendencies of view and doubt do not lie dormant, does the latent tendency of sensual craving not lie dormant in him? In two individuals, only the latent tendency of doubt does not lie dormant, not the other; in non-returners and Arahants, both do not lie dormant.” And so on, by this method in the section on individuals,

“Yattha kāmarāgānusayo nānuseti, tattha paṭighānusayo nānusetīti? Dukkhāya vedanāya kāmarāgānusayova nānuseti, netaro, rūpārūpadhātupariyāpannesu tadubhayaṃ nānuseti. Yattha vā pana…pe… nānusetīti[M 0.0421]? Kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu paṭighānusayova, rūpārūpapariyāpannesu pana tadubhayaṃ nānuseti. Yattha kāmarāgānusayo nānuseti, tattha mānānusayo nānusetīti? Rūpārūpadhātūsu kāmarāgānusayova, dukkhāya pana vedanāya, apariyāpannesu ca tadubhayaṃ nānuseti. Yattha vā pana…pe… āmantā. Yattha kāmarāgānusayo nānuseti, tattha diṭṭhānusayo, vicikicchānusayo nānusetīti? Dukkhāya vedanāya rūpārūpadhātūsu kāmarāgānusayova, apariyāpanne pana tadubhayaṃ nānusetī”tiādinā nayena okāsavāre ca,

“Where the latent tendency of sensual craving does not lie dormant, does the latent tendency of aversion not lie dormant there? In painful feeling, only the latent tendency of sensual craving does not lie dormant, not the other; in what pertains to the form and formless spheres, both do not lie dormant. Or where the latent tendency of aversion does not lie dormant, does the latent tendency of sensual craving not lie dormant there? In the sensuous sphere, in two feelings, only the latent tendency of aversion does not lie dormant; but in what pertains to the form and formless spheres, both do not lie dormant. Where the latent tendency of sensual craving does not lie dormant, does the latent tendency of conceit not lie dormant there? In the form and formless spheres, only the latent tendency of sensual craving does not lie dormant; but in painful feeling and in the unincluded, both do not lie dormant. Or where the latent tendency of conceit does not lie dormant, does the latent tendency of sensual craving not lie dormant there? Yes. Where the latent tendency of sensual craving does not lie dormant, do the latent tendencies of view and doubt not lie dormant there? In painful feeling and in the form and formless spheres, only the latent tendency of sensual craving does not lie dormant; but in the unincluded, both do not lie dormant.” And so on, by this method in the section on occasions, and

“Yassa [V 0.0322] yattha kāmarāgānusayo nānuseti, tassa tattha paṭighānusayo nānusetīti? Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ dukkhāya vedanāya kāmarāgānusayova, rūpārūpapariyāpannesu tadubhayaṃ nānuseti, dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ sabbattha tadubhayaṃ nānuseti. Yassa vā pana yattha…pe… nānusetīti? Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu paṭighānusayova, rūpārūpapariyāpannesu tadubhayaṃ nānuseti, dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ sabbattha tadubhayaṃ nānuseti. Yassa yattha kāmarāgānusayo nānuseti, tassa tattha mānānusayo nānusetīti? Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ rūpārūpadhātuyā kāmarāgānusayova, netaro, dukkhāya vedanāya, apariyāpanne ca tadubhayaṃ nānuseti, anāgāmissa kāmadhātuyā dvīsu vedanāsu rūpārūpadhātuyā kāmarāgānusayova, arahato pana sabbattha tadubhayaṃ nānusetī”tiādinā puggalokāsavāre ca vuttānusārena nayo ñātabboti ayaṃ pāḷinayo.

“For whom, where the latent tendency of sensual craving does not lie dormant, does the latent tendency of aversion not lie dormant there for him? For three individuals, in painful feeling, only the latent tendency of sensual craving does not lie dormant; in what pertains to the form and formless spheres, both do not lie dormant. For two individuals, in all cases, both do not lie dormant. Or for whom, where the latent tendency of aversion does not lie dormant, does the latent tendency of sensual craving not lie dormant there for him? For three individuals, in the sensuous sphere, in two feelings, only the latent tendency of aversion does not lie dormant; in what pertains to the form and formless spheres, both do not lie dormant. For two individuals, in all cases, both do not lie dormant. For whom, where the latent tendency of sensual craving does not lie dormant, does the latent tendency of conceit not lie dormant there for him? For three individuals, in the form and formless spheres, only the latent tendency of sensual craving does not lie dormant, not the other; in painful feeling and in the unincluded, both do not lie dormant. For the non-returner, in the sensuous sphere, in two feelings, and in the form and formless spheres, only the latent tendency of sensual craving does not lie dormant; but for the Arahant, in all cases, both do not lie dormant.” And so on. The method should be understood according to what has been stated in the section on individuals and occasions. This is the Pāli method.

Tattha “yassa kāmarāgānusayo anuseti, tassa paṭighānusayo anusetī”ti ettha yadetaṃ “āmantā”ti paṭivacanaṃ dinnaṃ, taṃ duddinnaṃ viya khāyati. Kasmā? Kāmarāgapaṭighānaṃ ekakkhaṇe anuppattito. Yathā hi “yassa manāyatanaṃ [M 0.0422] uppajjati, tassa dhammāyatanaṃ uppajjatī”tiādīsu manāyatanadhammāyatanādīni ekakkhaṇe uppajjanti, na tathā kāmarāgapaṭighā, visuññeva uppajjanato, tasmā ettha “no”ti paṭisedho kattabbo siyā, taṃ pana akatvā “āmantā”ti paṭivacanassa dinnattā heṭṭhā yamakesu viya ettha khaṇapaccuppannavasena vattamānavohāraṃ aggahetvā aññathā gahetabbo. Kathaṃ gahetabbo? Appahīnavasena. Appahīnataṃ hi sandhāya ayaṃ anusetīti vattamānavohāro vutto, na khaṇapaccuppannataṃ, tasmā imissā pucchāya yassa kāmarāgānusayo appahīno, na anuppattidhammataṃ āpādito, tassa paṭighānusayo appahīno, na anuppattidhammataṃ āpādito, tassa paṭighānusayo appahīnoti evamattho gahetabbo. Yasmā ca tesu kāmarāgapaṭighesu yasseko appahīno, tassa itaropi appahīnova hoti, tasmā “āmantā”ti vuttaṃ. Ito paresupi evarūpesu uppajjativārādivissajjanesu eseva nayo. Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānanti puthujjanasotāpannasakadāgāmīnaṃ. Dvinnanti sotāpannasakadāgāmīnaṃ. Evaṃ uppajjanaṃ dīpitaṃ. Okāsavārassa paṭhamadutiyapucchāsu yasmā kāmarāgapaṭighā ekacitte na uppajjanti, tasmā “no”ti paṭisedho kato. Dukamūlādīsu ca yasmā kāmarāgapaṭighādayo ekasmiṃ ṭhānasaṅkhāte citte, ārammaṇe vā na uppajjanti, tasmā “natthī”ti tattha paṭikkhepo kato, ayaṃ pucchā apubbā [V 0.0323] evāti adhippāyo. Puggalokāsavāre catunnanti puthujjanasotāpannasakadāgāmianāgāmīnaṃ. Paṭilome dvinnanti anāgāmiarahante sandhāya vuttanti ayaṃ anusayavāre nayo.

Here, concerning the statement, 'For whom the underlying tendency of sensual desire lies dormant, for him the underlying tendency of aversion lies dormant,' the 'Yes' given as a reply appears to be poorly given. Why? Because sensual desire and aversion do not arise in a single moment. For just as in cases like, 'When the mind-base arises, the mind-object-base arises,' the mind-base and the mind-object-base arise in a single moment, sensual desire and aversion do not arise in that way; they arise separately. Therefore, a 'No' negation should have been made here. However, since 'Yes' was given as a reply, the present usage should not be understood in the sense of momentary occurrence, as in the preceding Yamakas, but must be understood differently. How should it be understood? In the sense of non-abandonment. For this present usage 'lies dormant' is stated with reference to non-abandonment, not to momentary occurrence. Therefore, the meaning of this question should be understood thus: 'For whom the underlying tendency of sensual desire is unabandoned, not brought to the state of being unable to arise, for him the underlying tendency of aversion is also unabandoned.' And because, with respect to sensual desire and aversion, for one for whom one is unabandoned, the other is also unabandoned, therefore 'Yes' was stated. In similar answers in the chapters on arising, etc., that follow, this is the method. 'Of three persons' means of ordinary persons, stream-enterers, and once-returners. 'Of two' means of stream-enterers and once-returners. Thus, arising is explained. In the first and second questions of the chapter on occasion, since sensual desire and aversion do not arise in a single mind, 'No' is given as a negation. And in the sections on the root-pairs, etc., since sensual desire, aversion, etc., do not arise in a single mind—designated as a 'locus'—or in relation to a single object, 'There is not' is given there as a rejection.
