In this context, the object-dominance that is mundane wholesome serves as the object-dominance for both mundane wholesome states and consciousness accompanied by greed, but not for others. However, that which is unwholesome is said to arise only in consciousness accompanied by greed, because in other cases there is no state to be made weighty. This applies also to the two-rooted, rootless, and other mundane resultant material aggregates—they are only for consciousness accompanied by greed, not for others. Similarly, it is stated in the commentary that this applies also to functional states. This should be examined, as it does not contradict the fact that functional states associated with knowledge—such as those proceeding from the mastery of previous practices like omniscience and super-knowledge—can be made weighty by sense-sphere wholesome states. However, the supramundane wholesome states serve as object-dominance conditions only for the sense-sphere impulsion-moments associated with knowledge. It should be understood that Nibbāna is the object-dominant for those same supramundane wholesome and resultant states. This is the method in the dominance condition.

Anantarabhāvena upakārako dhammo anantarapaccayo, sova samanantarapaccayo, byañjanamattameva nānaṃ “upacayasantatī”tiādīsu viya. Yampi “atthānantaratāya anantarapaccayo, kālānantaratāya samanantarapaccayo”ti ācariyānaṃ mataṃ, taṃ “nirodhā vuṭṭhahantassa nevasaññānāsaññāyatanakusalaṃ phalasamāpattiyā samanantarapaccayena paccayo”tiādīhi virujjhati, taṃniddese “cakkhuviññāṇadhātu taṃsampayuttakā ca dhammā manodhātuyā…pe… kāyaviññāṇadhātu…pe… manodhātu…pe… manoviññāṇadhātuyā…pe… purimā purimā kusalā [V 0.0340] dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ [M 0.0444] kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ…pe… abyākatānaṃ dhammānaṃ…pe… purimā purimā akusalā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ akusalānaṃ…pe… abyākatānaṃ…pe… yesaṃ yesaṃ dhammānaṃ anantarā ye ye dhammā uppajjanti cittacetasikā dhammā, te te dhammā tesaṃ tesaṃ dhammānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo”ti iminā anantarapaccayaniddesasamako eva samanantarapaccayo niddiṭṭho aññatra nāmanānāttāti ayaṃ anantarasamanantarapaccayadvaye nayo.

The condition that assists by way of immediacy is the contiguity condition, and that itself is the proximity condition; the difference is merely in expression, as in terms like 'accumulation and continuity' and so on. And the opinion held by the teachers—"the contiguity condition is due to the contiguity of meaning, the proximity condition is due to the contiguity of time"—is contradicted by such passages as, "For one emerging from cessation, the wholesome state of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is a condition for the attainment of fruition by way of the proximity condition." In the exposition, the proximity condition is explained as identical to the exposition of the contiguity condition, differing only in name: "The eye-consciousness element and its associated states are a condition for the mind-element... the body-consciousness element... the mind-element... the mind-consciousness element... preceding wholesome states are a condition for subsequent wholesome states... for indeterminate states... preceding unwholesome states are a condition for subsequent unwholesome states... for indeterminate states... Immediately following whichever states, whichever consciousness and mental factors arise, those preceding states are a condition for those subsequent states by way of the contiguity condition." This is the method regarding the two conditions of contiguity and proximity.

Uppajjamānova saha uppajjamānabhāvena upakārako dhammo sahajātapaccayo, so niddese “cattāro khandhā arūpino aññamaññaṃ sahajātapaccayena paccayo, cattāro mahābhūtā aññamaññaṃ…pe… okkantikkhaṇe nāmarūpaṃ aññamaññaṃ…pe… cittacetasikā dhammā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ…pe… mahābhūtā upādārūpānaṃ…pe… rūpino dhammā arūpīnaṃ dhammānaṃ kiñcikāle sahajātapaccayena paccayo, kiñcikāle nasahajātapaccayena paccayo”ti evaṃ chabbidho niddiṭṭho. Tattha aññamaññanti iminā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ ekakkhaṇe paccayabhāvañceva paccayuppannabhāvañca dīpeti, paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthurūpaṃ rūpaṃ nāma. Cittacetasikāti pavattiyaṃ cattāro khandhā, paṭisandhiyampīti keci tattha kaṭattārūpānampi cittasamuṭṭhāne paviṭṭhattā. Tesaṃ hi paṭisandhicittacetasikā sahajātapaccayā hontiyeva, tāni pana vatthuvirahitāni rūpāni pavattiyaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ viya cittacetasikānaṃ paccayatthaṃ na pharanti, tasmā “aññamañña”nti na vuttaṃ, tathā bhūtānaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Evaṃ hi agayhamāne paṭisandhiyaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ sahajātā nāma nissayatā na vuttāti sahajātapaccayaniddeso aparipuṇṇo eva siyā. Kiñcikāleti idampi okkantikkhaṇe hadayavatthumeva sandhāya vuttattā tatiyakoṭṭhāsameva bhajatīti atthato ayaṃ paccayo pañcavidhoti ayaṃ sahajātapaccaye nayo.

The condition that assists by way of co-arising at the very moment of arising is the conascence condition. In the exposition, it is explained in six ways: "The four immaterial aggregates are a condition for each other by way of conascence condition. The four great elements are a condition for each other... At the moment of conception, mentality-materiality are a condition for each other... Consciousness and mental factors are a condition for consciousness-originated materiality... The great elements are a condition for derived materiality... Material phenomena are sometimes a condition for immaterial phenomena by way of conascence condition, and sometimes not a condition by way of conascence condition." Here, 'mutually' indicates that these phenomena are both a condition and conditioned in the same moment. At the moment of rebirth-linking, the base-materiality is called 'materiality'. By 'consciousness and mental factors' are meant the four aggregates in the course of existence, and also at rebirth-linking, according to some, because even kamma-born materiality is included there as consciousness-originated. For them, the rebirth-linking consciousness and mental factors are indeed conascence conditions. However, those material phenomena, being devoid of a base, do not serve as a condition for consciousness and mental factors as do the consciousness-originated phenomena in the course of existence. Therefore, 'mutually' is not stated, likewise for derived materiality in relation to the great elements. For if it is not understood thus, the conascent dependence of kamma-born materiality at rebirth-linking would not be stated, and the exposition of the conascence condition would be incomplete. 'Sometimes' refers only to the heart-basis at the moment of conception, so this falls into the third category. Hence, in essence, this condition is fivefold. This is the method regarding the conascence condition.

Aññamaññaṃ [M 0.0445] uppādanupatthambhanabhāvena upakārako dhammo aññamaññapaccayo tidaṇḍakaṃ viya. So niddese “cattāro khandhā arūpino aññamaññapaccayena paccayo, cattāro mahābhūtā…pe… okkantikkhaṇe nāmarūpaṃ aññamaññapaccayena paccayo”ti evaṃ tidhā niddiṭṭhoti ayaṃ aññamaññapaccaye nayo.

The condition that assists by way of mutually producing and supporting is the mutuality condition, like a tripod. In the exposition, it is stated in three ways: "The four immaterial aggregates are a condition for each other by way of the mutuality condition; the four great elements... at the moment of conception, mentality-materiality are a condition for each other by way of the mutuality condition." This is the method regarding the mutuality condition.

Adhiṭṭhānākārena, nissayākārena ca upakārako dhammo nissayapaccayo tarucittakammādīnaṃ pathavīpaṭādayo viya, so niddese sahajātapaccaye viya chadhāva niddiṭṭho. Chaṭṭho panettha koṭṭhāso “cakkhāyatanaṃ [V 0.0341] cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā, sotaghānajivhākāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇadhātuyā…pe… yaṃ rūpaṃ nissāya manodhātu ca manoviññāṇadhātu ca vattanti, taṃ rūpaṃ manodhātuyā ca manoviññāṇadhātuyā ca taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ nissayapaccayena paccayo”ti evaṃ purejātanissayadassanavasena vibhatto, sesaṃ tādisameva. Tattha rūpanti hadayavatthu.

The condition that assists in the manner of a foundation and in the manner of a support is the dependence condition, like the earth and cloth for trees, paintings, and so on. In the exposition, it is explained in six ways, similar to the conascence condition. Here, the sixth section is distinguished by way of showing prenascent dependence, thus: "The eye-base is a condition for the eye-consciousness element by way of dependence; the ear, nose, tongue, and body-bases for the body-consciousness element... and whatever materiality is depended upon by the mind-element and mind-consciousness element to function, that materiality is a condition for the mind-element, mind-consciousness element, and their associated states by way of dependence condition." The rest is similar. Here, 'materiality' refers to the heart-basis.

Upanissayapaccayoti ettha panāyaṃ vacanattho – tadadhīnavuttitāya attano phalena nissito, nappaṭikkhittoti nissayo, yathā pana bhuso āyāso upāyāso, evaṃ bhuso nissayo upanissayo, balavakāraṇassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ, tasmā balavakāraṇabhāvena upakārako dhammo upanissayapaccayoti veditabbo. So ārammaṇūpanissayo anantarūpanissayo pakatūpanissayoti tividho hoti. Tattha ārammaṇūpanissayo tāva ārammaṇādhipatinā saddhiṃ nānattaṃ akatvā vibhatto. Tattha yaṃ ārammaṇaṃ garuṃ katvā cittacetasikā uppajjanti, taṃ niyamato tesaṃ ārammaṇesu balavārammaṇaṃ hoti, iti garukātabbamattaṭṭhena ārammaṇādhipati, balavakāraṇaṭṭhena ārammaṇūpanissayoti evametesaṃ nānattaṃ veditabbaṃ.

Herein, the meaning of the term 'decisive support condition' is as follows: 'Support' (nissaya) means that which is depended upon by its own result, due to its dependent occurrence, and is not rejected. Just as great exertion is 'upāyāso', so a strong support is 'upanissayo'; this is a designation for a powerful cause. Therefore, a condition that assists by being a powerful cause should be understood as the decisive support condition. It is of three kinds: object decisive support, contiguity decisive support, and natural decisive support. Herein, first, object decisive support is explained without making a distinction from object-dominance. In this case, whatever object is made weighty, upon which consciousness and mental factors arise—that object is invariably a powerful object among their objects. Thus, in the sense of merely being what is to be made weighty, it is object-dominance; in the sense of being a powerful cause, it is object decisive support. In this way, the distinction between them should be understood.

Anantarūpanissayopi [M 0.0446] anantarapaccayena nānattaṃ akatvāva vibhatto, evaṃ santepi attano attano anantaraṃ anurūpassa cittuppādassa pavattanasamatthatāya anantaratā, purimacittassa pacchimacittuppādane balavatāya anantarūpanissayatā ca veditabbā. Yathā hi hetupaccayādīsu kañci dhammaṃ vināpi cittaṃ uppajjati, na evaṃ anantaracittaṃ vinā cittassa uppatti nāma atthi, tasmā balavapaccayo hoti, iti balavakāraṇaṭṭhena anantarova anantarūpanissayoti evametesaṃ nānattaṃ veditabbaṃ.

The contiguity decisive support is also classified without making a distinction from the contiguity condition. Even so, contiguity (anantaratā) should be understood as the ability to cause the arising of a subsequent mind-moment appropriate to its own immediate predecessor, and contiguity decisive support (anantarūpanissayatā) as the strength of the preceding mind in producing the subsequent mind-moment. For just as in the case of root-condition and other conditions, a mind-moment can arise without some particular state, there is no arising of a mind-moment without an immediately preceding mind-moment. Therefore, it is a strong condition. Thus, the distinction between them should be understood in this way: the contiguity condition itself is the contiguity decisive support by way of being a strong cause.

Pakato upanissayo pakatūpanissayo, pakato nāma attano santāne uppādito vā saddhāsīlādiupasevito vā utubhojanādipakatiyāyeva vā upanissayo pakatūpanissayo, iti parūpanissayena amissoti attho. So ca pakatūpanissayo “saddhaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti, sīlaṃ samādiyati, uposathakammaṃ karoti, jhānaṃ uppādeti; vipassanaṃ, maggaṃ, abhiññaṃ, samāpattiṃ uppādeti; sīlaṃ, sutaṃ, cāgaṃ, paññaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādetī”tiādinā imesaṃ saddhādīnaṃ vasena bahudhā vibhatto, evaṃ upanissayapaccayo tividho. Niddese panāyaṃ “purimā purimā kusalā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ [V 0.0342] …pe… akusalānaṃ kesañci…pe… abyākatānaṃ dhammānaṃ…pe… purimā purimā akusalā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ akusalānaṃ…pe… kusalānaṃ kesañci…pe… abyākatānaṃ dhammānaṃ…pe… purimā purimā abyākatā dhammā…pe… abyākatānaṃ, kusalānaṃ, akusalānaṃ upanissayapaccayena paccayo, puggalopi upanissayapaccayena paccayo, senāsanampī”ti evaṃ niddiṭṭho. Tattha purimāti anantarūpanissaye samanantarātītāva labbhanti.

Natural decisive support is pakatūpanissayo. What is called 'natural' is a decisive support that is either produced in one's own continuum, or cultivated, such as faith, virtue, and so on, or is simply natural due to season, food, and so on. This means it is not mixed with another's decisive support. And this natural decisive support is classified in many ways based on these factors of faith, etc.: 'Relying on faith as decisive support, one gives alms, undertakes virtue, performs the Uposatha observance, arouses jhāna, insight, the path, higher knowledge, or attainments; relying on virtue, learning, generosity, or wisdom as decisive support, one gives alms... arouses attainments,' and so on. Thus, the decisive support condition is of three kinds. In the exposition, however, it is stated thus: 'Preceding wholesome states are a condition by way of decisive support for subsequent wholesome states... for some unwholesome states... for indeterminate states... Preceding unwholesome states are a condition by way of decisive support for subsequent unwholesome states... for some wholesome states... for indeterminate states... Preceding indeterminate states... are a condition by way of decisive support for indeterminate, wholesome, or unwholesome states. A person is also a condition by way of decisive support, as is a dwelling place.' Here, 'preceding' in the case of contiguity decisive support means only the immediately past is obtained.

Ārammaṇūpanissayapakatūpanissayesu [M 0.0447] pana nānāvidhivasena purimatarāvāti tayopi rāsī kusalena kusalapade labbhanti. Kusalena panākusale samanantarātītā na labbhanti, tenāha “kesañcī”ti. Idaṃ hi “kusalo dhammo akusalassa dhammassa ārammaṇūpanissayo pakatūpanissayo, ārammaṇūpanissayo pana dānaṃ datvā…pe… taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati…pe… pakatūpanissayo saddhaṃ upanissāya mānaṃ jappetī”tiādinā pañhāvāre āgataṃ imaṃ nayaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ.

However, in the cases of object decisive support and natural decisive support, in the wholesome-to-wholesome section, even much earlier states are obtained in various ways; thus all three groups are obtained. But in the unwholesome section conditioned by the wholesome, the immediately past are not obtained; hence it is said, 'for some.' For this is stated with reference to the method that comes in the question section: 'A wholesome state is an object decisive support or a natural decisive support for an unwholesome state. As object decisive support: having given a gift... making that an object of importance, lust arises... As natural decisive support: relying on faith, one generates conceit,' and so on.

Akusalena kusalapade hi samanantarātītā na labbhanti, tenāha “kesañcī”ti. Idaṃ pana “akusalo dhammo kusalassa dhammassa pakatūpanissayo. Rāgaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… pāṇaṃ hantvā tassa paṭighātatthāya dānaṃ detī”tiādinā nayena pañhāvāre āgataṃ pakatūpanissayameva sandhāya vuttaṃ. Yathā hi akusalaṃ kusalassa anantarūpanissayo na hoti, tathā ārammaṇūpanissayopi na hoti. Na hi taṃ garuṃ katvā kusalaṃ pavattati.

Indeed, in the wholesome section conditioned by the unwholesome, the immediately past are not obtained; hence it is said, 'for some.' This, however, is stated with reference only to natural decisive support, which comes in the question section by way of the method: 'An unwholesome state is a natural decisive support for a wholesome state. Relying on lust, one gives a gift... having killed a living being, one gives a gift for the purpose of counteracting it,' and so on. For just as an unwholesome state is not a contiguity decisive support for a wholesome state, so too it is not an object decisive support. For a wholesome state does not proceed by making that an object of importance.

Akusalena abyākatapade pana ārammaṇūpanissayova na labbhati. Na hi taṃ abyākatā garuṃ karonti, anantarā panassa honti. Tenevettha “kesañcī”ti na vuttaṃ. Sesapadesu tayopi upanissayā labbhanteva. “Puggalopi, senāsanampī”ti idampi dvayaṃ pakatūpanissayavasenevettha vuttaṃ, utubhojanādayo cettha saṅgahetabbā. Imasmiñca paccaye ekaccāya paññattiyā saddhiṃ sabbepi catubhūmakā dhammā saṅgahitāti veditabbāti ayaṃ upanissayapaccaye nayo.

However, in the indeterminate section conditioned by the unwholesome, object decisive support is not obtained. For indeterminate states do not make that an object of importance, but they can be contiguous to it. Therefore, 'for some' is not stated here. In the remaining sections, all three decisive supports are indeed obtained. 'A person also, and a dwelling place also'—this pair is also stated here by way of natural decisive support; and season, food, and so on should be included here. And it should be understood that in this condition, all phenomena of the four planes are included, together with certain concepts. This is the method regarding the decisive support condition.

Paṭhamataraṃ uppajjitvā vattamānabhāvena upakārakā rūpadhammā purejātapaccayo, so pasādatabbisayahadayavatthuvasena ekādasavidho. Niddese ca “cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā [M 0.0448] taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇadhātuyā [V 0.0343] …pe… rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇadhātuyā…pe… rūpāyatanaṃ saddagandharasaphoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ manodhātuyā…pe… yaṃ rūpaṃ nissāya…pe… taṃ rūpaṃ manodhātuyā ca manoviññāṇadhātuyā ca kiñcikāle purejātapaccayena paccayo, kiñcikāle na purejātapaccayena paccayo”ti evaṃ sabbathāpi pañcadvāre vatthārammaṇavasena, manodvāre vatthuvaseneva cāyaṃ niddiṭṭho. Pañhāvāre pana ārammaṇapurejātaṃ “arahā cakkhuṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassatī”ti āgatattā manodvārepi aṭṭhārasannaṃ rūpānaṃ vasena ārammaṇapurejātampi labbhatevāti ayaṃ purejātapaccaye nayo.

Material phenomena that, having arisen earlier, are helpful by way of their present existence, are the pre-nascence condition. It is of eleven kinds: by way of the sensitive materialities, their objects, and the heart-base. And in the exposition: 'The eye-base is a condition by way of pre-nascence for the eye-consciousness element and its associated states... The body-base... for the body-consciousness element... The visible form-base... for the eye-consciousness element... The tangible-base... for the body-consciousness element... The visible form-base, sound-base, odor-base, taste-base, and tangible-base... for the mind-element... That material form which is depended upon... that material form is a condition by way of pre-nascence for the mind-element and the mind-consciousness element at some time, and is not a condition by way of pre-nascence at some time.' Thus, this is explained in every way for the five doors by way of base and object, and for the mind door only by way of base. In the question section, however, since it is stated, 'An arahant contemplates the eye as impermanent, suffering, and non-self,' object pre-nascence is also obtained. Therefore, in the mind-door also, object pre-nascence is indeed obtained by way of the eighteen types of produced material phenomena. This is the method for the pre-nascence condition.

Purejātānaṃ rūpadhammānaṃ upatthambhakaṭṭhena upakārako arūpadhammo pacchājātapaccayo gijjhapotakasarīrānaṃ āhārāsā cetanā viya. Niddesepi cassa “pacchājātā cittacetasikā dhammā purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo”ti evaṃ vuttaṃ. Tattha imassa kāyassāti catusamuṭṭhānikatisamuṭṭhānikabhūtupādāyarūpakāyassa. Dhammato cāyaṃ ṭhapetvā paṭisandhivipāke āruppavipāke avasesā sabbe catubhūmakā arūpadhammāti veditabbāti ayaṃ pacchājātapaccaye nayo.

An immaterial phenomenon that is helpful to pre-nascent material phenomena by way of supporting them is the post-nascence condition, like the volition of desire for food for the bodies of young vultures. And in its exposition it is stated thus: 'Post-nascent consciousness and mental factors are a condition for this pre-nascent body by way of the post-nascence condition.' Therein, 'this body' means the material body consisting of primary elements and derived matter, which has four origins or three origins. And it should be understood that from the point of view of the Dhamma, this comprises all the remaining immaterial phenomena of the four planes, excluding the rebirth-linking resultants and the formless-sphere resultants. This is the method regarding the post-nascence condition.

Āsevanaṭṭhena anantarānaṃ paguṇabalavabhāvena upakārako dhammo āsevanapaccayo ganthādipurimābhiyogo viya. So kusalākusalakiriyajavanavasena tividho. Niddese panassa “purimā purimā kusalā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ…pe… akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ…pe… kiriyābyākatānaṃ dhammānaṃ āsevanapaccayena paccayo”ti niddiṭṭho. Tattha purimā purimāti sabbattha samanantarātītāva daṭṭhabbā, tatthāpi [M 0.0449] kusalādayo abyākatādīnaṃ bhinnajātikānaṃ samanantarānampi vāsanāsaṅkhātena āsevanena paguṇatarabalavabhāvavisiṭṭhaṃ attano kusalādibhāvasaṅkhātagatiṃ gāhāpetuṃ asamatthatāya āsevanapaccayā na honti, bhūmito, pana ārammaṇato ca bhinnāpi kāmāvacaratihetukakusalakiriyā attanā sadisavedanānameva mahaggatalokuttarakusalakiriyānampi, saṅkhārārammaṇañca anulomakusalaṃ nibbānārammaṇassa gotrabhukusalassa āsevanapaccayā hontiyeva. Lokuttaro pana āsevanapaccayo natthi, tathā vipāko kammapariṇāmitattāti ayaṃ āsevanapaccaye nayo.

A state that assists immediately succeeding states through proficiency and strength is the repetition condition, like the initial effort in learning texts and so on. It is threefold according to wholesome, unwholesome, and functional impulsion. In the exposition, it is stated: 'Earlier wholesome states are a condition by way of repetition for later wholesome states... for unwholesome states... for functional indeterminate states.' Herein, 'earlier' should be understood in all cases as only the immediately preceding. Even there, wholesome and other states do not become repetition conditions even for immediately succeeding states of a different class, such as indeterminate states. This is because they are unable to cause them to take up their own course, characterized as wholesome, etc., by means of that repetition called 'perfuming', which imparts a state of greater proficiency and strength. However, even those differing in plane or object—such as sense-sphere wholesome and functional states with three roots—can still be repetition conditions for the sublime and supramundane wholesome and functional states that share a similar feeling with them. And the conformity-wholesome state with formations as its object also serves as a repetition condition for the change-of-lineage wholesome state with Nibbāna as its object. But there is no supramundane repetition condition, nor for resultant states, because they are the maturation of kamma. This is the method regarding the repetition condition.

Cittappayogasaṅkhātena kiriyabhāvena upakārako dhammo kammapaccayo. So nānakkhaṇikāya [V 0.0344] kusalākusalacetanāya ceva sahajātāya ca sabbāyapi cetanāya vasena duvidho hoti. Niddesepi cassa “kusalākusalaṃ kammaṃ vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ…pe… cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo”ti dvidhāva vutto. Tattha kammanti cetanākammameva. Kaṭattā ca rūpānanti kammassa kaṭattā upacitattā nipphāditattā uppannānaṃ kammajānaṃ rūpānaṃ kaṭattā eva, kammampi kālantareyeva avasesapaccayasamāyoge sati attano phalaṃ uppādeti, na tu vinaṭṭhattā ṭhitattā taṃ vā ṭhitaṃ pana kammaṃ na janeti. Evaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānanti iminā paṭisandhiyaṃ kaṭattārūpaggahaṇaṃ daṭṭhabbanti ayaṃ kammapaccaye nayo.

A state that assists by way of functional activity, designated as mental application, is the kamma condition. It is twofold: by way of wholesome and unwholesome volition occurring at different moments, and by way of all co-arisen volition. In the exposition, it is said: 'Wholesome and unwholesome kamma is a condition by way of kamma for the resultant aggregates, and for kamma-produced materiality... Volition is a condition by way of kamma for the associated states and for the materiality produced by them.' Herein, 'kamma' means volitional kamma alone. And 'for kamma-produced materiality' means for kamma-born materiality that has arisen because the kamma has been done, accumulated, and accomplished. Kamma itself produces its result only after a lapse of time, when other conditions are present; it does not produce its result when it has perished, nor does kamma produce it while still present. Thus, by 'produced by them,' the inclusion of kamma-produced materiality at rebirth-linking should be understood. This is the method regarding the kamma condition.

Nirussāhasantabhāvena nirussāhasantabhāvāya upakārako vipākadhammo vipākapaccayo. So pavatte cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ, paṭisandhikkhaṇe kaṭattārūpānaṃ, sabbattha ca sampayuttadhammānaṃ paccayo hoti. Yathāha sabbapañhāvāre – “vipākābyākato [M 0.0450] eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ vipākapaccayena paccayo”tiādi. Niddese panassa “vipākā cattāro khandhā arūpino aññamaññaṃ vipākapaccayena paccayo”ti ettakameva vuttaṃ. Taṃ pañhāvāre vuttavidhānaṃ sandhāya sāvasesaṃ vuttanti ayaṃ vipākapaccaye nayo.

A resultant state, by way of its calm and effortless nature, which assists in producing a calm and effortless state, is the resultant condition. It serves as a condition for mind-originated materiality in the course of life, for kamma-produced materiality at the moment of rebirth-linking, and for associated states in all instances. As stated in the Sabbapañhāvāra: 'One resultant and indeterminate aggregate is a condition by way of resultant condition for three aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena, and at the moment of rebirth-linking... for kamma-produced materiality,' and so on. However, in the Niddesa, it is said only: 'The four immaterial resultant aggregates are mutually a condition by way of resultant condition for each other.' This was stated incompletely, with reference to the method stated in the Sabbapañhāvāra. This is the method regarding the resultant condition.

Rūpārūpānaṃ upatthambhakaṭṭhena upakārakā cattāro āhārā āhārapaccayo. Niddese pana “kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa kāyassa…pe… arūpino āhārā sampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ āhārapaccayena paccayo”ti evaṃ niddiṭṭho. Tattha catusamuṭṭhānamupagatā ojā kabaḷīkāro āhāro nāma. So yasmā āhārūpasevīnaññeva ajjhohaṭāhārautujāhārūpatthaddho eva ca kammajādiāhāro imassa kāyassa ṭhitiyā pavattati, na aññathā, tasmā kabaḷīkātabbautujavatthusannissitatādassanatthaṃ kabaḷīkāro āhāroti vutto. Kiñcāpi cāyaṃ “imassa kāyassā”ti avisesena vutto, visesato pana āhārajarūpassa janako ceva anupālako ca hutvā sesatisantatisamuṭṭhānarūpassa anupālako eva hutvā āhārapaccayo hoti. Taṃsamuṭṭhānānanti iminā paṭisandhiyaṃ kammasamuṭṭhānāni gahitāneva. Pañhāvāre hi “paṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākābyākatā āhārā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ āhārapaccayena paccayo”ti vuttanti ayaṃ āhārapaccaye nayo.

The four nutriments are a condition by way of nutriment, in the sense of supporting both material and immaterial phenomena. In the exposition, however, it is stated: 'Edible food is a nutriment for this body... immaterial nutriments are a condition by way of nutriment for associated states and for material phenomena arisen from them.' Herein, the nutritive essence that has attained fourfold origination is called edible food. Since this body continues to exist only for those who partake of nutriment, being sustained by ingested food, seasonal food, and kamma-originated food, etc., and not otherwise, it is called 'edible food' to show its dependence on what is to be eaten, on seasonal conditions, and on a physical basis. Although it is stated generally as 'for this body,' specifically, it is both the producer and sustainer of nutriment-born materiality, and merely the sustainer of the materiality arisen from the other three continuities, thus serving as the nutriment condition. By 'material phenomena arisen from them,' the kamma-originated material phenomena at rebirth-linking are indeed included. For in the section of questions, it is said: 'At the moment of rebirth-linking, the resultant and indeterminate nutriments are a condition by way of nutriment for the associated aggregates and for kamma-originated material phenomena.' This is the method in the nutriment condition.

Adhipatiyaṭṭhena [V 0.0345] upakārakā itthindriyapurisindriyavajjā vīsati indriyā indriyapaccayo. Itthindriyapurisindriyāni hi kiñcāpi itthipurisaliṅgākappādīnaṃ bījabhūtāni, neva pana tesaṃ, na aññesaṃ indriyādipaccayataṃ pharanti. Suttantikapariyāyena pana [M 0.0451] tesaṃ pakatūpanissayabhāvaṃ pharantīti bāvīsateva indriyāni. Tattha cakkhundriyādayo pañca arūpadhammānameva indriyapaccayo, rūpajīvitindriyaṃ kaṭattārūpānameva, sesā rūpārūpānaṃ. Niddese “cakkhundriyaṃ cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ…pe… kāyaviññāṇadhātuyā…pe… rūpajīvitindriyaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ, arūpino indriyā sampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo”ti evaṃ niddiṭṭho. Taṃsamuṭṭhānānanti etthāpi kaṭattārūpampi saṅgahitaṃ. Pañhāvāre hi “paṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākābyākatā indriyā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpāna”nti vuttanti ayaṃ indriyapaccaye nayo.

The twenty faculties, excluding the faculties of femininity and masculinity, are a condition by way of faculty, in the sense of assisting by way of dominance. Although the faculties of femininity and masculinity are indeed the seeds for characteristics such as the appearance of female and male sex, they do not function as faculty conditions for these or for other phenomena. However, according to the Sutta method, they function as a natural decisive support condition, thus making twenty-two faculties in total. Among these, the five physical sense faculties are a faculty condition only for immaterial phenomena, the material life faculty is a condition only for kamma-originated materiality, and the remaining faculties are conditions for both material and immaterial phenomena. In the exposition, it is stated: 'The eye faculty is a condition for the eye-consciousness element and the states associated with it... the body-consciousness element... the material life faculty is a condition for kamma-originated materiality. The immaterial faculties are a faculty condition for associated states and for material phenomena arisen from them.' By 'material phenomena arisen from them,' kamma-originated materiality is also included here. For in the section of questions, it is said: 'At the moment of rebirth-linking, the resultant and indeterminate faculties are conditions for the associated aggregates and for kamma-originated material phenomena.' This is the method in the faculty condition.

Upanijjhāyanaṭṭhena upakārakāni ṭhapetvā dvipañcaviññāṇesu vedanāttayaṃ, ekaggatañca sesāni kusalādibhedāni satta jhānaṅgāni jhānapaccayo. Dvipañcaviññāṇānaṃ hi abhinipātamattattā tesu vedanekaggatā upanijjhāyanākārassa abhāvena jhānaṅgesu na uddhaṭā, niddese panassa “jhānaṅgāni jhānasampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ jhānapaccayena paccayo”ti niddiṭṭho. Idhāpi taṃsamuṭṭhānānanti iminā ca kaṭattārūpampi gahitaṃ. Pañhāvārehi “paṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākābyākatāni jhānaṅgāni sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpāna”nti vuttanti ayaṃ jhānapaccaye nayo.

The seven jhāna factors—classified as wholesome and so forth—which assist by way of close contemplation, are the jhāna condition, with the exception of the three feelings and one-pointedness in the two sets of fivefold consciousness. For in the two sets of fivefold consciousness, due to their being mere impingement, feeling and one-pointedness in them are not enumerated among the jhāna factors because of the absence of the mode of close contemplation. However, in the exposition, it is stated: 'The jhāna factors are a condition by way of jhāna for the states associated with jhāna and for material phenomena arisen from them.' Here too, by 'arisen from them,' kamma-originated materiality is also included. For in the section of questions, it is said: 'At the moment of rebirth-linking, the resultant and indeterminate jhāna factors are conditions for the associated aggregates and for kamma-originated material phenomena.' This is the method in the jhāna condition.

Yato tato vā niyyānaṭṭhena upakārakāni kusalādibhedāni dvādasa maggaṅgāni maggapaccayo. Niddese pana “maggaṅgāni maggasampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ maggapaccayena paccayo”ti niddiṭṭho. Etthāpi taṃsamuṭṭhānānanti iminā kaṭattārūpaggahaṇaṃ. Pañhāvāre hi “paṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākābyākatāni maggaṅgāni sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpāna”nti vuttaṃ, ahetukacittesu cettha vijjamānāni maggaṅgāni maggapaccayā na honti. Ayaṃ maggapaccaye nayo.

The twelve path factors, classified as wholesome and so forth, are a condition by way of path, in the sense of assisting by leading out from this or that. In the exposition, however, it is stated: "The path factors are a condition by way of path for the states associated with the path and for material phenomena arisen from them." Here too, by "arisen from them," kamma-originated materiality is included. For in the section of questions, it is said: "At the moment of rebirth-linking, the resultant and indeterminate path factors are conditions for the associated aggregates and for kamma-originated material phenomena." However, in the case of rootless consciousnesses, the path factors present therein are not a condition by way of path. This is the method in the path condition.

Ekavatthukaekārammaṇaekuppādaekanirodhasaṅkhātena [M 0.0452] sampayuttabhāvena upakārakā arūpino dhammā [V 0.0346] sampayuttapaccayo. Niddese pana “cattāro khandhā arūpino dhammā aññamaññaṃ sampayuttapaccayena paccayo”ti niddiṭṭhoti ayaṃ sampayuttapaccaye nayo.

Immaterial phenomena are a condition by way of association, in the sense of assisting by way of being associated, characterized by having one basis, one object, one arising, and one cessation. In the exposition, however, it is stated: "The four immaterial aggregates are a condition for one another by way of the association condition." This is the method in the association condition.

Ekavatthukādibhāvānupagamena upakārakā rūpino dhammā arūpīnaṃ, arūpino dhammā rūpīnaṃ vippayuttapaccayo, so sahajātapurejātapacchājātavasena tividho hoti. Vuttaṃ hetaṃ “sahajātā kusalā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ…pe… pacchājātā kusalā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo”tiādi. Purejātaṃ pana chavatthuvaseneva veditabbaṃ. Niddese panassa “rūpino dhammā arūpīnaṃ…pe… arūpino dhammā rūpīnaṃ dhammānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo”ti evaṃ sāmaññato niddiṭṭho. Tattha rūpinoti idaṃ chavatthūnaṃ vasena vuttaṃ, rūpādayo pana ārammaṇadhammā sampayogāsaṅkāyābhāvena vippayuttapaccayā na vuttā. Cakkhādīnaṃ hi vatthūnaṃ abbhantarato arūpadhammā nikkhamantā viya uppajjanti, tattha sampayogāsaṅkā hoti. Pañhāvārepi hi “vatthu kusalānaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe… cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā”tiādinā cha vatthūneva uddhaṭāni, arūpino dhammā rūpīnanti etthāpi nibbānaṃ arūpampi samānaṃ rūpassa vippayuttapaccayo na hoti sabbathā sampayogāsaṅkābhāvato, “catūhi sampayogo catūhi vippayogo”ti (dhātu. 3) hi vuttanti ayaṃ vippayuttapaccaye nayo.

Material phenomena are a condition by way of dissociation for immaterial phenomena, and immaterial phenomena are a condition by way of dissociation for material phenomena, in the sense of assisting by not sharing the same basis, etc. This is threefold: co-arisen, pre-arisen, and post-arisen. For it is said: "The co-arisen wholesome aggregates are a condition by way of dissociation for mind-originated material phenomena... the post-arisen wholesome aggregates are a condition by way of dissociation for this pre-arisen body," and so on. The pre-arisen, however, should be understood only in terms of the six bases. In the exposition, however, it is stated generally: "Material phenomena are a condition by way of dissociation for immaterial phenomena... immaterial phenomena are a condition by way of dissociation for material phenomena." Herein, "material" is stated in terms of the six bases. But objects such as form, etc., are not mentioned as conditions by way of dissociation because there is no possibility of association. For immaterial phenomena arising internally from bases like the eye, etc., appear as if emerging outward, and there is a possibility of association there. Indeed, in the section of questions, only the six bases are enumerated: "The base is a condition for the wholesome aggregates... the eye-base is a condition for the eye-consciousness element," etc. Even in the phrase "immaterial phenomena for material phenomena," Nibbāna, though immaterial, is not a condition by way of dissociation for material phenomena, because there is no possibility of association at all. For it is said: "There is association with four, dissociation with four" (Dhātukathā 3). This is the method in the dissociation condition.

Paccuppannalakkhaṇena atthibhāvena tādisasseva dhammassa upatthambhakaṭṭhena upakārako dhammo atthipaccayo, so niddese “cattāro khandhā arūpino aññamaññaṃ…pe… cattāro mahābhūtā aññamaññaṃ, okkantikkhaṇe nāmarūpaṃ aññamaññaṃ, cittacetasikā [M 0.0453] dhammā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ, mahābhūtā upādārūpānaṃ, cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā…pe… rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ…pe… rūpāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ manodhātuyā…pe… manodhātuyā ca manoviññāṇadhātuyā ca taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo”ti evaṃ sahajātapurejātavasena ca bahudhā niddiṭṭho, pañhāvāre pana “sahajātaṃ purejātaṃ pacchājātaṃ āhāraṃ indriya”nti imesaṃ pañcannampi vasena āgatattā pacchājātakabaḷīkāraāhārarūpajīvitindriyānaṃ vasenāpi atthipaccayo gahetabbovāti ayaṃ atthipaccaye nayo.

A phenomenon that assists by supporting a similar phenomenon by way of its present characteristic and its existence is the presence condition. In the exposition, it is stated in various ways, by way of co-arisen and pre-arisen, thus: "The four immaterial aggregates for one another... the four great elements for one another; at the moment of conception, name-and-form for one another; consciousness and mental factors for mind-originated material phenomena; the great elements for derived material phenomena; the eye-base for the eye-consciousness element... the form-base for the eye-consciousness element and for the states associated with it... the form-base... the tangible-base for the mind-element... the mind-element and the mind-consciousness element and for the states associated with them—are a condition by way of presence." In the section of questions, however, since it is given by way of these five—"co-arisen, pre-arisen, post-arisen, nutriment, faculty"—the presence condition should also be understood by way of post-arisen phenomena, edible food, and the material life faculty. This is the method in the presence condition.

Attano anantaraṃ uppajjamānānaṃ arūpadhammānaṃ pavattiokāsadānavasena upakārakā samanantaraniruddhā [V 0.0347] arūpadhammā natthipaccayo, niddese pana “samanantaraniruddhā cittacetasikā dhammā paṭuppannānaṃ cittacetasikānaṃ dhammānaṃ natthipaccayena paccayo”ti evaṃ sāmaññatova niddiṭṭho. Sabbathā anantarapaccayasadisatāya tattha niddiṭṭhanayenevettha viseso ñātabboti ayaṃ natthipaccaye nayo.

Immediately ceased immaterial phenomena are the absence condition, in the sense of assisting by giving an opportunity for the occurrence of subsequent immaterial phenomena. In the exposition, however, it is stated generally: "Immediately ceased consciousness and mental factors are a condition by way of absence for presently arisen consciousness and mental factors." Since it is in every way similar to the contiguity condition, the distinction here should be understood in the same way as explained there. This is the method in the absence condition.

Natthipaccayadhammāva vigatabhāvena upakārakattā vigatapaccayoti saha niddesena natthipaccayasadisovāti.

The phenomena of the absence condition are themselves the disappearance condition, in that they assist by way of having disappeared; thus, together with the exposition, it is similar to the absence condition.

Avigatapaccayopi sabbathā atthipaccayasadisova, desanāvilāsena, veneyyavasena vā ayaṃ duko vuttoti ayaṃ avigatapaccaye nayo.

The non-disappearance condition, too, is in every way similar to the presence condition. This pair is stated either for the elegance of the teaching or for the sake of those to be trained. This is the method in the non-disappearance condition.

Pakiṇṇakavinicchayo

Miscellaneous Analysis

Imesu pana catuvīsatiyā paccayesu ñāṇacārassa visadabhāvatthaṃ –

Now, for the sake of clarity in the application of knowledge to these twenty-four conditions:

Dhammato kālato ceva, ekassānekapaccayā;

Anekesañca dhammānaṃ, ekapaccayabhāvato.

In terms of nature and time, and from one having many conditions, and from many phenomena having a single condition.

Sabhāgā [M 0.0454] visabhāgā ca, yugaḷā janakādito;

Sabbaṭṭhānādibhedā ca, rūpārūpavikappato;

Bhavato saṅgahā ñeyyo, pakiṇṇakavinicchayo.

From the homogeneous and heterogeneous, from pairs and from generators, etc.; and from distinctions of all occasions, etc., from the division of material and immaterial; from the summary of existence, the miscellaneous analysis should be understood.

Tattha dhammatoti imesu hi paccayesu hetupaccayo tāva nāmarūpadhammesu nāmadhammekadeso, tathā sahajātādhipatikammajhānamaggapaccayā, tathā āsevanavipākapaccayā, catukkhandhasaṅgahitāpi vipākadhammā anantarasamanantarapacchājātasampayuttanatthivigatapaccayā. Nibbānassa asaṅgahato nāmekadesotipi vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Purejātapaccayo rūpadhammova, sesā yathālābhavasena nāmarūpadhammā. Tattha ca ārammaṇādhipatiārammaṇūpanissayapakatūpanissayesu paññattipi saṅgahitāti ayaṃ dhammato vinicchayo.

Herein, in terms of nature (dhammato): Among these conditions, the root condition is a portion of mental phenomena within mind-and-matter phenomena; similarly, the co-nascence, dominance, kamma, jhāna, and path conditions; similarly, the repetition and resultant conditions (resultant phenomena being included in the four aggregates), as well as the contiguity, proximity, post-nascence, association, absence, and disappearance conditions. Since Nibbāna is not included, it is fitting to say that these are a portion of mental phenomena. The pre-nascence condition is only a material phenomenon, while the rest, as they are obtained, are mind-and-matter phenomena. And here, concepts (paññatti) are also included in the object, dominance (object-dominance), and decisive support (object-decisive support and natural decisive support) conditions. This is the analysis in terms of nature.

Kālato [V 0.0348] pana hetusahajātaaññamaññanissayapurejātapacchājātavipākaāhāraindriyajhānamaggasampayuttavippayuttaatthiavigatapaccayā pannarasa paccuppannāva hutvā attano phalassa paccayā honti, anantarasamanantaraāsevananatthivigatapaccayā pañca atītā eva hutvā, kammapaccayo paneko paccuppannopi atītopi hutvā, sesā ārammaṇaadhipatiupanissayapaccayā tayopi tekālikāpi, nibbānapaññattivasena kālavimuttāpi hutvā attano phalassa paccayā hontīti ayaṃ kālato vinicchayo.

In terms of time, the fifteen conditions—root, co-nascence, mutuality, support, pre-nascence, post-nascence, result, nutriment, faculty, jhāna, path, association, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance—being only present, are conditions for their own result. The five conditions—contiguity, proximity, repetition, absence, and disappearance—being only past, are conditions. The kamma condition, however, can be either present or past. The remaining three conditions—object, dominance, and decisive support—can pertain to all three times, or, by way of Nibbāna and concepts, can be timeless, and are conditions for their own result. This is the analysis in terms of time.

Ekassānekapaccayāti ekadhammassa, ekapaccayassa ca anekapaccayabhāvato. Kathaṃ? Hetupaccaye tāva amoho eko dhammo, so purejātakammaāhārajhānavajjānaṃ vīsatiyā paccayānaṃ vasena anekapaccayo hoti, hetupaccayattaṃ avijahantova adhipatisahajātaaññamaññanissayavipākindriyamaggasampayuttavippayuttaatthiavigatānaṃ aññesaṃ ekādasannaṃ vasena vā anekapaccayo hoti[M 0.0455], tathā alobhādayo, tesu pana alobhādosā indriyamaggapaccayā na honti, te tayo avipākabhūtā lobhadosamohā vipākapaccayāpi na honti, te pana amohavajjitā pañca adhipatipaccayā na honti, tathā sesāpi avipākabhūtā.

Regarding 'one having many conditions,' this is because a single phenomenon or a single condition can have the nature of many conditions. How so? In the root condition, for instance, non-delusion is a single phenomenon; it becomes a multiple condition by way of twenty conditions, excluding pre-nascence, kamma, nutriment, and jhāna. While not abandoning its nature as a root condition, it also becomes a multiple condition by way of eleven others: dominance, co-nascence, mutuality, support, result, faculty, path, association, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance. The same applies to non-greed and the others. Among them, however, non-greed and non-hatred are not faculty or path conditions. Those three wholesome roots, being non-resultant, and also greed, hatred, and delusion, are not resultant conditions. Furthermore, the five roots excluding non-delusion are not dominance conditions. Likewise for the other non-resultant phenomena.

Ārammaṇapaccaye rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā ārammaṇapurejātaatthiavigatānaṃ catunnaṃ vasena anekapaccayo hoti, tathā manodhātuyā, ahetukamanoviññāṇadhātuyā ca. Sahetukāya pana ārammaṇādhipatiārammaṇūpanissayānampi vasena, saddādīsupi eseva nayo. Dhammāyatanaṃ pana nissayavippayuttānaṃ vasenāpi anekapaccayo hoti, tathā ārammaṇapaccayattaṃ avijahantova ārammaṇādhipatinissayaupanissayapurejātavippayuttaatthiavigatānaṃ vasena aparesampi sattannaṃ vasena anekapaccayo hotīti ayamettha ukkaṭṭhaparicchedo. Tattha arūpānaṃ pana rūpānaṃ vā atītānāgatānaṃ ārammaṇapaccayabhāve sati ārammaṇādhipatiupanissayamattameva uttari labbhati.

In the object condition, the visible-form base becomes a multiple condition for the eye-consciousness element by way of four conditions: object, pre-nascence, presence, and non-disappearance. Likewise for the mind-element and for the rootless mind-consciousness element. For the rooted mind-consciousness element, however, it also becomes a multiple condition by way of object-dominance and object-decisive support. This same method applies to sounds and other sense objects. The mind-object base, however, also becomes a multiple condition by way of support and dissociation. And, without abandoning its nature as an object condition, it further becomes a multiple condition by way of seven others: object-dominance, support, decisive support, pre-nascence, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance. This is the supreme analysis here. Therein, when immaterial states or past and future material states serve as object conditions, only object-dominance and decisive support are additionally obtained.

Adhipatipaccaye ārammaṇādhipati vuttanayova. Sahajātādhipatīsu cittaṃ hetupurejātakammajhānamaggavajjānaṃ ekūnavīsatiyā paccayānaṃ vasena anekapaccayo hoti, adhipatipaccayattaṃ avijahanto aparesaṃ sahajātaaññamaññanissayavipākāhārindriyasampayuttavippayuttaatthiavigatānaṃ dasannaṃ vaseneva, tathā vīriyaṃ āhārapaccayavajjānaṃ maggapaccayasahitānaṃ [V 0.0349] vasena, chando āhārindriyavajjānaṃ vasena anekapaccayo hoti, vīmaṃsā hetupaccaye vuttanayāva.

In the dominance condition, object-dominance is as has been explained. Among the co-nascent dominants, consciousness becomes a multiple condition by way of nineteen conditions, excluding root, pre-nascence, kamma, jhāna, and path. While not abandoning its nature as a dominance condition, it also serves by way of ten others: co-nascence, mutuality, support, result, nutriment, faculty, association, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance. Similarly, energy becomes a multiple condition by way of those conditions excluding the nutriment condition but including the path condition. Desire becomes a multiple condition by way of those excluding the nutriment and faculty conditions. Investigation is as explained under the root condition.

Anantarapaccaye catūsu khandhesu vedanākkhandho tāva hetupurejātakammāhāramaggapaccayavajjānaṃ ekūnavīsatiyā vasena[M 0.0456], saññākkhandho tesu indriyajhānavajjānaṃ sattarasannaṃ vasena, saṅkhārakkhandho hetupurejātakammindriyajhānamaggavajjānaṃ aṭṭhārasannaṃ vasena, tathā cetanā kammasahitānaṃ, vitakko hetupurejātakammaāhārindriyavajjānaṃ jhānamaggasahitānaṃ, vicāro, pīti ca ānantariyānaṃ maggavajjānaṃ, ekaggatā hetupurejātakammāhāravajjānaṃ vīsatiyā paccayānaṃ vasena, saddhā, jīvitindriyañca anantarānaṃ hetupurejātakammāhārajhānamaggavajjānaṃ aṭṭhārasannaṃ, sati maggasahitānaṃ ekūnavīsatiyā, hiriottappakāyapassaddhādichayugā, yevāpanakesu adhimokkhamanasikāratatramajjhattatā, karuṇāmuditā ca hetupurejātakammāhārajhānamaggindriyavajjānaṃ sattarasannaṃ, viratiyo pana maggasahitānaṃ aṭṭhārasannaṃ, micchādiṭṭhi tato vipākavajjānaṃ sattarasannaṃ vasena, micchāvācākammantājīvā tehi ceva kammāhārapaccayehi cāti ekūnavīsatiyā paccayānaṃ vasena, ahirikaṃ anottappaṃ māno thinaṃ middhaṃ uddhaccanti ime hetupurejātakammavipākāhārindriyajhānamaggavajjānaṃ soḷasannaṃ, vicikicchā issāmacchariyakukkuccāni tato adhipativajjānaṃ pannarasannaṃ vasena anekapaccayā honti. Anantarapaccayattaṃ avijahantānaṃ panetesaṃ samanantaraupanissayakammanatthivigatānaṃ aparesaṃ channaṃ vasena ca. Viññāṇakkhandhassa adhipatipaccayeneva anekapaccayabhāvo veditabbo.

In the contiguity condition, among the four mental aggregates, the feeling aggregate, first, is a multiple condition by way of nineteen conditions, excluding root, pre-nascence, kamma, nutriment, and path. The perception aggregate is so by way of seventeen of those, excluding faculty and jhāna. The formations aggregate is so by way of eighteen, excluding root, pre-nascence, kamma, faculty, jhāna, and path. Similarly, volition includes the kamma condition; applied thought includes the jhāna and path conditions, while excluding root, pre-nascence, kamma, nutriment, and faculty; sustained thought and joy exclude the path condition; one-pointedness is a multiple condition by way of twenty conditions, excluding root, pre-nascence, kamma, and nutriment. Faith and the life-faculty are so by way of eighteen, excluding root, pre-nascence, kamma, nutriment, jhāna, and path; mindfulness is so by way of nineteen, including the path condition. The six pairs beginning with shame, fear of wrongdoing, and tranquility of the mental body; and among the miscellaneous factors, determination, attention, equanimity, compassion, and sympathetic joy are so by way of seventeen, excluding root, pre-nascence, kamma, nutriment, jhāna, path, and faculty. The abstinences, however, are so by way of eighteen, including the path condition. Wrong view is so by way of seventeen, excluding the resultant condition from that set. Wrong speech, wrong action, and wrong livelihood are so by way of nineteen conditions, including the kamma and nutriment conditions. Shamelessness, lack of fear of wrongdoing, conceit, sloth, torpor, and restlessness are so by way of sixteen, excluding root, pre-nascence, kamma, result, nutriment, faculty, jhāna, and path. Doubt, envy, avarice, and remorse are so by way of fifteen, excluding the dominance condition from that set—thus they are multiple conditions. Furthermore, without abandoning their nature as a contiguity condition, they are also conditions by way of six others: proximity, decisive support, repetition, kamma, absence, and disappearance. As for the consciousness aggregate, its nature as a multiple condition is to be understood by way of the dominance condition alone.

Sahajātapaccaye mahābhūtāni ārammaṇaārammaṇādhipatisahajātaaññamaññanissayaupanissayapurejātaatthiavigatānaṃ navannaṃ, hadayavatthu tesaññeva vippayuttasahitānaṃ vasena. Nissayapaccaye cakkhāyatanādīni ārammaṇaārammaṇādhipatinissayaupanissayapurejātaindriyavippayuttaatthiavigatānaṃ navannaṃ vasena. Purejātapaccaye rūpasaddagandharasāyatanādīni ārammaṇaārammaṇādhipatiupanissayapurejātaatthiavigatānaṃ channaṃ vasena. Āhārapaccaye ojā [M 0.0457] ārammaṇaārammaṇādhipatiupanissayāhāraatthiavigatānaṃ channaṃ paccayānaṃ vasena anekadhā paccayo hoti. Taṃtaṃpaccayattaṃ avijahantānaṃ tesaṃ tesaṃ sabbattha ārammaṇādhipatianantarasamanantarūpanissayādipaccayatā vuttanayena veditabbā. Sesaṃ suviññeyyamevāti ayaṃ ekassānekapaccayato vinicchayo.

In the co-nascence condition, the great elements are multiple conditions by way of nine: object, object-dominance, co-nascence, mutuality, support, decisive support, pre-nascence, presence, and non-disappearance. The heart-base is a multiple condition by way of those same, together with dissociation. In the support condition, the eye-base and so on are multiple conditions by way of nine: object, object-dominance, support, decisive support, pre-nascence, faculty, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance. In the pre-nascence condition, the bases of form, sound, odor, taste, and so on are multiple conditions by way of six: object, object-dominance, decisive support, pre-nascence, presence, and non-disappearance. In the nutriment condition, nutritive essence becomes a condition in manifold ways by way of six conditions: object, object-dominance, decisive support, nutriment, presence, and non-disappearance. The conditionality of each factor, without abandoning its respective conditional nature, should be understood everywhere according to the method stated for object, dominance, contiguity, proximity, decisive support, and other such conditions. The rest is easily understood. This is the analysis of 'one having many conditions'.

Anekesañca [V 0.0350] dhammānaṃ, ekapaccayabhāvatoti etesu hi ṭhapetvā kammapaccayaṃ sesesu tevīsatiyā paccayesu aneke anekesaṃ dhammānaṃ ekato ekekaṃ paccayā honti. Kammapaccayo pana cetanā ekadhammovāti ayaṃ anekadhammānaṃ ekapaccayabhāvato vinicchayo.

Regarding 'many phenomena having a single condition': Among the conditions, setting aside the kamma condition, in the remaining twenty-three conditions, many phenomena acting as conditions are collectively a single condition for many conditioned phenomena. The kamma condition, however, which is volition, is a single phenomenon. This is the analysis of 'many phenomena having a single condition'.

Sabhāgā visabhāgā cāti etesu hi anantarasamanantaraanantarūpanissayāsevananatthivigatapaccayā sabhāgā, tathā ārammaṇaārammaṇādhipatiārammaṇūpanissayā. Purejātapaccayo panettha pacchājātena visabhāgo, tathā sampayutto vippayuttena, atthi natthinā, vigato avigatenāti ayaṃ sabhāgavisabhāgato vinicchayo.

Regarding 'homogeneous and heterogeneous': among these, the contiguity, proximity, contiguity-decisive support, repetition, absence, and disappearance conditions are homogeneous; similarly, the object, object-dominance, and object-decisive support conditions. Herein, the pre-nascence condition is heterogeneous with the post-nascence, just as the associated is with the dissociated, presence with absence, and disappearance with non-disappearance. This is the analysis in terms of homogeneous and heterogeneous.

Yugaḷāti ettha atthasarikkhatāya saddasarikkhatāya kālapaṭipakkhatāya hetuphalatāya aññamaññapaṭipakkhatāyāti imehi kāraṇehi yugaḷaṃ veditabbaṃ. Anantarasamanantarā hi atthasarikkhatāya ekaṃ yugaḷaṃ nāma. Nissayūpanissayā saddasarikkhatāya, purejātapacchājātā kālapaṭipakkhatāya, kammavipākā hetuphalatāya, sampayuttavippayuttā aññamaññapaṭipakkhatāya ekaṃ yugaḷaṃ, tathā atthinatthipaccayā, vigataavigatapaccayāti ayaṃ yugaḷato vinicchayo.

Here, 'pairs' should be understood by these reasons: similarity in meaning, similarity in sound, opposition in time, cause and effect, and mutual opposition. Indeed, contiguity and proximity are called one pair due to similarity in meaning. Support and decisive support form a pair due to similarity in sound. Pre-nascence and post-nascence form a pair due to opposition in time. Kamma and result form a pair due to cause and effect. Associated and dissociated form one pair due to mutual opposition. Similarly, the presence and absence conditions, and the disappearance and non-disappearance conditions. This is the analysis in terms of pairs.

Janakāditoti janakopatthambhakato. Etesu hi anantarasamanantarūpanissayapakatūpanissayāsevanapaccayā, nānakkhaṇiko [M 0.0458] kammapaccayo, natthivigatapaccayā cāti ime janakā eva, na upatthambhakā. Pacchājātapaccayo upatthambhako eva, na janako. Sesā janakā ceva upatthambhakā cāti ayaṃ janakādito vinicchayo.

"From the generative, etc." means from the aspect of being generative and supportive. Among these, the proximity, contiguity, proximity decisive support, natural decisive support, repetition, non-momentary kamma, absence, and disappearance conditions are only generative, not supportive. The post-nascence condition is only supportive, not generative. The remaining ones are both generative and supportive. This is the analysis from the generative aspect, etc.

Sabbaṭṭhānādibhedāti sabbaṭṭhānikaasabbaṭṭhānikabhedato. Etesu hi sahajātanissayaatthiavigatapaccayā sabbaṭṭhānikā. Sabbesu paccayuppannesu icchitabbā. Etehi vinā uppajjamāno ekadhammopi natthi. Sesā asabbaṭṭhānikā. Tattha ca ārammaṇaārammaṇādhipatianantarasamanantarānantarūpanissayapakatūpanissayapurejātāsevanasampayutta atthinatthivigatapaccayā arūpadhammānaññeva kāraṇato asabbaṭṭhānikā. Tathā pacchājātapaccayo rūpānaññeva kāraṇato, sesā ekaccānaṃ rūpārūpadhammānaṃ kāraṇato asabbaṭṭhānikā. Ayaṃ sabbaṭṭhānādibhedato vinicchayo.

"Differentiated by universality, etc." means divided into universal and non-universal. Among these, the co-nascence, dependence, presence, and non-disappearance conditions are universal. They are to be found in all conditionally arisen phenomena. Without these, not even a single phenomenon can arise. The remaining conditions are non-universal. Among these, the object, object-dominance, proximity, contiguity, proximity decisive support, natural decisive support, pre-nascence, repetition, association, absence, and disappearance conditions are non-universal because they are causal only to immaterial phenomena. Similarly, the post-nascence condition is non-universal because it is causal only to material phenomena. The rest are non-universal because they are causal to some material and immaterial phenomena. This is the analysis from the perspective of universality, etc.

Rūpārūpavikappatoti [V 0.0351] rūpaṃ rūpassa, rūpaṃ arūpassātiādi vikappato. Etesu hi ekopi paccayo rūpameva hutvā rūpasseva paccayo bhavanto nāma natthi, rūpameva pana arūpasseva atthi, so purejātapaccayo eko eva. Rūpameva hutvā rūpārūpasseva paccayo nāmātipi natthi, arūpameva hutvā arūpasseva paccayopi atthi, so anantarasamanantaraāsevanasampayuttanatthivigatavasena chabbidho. Arūpameva pana rūpasseva paccayopi atthi, so pacchājātapaccayo eko eva. Arūpameva hutvā rūpārūpānampi atthi, so hetukammavipākajhānamaggavasena pañcavidho. Rūpārūpapaññatti hutvā arūpasseva paccayopi atthi, so ārammaṇaupanissayavasena duvidho. Rūpārūpaṃ pana rūpārūpassāpi atthi, so adhipatisahajātaaññamaññanissayāhārindriyavippayuttaatthiavigatavasena navavidhoti ayaṃ rūpārūpavikappato vinicchayo.

"Distinguished by material and immaterial" refers to the distinction based on material conditioning material, material conditioning immaterial, and so forth. Among these, there is no condition that, being material, is a condition only for material phenomena. However, there is one that, being material, is a condition only for immaterial phenomena—this is solely the pre-nascence condition. There is also no condition that, being material, is a condition for both material and immaterial phenomena. But there is a condition that, being immaterial, is a condition only for immaterial phenomena—this is sixfold: proximity, contiguity, repetition, association, absence, and disappearance. There is also a condition that, being immaterial, is a condition only for material phenomena—this is solely the post-nascence condition. There is also a condition that, being immaterial, is a condition for both material and immaterial phenomena—this is fivefold: root, kamma, result, jhāna, and path. There is also a condition that, being a concept of material and immaterial phenomena, is a condition only for immaterial phenomena—this is twofold: object and decisive support. There is also a condition that is both material and immaterial and is a condition for both material and immaterial phenomena—this is ninefold: dominance, co-nascence, mutuality, dependence, nutriment, faculty, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance. This is the analysis from the perspective of the distinction between material and immaterial.

Bhavatoti [M 0.0459] imesu hi paccayesu pañcavokārabhave tāva na koci paccayo na labbhati nāma, sabbepi labbhanti. Catuvokārabhave pana purejātapacchājātavippayuttapaccaye apanetvā sesā ekavīsatimeva. Ekavokārabhave sahajātaaññamaññanissayakammindriyaatthiavigatavasena satteva. Bāhire pana anindriyabaddharūpe tesu kammindriyavajjā pañceva labbhantīti ayaṃ bhavato vinicchayo.

"By existence": Among these conditions, in the five-aggregate existence, no condition is unobtainable; all are obtainable. In the four-aggregate existence, however, excluding the pre-nascence, post-nascence, and dissociation conditions, only twenty-one are found. In the one-aggregate existence, there are only seven: co-nascence, mutuality, dependence, kamma, faculty, presence, and non-disappearance. But in external matter not connected to faculties, only five of these are obtainable, excluding kamma and faculty. This is the analysis concerning existence.

Saṅgahāti sabbepi hi ime catuvīsati paccayā ārammaṇasahajātaupanissayapurejātapacchājātakammāhārindriyesu aṭṭhasu ca paccayesu saṅgahaṃ gacchanti. Kathaṃ? Tesu hi hetuaññamaññavipākajhānamaggasampayuttapaccayā cha sahajātapaccaye saṅgahaṃ gacchanti. Anantarasamanantarāsevananatthivigatapaccayā pañca anantarūpanissaye upanissayapaccaye. Nissayapaccayo sahajātapurejātabhedato duvidho. Tattha sahajāto sahajātapaccaye, purejāto purejātapaccaye. Adhipatipaccayopi ārammaṇabhūto ārammaṇūpanissaye, sahajātabhūto sahajātapaccaye. Vippayuttapaccayopi sahajātapurejātapacchājātabhūtatāya tattha tattha saṅgahaṃ gacchati. Atthiavigatapaccayāpi sahajātapurejātapacchājātāhārindriyabhūtatāya tattha tattha paccayesu saṅgahaṃ gacchanti. Evaṃ imesu paccayesu sabbapaccayānaṃ saṅgaho veditabbo. Teneva tikapaṭṭhānapāḷiyaṃ paccanīyanaye imesaṃ aṭṭhannaṃ paccayānaṃ vaseneva katipayapañhā vissajjitā. Imesaṃ pana aṭṭhannampi aññamaññasaṅgahopi atthiyeva. Tesu hi ārammaṇapaccayo adhipatibhūto upanissaye[V 0.0352], anadhipatibhūto na katthacīti ārammaṇapaccayo hutvā visuññeva tiṭṭhati. Kammapaccayopi sahajāto sahajāte. Nānakkhaṇiko pana [M 0.0460] balavā vipākadhammānaṃ upanissayo hotīti upanissayapaccaye saṅgahaṃ gacchati. Balavāpi pana kammajarūpānaṃ, dubbalo arūpānaṃ nānakkhaṇikakammapaccayo hutvā visuññeva tiṭṭhati. Āhārapaccayopi arūpabhūto sahajāte, rūpabhūto na katthacīti visuññeva tiṭṭhati, indriyapaccayopi arūpabhūto sahajāte, pasādindriyā purejāte, rūpajīvitindriyaṃ na katthaci saṅgahaṃ gacchatīti indriyapaccayo hutvā visuññeva tiṭṭhatīti evamevaṃ aññamaññasaṅgahopi attheva. Sabbepi panete catuvīsati paccayā ārammaṇaupanissayakammaatthipaccayesu catūsupi saṅgahaṃ gacchantīti ayaṃ saṅgahato vinicchayo. Ayaṃ anuttānapadatthasahito saṅkhepatthavinicchayo.

"By inclusion": All these twenty-four conditions are included in eight conditions: object, co-nascence, decisive support, pre-nascence, post-nascence, kamma, nutriment, and faculty. How so? Among them, the six conditions—root, mutuality, result, jhāna, path, and association—are included in the co-nascence condition. The five conditions—proximity, contiguity, repetition, absence, and disappearance—are included in the decisive support condition by way of proximity decisive support. The dependence condition is twofold, distinguished as co-nascent and pre-nascent. Therein, the co-nascent dependence is included in the co-nascence condition, and the pre-nascent dependence is included in the pre-nascence condition. The dominance condition, when it is an object, is included in the decisive support condition by way of object; when it is co-nascent, it is included in the co-nascence condition. The dissociation condition, by being co-nascent, pre-nascent, or post-nascent, is included in those respective conditions. The presence and non-disappearance conditions, by being co-nascent, pre-nascent, post-nascent, nutriment, or faculty, are included in those respective conditions. Thus, the inclusion of all conditions within these should be understood. For this reason, in the Tikapaṭṭhāna Pāḷi, under the negative method, several questions are answered by means of these eight conditions. Moreover, there is also mutual inclusion among these eight. Among them, the object condition, when it is dominant, is included in the decisive support condition; when it is not dominant, it stands apart as the object condition. The kamma condition, when co-nascent, is included in the co-nascence condition. The non-momentary kamma condition, however, when strong, is a decisive support for resultant phenomena and is thus included in the decisive support condition. But the strong non-momentary kamma condition for kamma-born matter, and the weak one for immaterial phenomena, stand apart as the non-momentary kamma condition. The nutriment condition, when immaterial, is included in the co-nascence condition; when material, it stands apart. The faculty condition, when immaterial, is included in the co-nascence condition; the sensitive sense faculties are included in the pre-nascence condition; the material life faculty is not included anywhere and thus stands apart as the faculty condition. In this way, mutual inclusion is also present. Furthermore, all these twenty-four conditions are included in just four conditions: object, decisive support, kamma, and presence. This is the analysis by inclusion. This is the concise analysis of the meaning, together with the explanation of profound terms.

Pakiṇṇakavinicchayo niṭṭhito.

The miscellaneous analysis is concluded.

Vibhaṅganaye panettha pāḷivavatthānaṃ tāva saṅkhepato evaṃ veditabbaṃ. Paṭṭhānapāḷiyaṃ hi “hetupaccayo…pe… avigatapaccayo”ti paccayapadāni mātikāvasena nikkhipitvā tesaṃ paccayānaṃ – “hetū hetusampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo”tiādinā nayena paccayabhājanīyasaṅkhāto niddesavāro paṭhamaṃ vutto. Sopi ca anantarasaṅkhepatthavinicchayo tattha tattha dassito eva. Tadanantaraṃ tesaṃ catuvīsatiyā paccayānaṃ kusalattikādayo dvāvīsatitike, hetudukādayo sataṃ duke ca nissāya nānānayato vibhajanavasena catuvīsatisamantapaṭṭhānasamodhānaṃ anantanayasamantapaṭṭhānaṃ vibhattaṃ. Kathaṃ? Catubbidhaṃ hi paṭṭhānaṃ – anulomapaṭṭhānaṃ, paccanīkapaṭṭhānaṃ, anulomapaccanīkapaṭṭhānaṃ, paccanīkānulomapaṭṭhānanti. Tattha “kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā”tiādinā, “hetuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca hetudhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā”tiādinā kusalādīnaṃ, hetuādīnañca dhammānaṃ anulomavasena pavattaṃ anulomapaṭṭhānaṃ nāma. “Nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā…pe… nahetuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetudhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā”tiādinā kusalādīnaṃ, hetuādīnañca [M 0.0461] dhammānaṃ paccanīkavasena pavattaṃ paccanīkapaṭṭhānaṃ nāma. “Kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā…pe… hetuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetudhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā”tiādinā pavattaṃ anulomapaccanīkapaṭṭhānaṃ nāma[V 0.0353]. “Nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo…pe… nahetuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca hetudhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā”tiādinā pavattaṃ paccanīkānulomapaṭṭhānaṃ nāma.

In the Vibhaṅga method, the arrangement of the Pāḷi text here should first be understood briefly as follows. In the Paṭṭhāna Pāḷi, the condition-terms such as "root condition... non-disappearance condition" are laid out by way of a matrix. Then, for those conditions, the exposition section known as the analysis of conditions is first presented, by the method beginning, "A root is a condition for states associated with roots and for material phenomena originating from them by way of root condition." And that concise determination of meaning immediately following has also been shown here and there. Subsequently, for these twenty-four conditions, relying on the twenty-two triads (such as the wholesome triad) and the hundred dyads (such as the root dyad), the combination of the twenty-four all-round Paṭṭhānas, the all-round Paṭṭhāna of infinite methods, is divided by way of various methods of classification. How? The Paṭṭhāna is fourfold: 1. Direct-order Paṭṭhāna (anulomapaṭṭhāna), 2. Reverse-order Paṭṭhāna (paccanīkapaṭṭhāna), 3. Direct-reverse Paṭṭhāna (anulomapaccanīkapaṭṭhāna), 4. Reverse-direct Paṭṭhāna (paccanīkānulomapaṭṭhāna). Here, the Direct-order Paṭṭhāna is so called because it proceeds in the direct sequence, such as: "A wholesome state arises dependent on a wholesome state by root condition," and "A root state arises dependent on a root state by root condition," and so forth for the wholesome, roots, and other categories. The Reverse-order Paṭṭhāna is so called because it proceeds in the reverse sequence, such as: "A not-wholesome state arises dependent on a not-wholesome state by root condition... a not-root state arises dependent on a not-root state by root condition," and so forth for the not-wholesome, not-roots, and other categories. The Direct-reverse Paṭṭhāna is so called because it proceeds in a mixed sequence, such as: "A not-wholesome state arises dependent on a wholesome state by root condition... a not-root state arises dependent on a root state by root condition," and so forth. The Reverse-direct Paṭṭhāna is so called because it proceeds in the opposite mixed sequence, such as: "A wholesome state arises dependent on a not-wholesome state... a root state arises dependent on a not-root state by root condition," and so forth.

Evametesu catūsu paṭṭhānesu yaṃ dhammaṃ anulomapaṭṭhānaṃ nāma, taṃ tāva chabbidhaṃ hoti – tikapaṭṭhānaṃ dukapaṭṭhānaṃ dukatikapaṭṭhānaṃ tikadukapaṭṭhānaṃ tikatikapaṭṭhānaṃ dukadukapaṭṭhānanti. Yathā cetaṃ, evaṃ paccanīkapaṭṭhānādīnipi tīṇi tīṇi paccekanti catuvīsatisamantapaṭṭhānasamodhānaṃ paṭṭhānappakaraṇaṃ veditabbaṃ. Sammāsambuddhena hi anulomapaṭṭhāne dvāvīsatitike nissāya tikapaṭṭhānaṃ nāma niddiṭṭhaṃ. Sataṃ duke nissāya dukapaṭṭhānaṃ nāma. Tato tike dukesu pakkhipitvā dukatikapaṭṭhānaṃ nāma. Tato duke tikesu pakkhipitvā tikadukapaṭṭhānaṃ nāma. Tike pana tikesuyeva pakkhipitvā tikatikapaṭṭhānaṃ nāma. Duke ca dukesu eva pakkhipitvā dukadukapaṭṭhānaṃ nāma niddiṭṭhaṃ. Paṭhamaṃ tāvettha anulomapaṭṭhāne tikapaṭṭhānanayo niddiṭṭho. Evaṃ paccanīkapaṭṭhāne, anulomapaccanīkapaṭṭhāne, paccanīkānulomapaṭṭhāneti catuvīsatisamantapaṭṭhānaṃ desitaṃ.

Among these four Paṭṭhānas, that which is called the Anuloma-Paṭṭhāna (Direct Conditionality) is first of six kinds: the Tika-Paṭṭhāna (Triad Conditionality), the Duka-Paṭṭhāna (Dyad Conditionality), the Duka-Tika-Paṭṭhāna (Dyad-Triad Conditionality), the Tika-Duka-Paṭṭhāna (Triad-Dyad Conditionality), the Tika-Tika-Paṭṭhāna (Triad-Triad Conditionality), and the Duka-Duka-Paṭṭhāna (Dyad-Dyad Conditionality). Just as this is, so also the three Paṭṭhānas beginning with the Paccanīka-Paṭṭhāna (Reverse Conditionality), etc., should each be understood separately, making up the twenty-four comprehensive Paṭṭhānas (Conditionality Relations) of the Paṭṭhāna treatise. For indeed, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One has taught the Tika-Paṭṭhāna in the Anuloma-Paṭṭhāna, based on the twenty-two triads. The Duka-Paṭṭhāna is based on the one hundred dyads. Then, by inserting triads into dyads, the Duka-Tika-Paṭṭhāna is designated. Next, by inserting dyads into triads, the Tika-Duka-Paṭṭhāna is designated. Further, by inserting triads into triads alone, the Tika-Tika-Paṭṭhāna is designated. And by inserting dyads into dyads alone, the Duka-Duka-Paṭṭhāna is designated. First, here in the Anuloma-Paṭṭhāna, the method of Tika-Paṭṭhāna has been taught. Thus, in the Paccanīka-Paṭṭhāna, the Anuloma-Paccanīka-Paṭṭhāna (Direct-Reverse Conditionality), and the Paccanīka-Anuloma-Paṭṭhāna (Reverse-Direct Conditionality), the twenty-four comprehensive Paṭṭhānas have been taught.

Ettha ca duvidhaṃ anulomaṃ, paccanīkañca dhammānulomaṃ dhammapaccanīkaṃ, paccayānulomaṃ paccayapaccanīkanti. Tattha “kusalaṃ dhammaṃ [M 0.0462] paṭicca kusalo dhammo”tiādinā kusalādīnaṃ tikadhammānaṃ, hetuādīnaṃ dukadhammānañca anulomadesanāvasena dhammānulomaṃ veditabbaṃ. “Nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nakusalo dhammo”tiādinā tikadukadhammānaṃ paccanīkavasena dhammapaccanīkaṃ veditabbaṃ. “Hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā”ti evaṃ catuvīsatiyā paccayānaṃ anulomadesanāvasena paccayānulomaṃ veditabbaṃ. “Nahetupaccayā nārammaṇapaccayā”ti evaṃ paccayānaṃ paccanīkavasena paccayapaccanīkañca veditabbaṃ. Tatra yadidaṃ dhammānulomaṃ dhammapaccanīkañca, tassa vasena catuvīsatisamantapaṭṭhānaṃ veditabbaṃ. Paccayānulomaṃ paccayapaccanīkañca anulomatikapaṭṭhānādīsu catuvīsatiyā paṭṭhānesu ekekatikadukesu evaṃ labbhati. Tañca upari pāḷinayadassane eva pākaṭaṃ bhavissati. Tatrimāni catuvīsati paṭṭhānāni imesaṃ tikadukānaṃ vasena niddiṭṭhattā tikapaṭṭhānaṃ…pe… dukadukapaṭṭhānanti vuccati.

Here, anuloma (direct) and paccanīka (reverse) are each twofold: the dhammānuloma (direct order of phenomena), dhammapaccanīka (reverse order of phenomena), paccayānuloma (direct order of conditions), and paccayapaccanīka (reverse order of conditions). Herein, the dhammānuloma should be understood as the teaching in the direct manner, such as 'A wholesome phenomenon is a condition for a wholesome phenomenon,' etc., with regard to the triad phenomena of the wholesome, etc., and the dyad phenomena of roots, etc. The dhammapaccanīka should be understood as the teaching in the reverse manner, such as 'A not-wholesome phenomenon is a condition for a not-wholesome phenomenon,' etc., with regard to the triad and dyad phenomena. The paccayānuloma should be understood as the teaching in the direct manner, such as 'By way of root condition, by way of object condition,' etc., with regard to the twenty-four conditions. The paccayapaccanīka should be understood as the teaching in the reverse manner, such as 'Not by way of root condition, not by way of object condition,' etc., with regard to the conditions. Here, the dhammānuloma and dhammapaccanīka should be understood as the twenty-four comprehensive Paṭṭhānas by means of them. The paccayānuloma and paccayapaccanīka are obtained in the twenty-four Paṭṭhānas, such as the Anuloma-Tika-Paṭṭhāna (Direct-Triad Conditionality), etc., in each triad and dyad set. And that will become clear in the subsequent exposition of the Pali method. Therein, these twenty-four Paṭṭhānas are called the Tika-Paṭṭhāna... the Duka-Duka-Paṭṭhāna, because they are specified by means of these triad and dyad sets.

Tesu tikadukesu ekekaṃ tikadukaṃ imesaṃ hetupaccayādīnaṃ catuvīsatiyā paccayānaṃ anulomādinayacatukkavasena sattahi sattahi mahāvārehi vitthārato vibhattaṃ. Katamehi sattahi? Paṭiccavāro sahajātavāro paccayavāro nissayavāro saṃsaṭṭhavāro sampayuttavāro pañhāvāroti imehi[V 0.0354]. Tattha “kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo”tiādinā paṭiccābhidhānena vutto paṭiccavāro nāma. “Kusalaṃ dhammaṃ sahajāto, kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā, kusalaṃ dhammaṃ nissāya, kusalaṃ dhammaṃ saṃsaṭṭho, kusalaṃ dhammaṃ sampayutto”ti evaṃ sahajātādiabhidhānehi vuttā pañca vārā sahajātādivārāni. Parato ca saṃsaṭṭhasampayuttavāresu dvīsu arūpadhammavaseneva paccayapaccayuppannā ca, sesesu catūsu vāresu, sattameva pañhāvāre ca rūpārūpavasena, paccayavāre, nissayavāre ca sahajātapacchājātapurejātavasena, sesesu [M 0.0463] sahajātavasena paccayapaccayuppannā ca kathitāti ayaṃ viseso. Sattamavāre pana yasmā “kusalo dhammo kusalassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo”tiādinā nayena te te pañhe uddharitvā puna “kusalā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhāna”ntiādinā nayena sabbepi te pañhā nijjaṭā, niggumbā ca katvā vibhattā, tasmā so vāro pañhānaṃ sādhukaṃ vibhattattā pañhāvārotveva saṅkhaṃ gato. Iti imehi sattahi mahāvārehi catuvīsatiyā samantapaṭṭhānesu sabbepi tikadukā catuvīsatiyā paccayānaṃ anulomādivasena vitthārato vibhattā. Kathaṃ? Anulomapaṭṭhāne hi yadidaṃ dvāvīsatitike nissāya tikapaṭṭhānaṃ nāma sabbapaṭhamaṃ niddiṭṭhaṃ. Tattha kusalattikaṃ tāva imehi paṭiccavārādīhi mahāvārehi paccayānulomādinayacatukkato vibhattaṃ. Tattha yo tāvesa sabbapaṭhamo paṭiccavāro nāma, so uddesaniddesato duvidho hoti.

In these triad-dyad sets, each triad-dyad set is analyzed in detail by means of seven great sections (mahāvāra), following the fourfold method of the twenty-four conditions (paccaya) in direct order, etc. Which seven? The Paṭicca-Vāra (Section on Dependence), the Sahajāta-Vāra (Section on Co-nascence), the Paccaya-Vāra (Section on Condition), the Nissaya-Vāra (Section on Support), the Saṃsaṭṭha-Vāra (Section on Concomitance), the Sampayutta-Vāra (Section on Association), and the Pañhā-Vāra (Section on Questions)—these are the seven. Herein, the Paṭicca-Vāra is stated by the expression of dependence, such as 'A wholesome phenomenon depends on a wholesome phenomenon,' and so forth. The five sections—Sahajāta, etc.—are stated by the expressions of co-nascence, etc., such as 'A wholesome phenomenon is co-nascent with a wholesome phenomenon,' 'A wholesome phenomenon is a condition for a wholesome phenomenon,' 'A wholesome phenomenon is supported by a wholesome phenomenon,' 'A wholesome phenomenon is concomitant with a wholesome phenomenon,' and 'A wholesome phenomenon is associated with a wholesome phenomenon.' Moreover, in the two Saṃsaṭṭha-Vāra and Sampayutta-Vāra, the conditions and conditioned phenomena are only in terms of immaterial phenomena. In the remaining four sections, and in the seventh Pañhā-Vāra, they are in terms of material and immaterial phenomena. In the Paccaya-Vāra and Nissaya-Vāra, the conditions and conditioned phenomena are discussed in terms of co-nascence, subsequent arising, and prior arising. In the remaining sections, they are discussed in terms of co-nascence. This is the distinction. In the seventh Vāra, because questions such as 'A wholesome phenomenon is a root condition for a wholesome phenomenon' are raised, and then all those questions are thoroughly resolved and systematically analyzed by means such as 'Wholesome roots are conditions for the associated aggregates,' therefore, that Vāra has gone to the designation 'Section on Questions' (Pañhā-Vāra) due to its thorough analysis of questions. Thus, all triad-dyad sets in the twenty-four comprehensive Paṭṭhānas are analyzed in detail by these seven great sections, following the twenty-four conditions in direct order, etc. How? In the Anuloma-Paṭṭhāna, the Tika-Paṭṭhāna, which relies on the twenty-two triads, is first pointed out.
