Herein, the wholesome triad (kusalattika) is analyzed by these great sections—beginning with the Paṭicca-Vāra—according to the fourfold method of conditions in direct order, etc. Herein, that very first Paṭicca-Vāra is twofold: by way of recitation (uddesa) and by way of exposition (niddesa).

Tattha uddesavāro kusalādayo paṭicca hetupaccayādivasena kusalādīnaṃ yuttānaṃ, akusalādīnaṃ ayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ uppattipucchanavaseneva pavattattā “pucchāvāro”tipi, pucchānaññeva paññāpanato “paṇṇattivāro”tipi vuccati. Na hi tattha vissajjanaṃ atthi. Niddesavāro pana pucchāvāre paripucchitesu pañhesu “siyā akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca akusalo dhammo uppajjeyyā”tiādikaṃ ayuttaṃ pañhaṃ anuddharitvā labbhamānānaññeva pañhānaṃ vasena pavatto. Itaresu pana sahajātādīsu, sesesu ca tikesu, sesapaṭṭhānesu ca sabbattha pucchāvāro natthi, labbhamānavasena sabbavissajjanameva dassitanti idamettha saṅkhepato pāḷivavatthānaṃ.

Here, the recitation section (uddesavāra) is also called the 'question section' (pucchāvāra) because it proceeds by way of questions about the arising of phenomena—such as wholesome states, etc., that are appropriate, and unwholesome states, etc., that are inappropriate—in dependence on wholesome states, etc., by way of root condition, etc. It is also called the 'designation section' (paṇṇattivāra) because it merely presents the questions themselves. Indeed, there is no answer there. The exposition section (niddesavāra), however, proceeds by way of only the obtainable questions from among those fully questioned in the question section, without taking up inappropriate questions such as, 'Could an unwholesome phenomenon arise dependent on an unwholesome phenomenon?' In the other sections, however, such as the Sahajāta-Vāra, and in the remaining triads and remaining Paṭṭhānas, there is no question section anywhere; only all the obtainable answers are shown. This, in brief, is the arrangement of the Pāli text here.

Idāni panettha ādito paṭṭhāya evaṃ vibhaṅganayo veditabbo. Anulomapaṭṭhānasmiñhi tikapaṭṭhāne kusalattikassa sattasu mahāvāresu paṭhamassa paṭiccavārassa pucchāvāre tāva [M 0.0464] – “siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya hetupaccayā…pe… akusalo dhammo…pe… abyākato…pe… kusalo ca abyākato ca…pe… akusalo ca abyākato [V 0.0355] ca…pe… kusalo ca akusalo ca…pe… kusalo ca akusalo ca abyākato ca dhammā uppajjeyyuṃ hetupaccayā”ti kusalapadamūlā satta pucchā uddhaṭā.

Now, here, the method of analysis should be understood from the beginning thus. In the Anuloma-Paṭṭhāna, specifically the Tika-Paṭṭhāna, in the question section (pucchāvāra) of the first Paṭicca-Vāra among the seven great sections concerning the Kusalattika (wholesome triad), seven questions with the wholesome term as their basis are raised: 'Could a wholesome phenomenon arise dependent on a wholesome phenomenon by way of root condition? … an unwholesome phenomenon? … an indeterminate phenomenon? … both wholesome and indeterminate? … both unwholesome and indeterminate? … both wholesome and unwholesome? … and wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate phenomena arise by way of root condition?'

Evaṃ akusalapadamūlā, abyākatapadamūlā ca. “Siyā kusalañca abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca akusalo…pe… siyā akusalañca abyākatañca…pe… siyā kusalañca akusalañca…pe… siyā kusalañca akusalañca abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭiccā”ti dvimūlakā, timūlakā ca satta satta pucchāti ekūnapaññāsa pucchā hetupaccayamūlakā uddhaṭā.

Likewise, there are questions with the unwholesome term as their basis, and with the indeterminate term as their basis. 'Could an unwholesome phenomenon arise… dependent on a wholesome and indeterminate phenomenon? … dependent on an unwholesome and indeterminate phenomenon? … dependent on a wholesome and unwholesome phenomenon? … dependent on a wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate phenomenon?' Thus, for the double-rooted and triple-rooted sets, with seven questions each, forty-nine questions based on the root condition are raised.

Imināva nayena “siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya ārammaṇapaccayā…pe… avigatapaccayā”ti evaṃ sesapaccayamūlakāpi pucchāveditabbā. Ekamūlakanayo.

By this same method, the questions based on the remaining conditions should also be understood, such as: 'Could a wholesome phenomenon arise dependent on a wholesome phenomenon by way of object condition? … up to non-disappearance condition.' This is the method of a single root.

Yathā ca ekamūlake, evaṃ “siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā…pe… hetupaccayā avigatapaccayā”tiādinā dvimūlakepi. “Hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā adhipatipaccayā…pe… hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā anantarapaccayā…pe… hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā avigatapaccayā”tiādinā timūlakādīsu sabbamūlakapariyosānesu vāresu nayā veditabbā. Hetupaccayamūlakanayo.

Just as with a single root, so too with two roots, as in: 'Could a wholesome phenomenon arise dependent on a wholesome phenomenon by way of root condition and object condition? … up to root condition and non-disappearance condition?' Similarly, with three roots and so on, up to the conclusion with all roots, the methods should be understood in the sections, such as: 'By way of root condition, object condition, and dominance condition? … up to root condition, object condition, and contiguity condition? … up to root condition, object condition, and non-disappearance condition?' This is the method based on the root condition.

Yathā ca hetumūlake, evaṃ “siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya ārammaṇapaccayā”tiādinā sesapaccayamūlakesupi nayo ñātabbo. Paccayānulomavāro. Eteneva upāyena “siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya nahetupaccayā”tiādinā sabbappakārayutto [M 0.0465] paccayapaccanīkavāropi. “Siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ…pe… uppajjati hetupaccayā nārammaṇapaccayā”tiādinā anulomapaccanīkapaccayavāropi. “Siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ…pe… uppajjeyya nahetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā”tiādinā paccanīyānulomavāropi sabbattha netabboti ayaṃ tāvettha pucchāvāre nayo.

Just as with what is rooted in the root condition, so too the method should be understood in the cases rooted in the remaining conditions, such as: 'Could a wholesome phenomenon arise dependent on a wholesome phenomenon by way of object condition?' This is the Section on Conditions in Serial Order (Paccayānuloma-Vāra). By this same means, the Section on Negative Conditions (Paccayapaccanīka-Vāra), complete in every aspect, should also be understood, such as: 'Could a wholesome phenomenon arise dependent on a wholesome phenomenon by way of non-root condition?' And likewise, the Section on Serial-Negative Conditions (Anulomapaccanīka-Paccaya-Vāra), such as: 'Could a wholesome phenomenon… arise by way of root condition, but not by way of object condition?' Also, the Section on Negative-Serial Conditions (Paccanīyānuloma-Vāra), such as: 'Could a wholesome phenomenon… arise by way of non-root condition and object condition?' This is the method to be applied everywhere in the question section.

Niddesavāro pana uddesavāre dassitāsu pucchāsu kusalākusalādīnaṃ sahuppattiyā abhāvato yā etā “kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjatī”tiādikā pucchā sabbaso [V 0.0356] vissajjanaṃ labhanti, tā pahāya yā vissajjanaṃ labhanti, tāsameva vissajjanavasena pavatto. Tatrāyaṃ nayo – “kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Kusalaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā. Tayo khandhe paṭicca eko khandho. Dve khandhe paṭicca dve khandhā. Kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Kusale khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. Kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo ca abyākato ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. Kusalaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ. Tayo khandhe paṭicca eko khandho cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ. Dve khandhe paṭicca dve khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpa”nti evaṃ kusalapadamūlāsu sattasu pucchāsu tissova labbhamānā vissajjitā. Tathā akusalapadamūlāsupi tissova. Abyākatapadamūlāsu pana “abyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Vipākābyākataṃ kiriyābyākataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe paṭicca dve khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākābyākataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā kaṭattā ca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhā kaṭattā ca rūpaṃ. Khandhe paṭicca vatthu, vatthuṃ paṭicca khandhā. Ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca tayo mahābhūtā…pe… dve mahābhūte paṭicca [M 0.0466] dve mahābhūtā. Mahābhūte paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpa”nti ekāva. Dvimūlikādīsu ca “kusalañca abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Kusale khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpa”nti ekā. Tathā “akusalañca abyākatañca paṭiccā”ti, evaṃ hetupaccayamūlikāsu ekūnapaññāsāya pucchāsu naveva labbhamānā vissajjitā. Sesā cattālīsa moghapucchāti na vissajjitā. Evaṃ upari ārammaṇapaccayādīsu vissajjitāvasesā moghapucchāti gahetabbā. Vijānanasukhatthaṃ pana bhagavatā pucchāvāre labbhamānā, alabbhamānā ca sabbāpi tā dassitāti veditabbāti.

The Exposition Section, however, proceeds by way of answering only those questions from the Recitation Section that receive an answer, setting aside those that do not, because of the non-co-arising of wholesome and unwholesome states, etc. Here is the method: 'A wholesome phenomenon arises in dependence on a wholesome phenomenon by way of root condition. In dependence on one wholesome aggregate, three aggregates arise. In dependence on three aggregates, one aggregate arises. In dependence on two aggregates, two aggregates arise. An indeterminate phenomenon arises in dependence on a wholesome phenomenon by way of root condition. Mind-originated matter arises in dependence on wholesome aggregates. Both a wholesome phenomenon and an indeterminate phenomenon arise in dependence on a wholesome phenomenon by way of root condition. In dependence on one wholesome aggregate, three aggregates and mind-originated matter arise. In dependence on three aggregates, one aggregate and mind-originated matter arise. In dependence on two aggregates, two aggregates and mind-originated matter arise.' Thus, among the seven questions rooted in the wholesome term, only the three applicable ones are answered. Similarly, among those rooted in the unwholesome term, only three. But among those rooted in the indeterminate term, only one is answered: 'An indeterminate phenomenon arises in dependence on an indeterminate phenomenon by way of root condition. In dependence on one resultant-indeterminate or functional-indeterminate aggregate, three aggregates and mind-originated matter arise… and so on… in dependence on two aggregates, two aggregates and mind-originated matter arise. At the moment of rebirth-linking, in dependence on one resultant-indeterminate aggregate, three aggregates and kamma-born matter arise… and so on… in dependence on two aggregates, two aggregates and kamma-born matter arise. The aggregates are dependent on the physical basis; the physical basis is dependent on the aggregates. In dependence on one great element, three great elements arise… and so on… in dependence on two great elements, two great elements arise. In dependence on the great elements, mind-originated matter, kamma-born matter, and derived matter arise.' And in the cases of two roots, etc., only one is answered: 'An indeterminate phenomenon arises in dependence on a wholesome phenomenon and an indeterminate phenomenon by way of root condition. Mind-originated matter arises in dependence on wholesome aggregates and the great elements.' Similarly for 'in dependence on an unwholesome and an indeterminate phenomenon.' Thus, among the forty-nine questions rooted in the root condition, only the nine applicable ones are answered. The remaining forty are futile questions and are not answered. In the same way, for the subsequent conditions, such as object condition, the remaining unanswered questions should be taken as futile questions. It should be understood that for the sake of easy understanding, the Blessed One has shown all of them in the Question Section, both the applicable and the inapplicable.

Tattha kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭiccāti sahajātesu vedanākkhandhādibhedaṃ ekaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca paṭigantvā, sahuppattisaṅkhātena sadisabhāvena patvāti attho. Sadisattho hi ettha paṭisaddo “paṭipuggalo”tiādīsu viya. Kusalo dhammoti saññākkhandhādibhedo sahuppanno kusalo dhammo. Uppajjatīti pākaṭabhāvato uddhaṃ uppādādiṃ pāpuṇāti, attānaṃ vā paṭilabhati. Hetupaccayāti na kevalaṃ kusaladhammamattameva paṭicca uppajjati, atha kho kusalahetunā hetupaccayataṃ sādhentena ca uppajjatīti evamattho gahetabbo.

Herein, 'in dependence on a wholesome dhamma' means: having depended on one wholesome dhamma, such as the feeling aggregate, etc., among co-nascent states, and having attained a similar nature by way of what is termed co-arising. This is the meaning. For here the prefix paṭi has the sense of 'similar,' as in such expressions as paṭipuggala ('counterpart person'). 'A wholesome dhamma' is a co-arisen wholesome dhamma, such as the perception aggregate, etc. 'Arises' means it attains arising, etc., beyond the state of being manifest, or it acquires its own nature. 'By way of root condition' means: it does not arise merely in dependence on a wholesome dhamma alone, but it also arises with a wholesome root accomplishing the state of a root condition. This is how the meaning should be understood.

Evamidaṃ [V 0.0357] “uppajjeyyā”ti pucchāya “uppajjatī”ti avisesena vissajjanaṃ vatvā idāni yaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca ye dhammā uppajjanti, te paccayapaccayuppanne khandhavasena visesetvā dassetuṃ “kusalaṃ ekaṃ khandha”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Yasmā panettha eko khandho ekasseva, dvinnaṃyeva vā, dve vā pana ekasseva paccayā nāma na honti, tasmā te pakārena anāmasitvā “ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā”tiādinā paccayabhāvena gahitāvasesaṃ sabbaṃ paccayuppannaṃ katvā dassitanti veditabbaṃ. Evaṃ uparipi sabbattha. Cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpanti idaṃ paṭiccatthassa sahajātatthattā [M 0.0467] yaṃ kusalena sahajātañceva hetupaccayañca labhati, taṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “vipākābyākataṃ kiriyābyākata”nti. Ettha hetupaccayādhikāre ahetukā na gahetabbā. Khandhe paṭicca vatthūtiādi kaṭattārūpaggahaṇena vatthusmiṃ gahitepi vatthuṃ paṭicca arūpakkhandhānaṃ uppattidassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Ekaṃ mahābhūtantiādi pana rūpābyākataṃ paṭicca rūpābyākatassa uppattidassanatthaṃ. Hetupaccaye upatthambhakānameva cettha cittajānaṃ, paṭisandhiyaṃ kammajānañca aññamaññaṃ paccayapaccayuppannatā gahetabbā, na ahetukacittajautujādīnaṃ tesaṃ hetupaccayā uppattiyā abhāvato. Mahābhūte paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānantiādi mahābhūte paṭicca upādādīnaṃ uppattidassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Iminā upāyena ārammaṇapaccayādīsupi vissajjanānaṃ attho veditabbo.

Thus, having given the general answer 'it arises' to the question 'would it arise?', the text now says 'one wholesome aggregate,' etc., in order to show by specifying, in terms of aggregates, which dhammas arise in dependence on which, as condition and conditionally arisen. It should be understood that since one aggregate is not a condition for only one other, or for only two others, nor are two aggregates a condition for only one other, these cases are not mentioned. Instead, by stating 'in dependence on one aggregate, three aggregates arise,' etc., it is shown that all the remaining aggregates are made conditionally arisen by that which is taken as the condition. This should be understood similarly in all subsequent cases. The phrase 'mind-originated matter' is stated to show that which obtains both co-nascence with the wholesome and the root condition, since the meaning of 'in dependence on' is 'co-nascent'. In the section on root condition, rootless states are not to be included. The phrase 'in dependence on the aggregates, the physical basis,' etc., is stated to show the arising of the immaterial aggregates in dependence on the physical basis, even though the physical basis is already included with the inclusion of kamma-born matter. The phrase 'in dependence on one great element,' etc., is stated to show the arising of indeterminate matter in dependence on indeterminate matter. Here, in the root condition, only the supporting mind-born matter and, at rebirth-linking, kamma-born matter should be taken as mutually condition and conditionally arisen, not rootless mind-born, temperature-born matter, etc., because they do not arise by way of root condition. The phrase 'in dependence on the great elements, mind-originated,' etc., is stated to show the arising of derived matter, etc., in dependence on the great elements. By this method, the meaning of the answers concerning object condition, etc., should also be understood.

Ārammaṇapaccaye “kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā. Ekaṃ khandhaṃ…pe… dve khandhe paṭicca dve khandhā. Akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca akusalo dhammo…pe… abyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā. Vipākābyākataṃ kiriyābyākataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ…pe… dve khandhā. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākābyākataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ…pe… dve khandhā. Vatthuṃ paṭicca khandhā”ti evaṃ tisso vissajjitā. Sesā rūpamissakattā, rūpassa ca ārammaṇapaccayena anuppattito na gahitā. Teneva “vatthuṃ paṭicca khandhā”ti vatvā “khandhe paṭicca vatthū”ti na vuttaṃ. Ettha ca ārammaṇapaccayāti sahajātaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca uppajjamāno kusalo dhammo tato aññena asahajātena chabbidhena ārammaṇabhūtena paccayenāti evaṃ attho gahetabbo. Na hi attanā sahajātaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā cittacetasikā uppajjanti.

In the object condition: 'A wholesome dhamma arises in dependence on a wholesome dhamma by way of object condition. One aggregate… pe … two aggregates in dependence on two aggregates. An unwholesome dhamma arises in dependence on an unwholesome dhamma… pe … an indeterminate dhamma arises in dependence on an indeterminate dhamma by way of object condition. Resultant-indeterminate and functional-indeterminate, one aggregate… pe … two aggregates. At the moment of rebirth-linking, resultant-indeterminate, one aggregate… pe … two aggregates. Aggregates in dependence on the physical basis.' Thus, three answers are given. The rest are not included because they are mixed with matter, and matter does not arise by way of object condition. For that reason, having said 'aggregates in dependence on the physical basis,' it is not said 'the physical basis in dependence on the aggregates.' Here, 'by way of object condition' should be understood to mean this: a wholesome dhamma, while arising in dependence on a co-nascent wholesome dhamma, is conditioned by another, non-co-nascent dhamma that has become an object in six ways. For consciousness and mental factors do not arise taking a co-nascent state as their object.

Adhipatipaccaye hetupaccayasadisaṃ vissajjanaṃ. Anantarasamanantaresu pana rūpābhāvato ārammaṇapaccayasadisaṃ. Sahajātapaccayepi [M 0.0468] hetupaccayasadisaṃ. Abyākataṃ paṭicca abyākatuppattiyā [V 0.0358] pana “bāhiraṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca…pe… dve mahābhūtā. Mahābhūte paṭicca upādārūpaṃ…pe… āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… dve mahābhūtā…pe… utusamuṭṭhānaṃ ekaṃ…pe… dve mahābhūtā…pe… asaññasattānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca…pe… dve mahābhūtā…pe… kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpa”nti idaṃ adhikaṃ. Evaṃ aññamaññapaccayepi. Kevalaṃ tattha kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpañca na gahitaṃ tesaṃ aññamaññapaccayattābhāvā. Nissayapaccayepi sahajātapaccayasadisaṃ vissajjanaṃ. Paṭiccatthassa pana sahajātatthattā cakkhādīsu purejātanissayā idha na gahitāti. Upanissayapaccayepi rūpassa upanissayapaccayuppannattābhāvā ārammaṇapaccayasadisameva vissajjanaṃ.

In dominance condition, the answer is similar to that for root condition. In contiguity and immediate contiguity conditions, however, it is similar to that for object condition due to the absence of matter. In co-nascence condition, it is also similar to that for root condition. However, regarding the arising of an indeterminate dhamma in dependence on an indeterminate dhamma, the following is additional: 'in dependence on one external great element… pe … two great elements; in dependence on the great elements, derived matter… pe … nutriment-originated, one great element… pe … two great elements… pe … temperature-originated, one… pe … two great elements… pe … of non-percipient beings, in dependence on one great element… pe … two great elements… pe … kamma-born matter, derived matter.' It is similar in mutuality condition. Only, there, kamma-born matter and derived matter are not included because they lack the nature of a mutuality condition. In dependence condition, too, the answer is similar to that for co-nascence condition. However, since the meaning of the term 'in dependence on' is co-nascence, pre-nascence dependence in regard to the eye, etc., is not included here. In decisive support condition, too, since matter does not arise as conditionally arisen by decisive support, the answer is similar to that for object condition.

Purejātapaccaye pana “kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjati purejātapaccayā. Kusalaṃ ekaṃ…pe… dve khandhā. Vatthuṃ purejātapaccayā. Akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca akusalo…pe… abyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato…pe… purejātapaccayā. Vipākābyākataṃ kiriyābyākataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ…pe… dve khandhā. Vatthuṃ purejātapaccayā”ti evaṃ tisso pucchā vissajjitā. Tattha vatthuṃ purejātapaccayāti idaṃ ārammaṇapurejātanivattanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Taṃ hi cakkhuviññāṇādīnaṃyeva purejātapaccayataṃ sādhayati, na manoviññāṇadhātuyāti idha na gahitaṃ.

In pre-nascence condition, however, three questions are answered thus: 'A wholesome dhamma arises in dependence on a wholesome dhamma by way of pre-nascence condition. One wholesome aggregate… pe … two aggregates. The physical basis by way of pre-nascence condition. An unwholesome dhamma arises in dependence on an unwholesome dhamma… pe … an indeterminate dhamma arises in dependence on an indeterminate dhamma… pe … by way of pre-nascence condition. Resultant-indeterminate and functional-indeterminate—one aggregate… pe … two aggregates. The physical basis by way of pre-nascence condition.' Here, the phrase 'the physical basis by way of pre-nascence condition' is stated to exclude object-prenascence. For that object-prenascence establishes pre-nascence conditionality only for eye-consciousness and so on, not for the mind-consciousness-element, so it is not included here.

Pacchājātapaccayo idha arūpadhammesu na labbhati. Rūpadhammesu ca upatthambhakova, na janako, tasmā “abyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato dhammo uppajjatī”tiādi na vattabbovāti ayaṃ na gahito. Āsevanapaccayepi ārammaṇapaccaye viya tissova pucchā vissajjitā.

The post-nascence condition is not found here among immaterial dhammas. Among material dhammas, it is only supportive, not generative; therefore, the statement 'an indeterminate dhamma arises in dependence on an indeterminate dhamma,' and so on, should not be stated—thus it is not included. In the habituation condition, as in the object condition, answers are given for the three categories.

Kammapaccaye [M 0.0469] “kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjati kammapaccayā. Kusalaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ…pe… abyākato dhammo uppajjati…pe… cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… kusalo ca abyākato ca dhammā…pe… cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpa”nti kusalapade tisso, tathā akusalapade. Abyākatapade pana “abyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato…pe… vipākābyākataṃ kiriyābyākataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ, asaññasattānaṃ…pe… kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpa”nti evaṃ tisso. “Kusalañca abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato…pe… kusale khandhe ca mahābhūte [V 0.0359] ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpa”ntiādinā sahajātasadisaṃ vissajjanaṃ. Natthivigatapaccayesu ārammaṇasadisaṃ.

In the kamma condition: 'A wholesome dhamma arises in dependence on a wholesome dhamma by way of kamma condition. One wholesome aggregate... an indeterminate dhamma arises... and mind-originated matter... a wholesome and an indeterminate dhamma... mind-originated matter.' Thus, there are three answers in the wholesome category, and likewise in the unwholesome category. But in the indeterminate category: 'An indeterminate dhamma arises in dependence on an indeterminate dhamma... resultant-indeterminate and functional-indeterminate—one aggregate... in dependence on the great elements, mind-originated matter, kamma-born matter, derived matter; for non-percipient beings... kamma-born matter, derived matter.' Thus, there are three answers. 'An indeterminate dhamma arises in dependence on a wholesome and an indeterminate dhamma... in dependence on wholesome aggregates and the great elements, mind-originated matter,' etc.—the answer is similar to that for the co-nascence condition. In the absence and disappearance conditions, the answer is similar to that for the object condition.

Evaṃ sabbapaccayesu labbhamānapañhe vissajjanaṃ dassetvā tato hetuadhipatijhānamaggapaccayā ekasadisā. Ārammaṇānantarasamanantarūpanissayāsevananatthivigatapaccayā ekasadisā. Sahajātaaññamaññanissayaatthiavigatā ekasadisā. Āsevanapaccaye vipāko na labbhati. Aññamaññapaccaye cittajarūpaṃ, upādārūpañca na labbhatītiādinā paccayānaṃ aññamaññasadisattaṃ vatvā puna tesaṃ “hetuyā nava. Ārammaṇe tīṇi. Adhipatiyā nava. Anantarasamanantaresu tīṇi. Sahajāte nava. Aññamaññe tīṇi. Nissaye nava. Upanissaye tīṇi. Purejāte tīṇi. Āsevane tīṇi. Kamme nava. Vipāke ekaṃ. Āhāre nava. Indriye nava. Jhāne nava. Magge nava. Sampayutte tīṇi. Vippayutte nava. Atthiyā nava. Natthiyā tīṇi. Vigate tīṇi. Avigate navā”ti evaṃ hetupaccayādīnaṃ ekekasmiṃ pucchāvissajjanavāragaṇanā vuttāti ayaṃ ekamūlakanayo.

Having thus shown the answers to the questions obtainable in all conditions, then the root condition, dominance condition, absorption condition, and path condition are similar. The object condition, immediate condition, contiguity condition, strong support condition, habituation condition, absence condition, and disappearance condition are similar. The co-nascence condition, reciprocity condition, support condition, presence condition, and non-disappearance condition are similar. In the habituation condition, result is not obtained. In the reciprocity condition, mind-produced materiality and derived materiality are not obtained. Thus, having stated the mutual similarities of the conditions, it is further said: "In the root condition, nine. In the object condition, three. In the dominance condition, nine. In the immediate and contiguity conditions, three. In the co-nascence condition, nine. In the reciprocity condition, three. In the support condition, nine. In the strong support condition, three. In the pre-nascence condition, three. In the habituation condition, three. In the kamma condition, nine. In the result condition, one. In the nutriment condition, nine. In the faculty condition, nine. In the absorption condition, nine. In the path condition, nine. In the association condition, three. In the separation condition, nine. In the presence condition, nine. In the absence condition, three. In the disappearance condition, three. In the non-disappearance condition, nine." Thus, the enumeration of the question-and-answer sets in each individual condition beginning with the root condition is stated. This is the single-root method.

Yathā ca ekamūlake, evaṃ “hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā”tiādinā dvimūlakādīsupi sabbamūlakapariyosānesu yathānurūpaṃ [M 0.0470] nayo netabbo. Pāḷiyampi vitthāranayaṃ adassetvā “hetupaccayā ārammaṇe tīṇī”tiādinā vissajjanavāragaṇanabhedo dassitoti ayaṃ paccayānulome nayo.

Just as in the single-root method, so too in the two-root methods and so on, up to the conclusion of all roots, the method should be applied accordingly, as in 'by way of root condition, by way of object condition,' and so on. Even in the Pāli, without showing the detailed method, the difference in the enumeration of the answer-sets is shown by 'in the root condition, in the object condition, three,' and so on. Thus, this is the method in the forward order of conditions.

Paccayapaccanīye pana “akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca akusalo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā. Vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe paṭicca vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho. Abyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā. Ahetukaṃ vipākābyākataṃ kiriyābyākataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ…pe… dve khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ. Ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākābyākataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ…pe… dve khandhā kaṭattā ca rūpaṃ…pe… vatthuṃ paṭicca khandhā. Ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ, kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ…pe… ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca…pe… upādārūpa”nti imā dve vissajjitā.

In the conditional relations of negation: "Dependent on an unwholesome phenomenon, an unwholesome phenomenon arises by way of the non-root condition. Dependent on aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness, delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness arises. Dependent on an indeterminate phenomenon, an indeterminate phenomenon arises by way of the non-root condition. A rootless resultant-indeterminate or functional-indeterminate single aggregate... two aggregates and mind-produced materiality. At the moment of rootless rebirth-linking, a resultant-indeterminate single aggregate... two aggregates and kamma-produced materiality...dependent on the base, the aggregates. Dependent on one great element... dependent on the great elements, mind-produced materiality, kamma-produced materiality, derived materiality... dependent on one great element... derived materiality." These two are answered.

Nārammaṇapaccaye [V 0.0360] “kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato…pe… kusale…pe… akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato…pe… akusale…pe… abyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato…pe… kusalañca abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato…pe… cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ, akusalañca abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpa”nti imā pañca vissajjitā.

In the non-object condition: "Dependent on a wholesome phenomenon, an indeterminate phenomenon arises... (and so on)... dependent on a wholesome phenomenon... (and so on)... dependent on an unwholesome phenomenon, an indeterminate phenomenon arises... (and so on)... dependent on an unwholesome phenomenon... (and so on)... dependent on an indeterminate phenomenon, an indeterminate phenomenon arises... (and so on)... dependent on a wholesome and indeterminate phenomenon, an indeterminate phenomenon arises... (and so on)... mind-produced materiality; dependent on an unwholesome and indeterminate phenomenon, an indeterminate phenomenon arises... (and so on)... dependent on the great elements, mind-produced materiality." These five are answered.

Nādhipatipaccaye “kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo…pe… kusalaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ…pe… dve khandhā. Kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato…pe… kusale khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. Kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo ca abyākato ca dhammā uppajjanti…pe… akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca akusalo…pe… dve khandhe paṭicca dve khandhā, akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato…pe… akusale khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. Akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca akusalo ca abyākato ca dhammā…pe… abyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato [M 0.0471] …pe… mahābhūte paṭicca…pe… kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Kusalañca abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato…pe… kusale khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. Akusalañca abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato…pe… akusale khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpa”nti nava pucchā vissajjitā. Nānantaranasamanantarapaccayā nārammaṇapaccayasadisā.

In the non-dominance condition: "Dependent on a wholesome phenomenon, a wholesome phenomenon arises... (and so on)... one wholesome aggregate... (and so on)... two aggregates. Dependent on a wholesome phenomenon, an indeterminate phenomenon arises... (and so on)... dependent on wholesome aggregates, mind-produced materiality arises. Dependent on a wholesome phenomenon, a wholesome phenomenon and an indeterminate phenomenon arise... (and so on)... Dependent on an unwholesome phenomenon, an unwholesome phenomenon arises... (and so on)... dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise. Dependent on an unwholesome phenomenon, an indeterminate phenomenon arises... (and so on)... dependent on unwholesome aggregates, mind-produced materiality arises. Dependent on an unwholesome phenomenon, an unwholesome phenomenon and an indeterminate phenomenon arise... (and so on)... Dependent on an indeterminate phenomenon, an indeterminate phenomenon arises... (and so on)... dependent on the great elements... (and so on)... kamma-produced materiality, derived materiality. Dependent on a wholesome and indeterminate phenomenon, an indeterminate phenomenon arises... (and so on)... dependent on wholesome aggregates and the great elements, mind-produced materiality arises. Dependent on an unwholesome and indeterminate phenomenon, an indeterminate phenomenon arises... (and so on)... dependent on unwholesome aggregates and the great elements, mind-produced materiality arises." These nine questions are answered. The non-immediate and non-contiguity conditions are similar to the non-object condition.

Nāññamaññapaccaye “kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato…pe… kusale…pe… cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. Akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato…pe… akusale…pe… cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. Abyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato…pe… vipākābyākate kiriyābyākate khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākābyākate…pe… kaṭattā rūpaṃ. Mahābhūte paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Bāhire mahābhūte paṭicca upādārūpaṃ. Āhārasamuṭṭhāne mahābhūte paṭicca upādārūpaṃ. Utusamuṭṭhāne…pe… upādārūpaṃ. Asaññasattānaṃ mahābhūte paṭicca kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Kusalañca abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato…pe… kusale khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. Akusalañca abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato…pe… akusale khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpa”nti pañca vissajjitā. Tattha vipākābyākate [V 0.0361] khandhe paṭicca kaṭattārūpanti hadayavatthuvajjaṃ veditabbaṃ. Naupanissayapaccayo nārammaṇapaccayasadiso.

In the non-reciprocity condition: "Dependent on a wholesome phenomenon, an indeterminate phenomenon...pe... dependent on wholesome...pe... mind-produced materiality. Dependent on an unwholesome phenomenon, an indeterminate phenomenon...pe... dependent on unwholesome...pe... mind-produced materiality. Dependent on an indeterminate phenomenon, an indeterminate phenomenon...pe... dependent on resultant-indeterminate and functional-indeterminate aggregates, mind-produced materiality. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on resultant-indeterminate...pe... kamma-produced materiality. Dependent on the great elements, mind-produced materiality, kamma-produced materiality, and derived materiality. Dependent on external great elements, derived materiality. Dependent on nutriment-produced great elements, derived materiality. Dependent on temperature-produced...pe... derived materiality. For non-percipient beings, dependent on the great elements, kamma-produced materiality and derived materiality. Dependent on a wholesome and indeterminate phenomenon, an indeterminate phenomenon...pe... dependent on wholesome aggregates and the great elements, mind-produced materiality. Dependent on an unwholesome and indeterminate phenomenon, an indeterminate phenomenon...pe... dependent on unwholesome aggregates and the great elements, mind-produced materiality." These five are answered. Herein, "dependent on resultant-indeterminate aggregates, kamma-produced materiality" should be understood as excluding the heart-base. The non-strong support condition is similar to the non-object condition.

Napurejātapaccaye “kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo…pe… arūpe kusalaṃ…pe… dve khandhā. Kusalaṃ paṭicca abyākato…pe… cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpa”nti kusalapade dve, tathā akusalapadepi. “Abyākataṃ paṭicca abyākato…pe… arūpe vipākābyākataṃ kiriyābyākataṃ…pe… bāhiraṃ…pe… upādārūpaṃ. Kusalañca [M 0.0472] abyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato. Kusale khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. Akusalañca abyākatañca…pe… akusale khandhe ca…pe… rūpa”nti imā tissoti satta vissajjitā. Napacchājātanāsevanapaccayā nādhipatipaccayasadisā. Tattha kusalākusalakiriyānaṃ paṭhamajavanavasena nāsevanapaccayappavatti veditabbā.

In the non-prenascence condition: "Dependent on a wholesome phenomenon, a wholesome phenomenon... in the immaterial, a wholesome phenomenon... two aggregates. Dependent on a wholesome phenomenon, an indeterminate phenomenon... mind-produced materiality." In the wholesome section, two; similarly in the unwholesome section. "Dependent on an indeterminate phenomenon, an indeterminate phenomenon... in the immaterial, resultant-indeterminate and functional-indeterminate... external... derived materiality. Dependent on a wholesome and indeterminate phenomenon, an indeterminate phenomenon. Dependent on wholesome aggregates and the great elements, mind-produced materiality. Dependent on an unwholesome and indeterminate phenomenon... dependent on unwholesome aggregates and... materiality." These three make seven answered. The non-postnascence and non-habituation conditions are similar to the non-dominance condition. Herein, the occurrence of the non-habituation condition should be understood as occurring in the first impulsion of wholesome, unwholesome, and functional states.

Nakammapaccaye “kusalaṃ paṭicca kusalo, kusalā cetanā. Akusalaṃ paṭicca akusalo, akusalā cetanā. Abyākataṃ paṭicca abyākato, vipākakiriyā cetanā. Bāhiraṃ, āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ, utusamuṭṭhāna”nti tisso vissajjitā.

In the non-kamma condition: "Dependent on a wholesome phenomenon, a wholesome phenomenon, that is, wholesome volition; dependent on an unwholesome phenomenon, an unwholesome phenomenon, that is, unwholesome volition; dependent on an indeterminate phenomenon, an indeterminate phenomenon, that is, resultant and functional volition. External, nutriment-produced, and temperature-produced." These three are answered.

Navipākapaccaye “kusalaṃ paṭicca kusalo, abyākato. Kusalo ca abyākato cā”ti kusalapade tisso, tathā akusalapadepi. “Abyākataṃ paṭicca abyākato…pe… bāhiraṃ āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ utusamuṭṭhānaṃ asañña…pe… upādārūpaṃ…pe… akusalañca abyākatañca abyākato”ti imā tissoti nava vissajjitā.

In the non-result condition: "Dependent on a wholesome phenomenon: a wholesome phenomenon; an indeterminate phenomenon; and both a wholesome and an indeterminate phenomenon." Three under the wholesome term, and likewise under the unwholesome term. "Dependent on an indeterminate phenomenon, an indeterminate phenomenon… external, nutriment-produced, temperature-produced, non-percipient beings… derived materiality… Dependent on an unwholesome and an indeterminate phenomenon, an indeterminate phenomenon." These three make nine answered.

Nāhārapaccaye “abyākataṃ paṭicca abyākato. Bāhiraṃ utusamuṭṭhānaṃ, asañña…pe… upādārūpa”nti ekāva.

In the non-nutriment condition: "An indeterminate phenomenon depends on an indeterminate phenomenon. External, temperature-originated, non-percipient-being-originated… derived materiality." Only one.

Naindriyapaccaye “abyākataṃ paṭicca abyākato. Bāhiraṃ āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… utusamuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… asaññasattānaṃ mahābhūte paṭicca rūpajīvitindriya”nti ekāva.

In the non-faculty condition: "An indeterminate phenomenon depends on an indeterminate phenomenon. External, nutriment-originated… temperature-originated… in non-percipient beings, the material life faculty depends on the great elements." Only one.

Najhānapaccaye [V 0.0362] “abyākataṃ paṭicca abyākato. Pañcaviññāṇasahagataṃ…pe… bāhiraṃ āhārautuasaññaupādārūpa”nti ekāva.

In the non-jhāna condition: "An indeterminate phenomenon depends on an indeterminate phenomenon. Accompanied by the five sense-consciousnesses… external, nutriment-originated, temperature-originated, and non-percipient-being-originated derived materiality." Only one.

Namaggapaccaye “abyākataṃ paṭicca abyākato. Ahetukaṃ vipākābyākataṃ kiriyābyākataṃ…pe… cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe [M 0.0473] vipākā…pe… kaṭattā ca rūpaṃ…pe… bāhiraṃ āhārautuasaññaupādārūpa”nti ekāva.

In the non-path condition: "An indeterminate phenomenon depends on an indeterminate phenomenon. Rootless resultant-indeterminate, functional-indeterminate… mind-originated… at the rootless rebirth-moment, resultant… and kamma-produced materiality… external, nutriment-originated, temperature-originated, and non-percipient-being-originated derived materiality." Only one.

Nasampayuttapaccayo nārammaṇapaccayasadiso.

The non-conjoined condition is similar to the non-object condition.

Navippayuttapaccaye “kusalaṃ paṭicca kusalo. Arūpe kusalova. Akusalaṃ…pe… arūpe akusalo. Abyākataṃ paṭicca abyākato, arūpe vipākakiriyābyākataṃ. Bāhiraṃ asañña…pe… upādārūpa”nti imā tissova pucchā vissajjitā. Nonatthinovigatapaccayā nārammaṇapaccayasadisā. Nasahajātananissayanoatthinoavigatapaccayā panettha cattāropi na labbhantīti.

In the non-disjoined condition: "A wholesome phenomenon depends on a wholesome phenomenon. In the immaterial sphere, only the wholesome. An unwholesome phenomenon… in the immaterial sphere, only the unwholesome. An indeterminate phenomenon depends on an indeterminate phenomenon; in the immaterial sphere, resultant and functional indeterminate. External, non-percipient-being-originated… derived materiality." These three questions are answered. The non-existence and non-disappearance conditions are similar to the non-object condition. The non-co-nascent, non-support, non-existence, and non-disappearance conditions are not obtained here.

Evaṃ paccanīke labbhamānapañhavissajjanaṃ dassetvā tato “nahetuyā dve. Nārammaṇe pañca. Nādhipatiyā nava. Nānantare nasamanantare nāññamaññe naupanissaye pañca. Napurejāte satta. Napacchājāte nāsevane nava. Nakamme tīṇi. Navipāke nava. Nāhāre naindriye najhāne namagge ekaṃ. Nasampayutte pañca. Navippayutte tīṇi. Nonatthinovigatesu pañcā”ti vissajjanavāragaṇanā vuttāti ayaṃ ekamūlakanayo.

Having thus shown the answers to the questions obtainable in the negative section, then: "In non-root condition, two. In non-object condition, five. In non-predominance condition, nine. In non-proximity, non-contiguity, non-mutuality, and non-support conditions, five. In non-pre-nascence condition, seven. In non-post-nascence and non-repetition conditions, nine. In non-kamma condition, three. In non-result condition, nine. In non-nutriment, non-faculty, non-jhāna, and non-path conditions, one. In non-conjoined condition, five. In non-disjoined condition, three. In non-existence and non-disappearance conditions, five." Thus is stated the enumeration of the sections of answers. This is the single-root method.

Imināva nayena dvimūlakādīsupi yathānurūpaṃ nayo netabbo, pāḷiyaṃ pana “nahetupaccayā nārammaṇe eka”ntiādinā vissajjanavāragaṇanāva dassitāti ayaṃ paccayapaccanīyanayo.

By this same method, the method should be applied appropriately to the two-root sections and so on. In the Pāḷi text, however, only the enumeration of the sections of answers is shown, beginning with: "Not by way of root condition, in non-object condition, one." This is the condition-negative method.

Iminā vuttānusāreneva “kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā nārammaṇapaccayā”tiādinā anulomapaccanīyanaye, “akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca akusalo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā”tiādinā paccanīyānulomanaye pañhavissajjananayo veditabbo[V 0.0363]. Pāḷiyaṃ panettha vissajjanavāragaṇanāva dassitāti [M 0.0474] ayaṃ anulomapaccanīyakusalattike paṭiccavāranayo.

In accordance with what has been said, the method of answering questions should be understood in the positive-negative method, beginning with, "Dependent on a wholesome phenomenon, an indeterminate phenomenon arises by way of root condition, not by way of object condition," and so on; and in the negative-positive method, beginning with, "Dependent on an unwholesome phenomenon, an unwholesome phenomenon arises not by way of root condition, but by way of object condition," and so on. Here in the Pāḷi, only the enumeration of the sections of answers is shown. This is the method of the conditionality section in the wholesome triad of the positive-negative method.

Sahajātavārādīsupi chavāresu paṭiccavāre vuttānusārena sabbattha nayo netabbo. Ye pana tattha tattha pāḷivisesā, atthavisesā ca upalabbhanti, te paṭṭhānapāḷiaṭṭhakathāsu eva sabbākārato gahetabbā. Idha pana te sabbe saṅkhepanayato dassiyamānāpi ganthabhāriyaṃ karontīti na dassitā.

In the six sections beginning with the co-nascent section, too, the method should be applied everywhere in accordance with what has been said in the conditionality section. However, whatever particular distinctions in the Pāḷi and particular meanings are found in various places, these should be grasped in all their aspects only from the Paṭṭhāna Pāḷi and its commentaries. Here, however, even if they were all to be shown in a condensed manner, they are not shown because they would make the book too heavy.

Tesu pana vāresu “kusalaṃ dhammaṃ sahajāto kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā… kusalaṃ dhammaṃ nissāya… kusalaṃ dhammaṃ saṃsaṭṭho… kusalaṃ dhammaṃ sampayutto kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā”ti evaṃ ādito pañcasu vāresu pāḷigati ñātabbā. Tesu ca paṭiccasahajātā ekatthā, paccayanissayā ekatthā, saṃsaṭṭhasampayuttā ekatthā. Tattha “kusalaṃ dhammaṃ sahajāto”tiādīsu kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca tena sahajāto hutvātiādinā yathānurūpaṃ attho veditabbo. Pacchime pana pañhāvāre “kusalo dhammo kusalassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo. Kusalā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. Kusalo abyākatassa…pe… kusalassa ca abyākatassa ca…pe… kusalā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañcā”tiādinā hetupaccaye,

In these sections, the course of the Pāḷi in the first five sections should be known as follows: "Co-nascent with a wholesome phenomenon, a wholesome phenomenon arises by way of root condition. By way of condition for a wholesome phenomenon… by way of support for a wholesome phenomenon… intermingled with a wholesome phenomenon… associated with a wholesome phenomenon, a wholesome phenomenon arises by way of root condition." And among these, the conditionality and co-nascent sections have one meaning; the condition and support sections have one meaning; the intermingled and associated sections have one meaning. Therein, in phrases such as "co-nascent with a wholesome phenomenon," the meaning should be understood appropriately as "dependent on that wholesome phenomenon and having become co-nascent with it," and so on. But in the last section, the question section, regarding root condition: "A wholesome phenomenon is a condition for a wholesome phenomenon by way of root condition. Wholesome roots are a condition for the associated aggregates by way of root condition. A wholesome phenomenon for an indeterminate one… for a wholesome one and an indeterminate one… wholesome roots for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter," and so on, in the root condition.

“Kusalo dhammo kusalassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ samādiyitvā uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ paccavekkhati. Pubbe suciṇṇāni…pe… jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā jhānaṃ… sekhā gotrabhuṃ vodānaṃ maggaṃ paccavekkhanti. Sekhā vā puthujjanā vā kusalaṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassanti. Cetopariyañāṇena kusalacittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānanti[M 0.0475]. Ākāsānañcāyatanakusalaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanakusalassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Ākiñcaññāyatanakusalaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanakusalassa… kusalā khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa cetopariyapubbenivāsayathākammūpagaanāgataṃsañāṇassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo.

"A wholesome phenomenon is a condition for a wholesome phenomenon by way of object condition. Having given a gift, undertaken the precepts, or performed the Uposatha observance, one reflects upon it. Past well-done deeds… having emerged from jhāna, one reviews the jhāna… trainees review the change-of-lineage consciousness, purification, and the path. Trainees or worldlings contemplate a wholesome phenomenon as impermanent, suffering, and non-self. With the knowledge of penetration of others' minds, one knows the mind of one endowed with a wholesome mind. The wholesome sphere of infinite space is a condition for the wholesome sphere of infinite consciousness by way of object condition. The wholesome sphere of nothingness is a condition for the wholesome sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception… Wholesome aggregates are a condition, by way of object condition, for the knowledge of psychic powers, the knowledge of penetration of others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their kamma, and the knowledge of the future.

Kusalo akusalassa…pe… dānaṃ datvā…pe… katvā taṃ assādeti abhinandati. Taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati. Diṭṭhi vicikicchā uddhaccaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati. Pubbe suciṇṇāni assādeti [V 0.0364] …pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati. Jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā jhānaṃ assādeti…pe… uddhaccaṃ uppajjati. Jhāne parihīne vippaṭisārissa domanassaṃ uppajjati.

"A wholesome phenomenon is a condition for an unwholesome phenomenon… Having given a gift… having performed it, one savors it and delights in it. Taking that as object, lust arises. Wrong view, doubt, restlessness, and displeasure arise. One savors past well-done deeds… displeasure arises. Having emerged from jhāna, one savors the jhāna… restlessness arises. When one has fallen away from jhāna, displeasure arises for one who is remorseful.

Kusalo abyākatassa…pe… paccayo. Arahā maggaṃ paccavekkhati. Pubbe suciṇṇāni… kusala…pe… vipassati…pe… vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjati. Ākāsānañcāyatanakusalaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanavipākassa…pe… kiriyassa. Ākiñcaññāyatana…pe… vipākassa ca kiriyassa ca. Kusalā khandhā cetopariya…pe… anāgataṃsañāṇassa āvajjanāya.

"A wholesome phenomenon is a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon… An Arahant reviews the path. Past well-performed deeds… wholesome… contemplates with insight… resultant consciousness and registering arise. The wholesome sphere of infinite space is a condition for the resultant consciousness of the sphere of infinite consciousness… and for the functional consciousness. The sphere of nothingness… is a condition for the resultant and functional consciousness. Wholesome aggregates are a condition for the knowledge of penetration of others' minds… and for the adverting to the knowledge of the future.

Akusalo akusalassa…pe… paccayo. Rāgaṃ assādeti…pe… uddhaccaṃ uppajjati. Akusalo kusalassa…pe… paccayo. Sekhā pahīne kilese…pe… anāgataṃsañāṇassa. Akusalo abyākatassa… arahā pahīne kilese…pe… āvajjanāya.

"An unwholesome phenomenon is a condition for an unwholesome phenomenon… One savors lust… restlessness arises. An unwholesome phenomenon is a condition for a wholesome phenomenon… Trainees review abandoned defilements… for the knowledge of the future. An unwholesome phenomenon is a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon… An Arahant reviews abandoned defilements… for adverting.

Abyākato abyākatassa… arahā phalaṃ paccavekkhati. Nibbānaṃ, cakkhuṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbaṃ vipassati. Dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati…pe… ākiñcaññāyatanakiriyaṃ…pe… kiriyassa. Rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… āvajjanāya. Abyākato kusalassa… sekhā phalaṃ…pe… anāgataṃsañāṇassa. Abyākato akusalassa… cakkhuṃ assādetī”tiādinā ārammaṇapaccaye ca,

"An indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon… An Arahant reviews the fruition. One contemplates Nibbāna, the eye… the tangible object with insight. With the divine eye, one sees forms… the functional consciousness of the sphere of nothingness… for the functional consciousness. The form base is a condition for eye-consciousness… for adverting. An indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for a wholesome phenomenon… Trainees review the fruition… for the knowledge of the future. An indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for an unwholesome phenomenon… one savors the eye," and so on, in the object condition,

“Kusalo [M 0.0476] kusalassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ datvā”tiādinā adhipatipaccaye ca,

"A wholesome phenomenon is a condition for a wholesome phenomenon by way of predominance condition. There is object-predominance and co-nascent predominance. As to object-predominance: 'having given a gift,' and so on, in the predominance condition,

“Kusalo kusalassa anantarapaccayena paccayo”tiādinā vitthārato anantarasamanantarasahajātaaññamaññanissayapaccayesu ca,

"'A wholesome phenomenon is a condition for a wholesome phenomenon by way of proximity condition,' and so on, in detail in the proximity, contiguity, co-nascence, mutuality, and support conditions,

“Kusalo kusalassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇūpanissayo anantarūpanissayo pakatūpanissayo. Ārammaṇūpanissayo – dānaṃ datvā”tiādinā ārammaṇapaccaye vuttanayena, “anantarūpanissayo – purimā purimā kusalā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimāna”ntiādinā [V 0.0365] anantarapaccaye vuttanayeneva, “pakatūpanissayo – saddhaṃ upanissāya…pe… uposathakammaṃ karoti. Jhānaṃ, vipassanaṃ, maggaṃ, abhiññaṃ, samāpattiṃ uppādeti. Sīlaṃ, sutaṃ, cāgaṃ, paññaṃ upanissāya…pe… paṭhamassa jhānassa parikammaṃ paṭhamassa jhānassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo…pe… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassa…pe… yathākammūpagañāṇaṃ anāgataṃsañāṇassa…pe… paṭhamassa maggassa parikammaṃ paṭhamassa…pe… tatiyo maggo catutthassa. Maggo sekhānaṃ atthapaṭisambhidāya…pe… ṭhānāṭhānakosallassa upanissaya. Kusalo akusalassa…pe… ārammaṇūpanissayo. Pakatūpa…pe… pakatūpanissayo – saddhaṃ upanissāya mānaṃ jappeti. Diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti…pe… saddhā sīlaṃ sutaṃ cāgo paññā rāgassa, dosassa, mohassa, mānassa, diṭṭhiyā. Patthanāya…pe… kusalo abyākatassa…pe… ārammaṇūpanissayo. Anantarūpanissayo. Pakatūpa…pe… pakatūpanissayo – saddhaṃ upanissāya attānaṃ ātāpeti…pe… kāyikassa sukhassa, dukkhassa, phalasamāpattiyā. Kusalaṃ kammaṃ vipākassa…pe… maggo arahato atthapaṭisambhidāya paccayo.

A skillful state is a condition for a skillful state by way of decisive support condition. There are three types: object decisive support, immediate decisive support, and natural decisive support. Object decisive support—‘having given a gift,’ etc., is explained in the same manner as in the object condition. Immediate decisive support—‘the preceding skillful aggregates are a condition for the succeeding ones,’ etc., is explained in the same way as in the contiguity condition. Natural decisive support—relying on faith… one performs the Uposatha observance. One develops jhāna, insight, the path, higher knowledge, or attainments. Relying on virtue, learning, generosity, or wisdom… the preliminary work for the first jhāna is a condition for the first jhāna by way of decisive support condition… the base of nothingness for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception… knowledge of rebirth according to kamma for knowledge of the future… the preliminary work for the first path for the first path… the third path for the fourth. The path is a decisive support for the analytical knowledge of meaning for trainees… for skill in discerning what is possible and impossible. A skillful state is a condition for an unskillful state… by way of object decisive support. Natural decisive support… relying on faith, one engenders conceit. One grasps a view… faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom are a decisive support for lust, hatred, delusion, conceit, and wrong view. Aspiration… A skillful state is a condition for an indeterminate state… by way of object decisive support, immediate decisive support, and natural decisive support. Natural decisive support—relying on faith, one torments oneself… for bodily pleasure, pain, or fruition attainment. Skillful kamma is a condition for its result… the path is a condition for the analytical knowledge of meaning for an arahant.

Akusalo [M 0.0477] akusalassa…pe… pakatūpanissayo – rāgaṃ upanissāya pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… samphaṃ palapati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati. Dosaṃ, mohaṃ, mānaṃ, diṭṭhiṃ, patthanaṃ upanissāya…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati…pe… pāṇātipāto pāṇātipātassa…pe… saṅghabhedakammassa…pe… paccayo.

An unskillful state is a condition for an unskillful state… by way of natural decisive support—relying on lust, one kills a living being… engages in frivolous talk… splits the Sangha. Relying on hatred, delusion, conceit, wrong view, or aspiration… one splits the Sangha… killing a living being is a condition for killing a living being… for schismatic action… is a condition.

Akusalo kusalassa…pe… pakatūpanissayo – rāgaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… maggaṃ uppādeti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti. Rāgo…pe… patthanā. Saddhāya, sīlassa…pe… paññāya upanissaya. Pāṇaṃ hantvā tassa paṭighātatthāya dānaṃ detī”tiādinā ca upanissayapaccaye ca,

An unskillful state is a condition for a skillful state… by way of natural decisive support—relying on lust, one gives a gift… develops the path… produces an attainment. Lust… aspiration is a decisive support for faith, for virtue… for wisdom. And in the decisive support condition: ‘Having killed a living being, one gives a gift for the purpose of counteracting it,’ and so on.

“Abyākato abyākatassa purejātapaccayena paccayo…pe… ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – arahā cakkhuṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbe, vatthuṃ vipassati…pe… dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati…pe… rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… vatthupurejātaṃ – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… vatthu vipākābyākatāna”ntiādinā purejātapaccaye ca,

‘An indeterminate state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of prenascence condition… Object-prenascence: an arahant sees with insight the eye… tangible objects, the base… sees form with the divine eye… the form base is a condition for eye-consciousness… Base-prenascence: the eye base is a condition for eye-consciousness… the base for the resultant indeterminate aggregates,’ and so on, and in the prenascence condition.

“Kusalo [V 0.0366] abyākatassa…pe… pacchājātā kusalā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassā”tiādinā pacchājātapaccaye ca,

‘A skillful state is a condition for an indeterminate state… Post-nascent skillful aggregates are a condition for this pre-nascent body,’ and so on, and in the post-nascence condition.

“Kusalo kusalassa…pe… purimā purimā kusalā khandhā”tiādinā āsevanapaccaye ca,

‘A skillful state is a condition for a skillful state… The preceding skillful aggregates,’ and so on, and in the repetition condition.

“Sahajātā nānākkhaṇikā, sahajātā kusalā cetanā…pe… sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ. Nānākkhaṇikā vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpāna”ntiādinā kammapaccaye ca,

‘Co-nascent and non-contemporaneous. Co-nascent skillful volition is a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter. Non-contemporaneous volition is a condition for the resultant aggregates and for kamma-produced matter,’ and so on, and in the kamma condition.

“Abyākato abyākatassa…pe… eko khandho tiṇṇanna”ntiādinā vipākapaccaye ca,

‘An indeterminate state is a condition for an indeterminate state… One aggregate is a condition for three,’ and so on, and in the result condition.

“Kusalo [M 0.0478] kusalassā”tiādinā āhārapaccayādīsu ca, “kusalo abyākatassa, sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, sahajātā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ. Pacchājātā imassa kāyassa…pe… abyākato kusalassa…pe… purejātaṃ vatthu kusalānaṃ khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo”tiādinā vippayuttapaccayādīsu ca pāḷigati veditabbā.

‘A skillful state is a condition for a skillful state,’ and so on, and in the nutriment condition and others; ‘A skillful state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of co-nascence and post-nascence. Co-nascent states are a condition for mind-originated matter. Post-nascent states are a condition for this body… An indeterminate state is a condition for a skillful state… A pre-nascent base is a condition for the skillful aggregates by way of dissociation condition,’ and so on, and in the dissociation condition and others—the course of the Pāli text should be understood.

Tattha kusaladhammo nāmesa yasmā uppajjanto ṭhapetvā pacchājātapaccayaṃ, vipākapaccayañca sesehi dvāvīsatiyā paccayehi uppajjati. Kusalassa ca paccayo honto ṭhapetvā purejātapacchājātavipākavippayuttapaccaye sesehi vīsatiyā paccayehi paccayo hoti. Evaṃ kusalo kusalādīnaṃ, akusalo ca akusalādīnaṃ yathānurūpaṃ paccayā honti, tasmā kusalādīnaṃ taṃtaṃpaccayuppannavibhāgaṃ dassetuṃ pañhāvāro vutto. Tattha sekhā gotrabhunti sotāpannaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, vodānanti sakadāgāmianāgāmino. Tesaṃ hi gotrabhucittaṃ vodānaṃ nāma. Maggā vuṭṭhahitvāti maggavīthito vuṭṭhāya. Na hi maggānantarā paccavekkhaṇā nāma atthīti ayaṃ anulomapaṭṭhāne kusalattikanayo.

Here, a skillful state, when arising, arises by means of twenty-two conditions, excluding the post-nascence condition and the result condition. And when a skillful state is a condition, it is a condition by means of twenty conditions, excluding the pre-nascence, post-nascence, result, and dissociation conditions. Thus, a skillful state is a condition for a skillful state and others, and an unskillful state is a condition for an unskillful state and others, as is appropriate. Therefore, the question section is stated to show the classification of the skillful states and so on, which arise from their respective conditions. Herein, ‘the learner’s change-of-lineage’ is said with reference to the stream-enterer. ‘Purification’ refers to the once-returner and the non-returner. For them, the change-of-lineage consciousness is called purification. ‘Having emerged from the path’ means having emerged from the path process. For there is no reviewing immediately after the path. This is the method of the skillful triad in the forward order of the Paṭṭhāna.

Vedanāttikādīsu “sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca dve khandhā. Dve khandhe [V 0.0367] paṭicca eko khandho”tiādinā kusalattike vuttānusārena paṭiccavārādīsu pañhāvārapariyosānesu sattasu vāresu ekekasmiṃ paccayānulomādīhi ca ekamūlādīhi nayehi ca sabbattikesu labbhamānapadavasena gaṇanānayo yojetvā ñātabbo. Tattha vedanāttike vedanākkhandhassa alabbhanato “ekaṃ khandhaṃ nissāya dve khandhā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Sabbattha viseso [M 0.0479] pāḷiaṭṭhakathānusāreneva ñātabboti ayaṃ anulomapaṭilome tikapaṭṭhānanayo.

In the triad of feelings and others, ‘Dependent on a state associated with pleasant feeling, a state associated with pleasant feeling arises by way of root condition. Dependent on one aggregate associated with pleasant feeling, two aggregates arise. Dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate arises,’ and so on. Following the method explained in the skillful triad, in the dependent origination section and others, in each of the seven sections ending with the question section, the method of calculation should be applied and understood according to the terms obtainable in all the triads, by the methods of the forward order of conditions and so on, and the single-root method and so on. There, in the triad of feelings, since the feeling aggregate is not included, it is said, ‘dependent on one aggregate, two aggregates,’ and so on. Everywhere, the specific details should be understood only in accordance with the Pāli text and the commentaries. This is the method of the triad section of the Paṭṭhāna in the forward and reverse order.

Dukapaṭṭhāne pana “hetuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Alobhaṃ paṭicca adoso. Amoho. Adosaṃ amohaṃ paṭicca alobho. Adoso. Lobhaṃ paṭicca moho. Mohaṃ paṭicca lobho. Dosaṃ paṭicca moho. Mohaṃ paṭicca doso. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe hetuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu dhammo uppajjati…pe… hetū ca nahetū ca. Nahetuṃ paṭicca nahetu dhammo na…pe… hetū ca nahetū cā”tiādinā hetuduke,

Now, in the dyad section of the Paṭṭhāna: ‘Dependent on a root state, a root state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on non-greed, non-hatred arises; non-delusion arises. Dependent on non-hatred and non-delusion, non-greed arises; non-hatred arises. Dependent on greed, delusion arises. Dependent on delusion, greed arises. Dependent on hatred, delusion arises. Dependent on delusion, hatred arises. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on a root state, a non-root state arises… roots and non-roots. Dependent on a non-root state, a non-root state… roots and non-roots,’ and so on, in the root dyad.

“Sahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Sahetukaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ…pe… sahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca. Ahetuko…pe… cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… sahetuko ca, ahetuko ca…pe… ahetukaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca ahetuko. Vicikicchāsahagataṃ uddhaccasahagataṃ mohaṃ paṭicca sampayuttakā khandhā…pe… cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ. Āhārasamuṭṭhāna”ntiādinā sahetukadukādīsu ca kenaciviññeyyadukavajjitesu sabbadukesu paccekaṃ paṭiccavārādīsu sattasu mahāvāresu ekekasmiṃ paccayānulomādīsu catūsu nayesu ekamūlakādīhi sabbavārehi kusalattike vuttānusārena yathānurūpaṃ vibhaṅganayo yojetvā ñātabbo. Sabbasmimpi hi paṭṭhāne kenaciviññeyyadukaṃ na labbhatīti ayaṃ dukapaṭṭhānanayo.

A state with roots arises dependent on a state with roots by way of root condition. One aggregate with roots... dependent on a state with roots... A state without roots... mind-originated matter. At the moment of rebirth... with roots and without roots... a state without roots arises dependent on an aggregate without roots. Dependent on delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness, the associated aggregates arise... mind-originated matter. ‘Nutriment-originated matter,’ and so on in the dyads of with-roots, etc., except for the ‘knowable-by-some-means’ dyad. In all dyads, in each of the seven great sections on conditionality, etc., in the four methods of condition-sequence, etc., and in all sections by means of the single-root method, etc., the method of analysis should be applied appropriately, following the method explained in the wholesome triad. For in the entire Paṭṭhāna, the ‘knowable-by-some-means’ dyad is not obtainable. This is the method of the Dyad Paṭṭhāna.

Dukatikapaṭṭhāne pana “hetuṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā”tiādinā hetudukena saddhiṃ kusalattike kusalaṃ padaṃ yojetvā paṭiccavārādīsu sattasu vāresu paccayānulomādīnaṃ catunnaṃ nayānaṃ vasena labbhamānakapaccayā ekamūlakādinayehi dassitā[M 0.0480]. Yathā ca kusalaṃ padaṃ, evaṃ akusalaṃ padaṃ, abyākatañca hetudukena yojetvā vuttanayena dassetvā hetukusaladukatikanti ṭhapitaṃ. Pāḷi pana atisaṃkhittā. Yathā kusalattikaṃ, evaṃ “hetuṃ sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā”tiādinā labbhamānakapadavasena vedanāttikādayopi hetudukena [V 0.0368] yojetvā hetuvedanadukatikādīni ekavīsatidukatikāni dassitānīti. Yathā ca hetudukena saddhiṃ labbhamānakapadavasena dvāvīsatitikā yojitā, evaṃ sahetukadukādīhi sabbehi saddhiṃ paccekaṃ dvāvīsatitikā yojetabbā. Pāḷi panettha ito paresupi sabbattha atisaṃkhittā. Evaṃ dvāvīsatitike gahetvā dukasate pakkhipitvā dukatikapaṭṭhānaṃ desitanti ayaṃ dukatikapaṭṭhānanayo.

Now, in the Dyad-Triad Paṭṭhāna, with such phrases as, “a wholesome phenomenon that is a root arises dependent on a wholesome phenomenon that is a root by way of root condition,” the term “wholesome” in the Wholesome Triad is connected with the Root Dyad. In the seven sections, beginning with the Conditionality Section, the conditions obtained by way of the four methods, such as the Causal Sequence, are shown by means of the single-root method and others. Just as the term “wholesome” is treated, so too the terms “unwholesome” and “indeterminate” are connected with the Root Dyad and presented in the same way, thus establishing the Root-Wholesome Dyad-Triad. The Pāḷi, however, is extremely condensed. As with the Wholesome Triad, so too with such phrases as, “a phenomenon that is a root and is associated with pleasant feeling arises dependent on a phenomenon that is a root and is associated with pleasant feeling by way of root condition,” the twenty-one dyad-triads, such as the Root-Feeling Dyad-Triad, are presented by connecting them with the Root Dyad by way of the terms obtained. Just as the twenty-two triads are connected with the Root Dyad by way of the terms obtained, so too each of the twenty-two triads should be connected individually with all the dyads, such as the ‘with-roots’ dyad. Here too, and in all subsequent instances, the Pāḷi is extremely condensed. Thus, by taking the twenty-two triads and incorporating them into the hundred dyads, the Dyad-Triad Paṭṭhāna is taught. This is the method of the Dyad-Triad Paṭṭhāna.

Tikadukapaṭṭhānepi “kusalaṃ hetuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo hetu dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā”tiādinā kusalattikena saddhiṃ hetupadaṃ yojetvā paṭiccavārādīsu sattasu mahāvāresu paccayānulomādinayacatukkavasena labbhamānakapaccayā ekamūlādīhi sabbavārehi dassitā. Yathā hetupadaṃ, evaṃ nahetupadampi kusalattikena saddhiṃ yojetvā kusalahetu tikadukanti ṭhapitaṃ. Yathā ca kusalattikena saddhiṃ hetudukaṃ, evaṃ “sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ hetuṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭiccā”tiādinā vedanāttikādīhipi taṃ yojetvā vedanāttikadukādīni ekavīsatitikadukādīni dassitāni. Yathā ca hetudukaṃ, evaṃ sahetukādayopi sabbe paccekaṃ dvāvīsatiyā tikehi labbhamānapadavaseneva yojitā. Evaṃ dukasataṃ dvāvīsatiyā tikesu pakkhipitvā tikadukapaṭṭhānaṃ desitanti ayaṃ tikadukapaṭṭhānanayo.

Also in the Triad-Dyad Paṭṭhāna, with such phrases as, “a wholesome phenomenon that is a root arises dependent on a wholesome phenomenon that is a root by way of root condition,” the term “root” is connected with the Wholesome Triad, showing the conditions obtained by way of the four methods, such as the Causal Sequence, in the seven great sections beginning with the Conditionality Section, in all sections beginning with the single-root method. Just as the term “root” is explained, so too the term “not-a-root” is combined with the Wholesome Triad, establishing the Wholesome-Root Triad-Dyad. And just as the Root Dyad is combined with the Wholesome Triad, so too, with such phrases as, “dependent on a wholesome phenomenon that is a root and is associated with pleasant feeling…,” it is connected with the Feeling Triad and others, showing the twenty-one triad-dyads, such as the Feeling Triad-Dyad. And just as the Root Dyad is explained, so too all those beginning with the ‘with-roots’ dyad are each individually connected with the twenty-two triads by way of the terms obtained. Thus, by taking the hundred dyads and incorporating them into the twenty-two triads, the Triad-Dyad Paṭṭhāna is taught. This is the method of the Triad-Dyad Paṭṭhāna.

Tikatikapaṭṭhānepi [M 0.0481] “kusalaṃ sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā”tiādinā kusalattikaṃ vedanāttikādīhi sabbattikehi, vedanāttikādayo ca kusalattikādīhi vuttanayena yojetvā paccayā dassitā. Evaṃ tikesu eva tike pakkhipitvā tikatikapaṭṭhānaṃ desitanti ayaṃ tikatikapaṭṭhānanayo.

Also in the Triad-Triad Paṭṭhāna, with such phrases as, “a wholesome phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling arises dependent on a wholesome phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling by way of root condition,” the Wholesome Triad is connected with the Feeling Triad and all other triads, and the Feeling Triad and others are in turn connected with the Wholesome Triad and others, in the manner stated, and the conditions are shown. Thus, by incorporating triads into triads, the Triad-Triad Paṭṭhāna is taught. This is the method of the Triad-Triad Paṭṭhāna.

Dukadukapaṭṭhānepi “hetuṃ sahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu sahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā”tiādinā hetudukaṃ sahetukādīhi, sahetukañca hetudukādīhi yojetvā heṭṭhā vuttanayehi paccayā dassitā. Evaṃ dukesu eva duke pakkhipitvā dukadukapaṭṭhānaṃ desitanti ayaṃ dukadukapaṭṭhānanayo. Evaṃ tāva anulomapaṭṭhāne –

Also in the Dyad-Dyad Paṭṭhāna, with such phrases as, “a phenomenon that is a root and is with roots arises dependent on a phenomenon that is a root and is with roots by way of root condition,” the Root Dyad is connected with the ‘with-roots’ dyad and others, and the ‘with-roots’ dyad is in turn connected with the Root Dyad and others, and the conditions are shown by the methods stated above. Thus, by incorporating dyads into dyads, the Dyad-Dyad Paṭṭhāna is taught. This is the method of the Dyad-Dyad Paṭṭhāna. Thus far, in the Anuloma Paṭṭhāna—

“Tikañca paṭṭhānavaraṃ dukuttamaṃ,

Dukatikañceva [V 0.0369] tikadukañca;

Tikatikañceva dukadukañca,

Cha anulomamhi nayā sugambhīrā”ti. –

“The supreme Paṭṭhāna is the Triad, the best is the Dyad, the Dyad-Triad and the Triad-Dyad; the Triad-Triad and the Dyad-Dyad—these six profound methods are in the Anuloma.”

Vuttā cha nayā veditabbā. Paccayavasena panetesu chasu ekekasmiṃ paṭṭhāne paccayānulomādīnaṃ catunnaṃ nayānaṃ vasena etena pariyāyena catuvīsatinayapaṭimaṇḍitamidaṃ dhammānulomapaṭṭhānanti veditabbaṃ. Ayaṃ anulomapaṭṭhānanayo.

The six methods thus stated should be understood. However, by way of conditions, in each of these six Paṭṭhānas, by way of the four methods beginning with the Causal Sequence, this Dhammānuloma Paṭṭhāna is adorned with twenty-four methods in this sequence, and should be understood as such. This is the method of the Anuloma Paṭṭhāna.

Paccanīyapaṭṭhāne pana “nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Akusalaṃ abyākataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca…pe… dve khandhā, cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpa”ntiādinā tikapaṭṭhāne, “nahetuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nahetuṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca…pe… cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpa”ntiādinā dukapaṭṭhāne ca, “nahetuṃ nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu nakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nahetuṃ nakusalaṃ abyākataṃ [M 0.0482] ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā”tiādinā dukatikapaṭṭhāne ca, “nakusalaṃ nahetuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nakusalo nahetu dhammo uppajjatī”tiādinā tikadukapaṭṭhāne ca, “nakusalaṃ nasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nakusalo nasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto dhammo uppajjatī”tiādinā tikatikapaṭṭhāne ca, “nahetuṃ nasahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu nasahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā”tiādinā dukadukapaṭṭhāne cāti chasu paccanīyapaṭṭhānesu anulomatikapaṭṭhānādīsu chasu paṭṭhānesu vuttena sabbena pakārena pāḷinayo veditabbo. Idañca kusalādīnaṃ, hetuādīnañca dhammānaṃ paccayuppannabhāvapaṭikkhepavasena pavattattā dhammapaccanīyapaṭṭhānaṃ nāma jātaṃ. Tattha hi nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭiccāti kusalassa paccayapaṭikkhepo. Nakusalo dhammo uppajjatīti kusalassa paccayuppannabhāvapaṭikkhepo. Tathā “akusalaṃ abyākataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca…pe… akusalā, abyākatā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ uppajjatī”ti evamādinā nayenettha attho veditabbo. Evamettha paccanīyapaṭṭhāne –

Now, in the Paccanīya Paṭṭhāna, the method of the Pāḷi should be understood in all aspects as stated in the six Anuloma Paṭṭhānas. In the six Paccanīya Paṭṭhānas: in the Tika Paṭṭhāna, with such phrases as, “a not-wholesome phenomenon arises dependent on a not-wholesome phenomenon by way of root condition. Dependent on one unwholesome or indeterminate aggregate… and so on… two aggregates, and mind-originated matter”; in the Duka Paṭṭhāna, with such phrases as, “a phenomenon that is not-a-root arises dependent on a phenomenon that is not-a-root by way of root condition. Dependent on one aggregate that is not-a-root… and so on… mind-originated matter”; in the Dukatika Paṭṭhāna, with such phrases as, “a not-wholesome phenomenon that is not-a-root arises dependent on a not-wholesome phenomenon that is not-a-root by way of root condition. Dependent on one not-wholesome, indeterminate aggregate that is not-a-root… three aggregates”; in the Tikaduka Paṭṭhāna, with such phrases as, “a not-wholesome phenomenon that is not-a-root arises dependent on a not-wholesome phenomenon that is not-a-root”; in the Tikatika Paṭṭhāna, with such phrases as, “a not-wholesome phenomenon not associated with pleasant feeling arises dependent on a not-wholesome phenomenon not associated with pleasant feeling”; and in the Dukaduka Paṭṭhāna, with such phrases as, “a phenomenon that is not-a-root and not with roots arises dependent on a phenomenon that is not-a-root and not with roots by way of root condition.” This is called the Dhamma Paccanīya Paṭṭhāna because it proceeds by way of rejecting the state of being conditionally arisen for wholesome and other phenomena, as well as for roots and other phenomena. Here, “dependent on a not-wholesome phenomenon” is the rejection of the wholesome as a condition. “A not-wholesome phenomenon arises” is the rejection of the wholesome’s state of being conditionally arisen. Similarly, the meaning here should be understood by the method: “Dependent on one unwholesome or indeterminate aggregate… and so on… unwholesome and indeterminate aggregates and mind-originated matter arise.” Thus, in this Paccanīya Paṭṭhāna—

“Tikañca paṭṭhānavaraṃ dukuttamaṃ,

Dukatikañceva tikadukañca;

Tikatikañceva dukadukañca,

Cha paccanīyamhi nayā sugambhīrā”ti. –

“The triad, the supreme Paṭṭhāna, and the dyad, the best; the dyad-triad and the triad-dyad; the triad-triad and the dyad-dyad—these six profound methods are in the Paccanīya.”

Vuttā [V 0.0370] cha nayā veditabbā. Paccayavasena panetthāpi ekekasmiṃ paccayānulomādīnaṃ catunnaṃ catunnaṃ nayānaṃ vasena catuvīsatinayapaṭimaṇḍitamidaṃ dhammapaccanīyapaṭṭhānanti veditabbanti ayaṃ paccanīyapaṭṭhānanayo.

The six methods thus stated should be understood. However, by way of conditions, here too, in each one, by way of the four methods each, such as the progressive order of conditions, this Dhamma Paccanīya Paṭṭhāna is adorned with twenty-four methods, thus it should be understood. This is the method of the Paccanīya Paṭṭhāna.

Anulomapaccanīyapaṭṭhāne pana “kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Kusale khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpa”ntiādinā tikapaṭṭhāne, “hetuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu [M 0.0483] dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā”tiādinā dukapaṭṭhāne ca, “hetuṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu nakusalo dhammo uppajjatī”tiādinā dukatikapaṭṭhāne ca, “kusalaṃ hetuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nakusalo nahetu dhammo uppajjatī”tiādinā tikadukapaṭṭhāne ca, “kusalaṃ sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nakusalo nasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto dhammo uppajjatī”tiādinā tikatikapaṭṭhāne ca, “hetuṃ sahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu nasahetuko dhammo uppajjatī”tiādinā dukadukapaṭṭhāne ca heṭṭhā vuttanayena sabbena pakārena pāḷinayo veditabbo. Idaṃ kusalādīnaṃ dhammānaṃ paccayattaṃ appaṭikkhipitvā paccayuppannānaṃ kusalādibhāvapaṭikkhepavasena pavattattā dhammānulomapaccanīyapaṭṭhānaṃ nāma jātaṃ. Tattha hi kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭiccāti kusalassa paccayabhāvavidhānaṃ. Nakusalo dhammo uppajjatīti kusalassa paccayuppannabhāvanivāraṇaṃ, tasmā “kusale khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpa”ntiādinā vissajjanaṃ vuttanti veditabbanti evamettha anulomapaccanīyapaṭṭhāne –

Now, in the Anuloma Paccanīya Paṭṭhāna, the method of the Pāḷi should be understood in all aspects according to the method stated below: in the Tika Paṭṭhāna, with such phrases as, “Dependent on a wholesome phenomenon, a not-wholesome phenomenon arises by root condition.
