Dependent on wholesome aggregates, mind-originated materiality arises”; in the Duka Paṭṭhāna, with such phrases as, “Dependent on a root phenomenon, a rootless phenomenon arises by root condition”; in the Dukatika Paṭṭhāna, with such phrases as, “Dependent on a wholesome root phenomenon, a not-wholesome, rootless phenomenon arises”; in the Tikaduka Paṭṭhāna, with such phrases as, “Dependent on a wholesome root phenomenon, a not-wholesome, rootless phenomenon arises”; in the Tikatika Paṭṭhāna, with such phrases as, “Dependent on a wholesome phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling, a not-wholesome phenomenon not associated with pleasant feeling arises”; and in the Dukaduka Paṭṭhāna, with such phrases as, “Dependent on a root phenomenon accompanied by roots, a rootless phenomenon not accompanied by roots arises.” This is called the Dhamma Anuloma Paccanīya Paṭṭhāna because it proceeds by way of negating the wholesome nature, etc., of the conditionally arisen phenomena, without negating the nature as a condition of the wholesome phenomena, etc. For herein, “dependent on a wholesome phenomenon” is the establishment of the wholesome’s nature as a condition. “A not-wholesome phenomenon arises” is the negation of the wholesome nature of the conditionally arisen phenomenon. Therefore, it should be understood that the answer is given as, “dependent on wholesome aggregates, mind-originated materiality arises,” and so on. Thus, in this Anuloma Paccanīya Paṭṭhāna—

“Tikañca paṭṭhānavaraṃ dukuttamaṃ,

Dukatikañceva tikadukañca;

Tikatikañceva dukadukañca,

Cha anulomapaccanīyamhi nayā sugambhīrā”ti. –

“The triad, the supreme Paṭṭhāna, and the dyad, the best; the dyad-triad and the triad-dyad; the triad-triad and the dyad-dyad—these six profound methods are in the Anuloma Paccanīya.”

Vuttā cha nayā veditabbā. Paccayavasena panetthāpi ekekasmiṃ paccayānulomādīnaṃ catunnaṃ catunnaṃ nayānaṃ vasena catuvīsatinayapaṭimaṇḍitamidaṃ dhammānulomapaccanīyapaṭṭhānanti veditabbanti ayaṃ anulomapaccanīyapaṭṭhānanayo.

The six methods thus stated should be understood. However, by way of conditions, here too, in each one, by way of the four methods each, such as the progressive order of conditions, this Dhamma Anuloma Paccanīya Paṭṭhāna, adorned with twenty-four methods, should be understood. This is the method of the Anuloma Paccanīya Paṭṭhāna.

Paccanīyānulomapaṭṭhāne “nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca akusalo dhammo…pe… nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca [V 0.0371] abyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā”tiādinā tikapaṭṭhāne, “nahetuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu dhammo uppajjatī”tiādinā dukapaṭṭhāne ca, “nahetuṃ [M 0.0484] nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu akusalo dhammo…pe… hetu abyākato dhammo uppajjatīti”ādinā dukatikapaṭṭhāne ca, “nakusalaṃ nahetuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca akusalo hetu dhammo…pe… abyākato hetu dhammo uppajjatī”tiādinā tikadukapaṭṭhāne ca, “nakusalaṃ nasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca akusalo sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto dhammo…pe… abyākato sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto dhammo uppajjatī”tiādinā tikatikapaṭṭhāne ca, “nahetuṃ nasahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu sahetuko dhammo uppajjatī”tiādinā dukadukapaṭṭhāne ca, heṭṭhā vuttena pakārena pāḷinayo veditabbo. Idañca kusalādidhammānaṃ paccayattaṃ paṭikkhipitvā tesaṃ paccayuppannabhāvaappaṭikkhepavasena pavattattā dhammapaccanīyānulomapaṭṭhānaṃ nāma jātaṃ. Tattha nakusalaṃ dhammanti kusalassa paccayabhāvanivāraṇaṃ. Akusalo dhammo uppajjatīti akusalassa uppattividhānaṃ. Kusalaṃ pana paṭicca kusalassa uppattiabhāvato “kusalo dhammo uppajjatī”ti avatvā “akusalo dhammo uppajjatī”ti labbhamānapadavasena vuttaṃ. Kusalaṃ, hi akusalaṃ, abyākataṃ vā sahajātapaccayaṃ katvā uppajjamāno kusalo nāma natthi, tasmā akusalassa ca abyākatassa ca vasena desanā katā. Evamaññattha. Evamettha dhammapaccanīyānulomapaṭṭhāne –

In the Paccanīya Anuloma Paṭṭhāna, the method of the Pāḷi should be understood in the manner stated below: in the Tika Paṭṭhāna, with such phrases as, “Dependent on a not-wholesome phenomenon, an unwholesome phenomenon arises… an indeterminate phenomenon arises by root condition”; in the Duka Paṭṭhāna, with such phrases as, “Dependent on a not-root phenomenon, a root phenomenon arises”; in the Dukatika Paṭṭhāna, with such phrases as, “Dependent on a not-wholesome, not-root phenomenon, a wholesome root phenomenon arises… an indeterminate root phenomenon arises”; in the Tikaduka Paṭṭhāna, with such phrases as, “Dependent on a not-wholesome, not-root phenomenon, an unwholesome root phenomenon arises… an indeterminate root phenomenon arises”; in the Tikatika Paṭṭhāna, with such phrases as, “Dependent on a not-wholesome phenomenon not associated with pleasant feeling, an unwholesome phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling arises… an indeterminate phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling arises”; and in the Dukaduka Paṭṭhāna, with such phrases as, “Dependent on a not-root, not-accompanied-by-roots phenomenon, a root phenomenon accompanied by roots arises.” And this is called the Dhamma Paccanīya Anuloma Paṭṭhāna because it proceeds by negating the nature as a condition of wholesome and other phenomena, while not negating their state of being conditionally arisen. Herein, “a not-wholesome phenomenon” is the negation of the wholesome’s nature as a condition. “An unwholesome phenomenon arises” is the establishment of the unwholesome’s arising. However, since a wholesome phenomenon does not arise dependent on a not-wholesome phenomenon, instead of saying “a wholesome phenomenon arises,” the statement “an unwholesome phenomenon arises” is made based on the terms that are applicable. For there is no wholesome phenomenon that arises having made an unwholesome or indeterminate phenomenon its conascent condition; therefore, the teaching is given in terms of the unwholesome and the indeterminate. The same applies elsewhere. Thus, in this Dhamma Paccanīya Anuloma Paṭṭhāna—

“Tikañca paṭṭhānavaraṃ dukuttamaṃ,

Dukatikañceva tikadukañca;

Tikatikañceva dukadukañca,

Cha paccanīyānulomamhi nayā sugambhīrā”ti. –

“The triad, the supreme Paṭṭhāna, and the dyad, the best; the dyad-triad and the triad-dyad; the triad-triad and the dyad-dyad—these six very profound methods are in the Paccanīya Anuloma.”

Vuttā cha nayā veditabbā. Paccayavasena panetthāpi tikapaṭṭhānādīsu ekekasmiṃ paccayānulomādīnaṃ catunnaṃ catunnaṃ [M 0.0485] nayānaṃ vasena ekena pariyāyena catuvīsatinayapaṭimaṇḍitamidaṃ dhammapaccanīyānulomapaṭṭhānanti veditabbanti ayaṃ paccanīyānulomapaṭṭhānanayo.

The six methods thus stated should be understood. However, by way of conditions, here too, in each of the Tika Paṭṭhāna and so on, by way of the four methods each, such as the progressive order of conditions, in one permutation, this Dhamma Paccanīya Anuloma Paṭṭhāna, adorned with twenty-four methods, should be understood. This is the method of the Paccanīya Anuloma Paṭṭhāna.

Evamidaṃ bhagavatā anulomapaṭṭhānādīsu catūsu ekekasmiṃ paṭṭhāne tikadukādīnaññeva channaṃ channaṃ nayānaṃ vasena catuvīsatinayapaṭimaṇḍitaṃ samantapaṭṭhānamahāpakaraṇaṃ desitaṃ. Paccayavasena panetesu catuvīsatiyā paṭṭhānesu ekekasmiṃ paccayānulomādīnaṃ catunnaṃ catunnaṃ nayānaṃ [V 0.0372] vasenetaṃ channavutinayapaṭimaṇḍitaṃ hoti, dhammavaseneva cetaṃ pakaraṇaṃ catuvīsatisamantapaṭṭhānaṃ vuttanti ayamettha vibhaṅganayo.

Thus, by the Blessed One, in each of the four Paṭṭhānas, such as the Anuloma Paṭṭhāna, this great treatise of the Samanta Paṭṭhāna, adorned with twenty-four methods by way of the six methods each, such as the triad-dyad, was taught. Moreover, in each of these twenty-four Paṭṭhānas, by way of conditions, through the four methods each, such as the progressive order of conditions, it becomes adorned with ninety-six methods. And indeed, this treatise is called the twenty-four Samanta Paṭṭhānas by way of phenomena. This is the method of analysis here.

Mohavicchedaniyā abhidhammamātikatthavaṇṇanāya

Of the Mohavicchedanī, the Explanation of the Meaning of the Abhidhamma Matrix

Paṭṭhānamātikatthavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the meaning of the Paṭṭhāna matrix is completed.

Nigamanakathā

Concluding Discourse

Ettāvatā [M 0.0486] ca –

And thus far—

1.

1.

Mātikāyābhidhammassa, āraddhā atthavaṇṇanā;

Mohavicchedanī nāma, yā sā niṭṭhamupāgatā.

The explanation of the meaning of the Abhidhamma’s matrix, which was begun, called the Mohavicchedanī, has now come to completion.

2.

2.

Niṭṭhaṃ yathāyaṃ sampattā, lajjīhi abhipatthitā;

Sabbe niṭṭhaṃ tathā santā, samentu sumanorathā.

As this work, desired by the conscientious, has reached completion, so too may all good beings, reaching the final end, fulfill their noble wishes.

3.

3.

Yo gambhīro sasādīnaṃ, samuddova bhayāvaho;

Kālesmiṃ dhīmatañcāpi, api ganthāvalokane.

That which is deep, like the ocean, fear-inspiring to those with attachments, and even for the wise at times when examining the texts.

4.

4.

Paṭhamantaradhānassa, abhidhammassa tassa yaṃ;

Silālekhā nidhīnaṃva, dhammatthānaṃ pakāsikā.

For that Abhidhamma, which is the first to disappear, this commentary is an illuminator of the grounds of the Dhamma, like a stone inscription for treasures.

5.

5.

Nāvā viya samuddassa, sukhotaraṇapaddhati;

Pāḷiaṭṭhakathā cesā, parisuddhā anākulā.

Like a boat for the ocean, a path for easy crossing, this Pāḷi commentary is pure and unconfused.

6.

6.

Nayatopi [V 0.0373] avikkiṇṇā, asaṃkiṇṇā nikāyato;

Yato sakkacca sotabbā, saddhammaṭṭhitiyā satā.

It is not scattered in method, nor mixed with other collections; therefore, it should be listened to respectfully by the mindful for the sake of the True Dhamma’s endurance.

7.

7.

Saddhammaṭṭhitikāmena, anattukkaṃsanādito;

Mayāpi vaṇṇayantena, racitā suddhacetasā;

Tettiṃsabhāṇavārāya, parimāṇena tantiyā.

By me, desiring the stability of the True Dhamma, free from self-exaltation and the like, explaining this with a pure heart, this treatise was composed, its measure being thirty-three recitation sections.

8.

8.

Mātikāvaṇṇanā yā sā, yāva niṭṭhaṃ yathābalaṃ;

Sabbatthasaṅgahā esā, anākulapadakkamā.

This explanation of the Mātikā, which has reached completion according to my ability, is comprehensive in all respects, with an unconfused sequence of passages.

9.

9.

Yaṃ pattaṃ kusalaṃ tena, patvā sambodhimuttamaṃ;

Niṭṭhaṃ pāpeyyamakhile, pāṇino hitacetasā.

By the wholesome merit thereby attained, may I, having attained supreme perfect enlightenment, lead all beings to the final end, with a mind intent on their welfare.

10.

10.

Nānājanādhiramaṇīyatarassa,

Coḷaraṭṭhassa bhāramadhivāhakulandharassa;

Kāveripūtasalilena hitālayassa,

Rājādhirājavaravaṃsasupīṇitassa.

Of the Cola country, most delightful to its diverse people, bearing its burden like a mountain range; its dwellings benefited by the pure waters of the Kāverī, and well-nourished by the excellent lineage of the supreme king.

11.

11.

Majjhamhi [M 0.0487] coḷakakalaṅkanibhena maggaṃ,

Pūraṃ visālavibhavehi mahākulehi;

Pākāracakkaparikhāhi ca gopurehi,

Yuttaṃ janākulasusajjitarājamaggaṃ.

In its midst, a city, like the very moon of the Colas, full of great families with vast wealth; furnished with circles of ramparts, moats, and gate-towers, and with well-adorned royal roads crowded with people.

12.

12.

Sabbūpabhogaparibhogadhanehi nānā-

Vaṇṇehi puṇṇavividhāpaṇikehi sobhaṃ;

Coḷādhināgapuranandananāthabhūtaṃ,

Ye tattha sogatavihāravarābhirāmā.

Shining with wealth for all use and enjoyment, and with various shops full of diverse goods; the city of Coḷādhināgapura, a delight and a protector, wherein are those excellent and most delightful monasteries of the Sugata.

13.

13.

Tesaṃ [V 0.0374] mukhe janamanoharasatthubimba-

Sambhāvite mahati sajjanamānanīye;

Vijjālayehi udayācalasannibhehi,

Kelāsakūṭasikharopamacetiyehi.

In that great and noble place, honored by good people, at the entrance to those monasteries, are images of the Teacher that charm the minds of people; with schools resembling the sunrise mountain, and with stupas like the peaks of Mount Kelāsa.

14.

14.

Pāsādahammiyavarehi ca maṇḍapehi,

Jambambatālapanasāditarāvalīhi;

Nandopanandabhujagassa varassa bhoga-

Cakkāvalīsamasudhākatagopurehi.

With excellent palaces, mansions, and pavilions; with rows of jambu, mango, palm, jackfruit, and other trees; and with whitewashed gateways like the series of coils of the noble serpent Nandopananda.

15.

15.

Yutte visālasikatāsitamāḷakehi,

Yutte susīlayatisaṅghanisevitamhi;

Kalyāṇakammaniratehi haṭūpahāre,

Nāgajjunavhayavihāravare vasanto.

Dwelling in the excellent monastery called Nāgārjuna, which is furnished with spacious courtyards of white sand and frequented by communities of monks of excellent virtue, who are devoted to wholesome deeds and for whom offerings are brought.

16.

16.

Nāmena yo dhutadharaggasamānanāmo,

Candova pākaṭanabhoditavītapañño;

Satthantaresu nipuṇo piṭakattaye ca,

Vādībhayūthavipine migarājalīlo.

He whose name is like that of the foremost of ascetic practitioners, whose wisdom is like the moon clearly risen in the sky; skilled in other scriptures and in the three Piṭakas, with the bearing of a lion in the forest of disputants.

17.

17.

Yo [M 0.0488] sāgarova na vilaṅghati sīlavela-

Mappicchatādiguṇasāravibhūsitatto;

Joteti sāsanamalaṃ nikhilaṃ jahanto,

Sakkacca dhammavinayaṃ paridīpayanto.

He, like the ocean, does not transgress the shore of virtue, his person adorned with the essence of qualities such as fewness of desires; he illuminates the Dispensation, abandoning all defilement, carefully clarifying the Dhamma and Vinaya.

18.

18.

Tenābhidhammapiṭakaṇṇavavippakiṇṇa-

Sārattharatnanikareva samuddharitvā;

Sammāpajānagaḷalaṅkaraṇāya [V 0.0375] moha-

Vicchedanī viracitā ratanāvalī yā.

By him, having extracted the collection of essential meaning-jewels scattered throughout the ocean of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka, this Mohavicchedanī, also known as Ratanāvalī, was composed as an adornment for the wise.

19.

19.

Sāyaṃ pabhāsatu sukittivirājamānā,

Dhammesu mohatimiraṃ vinihacca sammā;

Ābhātu tāva jinasāsanajoti yāva,

Vattissatissa janatāhitamāvahantī.

May this work shine forth, resplendent with good fame, rightly dispelling the darkness of delusion concerning the Dhamma; may it shine as long as the light of the Conqueror’s Dispensation shall last, bringing benefit to the people.

Iti coḷaraṭṭhe mahākassapattherena viracitā

Thus, composed in the Cola country by the Elder Mahākassapa,

Mohavicchedanī nāma

named Mohavicchedanī,

Abhidhammamātikatthavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

the explanation of the meaning of the Abhidhamma Matrix is completed.
